God links *EHYEH* to the sacred 4-letter Name **YHVH** (Yahweh): **'THIS IS MY NAME FOREVER, AND THIS IS MY MEMORIAL NAME TO ALL GENERATIONS!'** (*zeh-shemi le-olam ve-zeh zikhri le-dor dor*).
cccReferences: CCC 203-213 (The Tetragrammaton YHWH as God's eternal covenant memorial name); CCC 209 (Reverence for the holy Name YHWH); Ps 135:13.
historicalContext: Establishing the Tetragrammaton (Y-H-W-H, *Yahweh*) as Israel's covenant name.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer od Elohim el-Moshe koh-thomar el-bney Yisra'el YHVH Elohey avotheykhem Elohey Avraham Elohey Yitzchaq v-Elohey Ya'aqov shlachani alehkhem zeh-shemi le-olam ve-zeh zikhri le-dor dor*: *YHVH* (Yahweh, derived from root *hayah* = to be). *zikhri* (my memorial name).
crossReferences: Exodus 6:3; Psalm 135:13 ('Your name, O Lord, endures forever, your renown / memorial name throughout all generations!'); Hosea 12:5.
historicalTrivia: Out of profound reverence, Jewish tradition refrains from pronouncing the Tetragrammaton YHWH aloud, substituting *Adonai* ('Lord') or *Ha-Shem* ('The Name').

dominicalIntent: 'Go and gather the elders of Israel together and say to them, "The Lord, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, has appeared to me, saying, 'I have observed you and what has been done to you in Egypt...'"' MANDATE TO GATHER THE ELDERS! Moses is instructed to assemble the **elders of Israel (*ziqney Yisra'el*)** and announce: **'I HAVE OBSERVED YOU (*Paqod paqadti ethkhem*)!'** FULFILLMENT OF JOSEPH'S DYING PROPHECY (GEN 50:24-25)!
historicalContext: Assembling the tribal council of elders (*ziqney*) in Egypt.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Lekh ve-assaphta eth-ziqney Yisra'el ve-amartha alehem YHVH Elohey avotheykhem nir'ah elai... le'mor paqod paqadti ethkhem ve-eth-he-assuy lakhem be-Mitzrayim*: *Paqod paqadti* (infinitive absolute: 'visiting I have surely visited you!').
historicalTrivia: Moses uses Joseph's exact dying password from Genesis 50:24: *Paqod paqadti* ('I have surely visited you')!

dominicalIntent: '...and I promise that I will bring you up out of the affliction of Egypt to the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, a land flowing with milk and honey.' Re-stating the divine promise of the 6-nation territory in Canaan flowing with milk and honey.
historicalContext: 6-nation territorial list of Canaan.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Va-omar a'aleh ethkhem me-oni Mitzrayim el-eretz ha-Kena'ani ve-ha-Chitti ve-ha-Emori ve-ha-Prizzi ve-ha-Chivvi ve-ha-Yevusi el-eretz zavath chalav u-dvash*.
historicalTrivia: The 6 (or 7) nations of Canaan represent the native populations Israel was called to dispossess.

dominicalIntent: 'And they will listen to your voice, and you and the elders of Israel shall go to the king of Egypt and say to him, "The Lord, the God of the Hebrews, has met with us; and now, please let us go a three days' journey into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to the Lord our God."' MANDATE FOR A 3 DAYS' JOURNEY TO SACRIFICE! God instructs Moses and the elders to petition Pharaoh for **a three days' journey (*derekh shelosheth yamim*) into the wilderness to offer sacrifice (*ve-nizbechah*) to Yahweh**.
cccReferences: CCC 2099 (Sacrifice as the essential act of covenant worship demanded by God); CCC 2575; Exod 5:1-3; Exod 8:27.
historicalContext: Initial diplomatic petition requesting permission for liturgical pilgrimage into the desert to offer animal sacrifices.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-sham'u le-qolekha u-va'tha attha ve-ziqney Yisra'el el-melekh Mitzrayim va-amarthem elav YHVH Elohey ha-Ivriyyim niqrah alenu ve-attah nelakh-na derekh shelosheth yamim ba-midbar ve-nizbechah le-YHVH Eloheynu*: *derekh shelosheth yamim* ('a way of three days'). *ve-nizbechah* ('and let us sacrifice').
historicalTrivia: The 3 days' journey (*shelosheth yamim*) prefigures the Three Days of Christ's Passion, Death, and Resurrection!

dominicalIntent: 'But I know that the king of Egypt will not let you go unless compelled by a mighty hand' (*Ve-ani yada'ti ki lo-yitten ethkhem melekh Mitzrayim la-halokh ve-lo be-yad chazaqah*). GOD PREDICTS PHARAOH'S HARD HEART! God forewarns Moses: Pharaoh will refuse to release Israel **except by a Mighty Hand (*be-yad chazaqah*)**.
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (God's Mighty Hand shattering totalitarian tyranny); CCC 2575; Deut 6:21.
historicalContext: Foretelling royal Egyptian stubbornness requiring miraculous intervention.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-ani yada'ti ki lo-yitten ethkhem melekh Mitzrayim la-halokh ve-lo be-yad chazaqah*: *be-yad chazaqah* ('by a strong/mighty hand').
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 6:21 ('The Lord brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand'); Exodus 6:1; Exodus 13:3.
historicalTrivia: Deuteronomy 6:21 incorporates *be-yad chazaqah* ('with a mighty hand') into the core Israelite confession of faith!

dominicalIntent: 'So I will stretch out my hand and strike Egypt with all the wonders that I will do in it; after that he will let you go' (*Ve-shalachti eth-yadi ve-hikkethi eth-Mitzrayim be-khol niphle'othai...*). STRIKING EGYPT WITH ALL DIVINE WONDERS! God promises: **'I will stretch out my hand and strike Egypt with all my wonders (*be-khol niphle'othai*)!'** The 10 Plagues announced.
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (The miraculous Plagues dismantling Egyptian idolatry); CCC 2575; Ps 105:27-36.
historicalContext: Prophetic announcement of the 10 Plagues (*niphla'oth*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-shalachti eth-yadi ve-hikkethi eth-Mitzrayim be-khol niphle'othai asher e'esseh be-qirbo ve-acharey-khen yeshallach ethkhem*: *niphle'othai* ('my wonders/miracles').
historicalTrivia: Acts 7:36 summarizes: 'He led them out, performing wonders and signs in Egypt and at the Red Sea'.

dominicalIntent: 'And I will give this people favor in the sight of the Egyptians; and when you go, you shall not go empty...' (*ve-hayah ki thelekhun lo thelekhu reqam*). YOU SHALL NOT GO OUT EMPTY-HANDED! God promises: **'WHEN YOU GO, YOU SHALL NOT GO EMPTY!'** (*lo thelekhu reqam*). Fulfilling the 400-year-old prophecy given to Abraham in Genesis 15:14 ('They shall come out with great possessions')!
cccReferences: CCC 2413 (Just back-pay for centuries of unpaid forced labor); CCC 2575; Gen 15:14; Exod 12:35-36.
historicalContext: Just legal compensation (*back-pay / wages*) for 400 years of unpaid slave labor.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-nathatti eth-chen ha-am ha-zeh be-eyney Mitzrayim ve-hayah ki thelekhun lo thelekhu reqam*: *lo thelekhu reqam* ('you shall not go empty-handed').
historicalTrivia: St. Augustine noted that plundering the Egyptians was not theft, but God awarding retroactive back-wages to unpaid slaves!

dominicalIntent: '...but each woman shall ask of her neighbor, and any woman who lives in her house, for silver and gold jewelry and for clothing. You shall put them on your sons and on your daughters. So you shall plunder the Egyptians' (*...u-ntzaltem eth-Mitzrayim*). PLUNDERING THE EGYPTIANS (*U-NTZALTEM ETH-MITZRAYIM*)—THE SPOILS FOR THE TABERNACLE! Hebrew women will ask their Egyptian neighbors for silver, gold, and fine garments. **PATRISTIC ALLEGORY (ST. AUGUSTINE, ST. ORIGEN): 'PLUNDERING EGYPT' PREFIGURES CHRISTIANS SECULAR KNOWLEDGE, PHILOSOPHY, AND RESOURCES TO BUILD THE CHURCH AND SACRED THEOLOGY!**
cccReferences: CCC 2413; CCC 2575; Exod 12:35-36 (Plundering Egypt to build the Tabernacle); St. Augustine *On Christian Doctrine* II.40.
historicalContext: Receiving gold (*khesseph*), silver (*zahav*), and garments (*smloth*) that later construct the Tabernacle in Exodus 25-35.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-sha'alah ishah mi-shekhentah u-mi-ggarath beythah kley-khesseph u-khley zahav u-ssmaloth ve-samtem al-bneykhem ve-al-bnothaykhem u-ntzaltem eth-Mitzrayim*: *u-ntzaltem* ('and you shall deliver/strip/plunder', root *natzal*).
crossReferences: Exodus 12:35-36; Exodus 25:2-8; Psalm 105:37; St. Augustine *De Doctrina Christiana* II.40.
historicalTrivia: St. Augustine (*De Doctrina Christiana* II.40) famously argued that just as Israel took Egyptian gold to build the Tabernacle, so Christians should take pagan philosophy (like Plato and Aristotle) to serve Christian truth!

dominicalIntent: Then Moses answered: 'But behold, they will not believe me or listen to my voice, for they will say, "The Lord did not appear to you."' THIRD OBJECTION: 'THEY WILL NOT BELIEVE ME!' Moses expresses fear that Israel will doubt his divine commission.
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Moses' hesitation and need for divine signs to confirm his mission); Exod 3:11; Exod 3:13.
historicalContext: Patriarchal leader anticipating skepticism from oppressed slaves.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'an Moshe vayyo'mer ve-hen lo-ya'aminu li ve-lo yishme'u be-qoli ki yo'mru lo-nir'ah eleykha YHVH*: *lo-ya'aminu* ('they will not believe/trust', root *aman*).
historicalTrivia: Moses' fear (*lo-ya'aminu*) is answered by God granting 3 miraculous credentials (*othoth*).

dominicalIntent: The Lord said to him: 'What is that in your hand?' He said: 'A staff' (*Vayyo'mer elav YHVH mah-zeh ve-yadekha vayyo'mer matteh*). THE SHEPHERD'S STAFF (*MATTEH*)! Yahweh points to the humble shepherd's staff in Moses' hand: **'A staff' (*matteh*)**. God transforms this simple wooden shepherd's crook into **The Staff of God (*Matteh ha-Elohim*)** to work wonders!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (God elevating humble instruments to work divine miracles); Exod 4:20.
historicalContext: The shepherd's wooden rod (*matteh*), used for driving sheep, measuring, and walking.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer elav YHVH mah-zeh ve-yadekha vayyo'mer matteh*: *matteh* (staff/rod/branch/scepter).
historicalTrivia: This simple staff becomes titled **'The Staff of God' (*Matteh ha-Elohim*)** in Exod 4:20!

dominicalIntent: And he said: 'Throw it on the ground.' So he threw it on the ground, and it became a serpent, and Moses ran from it (*Vayyo'mer hashlikhehu artzah vayyashlikhehu artzah vayyehi le-nachash vayyanass Moshe mi-ppanav*). FIRST MIRACULOUS SIGN: THE STAFF BECOMES A SERPENT (*NACHASH*)! Moses casts his staff to the ground; it instantly transforms into a living **serpent (*nachash*)**! Moses recoils in terror. The serpent was the sacred royal emblem (*Uraeus*) on Pharaoh's crown; transforming the staff into a serpent demonstrates God's absolute authority over Egypt's demonic powers!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Miraculous signs proving divine authority); Exod 7:10-12; Rev 12:9.
historicalContext: The cobra/viper emblem (*Uraeus*) worn on the royal brow of Egyptian Pharaohs as a symbol of divine sovereignty.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer hashlikhehu artzah vayyashlikhehu artzah vayyehi le-nachash vayyanass Moshe mi-ppanav*: *nachash* (serpent/snake).
historicalTrivia: In Exodus 7:10 before Pharaoh, the staff becomes a *tannin* (sea-monster/dragon/large serpent).

dominicalIntent: But the Lord said to Moses: 'Put out your hand and catch it by the tail'—so he reached out his hand and caught it, and it became a staff in his hand— GRABBING THE SERPENT BY THE TAIL! God commands Moses to do the unthinkable: grab the venomous serpent by the tail! Moses obeys; the serpent instantly solidifies back into a rigid wooden staff. Faith subdues demonic powers.
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Power over serpents given to God's messengers); Mark 16:18; Luke 10:19.
historicalContext: Grabbing a snake by the tail normally invites a deadly strike; grabbing by the neck is human practice. Grabbing by the tail required absolute faith.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe shelach yadkha ve-echoz bi-znavo vayyishlach yado vayyachaz-bo vayyehi le-matteh be-khappo*: *bi-znavo* ('by its tail').
crossReferences: Mark 16:18 ('they will pick up serpents'); Luke 10:19 ('I have given you authority to tread on serpents'); Psalm 91:13.
historicalTrivia: Jesus echoes this power over serpents in Luke 10:19 and Mark 16:18!

dominicalIntent: '...that they may believe that the Lord, the God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has appeared to you.' Purpose of the 1st sign: establishing belief in the God of the Patriarchs.
cccReferences: CCC 2575; Exod 3:6.
historicalContext: Miraculous credentials to awaken covenant faith.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Le-ma'an ya'aminu ki-nir'ah eleykha YHVH Elohey avotham Elohey Avraham Elohey Yitzchaq v-Elohey Ya'aqov*.
historicalTrivia: Miracles (*othoth*) in Scripture always serve to generate faith (*ya'aminu*).

dominicalIntent: Again, the Lord said to him: 'Put your hand inside your cloak.' And he put his hand inside his cloak, and when he took it out, behold, his hand was leprous like snow (*...ve-hinneh yado metzora'ath ka-ssaleg*). SECOND MIRACULOUS SIGN: THE LEPROUS HAND (*METZORA'ATH*)! Moses puts his hand inside his cloak; withdrawing it, it is stricken with **white scale-leprosy (*tzara'ath*) like snow**! Human nature corrupted by sin.
cccReferences: CCC 1506 (Miracles of healing scale-disease/leprosy prefiguring Christ's cleansing power); CCC 2575; Lev 13:2-3; 2 Kings 5:27.
historicalContext: Scale-disease (*tzara'ath*), an incurable ritual impurity under ancient law.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH lo od hve-na yadkha be-cheyqekha vayyave yado be-cheyqo vayyotzi'ah ve-hinneh yado metzora'ath ka-ssaleg*: *metzora'ath* (stricken with scale-leprosy). *ka-ssaleg* ('like snow').
historicalTrivia: Scale-leprosy (*tzara'ath*) was considered a living death; only God could inflict and heal it.

dominicalIntent: Then he said: 'Put your hand back inside your cloak.' So he put his hand back inside his cloak, and when he took it out, behold, it was restored like the rest of his flesh (*...vat-tashuv ki-vssaro*). INSTANT RESTORATION AND HEALING! Moses puts his hand back into his bosom; withdrawing it, his flesh is **instantly restored (*vat-tashuv ki-vssaro*)** clean and whole! **PREFIGURING CHRIST CLEANSING LEPERS AND RESTORING CORRUPTED HUMAN NATURE IN THE SACRAMENTS!**
cccReferences: CCC 1506 (Sacramental restoration and cleansing of human nature); CCC 2575; Matt 8:3.
historicalContext: Miraculous divine purification and restoration.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer hashev yadkha el-cheyqekha vayyashev yado el-cheyqo vayyotzi'ah mi-cheyqo ve-hinneh-shavah ki-vssaro*: *shavah* (returned / was restored).
crossReferences: Matthew 8:3 ('I will; be clean!'); 2 Kings 5:14 ('his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child'); Leviticus 14:1-32.
historicalTrivia: 2 Kings 5:14 uses this exact phrasing when Naaman the Syrian is cleansed of leprosy in the Jordan!

dominicalIntent: 'If they will not believe you or heed the first sign, they may believe the voice of the latter sign.' The escalation of divine miraculous testimony.
historicalContext: Layered miraculous signs for Israel's elders.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-hayah im-lo ya'aminu lakh ve-lo yishme'u le-qol ha-oth ha-rishon ve-he'eminu le-qol ha-oth ha-acharon*: *qol ha-oth* ('the voice of the sign'!).
historicalTrivia: Scripture calls signs 'speaking' (*qol ha-oth* = 'the voice of the sign'), because miracles communicate divine truth!

dominicalIntent: 'If they will not believe even these two signs or listen to your voice, you shall take some water from the Nile and pour it on the dry ground, and the water that you shall take from the Nile will become blood on the dry ground' (*...ve-hayu ha-mmayim... le-dam ba-yyabasheshet*). THIRD MIRACULOUS SIGN: WATER FROM THE NILE TURNED TO BLOOD (*LE-DAM*)! If they disbelieve the first two signs, Moses must scoop water from the Nile and pour it on dry ground; it will **instantly turn to blood (*le-dam*)**! PREFIGURING THE 1ST PLAGUE OF EGYPT AND THE BLOOD OF REDEMPTION!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The 3rd sign prefiguring the 1st Plague of Egypt and Eucharistic blood transformation); Exod 7:17-21; Rev 16:4.
historicalContext: Striking the sacred Nile River (*Hapi*), transforming its waters into blood.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-hayah im lo ya'aminu gam li-sheney ha-othoth ha-elleh ve-lo yishme'un le-qolekha ve-laqachta mi-meymey ha-Ye'or ve-shaphakhta ha-yyabasht ve-hayu ha-mmayim asher tiqqach min-ha-Ye'or ve-hayu le-dam ba-yyabasheshet*: *le-dam* ('into blood').
historicalTrivia: Notice the progression: Moses' first miracle turns water to blood (death/judgment); Jesus' first miracle turns water into wine (life/wedding feast)!

dominicalIntent: But Moses said to the Lord: 'Oh, my Lord, I am not eloquent, either in the past or since you have spoken to your servant, but I am slow of speech and of tongue' (*Bhi Adonai lo ish dvarim anokhi... ki khevad-peh u-khevad lashon anokhi*). FOURTH OBJECTION: 'I AM SLOW OF SPEECH AND TONGUE!' Moses pleads his speech impediment: **'I am slow of speech and slow of tongue!'** (*khevad-peh u-khevad lashon* = heavy-mouthed and heavy-tongued).
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Human weakness contrasted with divine grace); Exod 6:12; Jer 1:6.
historicalContext: Moses feeling inadequate as an orator before Pharaoh's court.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Moshe el-YHVH Bi Adonai lo ish dvarim anokhi gam mi-ttmol gam mi-shilshom gam me-az dibberkha el-avdekha ki khevad-peh u-khevad lashon anokhi*: *khevad-peh* ('heavy of mouth'). *khevad lashon* ('heavy of tongue').
historicalTrivia: Moses' 'heavy tongue' contrasts with St. Paul's weakness in 1 Cor 2:3-4, proving God chooses weak vessels to manifest His power.

dominicalIntent: The Lord said to him: 'Who has made man's mouth? Who makes him mute, or deaf, or seeing, or blind? Is it not I, the Lord?' (*Mi sam peh la-adam o mi-yasum illem o cheresh o phioqach o ivver ha-lo anokhi YHVH*). GOD CREATOR OF MOUTH AND SENSES! Yahweh responds in divine majesty: **'WHO HAS MADE MAN'S MOUTH?! WHO MAKES HIM MUTE, OR DEAF, OR SEEING, OR BLIND?! IS IT NOT I, THE LORD?!'** Almighty God is the Creator of all human faculties.
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (God as Creator of human speech and senses empowering His prophets); Ps 94:9; Isa 35:5-6.
historicalContext: Divine creator monologue asserting absolute sovereignty over human physical bodies and senses.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH elav Mi sam peh la-adam o mi-yasum illem o cheresh o phioqach o ivver ha-lo anokhi YHVH*: *illem* (mute). *cheresh* (deaf). *phioqach* (seeing). *ivver* (blind).
crossReferences: Psalm 94:9 ('He who planted the ear, does he not hear?'); Isaiah 35:5-6; Mark 7:37.
historicalTrivia: Jesus fulfills Isaiah 35:5-6 and Exodus 4:11 when He makes the deaf hear and the mute speak in Mark 7:37!

dominicalIntent: 'Now therefore go, and I will be with your mouth and teach you what you shall speak' (*Ve-attah lekh ve-anokhi ehyeh im-pikha ve-horaythikha asher tedabber*). 'I WILL BE WITH YOUR MOUTH!' God promises divine inspiration: **'GO, AND I WILL BE WITH YOUR MOUTH (*anokhi ehyeh im-pikha*) AND TEACH YOU WHAT YOU SHALL SPEAK!'** PREFIGURING CHRIST'S PROMISE TO THE APOSTLES (MATT 10:19-20; LUKE 21:15)!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Divine inspiration of prophetic speech); Matt 10:19-20; Luke 21:15; Jer 1:9.
historicalContext: Promise of divine prophetic utterance.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-attah lekh ve-anokhi ehyeh im-pikha ve-horaythikha asher tedabber*: *ehyeh im-pikha* ('I will be with your mouth'). *ve-horaythikha* ('and I will instruct/teach you', root *yarah* -> Torah!).
crossReferences: Matthew 10:19-20 ('for it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father'); Luke 21:15 ('I will give you a mouth and wisdom'); Jeremiah 1:9.
historicalTrivia: The verb *ve-horaythikha* ('I will instruct you') shares the exact root with **Torah** (*instruction/law*)!

dominicalIntent: But he said: 'Oh, my Lord, please send someone else' (*Bi Adonai shlach-na be-yad-tishlach*). FIFTH OBJECTION: 'PLEASE SEND SOMEONE ELSE!' Moses pleads final resistance: **'Oh, my Lord, please send by the hand of whomever else You will send!'** (*shlach-na be-yad-tishlach*).
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Human reluctance yielding to divine mandate).
historicalContext: Moses begging to be excused from the mission.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Bi Adonai shlach-na be-yad-tishlach*: *shlach-na be-yad-tishlach* ('send, I pray, by the hand of [anyone] you will send!').
historicalTrivia: Moses' total reluctance proves he was not seeking self-glorification or political ambition.

dominicalIntent: Then the anger of the Lord was kindled against Moses, and he said: 'Is there not Aaron, your brother, the Levite? I know that he can speak well. Behold, he is coming out to meet you, and when he sees you, he will be glad in his heart' (*Vayyichar-aph YHVH ba-Moshe... Ha-lo Aaron achikha ha-Levi...*). AARON APPOINTED AS SPOKESMAN! God's anger burns at Moses' hesitation, but in divine mercy He appoints **AARON THE LEVITE (*Aaron achikha ha-Levi*)**, Moses' elder brother, as his official speaker and prophet! Aaron is already on his way to meet him.
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Aaron appointed as spokesman and future High Priest); CCC 1539 (Levitical priesthood of Aaron); Exod 7:1-2; Heb 5:4.
historicalContext: Appointing Aaron as Moses' official spokesman (*mleitz / nabi*) before Pharaoh and Israel.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyichar-aph YHVH ba-Moshe vayyo'mer Ha-lo Aaron achikha ha-Levi yada'ti ki-dhabber yedhabber hu ve-gham hinneh-hu yotze li-qra'thekha ve-ra'akha ve-samach bi-lbo*: *ha-Levi* ('the Levite', underscoring priestly lineage).
crossReferences: Exodus 7:1-2; Hebrews 5:4 ('called by God, just as Aaron was'); Exodus 4:27; Psalm 133:1-2.
historicalTrivia: Aaron was 3 years older than Moses (Exod 7:7) and already a respected elder among the Hebrews in Egypt.

dominicalIntent: 'You shall speak to him and put the words in his mouth, and I will be with your mouth and with his mouth and will teach you both what to do.' Moses will deliver God's words to Aaron, who will speak them.
historicalContext: Prophetic delegation chain: God -> Moses -> Aaron -> Pharaoh.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-dibbartha elav ve-samtha eth-ha-dvarim be-phiv ve-anokhi ehyeh im-pikha ve-im-pihu ve-horaythi ethkhem eth asher ta'assun*.
historicalTrivia: Exodus 7:1 clarifies this relationship: 'I have made you like God to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron shall be your prophet'.

dominicalIntent: 'He shall speak for you to the people, and he shall be your mouth, and you shall be as God to him' (*Ve-dibber-hu lekha el-ha-am ve-hayah hu yihyeh-lekha le-pheh ve-attha thihyeh-lo le-Elohim*). MOSES AS GOD TO AARON! Aaron will be Moses' **mouth (*le-pheh*)**, and Moses will be **as God (*le-Elohim*)** to Aaron! Moses acts as the divine source of revelation, Aaron as the prophet.
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Moses as mediator standing in the place of God to reveal His word); Exod 7:1.
historicalContext: Theological hierarchy of revelation.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-dibber-hu lekha el-ha-am ve-hayah hu yihyeh-lekha le-pheh ve-attha thihyeh-lo le-Elohim*: *le-Elohim* ('as God / in the place of God').
historicalTrivia: Moses is called *le-Elohim* ('as God') because he directly receives the unmediated Word of God!

dominicalIntent: 'And take in your hand this staff, with which you shall do the signs' (*Ve-eth-ha-mmatteh ha-zeh tiqqach be-yadekha...*). MANDATE TO TAKE THE STAFF OF SIGNS! God commands Moses to take the wooden shepherd's staff in his hand to work the signs (*ha-othoth*).
cccReferences: CCC 2575; Exod 4:2; Exod 4:20.
historicalContext: Empowering the staff as the official rod of divine judgment.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-eth-ha-mmatteh ha-zeh tiqqach be-yadekha asher ta'asseh-bo eth-ha-othoth*.
historicalTrivia: This staff will part the Red Sea, strike the rock for water, and defeat Amalek!

dominicalIntent: Moses went back to Jethro his father-in-law and said to him: 'Please let me go back to my brothers in Egypt to see whether they are still alive.' And Jethro said to Moses: 'Go in peace' (*Vayyelech Moshe vayyashav el-Yether chothno... Vayyo'mer Yithro le-Moshe lekh le-shalom*). MOSES TAKES LEAVE OF JETHRO! Moses returns to his father-in-law **Jethro (*Yether*)** to seek permission to return to Egypt. Jethro bestows his blessing: **'GO IN PEACE' (*Lekh le-shalom*)**.
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Filial respect and peaceful departure).
historicalContext: Seeking patriarchal permission from his employer and father-in-law Jethro.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyelech Moshe vayyashav el-Yether chothno vayyo'mer lo elekhah na ve-ashuvah el-achai asher-be-Mitzrayim ve-er'eh ha-odam chayyim vayyo'mer Yithro le-Moshe lekh le-shalom*: *Yether* (Jethro). *lekh le-shalom* ('go in peace').
historicalTrivia: Jethro is here called *Yether* (his basic name, short for *Yithro* = 'Excellency').

dominicalIntent: And the Lord said to Moses in Midian: 'Go back to Egypt, for all the men who were seeking your life are dead' (*...ki-methu kol-ha-anashim ha-mvaqshim eth-naphtsekha*). 'ALL WHO SOUGHT YOUR LIFE ARE DEAD!'—QUOTED IN MATTHEW 2:20 FOR THE HOLY FAMILY'S RETURN FROM EGYPT! God commands Moses to return, for all who sought his life are dead. **THE ANGEL OF THE LORD USES THESE EXACT WORDS TO ST. JOSEPH IN MATTHEW 2:20 TO COMMAND THE RETURN OF THE INFANT JESUS FROM EGYPT!**
cccReferences: CCC 530 (The Return of the Holy Family from Egypt fulfilling Exodus 4:19); Matt 2:20.
historicalContext: Death of Thutmose III and his hostile court officials.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe be-Midyan lekh shuv Mitzrayim ki-methu kol-ha-anashim ha-mvaqshim eth-naphtsekha*: *ha-mvaqshim eth-naphtsekha* ('those seeking your life', LXX *tethnēkasi gar pantes hoi zētountes tēn psychēn sou*).
crossReferences: Matthew 2:20 ('for those who sought the child's life are dead'); Exodus 2:15.
historicalTrivia: Matthew 2:20 quotes Exodus 4:19 Septuagint word-for-word (*tethnēkasi gar hoi zētountes tēn psychēn tou paidiou*)!

dominicalIntent: So Moses took his wife and his sons and had them ride on a donkey, and went back to the land of Egypt. And Moses took the staff of God in his hand (*Vayyiqqach Moshe eth-ishto ve-eth-bnav... ve-eth-matteh ha-Elohim be-yado*). MOSES TAKES THE STAFF OF GOD (*MATTEH HA-ELOHIM*)! Moses mounts Zipporah and his two sons (Gershom & Eliezer) on a donkey. In his hand he carries no longer a shepherd's crook, but **THE STAFF OF GOD (*Matteh ha-Elohim*)**!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The Staff of God as the instrument of divine power); Exod 4:2; Exod 17:9.
historicalContext: Caravan journey from Midian across Sinai to Egypt. Moses holding the transformed rod.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiqqach Moshe eth-ishto ve-eth-bnav vayyarkivem al-ha-chamor vayyashav artzah Mitzrayim vayyiqqach Moshe eth-matteh ha-Elohim be-yado*: *matteh ha-Elohim* ('staff/rod of God').
historicalTrivia: Exodus 4:20 is the first time the shepherd's rod is called **The Staff of God (*Matteh ha-Elohim*)**!

dominicalIntent: And the Lord said to Moses: 'When you go back to Egypt, see that you do before Pharaoh all the miracles that I have put in your power. But I will harden his heart, so that he will not let the people go' (*...va-ani achazzeq eth-libbo ve-lo yeshallach eth-ha-am*). THE HARDENING OF PHARAOH'S HEART (*ACHAZZEQ ETH-LIBBO*)! God commands Moses to perform all wonders, but warns: **'I WILL HARDEN HIS HEART (*achazzeq eth-libbo*), SO THAT HE WILL NOT LET THE PEOPLE GO!'** (Scripture alternates between Pharaoh hardening his own heart in Exod 8:15 and God hardening it in judicial judgment!).
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Divine judicial hardening of the unrepentant heart); Rom 9:17-18 ('He has mercy on whomever he wills, and he hardens whomever he wills'); Exod 7:3; Exod 9:12.
historicalContext: Theological mystery of divine sovereignty and human free-will obstinacy.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe be-lekhtakha la-shuv Mitzraymah re'eh kol-ha-mophthim asher-ssamti ve-yadekha ve-assitham liphney Phar'oh va-ani achazzeq eth-libbo ve-lo yeshallach eth-ha-am*: *achazzeq* (I will make strong/stubborn/hard, root *chazaq*).
historicalTrivia: St. Paul in Romans 9:17-18 quotes this exact hardening narrative of Exodus to demonstrate God's supreme sovereignty.

dominicalIntent: Then you shall say to Pharaoh: 'Thus says the Lord, Israel is my firstborn son...' (*Koh amar YHVH beni bekhori Yisra'el*). ISRAEL MY FIRSTBORN SON (*BENI BEKHORI YISRA'EL*)! GOD ADOPTS ISRAEL AS HIS FIRSTBORN SON! God decrees to Pharaoh: **'THUS SAYS THE LORD: ISRAEL IS MY FIRSTBORN SON (*beni bekhori Yisra'el*)!'** **THIS IS THE FIRST TIME IN SCRIPTURE GOD CALLS ISRAEL HIS 'SON' AND 'FIRSTBORN'! PREFIGURING JESUS CHRIST, THE ONLY-BEGOTTEN SON OF GOD!**
cccReferences: CCC 238 (God as Father adopting Israel as His firstborn son); CCC 2575; Hos 11:1; Matt 2:15; Jer 31:9.
historicalContext: Royal covenant adoption decree issued to Pharaoh.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-amartha el-Par'oh koh amar YHVH beni bekhori Yisra'el*: *beni bekhori* ('my son, my firstborn').
crossReferences: Hosea 11:1 ('Out of Egypt I called my son'); Matthew 2:15; Jeremiah 31:9; Romans 9:4.
historicalTrivia: Hosea 11:1 and Matthew 2:15 ('Out of Egypt I called my son') fulfill Exodus 4:22!

dominicalIntent: '...and I say to you, "Let my son go that he may serve me." If you refuse to let him go, behold, I will kill your firstborn son.' THE ULTIMATUM OF THE 10TH PLAGUE! God warns Pharaoh: **'If you refuse to let my firstborn son go, BEHOLD, I WILL KILL YOUR FIRSTBORN SON!'** Announcement of the 10th Plague (Death of the Firstborn) before Moses even arrives in Egypt!
historicalContext: Divine talionic justice: if Pharaoh kills/enslaves God's firstborn son Israel, Pharaoh will lose his own firstborn son.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Va-omar eleykha shallach eth-beni ve-ya'avdeni vat-thema'en le-shallcho hinneh anokhi horegh eth-binkha bekhorakha*: *horegh* ('killing/slaying').
historicalTrivia: The 10th Plague (Exod 12:29) fulfills this exact warning given in Exodus 4:23!

dominicalIntent: At a lodging place on the way the Lord met him and sought to put him to death (*Vayehi va-dderekh ba-mmalon vayyiphgeshehu YHVH vayveqesh hamitho*). THE MYSTERIOUS NIGHT ASSAULT AT THE INN! At a desert lodging place (*malon*), Yahweh confronts Moses and seeks to put him to death (*vayveqesh hamitho*) because Moses had neglected to circumcise his second son Eliezer! **EVEN THE LEADER OF ISRAEL CANNOT EMBARK ON COVENANT REDEMPTION WHILE LIVING IN DISOBEDIENCE TO THE COVENANT OF CIRCUMCISION!**
cccReferences: CCC 1150 (Circumcision as the mandatory sign of the covenant precondition for divine service); CCC 2575; Gen 17:14.
historicalContext: Desert inn/encampment (*malon*). Severe covenant crisis over uncircumcised infant son.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi va-dderekh ba-mmalon vayyiphgeshehu YHVH vayveqesh hamitho*: *vayyiphgeshehu* (and He met him / confronted him). *vayveqesh hamitho* ('and sought to kill him').
historicalTrivia: Genesis 17:14 declared: 'Any uncircumcised male... shall be cut off from his people; he has broken my covenant'!

dominicalIntent: Then Zipporah took a flint and cut off her son's foreskin and touched Moses' feet with it and said: 'Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me!' (*Vattiqqach Tzipporah tzor vat-thikhroth eth-orlath bnah... Chathan-damim attah li*). THE BRIDEGROOM OF BLOOD (*CHATHAN-DAMIM*)! Realizing the danger, **Zipporah** grabs a sharp flint stone (*tzor*), circumcises her son, touches the bloody foreskin to Moses' feet/body, and cries: **'SURELY YOU ARE A BRIDEGROOM OF BLOOD (*Chathan-damim*) TO ME!'** ZIPPORAH SAVES MOSES' LIFE THROUGH BLOOD COVENANT CIRCUMCISION!
cccReferences: CCC 1150 (Circumcision sealing the covenant in blood prefiguring Baptism and Christ's Blood); CCC 2575; Gen 17:12-14.
historicalContext: Emergency circumcision performed with a sharp flint stone (*tzor*). Touching the blood to the body to ward off divine judgment.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vattiqqach Tzipporah tzor vat-thikhroth eth-orlath bnah vat-thagga le-raglav vat-to'mer ki chathan-damim attah li*: *tzor* (flint knife). *orlath* (foreskin). *Chathan-damim* ('Bridegroom of Blood').
crossReferences: Genesis 17:12-14; Joshua 5:2; Colossians 2:11-12 (Spiritual circumcision of Baptism!).
historicalTrivia: Zipporah is one of the heroic women of Exodus who steps into the breach to preserve the life of Israel's deliverer!

dominicalIntent: So he let him alone. It was then that she said: 'A bridegroom of blood,' because of the circumcision (*Vayyireph mimmennu az amrah chathan damim la-mmuloth*). DIVINE WRATH AVERTED! Upon the circumcision, Yahweh relents (*Vayyireph mimmennu*). Zipporah repeats: 'A bridegroom of blood,' because of the circumcisions (*la-mmuloth*). Blood covenant satisfies divine justice.
historicalContext: Cessation of divine judgment following covenant obedience.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyireph mimmennu az amrah chathan damim la-mmuloth*: *Vayyireph* (and He let go / relented, root *raphah*). *la-mmuloth* ('on account of the circumcisions').
historicalTrivia: Circumcision (*la-mmuloth*) prefigures the Sacrament of Baptism, which removes original sin through the Blood of Christ (Col 2:11-12).

dominicalIntent: The Lord said to Aaron: 'Go into the wilderness to meet Moses.' So he went and met him at the mountain of God and kissed him (*Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Aaron lekh li-qra'th Moshe ha-midbarah vayyelech vayyiphgeshehu be-har ha-Elohim vayyissaq-lo*). REUNION AT THE MOUNTAIN OF GOD! God prompts Aaron to march into the desert. Aaron meets Moses at **Mount Horeb (*har ha-Elohim*)** and **kisses him** in joyful fraternal reunion!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The joyful reunion of Moses and Aaron at Sinai); Ps 133:1.
historicalContext: Fraternal reunion at Mount Sinai after 40 years of separation.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Aaron lekh li-qra'th Moshe ha-midbarah vayyelech vayyiphgeshehu be-har ha-Elohim vayyissaq-lo*: *vayyissaq-lo* ('and kissed him').
crossReferences: Psalm 133:1 ('Behold, how good and pleasant it is when brothers dwell in unity!'); Exodus 4:14.
historicalTrivia: Psalm 133:1-2 ('how good and pleasant when brothers dwell in unity... like precious oil on Aaron's beard') captures this exact moment!

dominicalIntent: And Moses told Aaron all the words of the Lord with which he had sent him to speak, and all the signs that he had commanded him to do. Moses discloses the entire revelation of Yahweh and the 3 miraculous signs to Aaron.
historicalContext: Private briefing between prophet and spokesman.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyagged Moshe le-Aaron eth kol-divrey YHVH asher shlacho ve-eth kol-ha-othoth asher tzivvahu*.
historicalTrivia: Aaron immediately accepts Moses' divine commission without jealousy.

dominicalIntent: Then Moses and Aaron went and gathered together all the elders of the children of Israel (*Vayyelech Moshe ve-Aaron vayya'assphu eth-kol-ziqney bney Yisra'el*). CONVENING THE ELDERS OF ISRAEL! Moses and Aaron arrive in Egypt and assemble **all the elders of Israel (*ziqney bney Yisra'el*)**.
cccReferences: CCC 2575; Exod 3:16.
historicalContext: Convening the official governing council of 12-tribe elders in Goshen.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyelech Moshe ve-Aaron vayya'assphu eth-kol-ziqney bney Yisra'el*: *ziqney* (elders/sheikhs).
historicalTrivia: This is the first formal assembly of Israel's national leadership under Moses and Aaron.

dominicalIntent: Aaron spoke all the words that the Lord had spoken to Moses and did the signs in the sight of the people. Aaron functions as spokesman, declaring God's words and performing the 3 miraculous signs before the elders.
cccReferences: CCC 2575; Exod 4:16.
historicalContext: Demonstrating the 3 miraculous signs (serpent, leprous hand, water to blood) before Israel's leaders.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vaydedabber Aaron eth kol-ha-dvarim asher-dibber YHVH el-Moshe vayya'as ha-othoth le-eyney ha-am*.
historicalTrivia: Seeing the 3 signs convinced the skeptical elders immediately.

dominicalIntent: And the people believed; and when they heard that the Lord had visited the children of Israel and that he had looked on their affliction, they bowed their heads and worshiped (*Vayyamen ha-am vayyishma'u ki-phaqad YHVH eth-bney Yisra'el... vayyiqqdu vayyishtachavvu*). THE PEOPLE BELIEVED AND BOWED IN WORSHIP! FULFILLMENT! **'AND THE PEOPLE BELIEVED (*Vayyamen ha-am*)! AND WHEN THEY HEARD THAT YAHWEH HAD VISITED (*paqad*) THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL AND SEEN THEIR AFFLICTION, THEY BOWED THEIR HEADS AND WORSHIPED!'** (*vayyiqqdu vayyishtachavvu*). FAITH AND WORSHIP CROWN EXODUS 4!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The response of faith and liturgical worship from the redeemed people of God); Gen 50:24-25; Exod 3:16; Ps 106:12.
historicalContext: Liturgical prostration and belief (*amen*) of the 12 tribes of Israel.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyamen ha-am vayyishma'u ki-phaqad YHVH eth-bney Yisra'el ve-khi ra'ah eth-on'yam vayyiqqdu vayyishtachavvu*: *Vayyamen* (and they believed/trusted, root *aman* -> Amen!). *paqad* (visited). *vayyiqqdu vayyishtachavvu* ('they bowed their heads and prostrated in worship!').
crossReferences: Genesis 50:24-25; Exodus 3:16; Psalm 106:12 ('Then they believed his words and sang his praise'); Hebrews 11:28.
historicalTrivia: The verb *Vayyamen* ('and they believed') comes from *aman*—the exact root of our liturgical **AMEN**!

dominicalIntent: Afterward Moses and Aaron went and said to Pharaoh: 'Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, "Let my people go, that they may hold a feast to me in the wilderness."' (*...Koh-amar YHVH Elohey Yisra'el shallach eth-ammi ve-yachoggu li ba-midbar*). FIRST AUDIENCE BEFORE PHARAOH: 'LET MY PEOPLE GO!' Moses and Aaron enter Pharaoh's royal throne room at Rameses/Avaris. They issue the royal divine decree: **'THUS SAYS YAHWEH THE GOD OF ISRAEL: LET MY PEOPLE GO, THAT THEY MAY HOLD A SACRED FEAST TO ME IN THE WILDERNESS!'** (*shallach eth-ammi*). The clash of two kingdoms!
cccReferences: CCC 2060 (The command to liberate Israel for divine worship); CCC 2575; Exod 3:18; Exod 7:16.
historicalContext: Formal diplomatic audience before Pharaoh (18th/19th Dynasty) at the royal Delta capital.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-achar ba'u Moshe ve-Aaron vayyo'mru el-Par'oh koh-amar YHVH Elohey Yisra'el shallach eth-ammi ve-yachoggu li ba-midbar*: *shallach eth-ammi* ('release/send forth my people!'). *ve-yachoggu* ('and let them celebrate a pilgrimage festival', root *chagag* -> *Chag*!).
historicalTrivia: The verb *yachoggu* comes from *chagag* (to celebrate a pilgrimage feast), the source of the Hebrew word for holy feast (*Chag*)!

dominicalIntent: But Pharaoh said: 'Who is the Lord, that I should obey his voice and let Israel go? I do not know the Lord, and moreover, I will not let Israel go' (*...Mi YHVH asher eshma be-qolo... lo yada'ti eth-YHVH...*). PHARAOH'S ARROGANT DEFIANCE: 'WHO IS YAHWEH?! I DO NOT KNOW THE LORD!' Pharaoh sneers in supreme pagan arrogance: **'WHO IS YAHWEH, THAT I SHOULD OBEY HIS VOICE AND LET ISRAEL GO?! I DO NOT KNOW YAHWEH, AND I WILL NOT LET ISRAEL GO!'** Pharaoh sets himself up against the true God, setting the stage for the 10 Plagues!
cccReferences: CCC 2086 (The sin of total defiance against God); CCC 2575; Job 21:14-15; Ps 14:1.
historicalContext: Pharaoh considered himself the living god Horus/Re on earth; rejecting Yahweh as an unknown minor Asiatic deity.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Par'oh Mi YHVH asher eshma be-qolo le-shallach eth-Yisra'el lo yada'ti eth-YHVH ve-gham eth-Yisra'el lo ashalleach*: *Mi YHVH* ('Who is Yahweh?'). *lo yada'ti* ('I do not know / acknowledge').
historicalTrivia: The entire story of the 10 Plagues is designed to answer Pharaoh's arrogant question (*Mi YHVH*): 'And the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord!' (Exod 7:5).

dominicalIntent: Then they said: 'The God of the Hebrews has met with us. Please let us go a three days' journey into the wilderness that we may sacrifice to the Lord our God, lest he fall upon us with pestilence or with the sword.' Moses and Aaron reiterate the 3 days' wilderness worship petition, warning of divine judgment if worship is denied.
cccReferences: CCC 2099 (Sacrifice as essential duty of divine worship); CCC 2575; Exod 3:18.
historicalContext: Re-asserting the 3 days' journey to sacrifice to prevent covenant wrath (*dever* = pestilence).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mru Elohey ha-Ivriyyim niqrah alenu nelakh-na derekh shelosheth yamim ba-midbar ve-nizbechah le-YHVH Eloheynu pen-yiphga'enu va-ddever o va-charevh*: *dever* (pestilence/plague).
historicalTrivia: In ancient Near Eastern theology, neglecting obligatory cultic sacrifices to one's deity brought pestilence (*dever*) or war upon the nation.

dominicalIntent: But the king of Egypt said to them: 'Moses and Aaron, why do you take the people away from their work? Get back to your burdens' (*...Lammah Moshe ve-Aaron thaphri'u eth-ha-am mi-mma'assav lekhu le-ssivlothaykhem*). PHARAOH REBUKES MOSES AND AARON! Pharaoh accuses Moses and Aaron of inciting labor strikes (*thaphri'u* = distracting/unsettling the workers), commanding: **'GET BACK TO YOUR HEAVY BURDENS (*ssivlothaykhem*)!'**
cccReferences: CCC 2575; Exod 1:11.
historicalContext: Accusing labor organizers of disturbing state construction projects.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer alehem melekh Mitzrayim lammah Moshe ve-Aaron thaphri'u eth-ha-am mi-mma'assav lekhu le-ssivlothaykhem*: *thaphri'u* (cause to cease / distract / loosen, root *para*).
historicalTrivia: Luke 23:2 mirrors Pharaoh's charge: 'We found this man perverting our nation and forbidding us to give tribute to Caesar'.

dominicalIntent: And Pharaoh said: 'Behold, the people of the land are now many, and you make them rest from their burdens!' (*...ve-hishbatthem otham mi-ssivlotham*). Pharaoh complains that Moses is introducing a **Sabbath-rest (*hishbatthem*)** among the slaves!
cccReferences: CCC 2172 (The Sabbath rest for laborers opposed by totalitarian oppressors); CCC 2575.
historicalContext: Oppressors denying any rest or Sabbath (*shabbat*) to forced laborers.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Par'oh hen-rabbim attah am ha-aretz ve-hishbatthem otham mi-ssivlotham*: *ve-hishbatthem* ('and you make them keep Sabbath / cease work', root *shabath*!).
historicalTrivia: The verb *ve-hishbatthem* comes from *shabath* (Sabbath): Pharaoh accuses Moses of creating a Sabbath for slaves!

dominicalIntent: The same day Pharaoh commanded the taskmasters of the people and their foremen... Pharaoh issues an immediate retaliatory decree to his Egyptian taskmasters (*ssoghrim*) and Hebrew foremen (*shotrim*).
historicalContext: Two-tier labor administration: Egyptian state overseers (*noggssim*) and Hebrew slave foremen (*shotrim*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vaytzav Par'oh ba-yom ha-hu eth-ha-noggssim ba-am ve-eth-shotrav le'mor*: *noggssim* (Egyptian taskmasters). *shotrim* (Hebrew officers/foremen).
historicalTrivia: The Hebrew *shotrim* were native Hebrew officers responsible for keeping labor tallies.

dominicalIntent: 'You shall no longer give the people straw to make bricks, as in the past; let them go and gather straw for themselves' (*Lo tho'ssiphun la-theth teven la-am li-llbon ha-lvenim...*). BRICKS WITHOUT STRAW! Pharaoh's tyrannical punishment: **'YOU SHALL NO LONGER GIVE THE PEOPLE STRAW TO MAKE BRICKS! LET THEM GO AND GATHER STRAW FOR THEMSELVES!'** Straw chopped (*teven*) was vital binding material in Nile mud-brick manufacturing.
cccReferences: CCC 2413 (Cruel exploitation and impossible burdens imposed by oppressors); CCC 2575.
historicalContext: Ancient Egyptian mud-brick production: chopped straw (*teven*) provided organic acid and binding fiber preventing bricks from cracking during sun-drying.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Lo tho'ssiphun la-theth teven la-am li-llbon ha-lvenim ke-thmol shilshom hem yelkhu ve-qoshshu lahem teven*: *teven* (straw/chaff). *li-llbon ha-lvenim* ('to brick the bricks').
historicalTrivia: Chemical analysis shows that straw decaying in wet Nile clay releases tannic acid, making the mud far more plastic and pliable for brick-making!

dominicalIntent: 'But the number of bricks that they made in the past you shall impose on them; you shall not diminish it, for they are idle. Therefore they cry, "Let us go and offer sacrifice to our God."' DEMANDING FULL BRICK QUOTAS! Pharaoh demands the exact same daily brick quota while withholding straw, falsely claiming: 'They are idle (*nirpim*)!'
cccReferences: CCC 2575; Matt 23:4 ('They bind heavy burdens, hard to bear, and lay them on men's shoulders').
historicalContext: Fixed daily brick production quotas logged by Egyptian scribes.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-eth-mathqoneth ha-lvenim asher hem ossim thmol shilshom tassimu alehem lo thighr'u mimmennu ki-nirpim hem al-ken hem tzo'aqim le'mor nelkhah nizbechah l-Eloheynu*: *mathqoneth* (fixed measure/tally/quota). *nirpim* (idle/lazy/slothful).
historicalTrivia: Papyrus Anastasi III records Egyptian overseers logging daily brick tallies: 'The men are making their quota of bricks daily'.

dominicalIntent: 'Let heavier work be laid on the men that they may labor in it and pay no regard to lying words.' Increasing slave labor to suppress religious ideas.
historicalContext: Totalitarian strategy of crushing workers with exhaustion to prevent rebellion.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Thikhbad ha-avodah al-ha-anashim ve-ya'assu-vah ve-al-yish'u bi-dvarey-sheqer*: *ve-al-yish'u* ('and let them not regard / pay attention to').
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh labels Yahweh's word through Moses as 'lying words' (*dvarey-sheqer*).

dominicalIntent: So the taskmasters and the foremen of the people went out and said to the people: 'Thus says Pharaoh, "I will not give you straw."' The taskmasters announce Pharaoh's harsh decree.
historicalContext: Public reading of the royal decree to the Hebrew labor camps.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyetze'u noggssim ha-am ve-shotrav vayyo'mru el-ha-am le'mor koh amar Par'oh eyneyni nothen lakhem teven*.
historicalTrivia: Contrast: Pharaoh says 'Thus says Pharaoh' (*koh amar Par'oh*); Moses said 'Thus says Yahweh' (*koh amar YHVH*)!

dominicalIntent: '"Go, get your straw yourselves wherever you can find it, but your work will not be reduced in the least."' Slaves forced to scour fields for stubble.
historicalContext: Scouring harvested grain fields for leftover straw stubble.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Athem lekhu qchu lakhem teven me-asher thimtza'u ki eyn nigrah mi-avodathkhem davar*.
historicalTrivia: Searching for stubble added hours of grueling physical exertion to their daily labor.

dominicalIntent: So the people were scattered throughout all the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw (*Vayyaphetz ha-am be-khol-eretz Mitzrayim li-qoshash qash la-theven*). ISRAEL SCATTERED TO GATHER STUBBLE (*QASH*)! Hebrew slaves are scattered across Lower Egypt gathering **stubble (*qash*)** to mix into their mud-bricks.
historicalContext: Desperate search for agricultural wheat stubble (*qash*) across Delta fields.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyaphetz ha-am be-khol-eretz Mitzrayim li-qoshash qash la-theven*: *qash* (dry stubble/stalks). *li-qoshash* (to gather/stubble-collect).
crossReferences: Exodus 15:7 ('consumed them like stubble'); Isaiah 5:24; Obadiah 1:18.
historicalTrivia: Later in Exodus 15:7, God turns Pharaoh's army into *qash* (stubble) consumed by divine fire!

dominicalIntent: The taskmasters were urgent, saying: 'Complete your work, your daily task each day, as when there was straw.' Egyptian taskmasters beat and push the workers.
historicalContext: Egyptian overseers enforcing daily quotas with rods.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-ha-noggssim atzim le'mor kalu ma'asseykhem devar-yom be-yomo ka-asher bi-hโยth ha-theven*: *atzim* (were pressing/urgent).
historicalTrivia: Egyptian wall paintings frequently show overseers wielding wooden batons over brick-makers.

dominicalIntent: And the foremen of the people of Israel, whom Pharaoh's taskmasters had set over them, were beaten and were asked: 'Why have you not done all your task of making bricks today and yesterday, as in the past?' THE HEBREW FOREMEN BEATEN! The intermediate Hebrew foremen (*shotrey bney Yisra'el*) are **brutally beaten (*vayyukku*)** by Egyptian taskmasters for failing to meet impossible brick quotas.
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The suffering of Hebrew leaders standing between tyrant and slaves).
historicalContext: Corporal punishment inflicted on native officers for quota shortfalls.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyukku shotrey bney Yisra'el asher-ssamu alehem noggssay Par'oh le'mor maddua lo khillithem chuqqkhem li-llbon ki-thmol shilshom gam-ha-yom gam-thmol*: *vayyukku* (and they were struck/beaten).
historicalTrivia: The foremen absorbed the physical beatings to shield the common laborers.

dominicalIntent: Then the foremen of the people of Israel came and cried to Pharaoh: 'Why do you treat your servants like this?' The Hebrew foremen petition Pharaoh directly.
historicalContext: Formal labor grievance petition presented to Pharaoh.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyavo'u shotrey bney Yisra'el vayyiz'aqu el-Par'oh le'mor lammah tha'asseh kho la-avadeykha*.
historicalTrivia: They still refer to themselves as 'your servants' (*avadeykha*).

dominicalIntent: 'No straw is given to your servants, yet they say to us, "Make bricks!" And behold, your servants are beaten; but the fault is in your own people.' Complaining of unfair beatings when straw is withheld.
historicalContext: Exposing the injustice of the state labor decree.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Teven eyn nithan la-avadeykha u-lvenim omrim lanu 'assu ve-hinneh avadeykha mukkim ve-chatath ammekha*: *ve-chatath ammekha* ('and the sin/fault is in your own people').
historicalTrivia: They boldly point out that the fault lies with the Egyptian taskmasters (*chatath ammekha*).

dominicalIntent: But he said: 'You are idle, you are idle; that is why you say, "Let us go and offer sacrifice to the Lord."' Pharaoh mockingly dismisses their plea: 'You are lazy! (*nirpim*).'
historicalContext: Pharaoh's cynical rejection of their grievance.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer nirpim athem nirpim al-ken athem omrim nelkhah nizbechah le-YHVH*: *nirpim* (idle/slothful).
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh doubles down on his insult: *nirpim athem nirpim* ('Lazy are you, lazy!').

dominicalIntent: 'Go now and work. No straw will be given you, but you must still deliver the same number of bricks.' Re-affirming the harsh mandate.
historicalContext: Final rejection of the labor appeal.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-attah lekhu ivdu ve-theven lo-yinnathen lakhem ve-thokhen lvenim thittenut*.
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh refuses any compromise.

dominicalIntent: The foremen of the people of Israel saw that they were in evil plight when they were told: 'You shall not reduce your daily number of bricks.' The foremen realize they are in a desperate, inescapable trap.
historicalContext: Realization of systemic cruelty.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyar'u shotrey bney-Yisra'el otham be-ra le'mor lo-thighr'u mi-llveneykhem devar-yom be-yomo*: *be-ra* ('in an evil/desperate plight').
historicalTrivia: The situation deteriorates severely after Moses' first audience, testing Israel's faith.

dominicalIntent: They met Moses and Aaron, who were waiting for them, as they came out from Pharaoh. The beaten foremen confront Moses and Aaron waiting outside the palace gate.
historicalContext: Confrontation outside the royal audience hall.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiphg'u eth-Moshe ve-eth-Aaron nitzavim li-qra'tham be-tze'tham me-eth Par'oh*.
historicalTrivia: Moses and Aaron were waiting anxiously to hear the outcome.

dominicalIntent: and they said to them: 'The Lord look on you and judge, because you have made us stink in the sight of Pharaoh and his servants, and have put a sword in their hand to kill us' (*Yere YHVH alehkhem ve-yishpot asher hiv'ashthem eth-reychenu...*). THE FOREMEN CURSE MOSES: 'YOU HAVE MADE US STINK BEFORE PHARAOH!' The bitter foremen turn on Moses and Aaron: **'MAY YAHWEH LOOK ON YOU AND JUDGE, BECAUSE YOU HAVE MADE OUR ODOR STINK (*hiv'ashthem eth-reychenu*) BEFORE PHARAOH AND HIS SERVANTS, PUTTING A SWORD IN THEIR HAND TO KILL US!'**
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The prophet enduring bitter rejection from his own brethren); Gen 34:30; 1 Sam 13:4.
historicalContext: Hebrew leaders blaming Moses for escalating their persecution.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mru alehem yere YHVH alehkhem ve-yishpot asher hiv'ashthem eth-reychenu be-eyney Phar'oh u-ve-eyney avadav la-theth-cherev be-yadam le-horghenu*: *hiv'ashthem eth-reychenu* ('you have made our smell foul/stink').
historicalTrivia: The phrase *hiv'ashthem eth-reychenu* ('you made our scent stink') is an ancient idiom for bringing total public disgrace.

dominicalIntent: Then Moses turned to the Lord and said: 'O Lord, why have you done evil to this people? Why did you ever send me?' (*...Adonai lammah ha-re'othah la-am ha-zeh lammah zeh shelachtani*). MOSES' AGONIZED PRAYER: 'LORD, WHY HAVE YOU BROUGHT EVIL ON THIS PEOPLE? WHY DID YOU SEND ME?!' Moses falls on his knees in raw, agonized intercession: **'O LORD, WHY HAVE YOU BROUGHT EVIL ON THIS PEOPLE? WHY DID YOU EVER SEND ME?!'** (CCC 2575: MOSES' BOLD INTERCESSORY PRAYER OF COMPLAINT!).
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (THE INTERCESSORY PRAYER OF MOSES: Boldly complaining to God in raw intimacy on behalf of His suffering people); CCC 2577; Num 11:11; Jer 20:7; Ps 22:1.
historicalContext: Patriarchal intercessory prayer of lament (*lamentatio*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyashav Moshe el-YHVH vayyo'mer Adonai lammah ha-re'othah la-am ha-zeh lammah zeh shelachtani*: *ha-re'othah* ('brought trouble/harm/evil upon'). *shelachtani* ('did you send me').
historicalTrivia: CCC 2575 highlights Moses' prayer: 'From this intimacy with God, Moses' prayer is a striking pattern of intercessory prayer... he complains, questions, and intercedes'.

dominicalIntent: 'For since I came to Pharaoh to speak in your name, he has done evil to this people, and you have not delivered your people at all' (*...ve-hattzeil lo-hitzalta eth-ammekha*). 'YOU HAVE NOT DELIVERED YOUR PEOPLE AT ALL!' Moses concludes his anguish: **'Since I came to Pharaoh in your name, he has done evil to this people, AND YOU HAVE NOT DELIVERED YOUR PEOPLE AT ALL!'** (*ve-hattzeil lo-hitzalta*). The darkest moment before the dawn of Exodus 6!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The darkest hour before divine redemption); Exod 6:1; Ps 13:1-2.
historicalContext: The complete human breakdown before God reveals His Mighty Arm in Exodus 6.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-me-az ba'thi el-Par'oh le-dabber bi-shmekha he-ra la-am ha-zeh ve-hattzeil lo-hitzalta eth-ammekha*: *ve-hattzeil lo-hitzalta* (infinitive absolute: 'delivering You have NOT delivered!').
historicalTrivia: This lowest point of human despair in Exodus 5 sets up Yahweh's glorious 7-fold covenant oath in Exodus 6:1-8!

dominicalIntent: But the Lord said to Moses: 'Now you shall see what I will do to Pharaoh; for with a strong hand he will send them out, and with a strong hand he will drive them out of his land' (*...Attah thir'eh asher e'esseh le-Phar'oh ki ve-yad chazaqah yeshallchem...*). DIVINE RESPONSE TO DESPAIR: 'NOW YOU SHALL SEE WHAT I WILL DO!' Yahweh answers Moses' anguish: **'NOW YOU SHALL SEE WHAT I WILL DO TO PHARAOH; FOR WITH A STRONG HAND HE WILL DRIVE THEM OUT OF HIS LAND!'** (*be-yad chazaqah*). God's power is revealed at man's lowest point.
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (God's strong hand shattering Pharaoh's resistance); CCC 2575; Exod 3:19; Deut 6:21.
historicalContext: The turn of the tide in the Exodus narrative: God answering Moses' prayer of complaint.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe attah thir'eh asher e'esseh le-Phar'oh ki ve-yad chazaqah yeshallchem u-ve-yad chazaqah yegharsshem me-artzo*: *be-yad chazaqah* ('by a strong/mighty hand'). *yegharsshem* ('he will drive them out', root *garash*).
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh will not merely permit them to leave; he will desperately force them out (*yegharsshem*)!

dominicalIntent: God spoke to Moses and said to him: 'I am the Lord' (*Vaydedabber Elohim el-Moshe vayyo'mer elav Anokhi YHVH*). THE SOLEMN RE-ANNOUNCEMENT: 'I AM YAHWEH!' (*ANOKHI YHVH*). God opens His supreme covenant discourse with the foundational self-proclamation: **'I AM YAHWEH!'**
cccReferences: CCC 203-213 (The revelation of YHWH as the eternal, faithful Covenant Lord); CCC 2063; CCC 2575.
historicalContext: Re-affirming the divine identity before issuing the 7-fold covenant redemption oath.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vaydedabber Elohim el-Moshe vayyo'mer elav Anokhi YHVH*: *Anokhi YHVH* ('I am Yahweh').
crossReferences: Exodus 3:14; Exodus 20:2; Isaiah 42:8 ('I am the Lord; that is my name'); Hosea 13:4.
historicalTrivia: The phrase *Anokhi YHVH* ('I am Yahweh') opens both this redemption charter and the Ten Commandments (Exod 20:2).

dominicalIntent: 'I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, as God Almighty, but by my name the Lord I did not make myself known to them' (*...be-El Shaddai u-shemi YHVH lo noda'ti lahem*). EL SHADDAI AND THE FULL COVENANT REVELATION OF YHWH! God explains progressive revelation: He appeared to the patriarchs as **El Shaddai (*El Shaddai* = God Almighty)**, but now reveals the full redemptive power of His Covenant Name **YAHWEH** (*YHVH*).
cccReferences: CCC 203 (Progressive revelation of the Divine Name from El Shaddai to YHWH); CCC 205-206; CCC 2575; Gen 17:1; Gen 28:3.
historicalContext: Distinction between the Patriarchal era (characterized by *El Shaddai*) and the Exodus era (characterized by *YHWH* as Covenant Redeemer).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Va-era el-Avraham el-Yitzchaq ve-el-Ya'aqov be-El Shaddai u-shemi YHVH lo noda'ti lahem*: *El Shaddai* (God Almighty). *lo noda'ti* ('I was not fully known / experienced in redemptive action').
historicalTrivia: The patriarchs knew the name *YHWH*, but did not experience YHWH in His full redemptive, plague-working, nation-saving power until the Exodus!

dominicalIntent: 'I also established my covenant with them to give them the land of Canaan, the land in which they lived as sojourners.' Re-affirming the Abrahamic Covenant pledge of the Promised Land.
historicalContext: Covenant charter with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-gham haqimothi eth-berithi ittham la-theth lahem eth-eretz Kena'an eth eretz megureyhem asher-garu vah*.
historicalTrivia: The verb *haqimothi* ('I established') signifies an unalterable divine legal covenant.

dominicalIntent: 'Moreover, I have heard the groaning of the people of Israel whom the Egyptians hold as slaves, and I have remembered my covenant' (*...va-ezkor eth-berithi*). GOD REMEMBERS HIS COVENANT! Re-asserting that God has heard their groaning and **remembered His covenant (*va-ezkor eth-berithi*)**.
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (God remembering His covenant to liberate His people); CCC 2575; Exod 2:24; Luke 1:72.
historicalContext: Covenant remembrance driving divine intervention.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-gham anokhi shama'thi eth-na meqat bney Yisra'el asher Mitzrayim ma'avidim otham va-ezkor eth-berithi*: *va-ezkor* ('and I remembered').
historicalTrivia: Zechariah's *Benedictus* (Luke 1:72) proclaims that Christ's coming fulfills this exact covenant remembrance (*mneusthēnai diathēkēs hagias autou*).

dominicalIntent: 'Say therefore to the people of Israel, "I am the Lord, and I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians, and I will deliver you from slavery to them, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm and with great acts of judgment..."' THE 4 CUPS OF THE PASSOVER SEDER! Yahweh issues His solemn covenant oath containing **4 REDEMPTIVE PROMISES**: (1) **I WILL BRING YOU OUT (*ve-hotzeth*)**, (2) **I WILL DELIVER YOU (*ve-hitzalti*)**, (3) **I WILL REDEEM YOU (*ve-ga'alti*) with an outstretched arm (*bi-zro'a netuyah*)**, (4) **I WILL TAKE YOU FOR MY PEOPLE (*ve-laqachti*)** (v. 7). **THESE 4 PROMISES FORM THE FOUNDATION FOR THE 4 CUPS OF WINE DRUNK AT EVERY PASSOVER SEDER, CULMINATING IN CHRIST'S INSTITUTION OF THE EUCHARIST AT THE LAST SUPPER!**
cccReferences: CCC 1334 (The 4 Passover cups prefiguring Eucharistic redemption); CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Luke 22:17-20; 1 Cor 11:25.
historicalContext: The 4-fold covenant redemption charter of Exodus 6:6-7, commemorated in the 4 cups of the Seder (Kaddish, Haggadah, Barek/Blessing, Hallel).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Lakhen emor li-vney-Yisra'el Anokhi YHVH ve-hotzeth ethkhem mi-thachath ssivloth Mitzrayim ve-hitzalti ethkhem me-avodatham ve-ga'alti ethkhem bi-zro'a netuyah u-vi-shphatim gdolim*: *bi-zro'a netuyah* ('with an outstretched arm'). *ve-ga'alti* ('and I will redeem/act as Kinsman-Redeemer').
crossReferences: Luke 22:17-20; 1 Corinthians 10:16 ('The cup of blessing'); Psalm 136:12; Isaiah 51:9.
historicalTrivia: At the Last Supper, the 3rd Cup ('Cup of Redemption', *ve-ga'alti*) is the exact Cup Jesus consecrated as His Precious Blood (Luke 22:20; 1 Cor 10:16)!

dominicalIntent: '...I will take you to be my people, and I will be your God, and you shall know that I am the Lord your God, who has brought you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians' (*Ve-laqachti ethkhem li le-am ve-hayithi lakhem l-Elohim...*). THE COVENANT FORMULA: 'I WILL TAKE YOU AS MY PEOPLE AND BE YOUR GOD!' The 4th Passover promise (*ve-laqachti*): **'I WILL TAKE YOU TO BE MY PEOPLE, AND I WILL BE YOUR GOD!'** THIS IS THE CLASSIC FORMULA OF COVENANT ADOPTION IN SACRED SCRIPTURE!
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (The covenant adoption formula forming the People of God); CCC 2575; Lev 26:12; Jer 31:33; Rev 21:3.
historicalContext: The bilateral covenant marriage/adoption declaration between Yahweh and Israel.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-laqachti ethkhem li le-am ve-hayithi lakhem l-Elohim vi-yda'them ki anokhi YHVH Eloheykhem ha-motzi ethkhem mi-thachath ssivloth Mitzrayim*: *Ve-laqachti* (and I will take, root *laqach* = marriage/adoption verb!).
historicalTrivia: Revelation 21:3 echoes this Exodus 6:7 covenant formula for eternal heaven: 'They will be his people, and God himself will be with them as their God'.

dominicalIntent: 'And I will bring you into the land that I swore to give to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob. I will give it to you for a possession. I am the Lord' (*...ve-nathatti othah lakhem morashah Anokhi YHVH*). THE FIFTH PROMISED LAND PLEDGE! God pledges to bring them into Canaan, giving it as an **enduring heritage (*morashah*)**. Sealing it with: **'I AM THE LORD!' (*ANOKHI YHVH*)**.
historicalContext: Solemn divine oath swearing by Himself to bestow Canaan.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-heve'thi ethkhem el-ha-aretz asher nassathi eth-yadi la-theth othah le-Avraham le-Yitzchaq u-le-Ya'aqov ve-nathatti othah lakhem morashah Anokhi YHVH*: *nassathi eth-yadi* ('I lifted my hand / swore an oath'). *morashah* (heritage/possession).
historicalTrivia: The Hebrew idiom *nassathi eth-yadi* ('I lifted my hand') means raising the right hand to swear a binding oath.

dominicalIntent: Moses spoke thus to the people of Israel, but they did not listen to Moses, because of their broken spirit and harsh slavery (*...ve-lo sham'u el-Moshe mi-qqotzer ruach u-me-avodah qashah*). CRUSHED SPIRITS: 'THEY WOULD NOT LISTEN BECAUSE OF A BROKEN SPIRIT!' Moses delivers God's 7-fold oath, but the crushed slaves **cannot hear because of brokenness of spirit (*mi-qqotzer ruach*) and brutal slavery**! Extreme suffering can paralyze human hope.
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The paralyzing weight of oppression obscuring divine hope); Exod 5:21.
historicalContext: Psychological breakdown of enslaved workers under cruel speed-ups.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vaydedabber Moshe ken el-bney Yisra'el ve-lo sham'u el-Moshe mi-qqotzer ruach u-me-avodah qashah*: *mi-qqotzer ruach* ('from shortness/brokenness of spirit').
crossReferences: Exodus 5:21; Proverbs 18:14 ('a broken spirit who can bear?'); Psalm 34:18.
historicalTrivia: The Hebrew phrase *qotzer ruach* ('shortness of breath/spirit') describes gasping exhaustion and despair under trauma.

dominicalIntent: So the Lord spoke to Moses, saying... Re-commissioning Moses to return to Pharaoh.
historicalContext: Divine command renewing Moses' mission.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vaydedabber YHVH el-Moshe le'mor*.
historicalTrivia: God does not abandon the mission despite Israel's broken spirit.

dominicalIntent: 'Go in, tell Pharaoh king of Egypt to let the people of Israel go out of his land.' Command to enter Pharaoh's court again.
historicalContext: Diplomatic mandate for 2nd formal audience with Pharaoh.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Bo dabber el-Par'oh melekh Mitzrayim ve-yeshallach eth-bney-Yisra'el me-artzo*.
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh is explicitly titled 'King of Egypt' (*melekh Mitzrayim*).

dominicalIntent: But Moses said to the Lord: 'Behold, the people of Israel have not listened to me. How then shall Pharaoh listen to me, for I am of uncircumcised lips?' (*...ve-ekh yishma'eni Phar'oh ve-anokhi aral ssephathayim*). UNCIRCUMCISED LIPS (*ARAL SSEPHATHAYIM*)! Moses pleads: 'If my own brothers will not listen, how will Pharaoh listen to me, **for I am of uncircumcised lips (*aral ssephathayim*)?!**' Uncircumcised lips = faltering, unpolished, clogged speech.
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Prophetic sense of inadequacy); Exod 4:10; Isa 6:5; Jer 1:6.
historicalContext: Eastern idiom for speech that is blocked or lacking eloquence.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vaydedabber Moshe liphney YHVH le'mor hen bney-Yisra'el lo-sham'u elai ve-ekh yishma'eni Phar'oh ve-anokhi aral ssephathayim*: *aral ssephathayim* ('uncircumcised of lips', blocked/clogged).
crossReferences: Exodus 4:10; Exodus 6:30; Isaiah 6:5 ('I am a man of unclean lips'); Jeremiah 6:10 ('their ears are uncircumcised').
historicalTrivia: Scripture uses 'uncircumcised' to describe anything clogged or unrefined: uncircumcised lips (Exod 6:12), ears (Jer 6:10), or heart (Lev 26:41)!

dominicalIntent: But the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and gave them a charge about the people of Israel and about Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring the people of Israel out of the land of Egypt. Yahweh issues a joint charge to Moses and Aaron.
historicalContext: Binding administrative charge given to Moses and Aaron together.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vaydedabber YHVH el-Moshe ve-el-Aaron vaytzavvem el-bney Yisra'el ve-el-Par'oh melekh Mitzrayim le-hotzi eth-bney-Yisra'el me-eretz Mitzrayim*.
historicalTrivia: At this point, Scripture inserts the sacred **Genealogy of Moses and Aaron** (vv. 14-27)!

dominicalIntent: These are the heads of their fathers' houses: the sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi; these are the clans of Reuben. Genealogy of Reuben's line.
historicalContext: Genealogical register establishing tribal order starting with Reuben.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Elleh rashey veyth-avotham bney Re'uven bekhor Yisra'el Chanoch u-Phallu Chetzron ve-Kharmi elleh mishpechoth Re'uven*.
historicalTrivia: Scripture lists Reuben and Simeon first to place Levi in proper 3rd-son genealogical order.

dominicalIntent: The sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman; these are the clans of Simeon. Genealogy of Simeon's line.
historicalContext: Clans of Simeon.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-vney Shim'on Yemu'el ve-Yamin ve-Ohad ve-Yakhin ve-Tzohar ve-Sha'ul ben-ha-Kena'anith elleh mishpechoth Shim'on*.
historicalTrivia: Shaul is noted as son of a Canaanite woman, recording intermarriage in Simeon's line.

dominicalIntent: These are the names of the sons of Levi according to their records: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. The years of the life of Levi were 137 years (*...Gershon u-Qehath u-Mrari...*). THE THREE BRANCHES OF LEVI! Levi lived **137 years**. His three sons form the three Levitical branches: (1) **GERSHON**, (2) **KOHATH** (ancestor of Moses, Aaron, and the Priesthood!), (3) **MERARI**.
cccReferences: CCC 1539 (The Levitical branches set apart for sanctuary service); Exod 6:18; Num 3:17-37.
historicalContext: The 3 foundational branches of the Levite tribe.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-elleh shemoth bney-Levi le-tholodotham Gershon u-Qehath u-Mrari u-shney chayey Levi sheva u-sheloshim u-m'ath shanah*: *Qehath* (Kohath).
historicalTrivia: The Kohathites (*Qehath*) were given charge of the Most Holy Objects in the Tabernacle (Num 4:4).

dominicalIntent: The sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei, by their clans. Clans of Gershon.
historicalContext: Gershonite families.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Bney Ghershon Livni ve-Shim'i le-mishpechotham*.
historicalTrivia: The Gershonites were responsible for the Tabernacle curtains and coverings (Num 3:25).

dominicalIntent: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. The years of the life of Kohath were 133 years. Sons of Kohath: **Amram** (father of Moses & Aaron!), Izhar (father of Korah!), Hebron, and Uzziel. Kohath lived 133 years.
historicalContext: The premier line of Kohath.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-vney Qehath Amram ve-Yitzhar ve-Chevron ve-Uzzi'el u-shney chayey Qehath shalosh u-sheloshim u-m'ath shanah*.
historicalTrivia: Izhar's son was Korah, who later led the famous rebellion against Moses and Aaron in Numbers 16!

dominicalIntent: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of the Levites according to their records. Clans of Merari.
historicalContext: Merarite families.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-vney Mrari Machli u-Mushi elleh mishpechoth ha-Levi le-tholodotham*.
historicalTrivia: The Merarites carried the heavy wooden frames, bars, and pillars of the Tabernacle (Num 4:31).

dominicalIntent: Amram took as his wife Jochebed his father's sister, and she bore him Aaron and Moses. The years of the life of Amram were 137 years (*Vayyiqqach Amram eth-Yokheved dodatho lo le-ishah vatteleth lo eth-Aaron ve-eth-Moshe...*). THE PARENTS OF MOSES AND AARON: AMRAM AND JOCHEBED! **Amram** marries **Jochebed** (*Yokheved* = 'Yahweh is Glory'—THE FIRST NAME IN THE BIBLE INCORPORATING THE NAME YAHWEH!). She gives birth to **Aaron and Moses**! Amram lived 137 years.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (The holy family line of Moses and Aaron); Exod 2:1; Num 26:59.
historicalContext: Amram marrying his aunt Jochebed (father's sister) before the Levitical marriage restrictions of Lev 18:12.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiqqach Amram eth-Yokheved dodatho lo le-ishah vatteleth lo eth-Aaron ve-eth-Moshe u-shney chayey Amram sheva u-sheloshim u-m'ath shanah*: *Yokheved* ('Yahweh is Glory / Honor'). *dodatho* (his aunt / father's sister).
historicalTrivia: Jochebed (*Yokheved*) is the very first person in biblical history whose name explicitly embeds the Divine Name YHWH (*Yo-* + *Kheved* = Yahweh is Glory)!

dominicalIntent: The sons of Izhar: Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri. Line of Izhar.
historicalContext: Families of Izhar.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-vney Yitzhar Qorach ve-Nephegh ve-Zikhri*.
historicalTrivia: Korah (*Qorach*) was Moses' first cousin.

dominicalIntent: The sons of Uzziel: Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri. Line of Uzziel.
historicalContext: Families of Uzziel.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-vney Uzzi'el Misha'el ve-Eltzaphan ve-Sithri*.
crossReferences: Leviticus 10:4 (Mishael and Elzaphan carrying Nadab and Abihu's bodies).
historicalTrivia: Mishael and Elzaphan were called by Moses in Leviticus 10:4 to carry away the dead bodies of Nadab and Abihu!

dominicalIntent: Aaron took as his wife Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon, and she bore him Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar (*...vattteleth lo eth-Nadav ve-eth-Avihu eth-El'azar ve-eth-Ithamar*). THE MARRIAGE OF AARON AND ELISHEBA—FOUNDATION OF THE HIGH PRIESTHOOD! Aaron marries **Elisheba** (*Elisheva* = 'God is my Oath' -> ELIZABETH!). She bears him 4 sons: (1) **Nadab**, (2) **Abihu**, (3) **Eleazar** (2nd High Priest!), (4) **Ithamar**. THIS IS THE FOUNDATIONAL HOUSE OF THE AARONIC HIGH PRIESTHOOD!
cccReferences: CCC 1539 (The institution of the High Priesthood of Aaron and Eleazar); Exod 28:1; Num 3:2-4.
historicalContext: Marriage uniting the royal tribe of Judah (Amminadab & Nahshon, Matt 1:4) with the priestly tribe of Levi!
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiqqach Aaron eth-Elisheva bath-Amminadav achoth Nachshon lo le-ishah vatteleth lo eth-Nadav ve-eth-Avihu eth-El'azar ve-eth-Ithamar*: *Elisheva* ('God is my Oath' / Elizabeth). *Nachshon* (Prince of Judah!).
crossReferences: Exodus 28:1; Numbers 3:2-4; Matthew 1:4; Luke 1:5 (Elizabeth mother of St. John the Baptist!).
historicalTrivia: Elisheba (*Elisheva*) is the exact Old Testament name of **St. Elizabeth**, mother of St. John the Baptist, who was also of Aaron's line (Luke 1:5)!

dominicalIntent: The sons of Korah: Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph; these are the clans of the Korahites. Line of Korah.
historicalContext: The Korahite Levitical guild.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-vney Qorach Assir ve-Elqanah ve-Avi'asaph elleh mishpechoth ha-Qorchi*.
crossReferences: Numbers 26:11 ('the line of Korah did not die out'); Psalm 42:1 (Psalms of the Sons of Korah!).
historicalTrivia: Korah's sons did not participate in Korah's rebellion (Num 26:11) and became the famous temple psalmists who wrote Psalms 42-49!

dominicalIntent: Eleazar, Aaron's son, took as his wife one of the daughters of Putiel, and she bore him Phinehas. These are the heads of the fathers' houses of the Levites by their clans (*...vatteleth lo eth-Pinechas...*). ELEAZAR BARS PHINEHAS! Eleazar (Aaron's son) marries Putiel's daughter, fathering **PHINEHAS** (*Pinechas* = 3rd High Priest, famed for holy zeal in Num 25:7-13!).
historicalContext: Birth of Phinehas, hero of divine zeal.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-El'azar ben-Aaron laqach-lo mi-bnovth Puti'el lo le-ishah vatteleth lo eth-Pinechas elleh rashey avoth ha-Leviyyim le-mishpechotham*: *Pinechas* (Phinehas, Egyptian *p3-nhsy* = 'The Dark-Skinned / Nubian').
historicalTrivia: Phinehas (*Pinechas*) is praised in Psalm 106:30-31: 'Then Phinehas stood up and intervened... and that was counted to him as righteousness to all generations forever'.

dominicalIntent: These are the Aaron and Moses to whom the Lord said: 'Bring out the people of Israel from the land of Egypt by their hosts.' CLIMAX OF THE GENEALOGY: THIS IS THAT AARON AND MOSES! Scripture circles back: **'THESE ARE THE AARON AND MOSES TO WHOM YAHWEH SAID: BRING OUT THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL BY THEIR HOSTS!'**
cccReferences: CCC 2575; Exod 6:13.
historicalContext: Formal genealogical authentication of Moses and Aaron as the divine liberators.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Hu Aaron ve-Moshe asher amar YHVH lahem hotzi'u eth-bney Yisra'el me-eretz Mitzrayim al-tziv'otham*: *al-tziv'otham* ('by their armies/hosts').
historicalTrivia: Israel is described not as a ragtag slave band, but as Yahweh's organized armies (*tzva'oth*)!

dominicalIntent: It was they who spoke to Pharaoh king of Egypt about bringing out the people of Israel from Egypt, this Moses and this Aaron. Re-affirming Moses and Aaron before Pharaoh.
historicalContext: Historical confirmation.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Hem ha-mdabrim el-Par'oh melekh-Mitzrayim le-hotzi eth-bney-Yisra'el mi-Mitzrayim hu Moshe ve-Aaron*.
historicalTrivia: Notice the reversed order: verse 26 says 'Aaron and Moses'; verse 27 says 'Moses and Aaron'!

dominicalIntent: On the day when the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt... Resuming the narrative thread from verse 12.
historicalContext: Narrative resumption.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi ba-yom dibber YHVH el-Moshe be-eretz Mitzrayim*.
historicalTrivia: Verses 28-30 pick up the story interrupted by the genealogy.

dominicalIntent: the Lord said to Moses: 'I am the Lord; tell Pharaoh king of Egypt all that I say to you.' Re-iterating: 'I AM YAHWEH!'
cccReferences: CCC 203; CCC 2575.
historicalContext: Divine command to deliver total revelation.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vaydedabber YHVH el-Moshe le'mor Anokhi YHVH dabber el-Par'oh melekh Mitzrayim eth kol-asher anokhi dover eleykha*.
historicalTrivia: Moses must hold back nothing of God's word.

dominicalIntent: But Moses said to the Lord: 'Behold, I am of uncircumcised lips. How then will Pharaoh listen to me?' Re-stating Moses' objection of uncircumcised lips (*aral ssephathayim*), perfectly setting up God's response in Exodus 7:1 ('I have made you like God to Pharaoh!')!
cccReferences: CCC 2575; Exod 6:12; Exod 7:1-2.
historicalContext: Final objection before God appoints Aaron as prophet in Exodus 7:1.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Moshe liphney YHVH hen anokhi aral ssephathayim ve-ekh yishma elai Par'oh*: *aral ssephathayim* ('uncircumcised of lips').
historicalTrivia: Exodus 6 ends on this cliffhanger, resolved in Exodus 7:1 when God declares: 'See, I have made you like God to Pharaoh, and Aaron your brother shall be your prophet'!

dominicalIntent: And the Lord said to Moses: 'See, I have made you like God to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron shall be your prophet' (*...Re'eh nethattikha Elohim le-Phar'oh ve-Aaron achikha yihyeh nevi'ekha*). MOSES MADE AS GOD TO PHARAOH! Yahweh resolves Moses' objection: **'SEE, I HAVE MADE YOU LIKE GOD (*ELOHIM*) TO PHARAOH, AND YOUR BROTHER AARON SHALL BE YOUR PROPHET (*NEVI'EKHA*)!'** Moses represents the unmediated divine authority; Aaron serves as his prophetic spokesman (*navi*).
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Moses standing in the place of God as divine mediator); Exod 4:16; Ps 82:6.
historicalContext: Establishing the divine hierarchy: God -> Moses (*Elohim*) -> Aaron (*Navi*) -> Pharaoh.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe re'eh nethattikha Elohim le-Phar'oh ve-Aaron achikha yihyeh nevi'ekha*: *Elohim* ('as God / in the place of God'). *nevi'ekha* ('your prophet', root *naba* -> *Navi*!).
historicalTrivia: This is the first time the noun **Navi** (*prophet*) is used for Aaron in the Bible!

dominicalIntent: 'You shall speak all that I command you, and your brother Aaron shall speak to Pharaoh, that he let the people of Israel go out of his land.' Command to deliver the divine message through Aaron.
historicalContext: Prophetic proclamation before the Egyptian court.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Attha thedabber eth kol-asher atzavvekha ve-Aaron achikha yedhabber el-Par'oh ve-shillach eth-bney-Yisra'el me-artzo*.
historicalTrivia: Moses receives the word; Aaron speaks the word.

dominicalIntent: 'But I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and though I multiply my signs and wonders in the land of Egypt...' GOD HARDENING PHARAOH'S HEART AND MULTIPLYING SIGNS (*OTHOTH*) AND WONDERS (*MOPHTHIM*)! God announces that He will judicially harden Pharaoh's heart to unleash His **signs (*othoth*)** and **wonders (*mophthim*)**.
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Signs and wonders dismantling Egyptian idolatry); CCC 2575; Rom 9:17-18; Exod 4:21.
historicalContext: The 10 Plagues as divine signs (*othoth*) and wonders (*mophthim*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-ani aqsheh eth-lev Par'oh ve-hirbeythi eth-othothai ve-eth-mophthai be-eretz Mitzrayim*: *aqsheh* (I will make hard/stiff, root *qashah*). *othothai* (my signs). *mophthai* (my wonders).
historicalTrivia: The 10 Plagues are called *othoth* (signs) because each plague systematically targeted and defeated a specific Egyptian idol/deity!

dominicalIntent: 'Pharaoh will not listen to you. Then I will lay my hand on Egypt and bring my hosts, my people the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great acts of judgment' (*...bi-shphatim gdolim*). BRINGING OUT MY HOSTS BY GREAT ACTS OF JUDGMENT! God promises to bring out His **hosts/armies (*tzva'othai*)** by **great acts of judgment (*bi-shphatim gdolim*)**.
