cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Divine judgments liberating Israel); CCC 2575; Exod 6:6.
historicalContext: Judicial dismantling of Egyptian empire power.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-lo yishma alehkhem Par'oh ve-nathatti eth-yadi be-Mitzrayim ve-hotzethi eth-tzva'othai eth-ammi vney-Yisra'el me-eretz Mitzrayim bi-shphatim gdolim*: *tzva'othai* ('my armies/hosts'). *bi-shphatim gdolim* ('by great judgments').
crossReferences: Exodus 6:6; Exodus 12:12 ('on all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgments'); Psalm 136:10.
historicalTrivia: Exodus 12:12 explicitly confirms that these 'great judgments' (*shphatim*) were executed against the demon-gods of Egypt!

dominicalIntent: 'The Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord, when I stretch out my hand against Egypt and bring out the people of Israel from among them' (*Vi-yadh'u Mitzrayim ki-ani YHVH...*). THE SOLE PURPOSE OF THE PLAGUES: 'THE EGYPTIANS SHALL KNOW THAT I AM YAHWEH!' Yahweh declares the supreme purpose of the 10 Plagues: **'AND THE EGYPTIANS SHALL KNOW THAT I AM YAHWEH (*Vi-yadh'u Mitzrayim ki-ani YHVH*), WHEN I STRETCH OUT MY HAND AGAINST EGYPT!'** This answers Pharaoh's defiant question in Exod 5:2 ('Who is Yahweh?').
cccReferences: CCC 2086 (Universal revelation of Yahweh's supreme deity over all pagan gods); CCC 2575; Exod 5:2; Exod 14:18; Ezek 36:23.
historicalContext: Evangelistic/judicial purpose of the plagues converting Egyptians and breaking idolatry.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vi-yadh'u Mitzrayim ki-ani YHVH bi-nthothi eth-yadi al-Mitzrayim ve-hotzethi eth-bney-Yisra'el mi-ttokham*: *Vi-yadh'u* ('And they shall know/acknowledge').
historicalTrivia: Many Egyptians came to know Yahweh through the plagues, forming the 'mixed multitude' (*erev rav*) that joined the Exodus in Exod 12:38!

dominicalIntent: Moses and Aaron did so; they did just as the Lord commanded them. Total obedience of Moses and Aaron.
historicalContext: Unwavering execution of divine instructions.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'as Moshe ve-Aaron ka-asher tzivvah YHVH otham ken assu*.
historicalTrivia: The formula 'they did just as the Lord commanded' echoes Noah's obedience in Gen 6:22.

dominicalIntent: Now Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh (*U-Moshe ben-shemonim shanah ve-Aaron ben-shalosh u-shemonim shanah...*). AGES OF THE REDEEMERS: MOSES AGE 80, AARON AGE 83! Scripture records their exact ages when standing before Pharaoh: **Moses was 80 years old (*ben-shemonim shanah*)**, and **Aaron was 83 years old (*ben-shalosh u-shemonim shanah*)**.
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The mature age of Moses and Aaron at the dawn of the Exodus); Acts 7:23; Acts 7:30.
historicalContext: Historical markers: Moses' life is divided into three 40-year periods: 40 years in Egypt (Acts 7:23), 40 years in Midian (Acts 7:30), and 40 years in the Wilderness (Deut 34:7)!
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-Moshe ben-shemonim shanah ve-Aaron ben-shalosh u-shemonim shanah be-dhabram el-Par'oh*.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 34:7 (Moses dying at 120); Acts 7:23; Acts 7:30; Numbers 33:39.
historicalTrivia: Moses' 120-year lifespan is perfectly divided into 3 equal 40-year epochs: 40 in Pharaoh's court, 40 as Midianite shepherd, 40 as leader of the Exodus!

dominicalIntent: Then the Lord said to Moses and Aaron... Mandate for the miraculous sign before Pharaoh.
historicalContext: Instructions for the court confrontation.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe ve-el-Aaron le'mor*.
historicalTrivia: First direct court miracle requested by Pharaoh.

dominicalIntent: 'When Pharaoh says to you, "Prove yourselves by working a miracle," then you shall say to Aaron, "Take your staff and cast it down before Pharaoh, that it may become a serpent."' Command to throw down the staff to become a dragon/serpent (*tannin*).
cccReferences: CCC 2575; Exod 4:3.
historicalContext: Court challenge for miraculous credentials.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ki yedhabber alehkhem Par'oh le'mor tnu lakhem mopheth ve-amartha el-Aaron qach eth-mattekha ve-hashlekh liphney-Phar'oh yehi le-thannin*: *le-thannin* (into a dragon / sea-monster / large serpent, distinct from *nachash* in Exod 4:3!).
historicalTrivia: Here the staff becomes a **tannin** (dragon/sea-monster), the exact title Ezekiel 29:3 uses for Pharaoh himself: 'the great dragon (*ha-tannin ha-gadol*) lying in the midst of his rivers'!

dominicalIntent: So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and did just as the Lord commanded. Aaron cast down his staff before Pharaoh and his servants, and it became a serpent (*...vayyehi le-thannin*). AARON'S STAFF BECOMES A DRAGON/SERPENT! Aaron casts down the Staff of God before Pharaoh and his court; it instantly transforms into a **dragon/serpent (*tannin*)**!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Miraculous sign before Pharaoh); Exod 4:3; Rev 12:9.
historicalContext: Court demonstration confronting Pharaoh's royal Uraeus cobra symbol.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyavo Moshe ve-Aaron el-Par'oh vayya'assu khen ka-asher tzivvah YHVH vayyashlekh Aaron eth-matthu liphney Phar'oh u-liphney avadav vayyehi le-thannin*: *le-thannin* (dragon/serpent).
historicalTrivia: Aaron throws down the staff (*matthu*), exercising his role as spokesman.

dominicalIntent: Then Pharaoh summoned the wise men and the sorcerers, and they, the magicians of Egypt, also did the same by their secret arts (*...chartummey Mitzrayim be-lahateyhem*). EGYPTIAN MAGICIANS JANNES AND JAMBRES COPY THE SIGN! Pharaoh summons his **wise men (*chakhamim*)**, **sorcerers (*mekhashphim*)**, and **magicians (*chartummim*)**. Using occult secret arts (*lahateyhem* / demonic magic), they copy the sign! **ST. PAUL IN 2 TIMOTHY 3:8 NAMES THE TWO CHIEF MAGICIANS: JANNES AND JAMBRES!**
cccReferences: CCC 2116 (Condemnation of sorcery, magic, and occult practices); CCC 2575; 2 Tim 3:8; Exod 8:7.
historicalContext: Egyptian Lector-Priests (*hry-hb*) performing demonic sorcery (*lahatim* = secret chants/incantations).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vyiqra gam-Par'oh le-chakhamim u-la-mkhashphim vayya'assu gham-hem chartummey Mitzrayim be-lahateyhem ken*: *lahateyhem* (their secret arts / flame-incantations, root *lahat*).
crossReferences: 2 Timothy 3:8 ('As Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so these men oppose the truth'); Exodus 8:7; Acts 13:8.
historicalTrivia: 2 Timothy 3:8 preserves the ancient Jewish oral tradition naming Pharaoh's two chief sorcerers **Jannes and Jambres** (*Iannēs kai Iambrēs*)!

dominicalIntent: For each man cast down his staff, and they became serpents. But Aaron's staff swallowed up their staffs (*Vayyashlikhu ish matthu vayyihyu le-thanninim vayyivla matteh-Aaron eth-mattham*). AARON'S STAFF SWALLOWS UP THEIR STAFFA! The magicians cast down their rods and they become serpents (*thanninim*). **BUT AARON'S STAFF SWALLOWS UP ALL THEIR STAFFA (*vayyivla matteh-Aaron eth-mattham*)!** Divine omnipotence devours occult sorcery!
cccReferences: CCC 2116 (The absolute triumph of God's power over occult sorcery); CCC 2575; 1 John 4:4 ('He who is in you is greater than he who is in the world').
historicalContext: Total humiliation of the Egyptian priesthood: Aaron's staff consumes all the magicians' staffs.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyashlikhu ish matthu vayyihyu le-thanninim vayyivla matteh-Aaron eth-mattham*: *vayyivla* (and it swallowed up, root *bala*).
crossReferences: 1 John 4:4; 1 Corinthians 15:54 ('Death is swallowed up in victory'); Exodus 15:12.
historicalTrivia: Aaron's staff swallowed their staffs (*vayyivla*), taking away their rods permanently while Aaron picked his rod back up!

dominicalIntent: Still Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he would not listen to them, as the Lord had said (*Vayyechazaq lev Par'oh ve-lo shama alehem...*). Pharaoh's heart remains hardened (*Vayyechazaq lev Par'oh*); he dismisses the miracle.
historicalContext: Obstinacy of Pharaoh despite the consumption of his magicians' rods.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyechazaq lev Par'oh ve-lo shama alehem ka-asher dibber YHVH*: *Vayyechazaq* (was strong/hardened).
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh attributes the miracle to superior magic rather than Yahweh's divine power.

dominicalIntent: Then the Lord said to Moses: 'Pharaoh's heart is hardened; he refuses to let the people go.' Yahweh declares Pharaoh's heart heavy (*kaved*), initiating the 1st Plague.
historicalContext: Transition to the 1st Plague.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe kaved lev Par me'en le-shallach ha-am*: *kaved* (heavy/stubborn).
historicalTrivia: Egyptian theology taught that at death, the heart was weighed against the feather of Ma'at; a 'heavy heart' (*kaved*) meant divine condemnation!

dominicalIntent: 'Go to Pharaoh in the morning, as he is going out to the water. Stand on the bank of the Nile to meet him, and take in your hand the staff that turned into a serpent.' Confronting Pharaoh at the Nile River during his morning worship/bathing.
historicalContext: Morning royal procession to the Nile River (*Hapi*), worshipped as a god of life and fertility.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Lekh el-Par'oh ba-boqer hinneh yotze ha-mmaymah ve-nitzavtha li-qra'tho al-ssphath ha-Ye'or ve-ha-mmatteh asher-nehphakh le-nachash tiqqach be-yadekha*.
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh went out to the Nile (*ha-mmaymah*) every morning to perform royal libation rituals to the river god Hapi.

dominicalIntent: 'And you shall say to him, "The Lord, the God of the Hebrews, sent me to you, saying, 'Let my people go, that they may serve me in the wilderness.' But so far, you have not listened."' Delivering the divine ultimatum at the riverbank.
cccReferences: CCC 2060; CCC 2575; Exod 3:18; Exod 5:1.
historicalContext: Formal heraldic message before the Nile confrontation.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-amartha elav YHVH Elohey ha-Ivriyyim shlachani eleykha le'mor shallach eth-ammi ve-ya'avduni ba-midbar ve-hinneh lo-shama'tha ad-koh*.
historicalTrivia: The phrase *ve-ya'avduni* ('that they may serve/worship me') underscores that liberation is ordered toward divine liturgy.

dominicalIntent: 'Thus says the Lord, "By this you shall know that I am the Lord: behold, with the staff that is in my hand I will strike the water that is in the Nile, and it shall be turned into blood."' (*...hineni makkeh... al-ha-mmayim... ve-nehphkhu le-dam*). THE 1ST PLAGUE ANNOUNCED: THE NILE TURNED TO BLOOD! Yahweh commands Moses to strike the sacred Nile with the Staff of God; its waters will **turn to blood (*ve-nehphkhu le-dam*)**!
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (The 1st Plague destroying the Egyptian river-god Hapi); CCC 2575; Rev 8:8; Rev 16:4; Ps 78:44.
historicalContext: The 1st Plague directly targeted **Hapi** (god of the Nile), **Khnum** (guardian of the Nile source), and **Osiris** (whose bloodstream was believed to be the Nile).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Koh amar YHVH be-zoth teda ki ani YHVH hinneh anokhi makkeh ba-mmatteh asher-be-yadi al-ha-mmayim asher ba-Ye'or ve-nehphkhu le-dam*: *ve-nehphkhu le-dam* ('and they shall be turned into blood').
crossReferences: Psalm 78:44 ('He turned their rivers to blood'); Psalm 105:29; Revelation 8:8; Revelation 16:4.
historicalTrivia: The Nile was the lifeblood of Egypt's economy and religion; turning it to blood demonstrated Yahweh's total execution of judgment upon Egypt's supreme water deities!

dominicalIntent: 'The fish in the Nile shall die, and the Nile will stink, and the Egyptians will grow weary of drinking water from the Nile.' Consequences of the 1st Plague: dead fish, stinking river, undrinkable water.
historicalContext: Ecological collapse of the Nile ecosystem.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-ha-dhadah asher-ba-Ye'or thamuth u-va'as ha-Ye'or ve-nil'u Mitzrayim li-sthoth mayim min-ha-Ye'or*: *u-va'as* ('and it shall stink/foul').
crossReferences: Psalm 105:29 ('He turned their waters into blood and caused their fish to die'); Revelation 16:3.
historicalTrivia: The sacred Nile fish (such as the *Lates niloticus*) were worshipped in various Egyptian nomes; their rotting corpses ruined temple purity.

dominicalIntent: And the Lord said to Moses: 'Say to Aaron, "Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt, over their rivers, their canals, their ponds, and all their pools of water, that they may become blood; and there shall be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, even in vessels of wood and vessels of stone."' TOTAL PLAGUE OF BLOOD IN CANALS, PONDS, WOOD, AND STONE VESSELS! Aaron stretches his staff over all Egyptian water systems: rivers (*naharoth*), canals (*ye'orim*), ponds (*agammim*), and even stored water in **vessels of wood (*etz*) and stone (*even*)**!
historicalContext: Extending the blood transformation to all irrigation canals, reservoirs, and household water storage jars.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe emor el-Aaron qach mattekha u-nheteh-yadkha al-meymey Mitzrayim al-naharotham al-ye'oreyhem ve-al-agammeyhem ve-al kol-miqveh meytheyhem ve-yihyu-dam ve-hayah dam be-khol-eretz Mitzrayim u-va-etzim u-va-avanim*: *u-va-etzim u-va-avanim* ('both in wooden and in stone vessels').
historicalTrivia: Even water filtered in porous stone jars (*avanim*) turned to blood!

dominicalIntent: Moses and Aaron did as the Lord commanded. In the sight of Pharaoh and in the sight of his servants he lifted up the staff and struck the water in the Nile, and all the water in the Nile turned into blood (*...vayyah eth-ha-mmayim... vayyehapkhu kol-ha-mmayim asher ba-Ye'or le-dam*). EXECUTION OF THE 1ST PLAGUE! Aaron strikes the Nile before Pharaoh and his court: **ALL THE WATER IN THE NILE INSTANTLY TURNS INTO BLOOD!** (*vayyehapkhu... le-dam*).
historicalContext: Public execution of the 1st Plague at the Nile riverbank.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'assu-khen Moshe ve-Aaron ka-asher tzivvah YHVH vayyarem ba-mmatteh vayyakh eth-ha-mmayim asher ba-Ye'or le-eyney Phar'oh u-le-eyney avadav vayyehapkhu kol-ha-mmayim asher ba-Ye'or le-dam*.
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh had ordered Hebrew baby boys thrown into the Nile (Exod 1:22); now God turns the Nile into blood!

dominicalIntent: And the fish in the Nile died, and the Nile stank, so that the Egyptians could not drink water from the Nile. There was blood throughout all the land of Egypt (*Ve-ha-dhadah asher-ba-Ye'or methah...*). Fulfillment: fish die, Nile stinks, blood covers Egypt.
historicalContext: Total paralysis of Egyptian water supply.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-ha-dhadah asher-ba-Ye'or methah vayyiv'as ha-Ye'or ve-lo-yakhalu Mitzrayim li-sthoth mayim min-ha-Ye'or vayyehi ha-ddam be-khol-eretz Mitzrayim*.
historicalTrivia: For 7 days, Egypt suffered total water loss.

dominicalIntent: But the magicians of Egypt did the same by their secret arts. So Pharaoh's heart remained hardened, and he would not listen to them, as the Lord had said (*Vayya'assu-khen chartummey Mitzrayim be-lahateyhem...*). MAGICIANS TRICK DEMONIC BLOOD COPY! The Egyptian magicians (*chartummim*) use demonic secret arts (*lahateyhem*) to turn a small bowl of dug water into blood as well, compounding Egypt's misery rather than curing it! Pharaoh hardens his heart.
cccReferences: CCC 2116 (Demonic trickery of sorcerers compounding evil); CCC 2575; 2 Tim 3:8.
historicalContext: Demonic sorcery (*lahatim*) imitating the plague on a small scale.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'assu-khen chartummey Mitzrayim be-lahateyhem vayyechazaq lev-Par'oh ve-lo-shama alehem ka-asher dibber YHVH*: *be-lahateyhem* ('with their secret arts/incantations').
historicalTrivia: Notice the foolishness of sorcery: instead of turning the blood back into clean water, the magicians only made more blood!

dominicalIntent: Pharaoh turned and went into his house, and he did not take even this to heart (*Vayyiphen Par'oh vayyavo el-beytho ve-lo-shath libbo gam-la-zoth*). PHARAOH TURNS AWAY HIS HEART! Pharaoh turns his back, enters his palace, and **does not take even this to heart (*lo-shath libbo*)**.
historicalContext: Hardened monarch ignoring state catastrophe.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiphen Par'oh vayyavo el-beytho ve-lo-shath libbo gam-la-zoth*: *lo-shath libbo* ('did not set his heart / pay attention').
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh retreats inside his air-conditioned royal palace while his people suffer.

dominicalIntent: And all the Egyptians dug along the Nile for water to drink, for they could not drink the water of the Nile (*Vayyachperu khol-Mitzrayim ssvivoth ha-Ye'or...*). EGYPTIANS DIGGING FOR WATER! Desperate Egyptians dig wells along the banks of the Nile to find filtered groundwater.
historicalContext: Emergency groundwater digging along riverbanks.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyachperu khol-Mitzrayim ssvivoth ha-Ye'or mayim li-sthoth ki lo yakhalu li-sthoth mi-mmeymey ha-Ye'or*.
historicalTrivia: Groundwater filtered through riverbank sand was marginally drinkable.

dominicalIntent: Seven full days passed after the Lord had struck the Nile (*Vayyimmale shiv'ath yamim achar hikoth-YHVH eth-ha-Ye'or*). DURATION OF THE 1ST PLAGUE: SEVEN FULL DAYS! The 1st Plague of Blood lasts for **seven full days (*shiv'ath yamim*)**.
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Seven days of divine warning and judgment).
historicalContext: 7-day duration of the blood plague before the 2nd Plague.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyimmale shiv'ath yamim achar hikoth-YHVH eth-ha-Ye'or*: *shiv'ath yamim* ('seven days').
historicalTrivia: 7 days gave Pharaoh ample time to repent before the next plague.

dominicalIntent: Then the Lord said to Moses: 'Go in to Pharaoh and say to him, "Thus says the Lord, 'Let my people go, that they may serve me.'"' REPEAT MANDATE: 'LET MY PEOPLE GO, THAT THEY MAY SERVE ME!' Yahweh sends Moses to announce the 2nd Plague, repeating the divine demand (*shallach eth-ammi ve-ya'avduni*).
cccReferences: CCC 2060 (Divine command to liberate Israel for liturgical worship); CCC 2575; Exod 3:18; Exod 7:16.
historicalContext: Formal heraldic warning before the 2nd Plague.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe bo el-Par'oh ve-amartha elav koh amar YHVH shallach eth-ammi ve-ya'avduni*: *shallach eth-ammi* ('release my people!').
historicalTrivia: The 2nd, 5th, and 8th plagues were preceded by a formal morning warning to Pharaoh.

dominicalIntent: 'And if you refuse to let them go, behold, I will plague all your country with frogs' (*...hinneh anokhi nogheph eth-kol-gvulakha ba-tthphard'im*). ANNOUNCEMENT OF THE 2ND PLAGUE: THE FROGS (*TZPHARD'IM*)! Yahweh warns: if Pharaoh refuses, He will strike all Egypt with **frogs (*tzphard'im*)**. Targets **Heqet**, the Egyptian frog-headed goddess of birth and fertility!
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Dismantling Egyptian animal deities); CCC 2575; Ps 78:45; Ps 105:30.
historicalContext: The 2nd Plague directly humiliated **Heqet**, the divine frog-goddess of creation and midwife of the gods.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-im-ma'en attha le-shallach hinneh anokhi nogheph eth-kol-gvulakha ba-tthphard'im*: *nogheph* (striking/plaguing). *tzphard'im* (frogs, Egyptian *kfr*).
crossReferences: Psalm 78:45; Psalm 105:30; Revelation 16:13 ('unclean spirits like frogs').
historicalTrivia: In ancient Egypt, killing a frog was a capital crime punishable by death; during this plague, millions of dead frogs rotted across Egypt!

dominicalIntent: 'The Nile shall swarm with frogs that shall come up and enter your palace, your bedroom and your bed, the houses of your servants and your people, into your ovens and your kneading bowls.' FROGS INVASION IN PALACE, BEDROOM, OVENS, AND KNEADING BOWLS! The frogs swarm out of the Nile into Pharaoh's private royal bedchamber, his bed, his servants' homes, ovens (*tannurim*), and bread-kneading bowls (*mish'aroth*). Total domestic disruption!
historicalContext: Frogs penetrating every sacred, private, and culinary sphere of Egyptian life.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-sharatz ha-Ye'or tzphard'im ve-alu u-va'u be-veythakha u-vi-chdar mishkavkha ve-al-mittathekha u-ve-beyth avadeykha u-ve-ammekha u-ve-thannureykha u-vi-mish'arotheykha*: *Ve-sharatz* ('shall swarm/teem', root *sharatz*!).
crossReferences: Psalm 105:30 ('Their land swarmed with frogs, even in the chambers of their kings'); Revelation 16:13.
historicalTrivia: Notice the divine irony: the Nile that swarmed with Hebrew growth (Exod 1:7) now swarms with invasive frogs (*Ve-sharatz*)!

dominicalIntent: 'The frogs shall come up on you and on your people and on all your servants.' Frogs swarming directly onto the physical bodies of Pharaoh and his subjects.
historicalContext: Physical contact with unclean, slimy creatures violating Egyptian ritual purity.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-vakha u-ve-ammekha u-ve-khol-avadeykha ya'alu ha-tzphard'im*.
historicalTrivia: Egyptian priests were obsessed with physical cleanliness, shaving their bodies every 2 days; frogs crawling over them created supreme ritual defilement!

dominicalIntent: And the Lord said to Moses: 'Say to Aaron, "Stretch out your hand with your staff over the rivers, over the canals, and over the pools, and make frogs come up on the land of Egypt!"' Mandate to Aaron to stretch out the Staff of God.
historicalContext: Execution command for the 2nd Plague.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe emor el-Aaron nteh eth-yadkha be-mattekha al-ha-nneharoth al-ha-ye'orim ve-al-ha-agammim ve-ha'al eth-ha-tzphard'im al-eretz Mitzrayim*.
historicalTrivia: Aaron again acts as the physical executor extending the rod.

dominicalIntent: So Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt (*Vayyet Aaron eth-yado... vat-ta'al ha-tzphardim vat-thekhass eth-eretz Mitzrayim*). EXECUTION OF THE 2ND PLAGUE! Aaron extends his hand; frogs swarm out of all waters and **cover the entire land of Egypt** (*vat-thekhass eth-eretz Mitzrayim*)!
historicalContext: Massive invasion of frogs blanketing every square inch of ground.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyet Aaron eth-yado al meymey Mitzrayim vat-ta'al ha-tzphardim vat-thekhass eth-eretz Mitzrayim*: *vat-thekhass* ('and it covered/blanketed').
historicalTrivia: The singular noun *ha-tzphardim* is used collectively as a gigantic sea of frogs.

dominicalIntent: But the magicians did the same by their secret arts and brought up frogs upon the land of Egypt. Magicians copy the frog plague with demonic sorcery (*lahateyhem*).
cccReferences: CCC 2116 (Demonic sorcery multiplying the plague rather than removing it); CCC 2575.
historicalContext: Demonic sorcery imitating the plague on a small scale.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'assu-khen ha-chartummim be-lahateyhem vayya'alu eth-ha-tzphard'im al-eretz Mitzrayim*.
historicalTrivia: Again, the magicians only added more frogs to Egypt's misery; they could not remove a single frog!

dominicalIntent: Then Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said: 'Plead with the Lord to take away the frogs from me and from my people, and I will let the people go to sacrifice to the Lord' (*...H'athiru el-YHVH ve-yasser ha-tzphard'im...*). PHARAOH'S FIRST BEGGING FOR PRAYER: 'PLEAD WITH YAHWEH!' Broken by the frogs, Pharaoh summons Moses and Aaron, pleading: **'PLEAD WITH YAHWEH (*H'athiru el-YHVH*) TO TAKE AWAY THE FROGS, AND I WILL LET THE PEOPLE GO TO SACRIFICE!'** Pharaoh first acknowledges Yahweh's power!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The intercessory power of Moses moving God to stay plagues); Exod 8:28; Exod 9:28; Exod 10:17.
historicalContext: Pharaoh begging the Hebrew prophet for intercessory prayer (*h'athiru*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vyiqra Par'oh le-Moshe u-le-Aaron vayyo'mer h'athiru el-YHVH ve-yasser ha-tzphard'im mimmenni u-me-ammi va-ashallchah eth-ha-am ve-yizbchu le-YHVH*: *H'athiru* (entreat/intercede/pray, root *atar*).
historicalTrivia: This is the first time Pharaoh asks Moses to intercede for him with Yahweh!

dominicalIntent: Moses said to Pharaoh: 'Be pleased to command me when I am to plead for you and for your servants and for your people, that the frogs be cut off from you and your houses and be left only in the Nile.' Moses grants Pharaoh the honor of setting the exact time for the prayer.
historicalContext: Demonstrating that the removal of frogs occurs strictly according to the set time, proving divine control.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Moshe le-Phar'oh hithpa'er alai le-mathai a'thir lekha u-le-avadeykha u-le-ammekha le-hakhrith ha-tzphard'im mimmenkha u-mi-bbattheykha raq ba-Ye'or tishsha'arnah*: *hithpa'er alai* ('have the honor/glory over me to specify!').
historicalTrivia: By letting Pharaoh set the exact time, Moses eliminated any claim of natural coincidence!

dominicalIntent: And he said: 'Tomorrow.' Moses said: 'Be it as you say, so that you may know that there is no one like the Lord our God' (*...Le-ma'an teda ki-eyn ka-YHVH Eloheynu*). 'TOMORROW!'—'THAT YOU MAY KNOW THERE IS NO ONE LIKE YAHWEH OUR GOD!' Pharaoh sets the time: **'Tomorrow' (*Le-machar*)**. Moses decrees: **'SO THAT YOU MAY KNOW THAT THERE IS NO ONE LIKE YAHWEH OUR GOD!'** (*ki-eyn ka-YHVH Eloheynu*).
cccReferences: CCC 2086 (Uniqueness and incomparability of God: 'There is none like Yahweh'); CCC 2575; 1 Sam 2:2; 1 Chron 17:20.
historicalContext: Prophetic declaration of Yahweh's absolute incomparability.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer le-machar vayyo'mer ki-dvarekha le-ma'an teda ki-eyn ka-YHVH Eloheynu*: *eyn ka-YHVH* ('there is none like Yahweh').
historicalTrivia: The formula *eyn ka-YHVH Eloheynu* ('there is none like the Lord our God') became a classic liturgical acclamation in Jewish and Christian worship.

dominicalIntent: 'The frogs shall depart from you and your houses and your servants and your people. They shall be left only in the Nile.' Promise of complete removal.
historicalContext: Specifying the boundaries of the relief.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-saru ha-tzphard'im mimmenkha u-mi-bbattheykha u-me-avadeykha u-me-ammekha raq ba-Ye'or tishsha'arnah*.
historicalTrivia: The frogs return only to their natural Nile habitat.

dominicalIntent: So Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh, and Moses cried to the Lord concerning the frogs, as he had agreed with Pharaoh (*Vayyitz'aq Moshe el-YHVH...*). MOSES' INTERCESSORY CRY TO GOD! Moses leaves Pharaoh's presence and **cries out in intense intercessory prayer (*Vayyitz'aq Moshe el-YHVH*)**.
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Moses as the powerful intercessor who cries to God to lift plagues); CCC 2577; Jas 5:16-18.
historicalContext: Patriarchal intercession lifting plagues.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyetze Moshe ve-Aaron me-eth Par'oh vayyitz'aq Moshe el-YHVH al-devar ha-tzphard'im asher-sam le-Phar'oh*: *Vayyitz'aq* (and he cried out loudly, root *tza'aq*).
historicalTrivia: James 5:16-18 ('The prayer of a righteous person has great power as it is working') is embodied by Moses' intercession.

dominicalIntent: And the Lord did according to the word of Moses. The frogs died out of the houses, the courtyards, and the fields (*Vayya'as YHVH ki-dvar Moshe...*). GOD HEARS MOSES! Yahweh acts according to Moses' word: millions of frogs die out of houses, courtyards, and fields.
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (God granting the intercessory petition of Moses); Exod 8:31.
historicalContext: Instant mass mortality of frogs across Egypt.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'as YHVH ki-dvar Moshe vayyamuthu ha-tzphard'im min-ha-bbattim min-ha-chatzeroth u-min-ha-ssadoth*.
historicalTrivia: Notice: God did not evaporate the frogs; He killed them in place to leave visible proof of the plague!

dominicalIntent: And they gathered them together in heaps, and the land stank (*Vayytzbru otham chomarim chomarim vat-thiv'as ha-aretz*). STINKING HEAPS OF DEAD FROGS! The Egyptians shovel the rotting frogs into massive **heaps upon heaps (*chomarim chomarim*)**, and **the entire land stank (*vat-thiv'as ha-aretz*)**! Total desecration of the frog-goddess Heqet!
historicalContext: Rotting piles of dead frogs causing national stench and pollution.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayytzbru otham chomarim chomarim vat-thiv'as ha-aretz*: *chomarim chomarim* ('heaps, heaps!'). *vat-thiv'as* ('and it stank/fould').
historicalTrivia: The goddess Heqet, symbol of life and birth, became a rotting stench (*chomarim chomarim*) across Egypt!

dominicalIntent: But when Pharaoh saw that there was a respite, he hardened his heart and would not listen to them, as the Lord had said (*Vayyar Par'oh ki haythah ha-rrevach ve-hakhbed eth-libbo...*). RELIEF BRINGS RELAPSE: PHARAOH HARDENS HIS HEART AGAIN! As soon as the respite (*ha-rrevach*) comes, Pharaoh **hardens his own heart (*ve-hakhbed eth-libbo*)** and breaks his promise! The classic pattern of superficial repentance during crisis.
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Relapse into stubbornness when trial passes); CCC 2575; Exod 7:13; Exod 9:34.
historicalContext: Pharaoh revoking his pledge once relief arrives.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyar Par'oh ki haythah ha-rrevach ve-hakhbed eth-libbo ve-lo shama alehem ka-asher dibber YHVH*: *ha-rrevach* (respite/relief/breathing space). *ve-hakhbed* ('and he made heavy/hardened').
historicalTrivia: Ecclesiastes 8:11 describes this: 'Because sentence against an evil deed is not executed speedily, the heart of the children of man is fully set to do evil'.

dominicalIntent: Then the Lord said to Moses: 'Say to Aaron, "Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the earth, so that it may become gnats in all the land of Egypt."' THE 3RD PLAGUE (UNANNOUNCED): DUST TURNED TO GNATS/LICE (*KIMNIM*)! Without warning, Yahweh commands Aaron to strike the dust (*aphar*); the dust turns into swarming **gnats/lice (*kinnim*)** throughout Egypt! Targets **Geb**, the Egyptian god of the earth!
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Dismantling the earth-god Geb); CCC 2575; Ps 105:31.
historicalContext: The 3rd Plague targeted **Geb**, god of the earth/dust. Unannounced strike.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe emor el-Aaron nteh eth-mattekha ve-hakh eth-aphar ha-aretz ve-hayah le-khinnim be-khol-eretz Mitzrayim*: *kinnim* (gnats/lice/biting insects). *aphar* (dust).
crossReferences: Psalm 105:31 ('He spoke, and there came swarms of flies and gnats throughout their country'); Isaiah 51:6.
historicalTrivia: The 3rd Plague (Gnats), 6th Plague (Boils), and 9th Plague (Darkness) were delivered without prior warning to Pharaoh!

dominicalIntent: And they did so. Aaron stretched out his hand with his staff and struck the dust of the earth, and there were gnats on man and beast. All the dust of the earth became gnats in all the land of Egypt (*...vat-tehi ha-kkinnam ba-adam u-va-bhemah kol-aphar ha-aretz hayah khinnim...*). EXECUTION OF THE 3RD PLAGUE! Aaron strikes the ground: **ALL THE DUST OF EGYPT BECOMES BITING GNATS/LICE ON MAN AND BEAST!**
historicalContext: Biting insect swarm arising out of dry soil desiccation.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'assu-khen vayyet Aaron eth-yado be-matthu vayyakh eth-aphar ha-aretz vat-tehi ha-kkinnam ba-adam u-va-bhemah kol-aphar ha-aretz hayah khinnim be-khol-eretz Mitzrayim*.
historicalTrivia: Ancient Egyptian priests had to be completely free of lice (*kinnim*) to enter temples; biting lice rendered every pagan priest in Egypt ritually disqualified!

dominicalIntent: The magicians tried by their secret arts to produce gnats, but they could not. So there were gnats on man and beast (*Vayya'assu-khen ha-chartummim be-lahateyhem le-hotzi eth-ha-khinnim ve-lo yakhalu...*). TOTAL FAILURE OF EGYPTIAN MAGICIANS! The magicians (*chartummim*) attempt to reproduce the gnats with their secret arts (*lahateyhem*), **BUT THEY COULD NOT (*ve-lo yakhalu*)**! Occult power hits its absolute limit.
cccReferences: CCC 2116 (The impotence of demonic sorcery before divine creation); CCC 2575; 2 Tim 3:8-9.
historicalContext: Defeat of the Egyptian Lector-Priests before the creation of life from dust.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'assu-khen ha-chartummim be-lahateyhem le-hotzi eth-ha-khinnim ve-lo yakhalu vat-tehi ha-kkinnam ba-adam u-va-bhemah*: *ve-lo yakhalu* ('and they were NOT able!').
crossReferences: 2 Timothy 3:9 ('their folly will be plain to all'); Genesis 1:24; Exodus 9:11.
historicalTrivia: 2 Timothy 3:9 refers to this moment: 'they will not get very far, for their folly will be plain to all'!

dominicalIntent: Then the magicians said to Pharaoh: 'This is the finger of God.' But Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he would not listen to them, as the Lord had said (*Vayyo'mru ha-chartummim el-Par'oh Etzba Elohim hi...*). THE PAGAN MAGICIANS CONFESS: 'THIS IS THE FINGER OF GOD!' (*ETZBA ELOHIM HI!*). The defeated sorcerers confess to Pharaoh: **'THIS IS THE FINGER OF GOD!' (*Etzba Elohim hi*)**. **JESUS QUOTES THIS EXACT PHRASE IN LUKE 11:20: 'IF IT IS BY THE FINGER OF GOD (*EN DAKTYLŌ THEOU*) THAT I CAST OUT DEMONS, THEN THE KINGDOM OF GOD HAS COME UPON YOU!'** Yet Pharaoh hardens his heart.
cccReferences: CCC 700 (THE FINGER OF GOD: The Holy Spirit as the Finger of God working divine miracles, cited from Exod 8:19 and Luke 11:20); CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Luke 11:20; Matt 12:28.
historicalContext: Pagan sorcerers forced to acknowledge supreme divine power (*Etzba Elohim*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mru ha-chartummim el-Par'oh Etzba Elohim hi vayyechazaq lev-Par'oh ve-lo-shama alehem ka-asher dibber YHVH*: *Etzba Elohim* ('Finger of God', LXX *Daktylos Theou*).
crossReferences: Luke 11:20 ('If I by the finger of God cast out demons'); Exodus 31:18 (Tables written by the finger of God); Psalm 8:3.
historicalTrivia: In Catholic hymnody (*Veni Creator Spiritus*), the Holy Spirit is explicitly invoked as *Digitus paternae dexterae* ('Finger of the Father's right hand'), drawn directly from Exodus 8:19 and Luke 11:20!

dominicalIntent: Then the Lord said to Moses: 'Rise up early in the morning and present yourself before Pharaoh, as he goes out to the water, and say to him, "Thus says the Lord, 'Let my people go, that they may serve me.'"' ANNOUNCEMENT OF THE 4TH PLAGUE: FLIES! Yahweh confronts Pharaoh at the Nile morning procession, issuing the repeated mandate (*shallach eth-ammi ve-ya'avduni*).
cccReferences: CCC 2060; CCC 2575; Exod 7:15; Exod 8:1.
historicalContext: Morning riverbank warning before the 4th Plague.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe hashkem ba-boqer ve-hithyatzev liphney Phar'oh hinneh yotze ha-mmaymah ve-amartha elav koh amar YHVH shallach eth-ammi ve-ya'avduni*.
historicalTrivia: The 4th Plague introduces the first explicit geographic separation of Goshen.

dominicalIntent: 'Else, if you will not let my people go, behold, I will send swarms of flies on you and your servants and your people and into your houses. And the houses of the Egyptians shall be full of swarms of flies, and also the ground on which they stand.' Announcement of swarms of biting flies/insects (**arov**). Targets **Khepri**, the Egyptian fly/beetle god of the sun!
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Dismantling Khepri, the beetle-god of Egypt); CCC 2575; Ps 78:45; Ps 105:31.
historicalContext: The 4th Plague targeted **Khepri** (the scarab/fly sun-god).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ki im-eynkha meshalleach eth-ammi hineni mashlich bekha u-ve-avadeykha u-ve-ammekha u-ve-vatteykha eth-ha-arov u-male'u batthey Mitzrayim eth-ha-arov ve-gham ha-adamah asher-hem aleha*: *ha-arov* (swarms of flies/biting insects/beetles, root *arav* = to mix/swarm).
crossReferences: Psalm 78:45 ('He sent swarms of flies among them, which devoured them'); Psalm 105:31.
historicalTrivia: The Hebrew word *arov* means a mixed swarm of biting insects (tabanid horseflies and scarab beetles).

dominicalIntent: 'But on that day I will set apart the land of Goshen, where my people dwell, so that no swarms of flies shall be there, that you may know that I am the Lord in the midst of the earth' (*Ve-hiphleythi va-yom ha-hu eth-eretz Goshen...*). THE SEPARATION OF GOSHEN! DIVINE PROTECTION OVER ISRAEL! Yahweh makes a supernatural distinction: **'ON THAT DAY I WILL SET APART THE LAND OF GOSHEN (*Ve-hiphleythi... eth-eretz Goshen*), WHERE MY PEOPLE DWELL, SO THAT NO SWARMS OF FLIES SHALL BE THERE!'** Israel is completely shielded from divine plague judgment!
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (God protecting His covenant people from plague judgments); CCC 2575; Exod 9:26; Exod 10:23; Exod 11:7.
historicalContext: Geographic division: Egyptian Delta plagued; Goshen (Hebrew zone) untouched.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-hiphleythi va-yom ha-hu eth-eretz Goshen asher ammi omad aleha le-vilti heyoth-sham arov le-ma'an teda ki anokhi YHVH be-qerev ha-aretz*: *Ve-hiphleythi* ('and I will set apart / make miraculous distinction', root *phalah*).
historicalTrivia: From the 4th Plague onward, Goshen was entirely immune to all plagues, proving Yahweh's personal presence (*be-qerev ha-aretz*) protecting His chosen ones!

dominicalIntent: 'I will put a division between my people and your people. Tomorrow this sign shall happen' (*Ve-samthi pheduth beyn ammi u-veyn ammekha...*). COVENANT REDEMPTION/DIVISION (*PHEDUTH*)! God declares: **'I WILL PUT A REDEMPTION / DIVISION (*pheduth*) BETWEEN MY PEOPLE AND YOUR PEOPLE!'** (*pheduth* = ransom / redemption!).
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Covenant redemption shielding the faithful); CCC 2575; Ps 111:9; Ps 130:7.
historicalContext: Setting a supernatural boundary line.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-samthi pheduth beyn ammi u-veyn ammekha le-machar yihyeh ha-oth ha-zeh*: *pheduth* (division/redemption/ransom, root *padah* -> *Pedyon* = redemption!).
crossReferences: Psalm 111:9 ('He sent redemption / *pheduth* to his people'); Psalm 130:7; Isaiah 43:3.
historicalTrivia: The Hebrew word *pheduth* means 'redemption / ransom price'; God's redemption creates a permanent boundary between the holy and the profane.

dominicalIntent: And the Lord did so. There came great swarms of flies into the house of Pharaoh and into his servants' houses. Throughout all the land of Egypt the land was ruined by the swarms of flies (*...vat-tishacheth ha-aretz mi-ppney ha-arov*). EXECUTION OF THE 4TH PLAGUE! Biting flies swarm into Pharaoh's palace and all Egypt; **the land was ruined (*vat-tishacheth*) by the flies**, while Goshen remained 100% untouched!
historicalContext: Ecological ruin caused by biting fly swarms.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'as YHVH ken vayyavo arov kaved beythah Phar'oh u-veyth avadav u-ve-khol-eretz Mitzrayim vat-tishacheth ha-aretz mi-ppney ha-arov*: *vat-tishacheth* ('was ruined/corrupted/destroyed').
historicalTrivia: Wisdom 16:9 notes: 'For the bites of locusts and flies killed them, and no remedy was found for their life'.

dominicalIntent: Then Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said: 'Go, sacrifice to your God within the land' (*...Lekhu zivchu l-Eloheykhem ba-aretz*). PHARAOH'S 1ST COMPROMISE OFFER: 'SACRIFICE WITHIN EGYPT!' Broken by the flies, Pharaoh offers a compromise: **'GO, SACRIFICE TO YOUR GOD WITHIN THE LAND [OF EGYPT]!'** Pharaoh tries to keep Israel inside Egypt.
cccReferences: CCC 2060 (Rejection of demonic compromises that compromise pure worship); CCC 2575; 2 Cor 6:14-17.
historicalContext: Pharaoh offering localized religious tolerance inside Egypt, refusing exodus separation.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vyiqra Par'oh el-Moshe u-le-Aaron vayyo'mer Lekhu zivchu l-Eloheykhem ba-aretz*: *ba-aretz* ('within this land [of Egypt]').
crossReferences: Exodus 8:26-27; 2 Corinthians 6:14-17 ('What fellowship has light with darkness?').
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh's 4 compromise offers (Exod 8:25; 8:28; 10:11; 10:24) represent classic worldly temptations to compromise divine worship!

dominicalIntent: But Moses said: 'It would not be right to do so, for the offerings we shall sacrifice to the Lord our God are an abomination to the Egyptians. If we sacrifice what is an abomination to the Egyptians before their eyes, will they not stone us?' (*...ki to'evath Mitzrayim nizbach le-YHVH...*). MOSES REJECTS THE COMPROMISE: 'OUR SACRIFICES ARE AN ABOMINATION TO EGYPTIANS!' Moses refuses: Israel's sacrifices (bulls, rams, goats) are the sacred animal-gods of Egypt (Apis bull, Khnum ram, Hathor cow)! **SACRIFICING EGYPT'S IDOLS BEFORE EGYPTIAN EYES WOULD CAUSE THEM TO STONE ISRAEL!**
cccReferences: CCC 2099 (True sacrifice rejecting pagan idolatry); CCC 2575; Gen 46:34; Exod 8:27.
historicalContext: Sacrificing sacred Egyptian animals (bulls/rams) inside Egypt was considered supreme sacrilege (*to'evah*) by Egyptians, inviting mob stoning.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Moshe lo nakhon la-assoth khen ki to'evath Mitzrayim nizbach le-YHVH Eloheynu hen nizbach eth-to'evath Mitzrayim le-eyneyhem ve-lo yissqlunu*: *to'evath* (abomination/sacrilege). *yissqlunu* ('they will stone us!').
historicalTrivia: The Egyptians worshipped the Apis Bull (sacred to Osiris) and the Ram (sacred to Amun-Re). Slitting their throats inside Egypt meant immediate death by stoning!

dominicalIntent: 'We must go a three days' journey into the wilderness and sacrifice to the Lord our God as he tells us.' Re-asserting total separation: 3 days' wilderness journey.
cccReferences: CCC 2060; CCC 2099; CCC 2575; Exod 3:18; Exod 5:3.
historicalContext: Insisting on complete exodus separation for liturgical sacrifice.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Derekh shelosheth yamim nelakh ba-midbar ve-zavachnu le-YHVH Eloheynu ka-asher yo'mar elenu*.
historicalTrivia: Total liturgical freedom requires complete separation from Egyptian pagan influence.

dominicalIntent: So Pharaoh said: 'I will let you go to sacrifice to the Lord your God in the wilderness; only you must not go very far away. Plead for me.' PHARAOH'S 2ND COMPROMISE OFFER: 'DON'T GO FAR AWAY!' Pharaoh relents slightly: 'Go into the wilderness, **only you must not go very far away (*raq harcheq lo-tharchequ la-lekheth*)**! Plead for me!'
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Worldly pressure keeping believers near pagan influences).
historicalContext: Pharaoh trying to limit Israel's distance to maintain control.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Par'oh anokhi ashalleach ethkhem ve-zavachthem le-YHVH Eloheykhem ba-midbar raq harcheq lo-tharchequ la-lekheth h'athiru ba'adi*: *raq harcheq lo-tharchequ* ('only far away do not go far!').
historicalTrivia: Satan's tactic: 'Be religious, but don't take it too far!'

dominicalIntent: Moses said: 'Behold, I am going out from you and I will plead with the Lord that the swarms of flies may depart from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people, tomorrow; only let not Pharaoh cheat again by not letting the people go to sacrifice to the Lord.' Moses agrees to pray, warning Pharaoh not to deal deceitfully (*ha-thel*).
historicalContext: Prophetic warning against deceitful royal pledges.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Moshe hinneh anokhi yotze me-immakh ve-he'tharthi el-YHVH ve-sar ha-arov mi-Phar'oh mi-vavadav u-me-ammo le-machar raq al-yosseph Par'oh ha-thel le-vilti shallach eth-ha-am li-zbo'ach le-YHVH*: *ha-thel* (to deal deceitfully/mock/cheat, root *hathal*).
historicalTrivia: Galatians 6:7 reflects this: 'Do not be deceived; God is not mocked' (*God is not ha-thel*)!

dominicalIntent: So Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed to the Lord. Moses intercedes again.
historicalContext: Patriarchal intercession.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyetze Moshe me-eth Par'oh vayye'thar el-YHVH*: *vayye'thar* (and he interceded/entreated).
historicalTrivia: Moses demonstrates total pastoral fidelity, praying for the tyrant who oppressed him.

dominicalIntent: And the Lord did according to the word of Moses, and removed the swarms of flies from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people; not one remained (*...lo nish'ar echad*). COMPLETE REMOVAL OF FLIES! Yahweh grants Moses' prayer: every fly departs; **not one remained (*lo nish'ar echad*)**!
historicalContext: Total miraculous removal of insect swarms.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'as YHVH ki-dvar Moshe vayyassar ha-arov mi-Phar'oh mi-vavadav u-me-ammo lo nish'ar echad*: *lo nish'ar echad* ('not one remained!').
crossReferences: Exodus 10:19 ('not one locust was left'); Exodus 14:28.
historicalTrivia: The complete removal (*lo nish'ar echad*) proved that the clearing of flies was as supernatural as their arrival.

dominicalIntent: But Pharaoh hardened his heart this time also, and did not let the people go (*Vayyakhbed Par'oh eth-libbo gam ba-ppa'am ha-zoth...*). PHARAOH BREAKS HIS PROMISE AGAIN! As soon as the flies are gone, Pharaoh **hardens his heart this time also (*Vayyakhbed Par'oh eth-libbo*)** and refuses to release Israel! Persistent obduracy.
cccReferences: CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Exod 7:13; Exod 8:15.
historicalContext: Continued royal obstinacy setting up the 5th Plague (Murrain on Livestock).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyakhbed Par'oh eth-libbo gam ba-ppa'am ha-zoth ve-lo shillach eth-ha-am*.
historicalTrivia: Romans 2:5 warns: 'Because of your hard and impenitent heart you are storing up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath'.

dominicalIntent: Then the Lord said to Moses: 'Go in to Pharaoh and say to him, "Thus says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews, 'Let my people go, that they may serve me.'"' ANNOUNCEMENT OF THE 5TH PLAGUE: MURRAIN ON LIVESTOCK! Yahweh sends Moses to Pharaoh with the heraldic demand (*shallach eth-ammi ve-ya'avduni*).
cccReferences: CCC 2060 (Divine demand for liturgical freedom); CCC 2575; Exod 3:18; Exod 8:1.
historicalContext: Formal warning before the 5th Plague targeting Egyptian livestock.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe bo el-Par'oh ve-dibbartha elav koh-amar YHVH Elohey ha-Ivriyyim shallach eth-ammi ve-ya'avduni*.
historicalTrivia: Livestock constituted the backbone of Egypt's agricultural economy and sacred religion.

dominicalIntent: 'For if you refuse to let them go and still hold them...' Warning Pharaoh against continued stubborn holding (*ve-odkha machaziq bam*).
historicalContext: Warning against obstinate refusal.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ki im-ma'en attha le-shallach ve-odkha machaziq bam*: *machaziq* ('holding fast / detaining').
historicalTrivia: The verb *machaziq* means holding by force.

dominicalIntent: 'behold, the hand of the Lord will fall with a very severe plague upon your livestock that are in the field, the horses, the donkeys, the camels, the herds, and the flocks' (*...yad-YHVH hoyah be-miqnekha... dever kaved me'od*). SEVERE PESTILENCE/MURRAIN (*DEVER KAVED*) ON EGYPTIAN LIVESTOCK! Yahweh warns that the **hand of Yahweh (*yad-YHVH*)** will strike all Egyptian livestock with a **very severe plague/murrain (*dever kaved me'od*)**. Targets **Hathor** (sacred cow goddess), **Apis** (sacred bull god), and **Mnevis**!
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Dismantling Hathor, Apis, and Mnevis); CCC 2575; Ps 78:48; Ps 105:31.
historicalContext: The 5th Plague targeted **Hathor** (cow goddess of love/fertility), **Apis** (sacred bull of Memphis), and **Mnevis** (sacred bull of Heliopolis).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Hinneh yad-YHVH hoyah be-miqnekha asher ba-ssadeh ba-ssussim ba-chamorim ba-ggmallim ba-bbaqar u-va-tzon dever kaved me'od*: *dever* (fatal pestilence/murrain). *ba-ggmallim* (on the camels!).
historicalTrivia: Mention of camels (*gamallim*) in Egypt matches archaeological evidence of camel transport during the Middle/New Kingdom.

dominicalIntent: 'But the Lord will make a distinction between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt, so that nothing of all that belongs to the people of Israel shall die' (*U-philah YHVH beyn miqneh Yisra'el...*). SEPARATION OF ISRAEL'S LIVESTOCK! Yahweh promises: **'YAHWEH WILL MAKE A DISTINCTION (*U-philah*) BETWEEN THE LIVESTOCK OF ISRAEL AND THE LIVESTOCK OF EGYPT!'** Not a single animal of Israel dies.
cccReferences: CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Exod 8:22.
historicalContext: Supernatural immunity shielding Goshen's herds.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-philah YHVH beyn miqneh Yisra'el u-veyn miqneh Mitzrayim ve-lo yamuth mi-kol-li-vney Yisra'el davar*: *U-philah* ('and he will make a miraculous distinction', root *phalah*).
historicalTrivia: The word *davar* here means 'a single thing/head of cattle'.

dominicalIntent: And the Lord set a time, saying: 'Tomorrow the Lord will do this thing in the land.' Setting a precise 24-hour timeframe.
historicalContext: Setting an exact time to eliminate chance.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyassem YHVH mo'ed le'mor machar ya'asseh YHVH ha-davar ha-zeh ba-aretz*: *mo'ed* ('appointed time').
historicalTrivia: Setting a *mo'ed* (appointed time) proved God's absolute control over nature.

dominicalIntent: And the next day the Lord did this thing. All the livestock of the Egyptians died, but not one of the livestock of the people of Israel died (*...vayyamoth kol miqneh Mitzrayim u-mi-mqneh bney-Yisra'el lo-meth echad*). EXECUTION OF THE 5TH PLAGUE! The next day, all Egyptian livestock in the fields die (*dever*), **BUT NOT ONE OF ISRAEL'S LIVESTOCK DIED (*lo-meth echad*)**!
historicalContext: Total devastation of Egyptian horses, donkeys, cattle, and sheep in the fields.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'as YHVH eth-ha-davar ha-zeh mi-mmachrath vayyamoth kol miqneh Mitzrayim u-mi-mqneh bney-Yisra'el lo-meth echad*: *lo-meth echad* ('not one died!').
crossReferences: Psalm 78:48 ('He gave over their cattle to the hail and their flocks to thunderbolts'); Exodus 9:7.
historicalTrivia: 'All the livestock of Egypt' refers to all livestock out in the fields (v. 3); animals kept indoors survived to face the 7th Plague of Hail.

dominicalIntent: And Pharaoh sent, and behold, not one of the livestock of the Israelites was dead. But the heart of Pharaoh was hardened, and he would not let the people go (*...ve-hinneh lo-meth mi-mqneh Yisra'el ad-echad vayyikhbad lev Par'oh...*). PHARAOH INVESTIGATES GOSHEN! Pharaoh sends royal inspectors to Goshen; they verify: **NOT ONE HEAD OF ISRAELITE LIVESTOCK DIED!** Yet Pharaoh's heart remains heavy (*vayyikhbad lev Par'oh*).
historicalContext: Royal inspection confirming the complete immunity of Goshen.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyishlach Par'oh ve-hinneh lo-meth mi-mqneh Yisra'el ad-echad vayyikhbad lev Par'oh ve-lo shillach eth-ha-am*: *ad-echad* ('even one').
historicalTrivia: Even eye-witness proof of Goshen's immunity could not break Pharaoh's stubbornness.

dominicalIntent: And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron: 'Take handfuls of soot from the kiln, and let Moses throw them toward heaven in the sight of Pharaoh' (*Qchu lakhem mlo chophneykhem phiash kivshan u-zraqo Moshe ha-ssamaymah...*). THE 6TH PLAGUE (UNANNOUNCED): KILN ASHES THROWN TOWARD HEAVEN! Without warning, Yahweh commands Moses and Aaron to take **handfuls of soot/ash (*phiash*) from the brick kiln (*kivshan*)**; Moses throws the soot toward heaven before Pharaoh's eyes!
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Divine irony: brick-kiln soot of Hebrew oppression becomes the weapon of plague); CCC 2575; Rev 16:2.
historicalContext: The 6th Plague targeted **Sekhmet** (goddess of healing/epidemics) and **Imhotep** (god of medicine). Soot from the very kilns where Hebrew slaves suffered.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe ve-el-Aaron qchu lakhem mlo chophneykhem phiash kivshan u-zraqo Moshe ha-ssamaymah le-eyney Phar'oh*: *phiash* (furnace soot/ash). *kivshan* (smelting furnace / brick kiln).
crossReferences: Genesis 19:28 (Smoke of Sodom like a furnace/*kivshan*); Exodus 19:18; Revelation 16:2.
historicalTrivia: Divine irony: the ash from the brick kilns (*kivshan*) where Pharaoh tortured Israel becomes the furnace-dust that causes boils across Egypt!

dominicalIntent: 'It shall become fine dust over all the land of Egypt, and become boils breaking out in sores on man and beast throughout all the land of Egypt' (*Ve-hayah le-avaq... li-shchin pore'ach a-va'abu'oth ba-adam u-va-bhemah...*). BOILS BREAKING OUT IN SORES (*SHCHIN PORE'ACH A-VA'ABU'OTH*)! The kiln dust becomes fine powder (*avaq*), producing painful **boils breaking out into open sores (*shchin pore'ach a-va'abu'oth*)** on man and beast!
cccReferences: CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Deut 28:27 (The boil of Egypt); Rev 16:2.
historicalContext: Severe epidemic of painful inflammatory boils and pustules (*a-va'abu'oth*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-hayah le-avaq al kol-eretz Mitzrayim ve-hayah al-ha-adam ve-al-ha-bhemah li-shchin pore'ach a-va'abu'oth be-khol-eretz Mitzrayim*: *shchin* (inflammatory boils). *a-va'abu'oth* (blistering pustules).
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 28:27 ('the boils of Egypt'); Job 2:7; Revelation 16:2 ('foul and painful sores').
historicalTrivia: Deuteronomy 28:27 warns Israel against apostasy by threatening 'the boils of Egypt (*shchin Mitzrayim*)'!

dominicalIntent: So they took soot from the kiln and stood before Pharaoh. And Moses threw it toward heaven, and it became boils breaking out in sores on man and beast. Moses throws the furnace soot into the air before Pharaoh, instantly triggering the outbreak of boils.
historicalContext: Public execution of the 6th Plague in the royal court.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiqchu eth-phiash ha-kkivshan vayya'amdu liphney Phar'oh vayyizroq otho Moshe ha-ssamaymah vayyehi shchin a-va'abu'oth pore'ach ba-adam u-va-bhemah*.
historicalTrivia: The boils broke out immediately in Pharaoh's presence.

dominicalIntent: And the magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils, for the boils were on the magicians and on all the Egyptians (*Ve-lo-yakhalu ha-chartummim la-amod liphney Moshe mi-ppney ha-shchin...*). TOTAL HUMILIATION: MAGICIANS CANNOT STAND BEFORE MOSES! The Egyptian magicians (*chartummim*) are so covered in painful boils that **THEY CANNOT EVEN STAND BEFORE MOSES (*Ve-lo-yakhalu ha-chartummim la-amod*)**! Absolute medical and magical defeat of Egypt's healing deities!
cccReferences: CCC 2116 (The ultimate collapse and humiliation of occult magic); CCC 2575; 2 Tim 3:9.
historicalContext: The court sorcerers fleeing the presence of Moses in physical agony.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-lo-yakhalu ha-chartummim la-amod liphney Moshe mi-ppney ha-shchin ki-hayah ha-shchin ba-chartummim u-ve-khol-Mitzrayim*: *la-amod* ('to stand').
historicalTrivia: This is the final appearance of the Egyptian magicians (*chartummim*) in Exodus; after this humiliating defeat, they vanish from the narrative!

dominicalIntent: But the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh, and he did not listen to them, as the Lord had spoken to Moses (*Vayyechazzeq YHVH eth-lev Par'oh...*). FIRST EXPLICIT STATEMENT: YAHWEH HARDENED PHARAOH'S HEART! For the first time in the plague narrative, Scripture explicitly states: **'BUT YAHWEH HARDENED THE HEART OF PHARAOH (*Vayyechazzeq YHVH eth-lev Par'oh*)'**! Judicial punishment after Pharaoh hardened his own heart 5 consecutive times (Exod 7:13; 7:22; 8:15; 8:19; 8:32).
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Judicial hardening of the unrepentant sinner); CCC 2575; Rom 9:17-18.
historicalContext: Divine judicial hardening following persistent human obduracy.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyechazzeq YHVH eth-lev Par'oh ve-lo shama alehem ka-asher dibber YHVH el-Moshe*: *Vayyechazzeq YHVH* ('And Yahweh hardened / made strong').
historicalTrivia: St. Augustine noted that God hardens not by imparting evil, but by withholding His grace from those who repeatedly reject it.

dominicalIntent: Then the Lord said to Moses: 'Rise up early in the morning and present yourself before Pharaoh and say to him, "Thus says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews, 'Let my people go, that they may serve me.'"' ANNOUNCEMENT OF THE 7TH PLAGUE: HEAVY HAIL AND FIRE! Yahweh commands Moses to rise early and deliver the heraldic decree (*shallach eth-ammi ve-ya'avduni*).
cccReferences: CCC 2060; CCC 2575; Exod 7:15; Exod 8:20.
historicalContext: Morning riverbank warning before the catastrophic 7th Plague of Hail.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe hashkem ba-boqer ve-hithyatzev liphney Phar'oh ve-amartha elav koh-amar YHVH Elohey ha-Ivriyyim shallach eth-ammi ve-ya'avduni*.
historicalTrivia: The 7th Plague marks a major escalation: for the first time, human life is directly threatened by death from heaven.

dominicalIntent: 'For this time I will send all my plagues on yourself, and on your servants, and your people, so that you may know that there is none like me in all the earth' (*...ki eyn kamoni be-khol-ha-aretz*). 'THERE IS NONE LIKE ME IN ALL THE EARTH!' Yahweh warns: 'I will send all my plagues into your very heart (*el-libbkha*), **THAT YOU MAY KNOW THAT THERE IS NONE LIKE ME IN ALL THE EARTH!'** (*ki eyn kamoni be-khol-ha-aretz*).
cccReferences: CCC 2086 (Uniqueness and supremacy of God over all earthly powers); CCC 2575; Deut 4:35; 1 Sam 2:2.
historicalContext: Solemn warning of cosmic plagues destroying Pharaoh's pride.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ki ba-ppa'am ha-zoth anokhi sholeach eth-kol-maggphothai el-libbkha u-ve-avadeykha u-ve-ammekha le-ba'ur teda ki eyn kamoni be-khol-ha-aretz*: *maggphothai* (my plagues/strikes). *eyn kamoni* ('there is none like Me!').
historicalTrivia: The noun *maggphoth* (plagues) refers to overwhelming divine blows.

dominicalIntent: 'For by now I could have put out my hand and struck you and your people with pestilence, and you would have been cut off from the earth.' God explains He could have wiped out Pharaoh instantly.
historicalContext: Demonstrating divine restraint: God chose not to obliterate Egypt instantly.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ki attah shalachti eth-yadi va-akh ethkha ve-eth-ammekha ba-ddaver vat-tikhakhed min-ha-aretz*: *vat-tikhakhed* ('and you would have been effaced/cut off').
historicalTrivia: God's restraint gave Egypt opportunity after opportunity to submit.

dominicalIntent: 'But for this purpose I have raised you up, to show you my power, so that my name may be proclaimed in all the earth' (*Ve-ulam ba'avur zoth he'emadthikha le-har'othkha eth-kochi u-le-ma'an ssapper shemi be-khol-ha-aretz*). GOD'S PURPOSE FOR PHARAOH—CITED IN ROMANS 9:17! **THE SUPREME THEOLOGICAL STATEMENT ON DIVINE SOVEREIGNTY!** God declares: **'BUT FOR THIS VERY PURPOSE I HAVE RAISED YOU UP: TO SHOW YOU MY POWER, AND THAT MY NAME MAY BE PROCLAIMED IN ALL THE EARTH!'** (**ST. PAUL QUOTES THIS VERSE WORD-FOR-WORD IN ROMANS 9:17**!).
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (God using even the stubbornness of tyrants to manifest His glory to all nations); CCC 2575; Rom 9:17; Ps 106:8; Josh 2:9-11.
historicalContext: Theological justification for permitting Pharaoh's temporary reign.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-ulam ba'avur zoth he'emadthikha le-har'othkha eth-kochi u-le-ma'an ssapper shemi be-khol-ha-aretz*: *he'emadthikha* ('I have caused you to stand / raised you up'). *ssapper shemi* ('that my Name may be recounted/proclaimed').
crossReferences: Romans 9:17 ('For the Scripture says to Pharaoh, "For this very purpose I have raised you up..."'); Joshua 2:9-11; Psalm 106:8.
historicalTrivia: Joshua 2:9-11 proves this verse was fulfilled: 40 years later in Jericho, Rahab tells the spies: 'We have heard how Yahweh dried up the Red Sea... our hearts melted because of you'!

dominicalIntent: 'You are still exalting yourself against my people and will not let them go.' Rebuking Pharaoh's prideful self-exaltation (*mistolel*).
historicalContext: Exposing Pharaoh setting up an obstacle (*mistolel*) against God.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Odkhah mistolel be-ammi le-vilti shallcham*: *mistolel* (exalting yourself / making a highway/dam against).
historicalTrivia: The verb *mistolel* implies building an embankment/rampart against God's people.

dominicalIntent: 'Behold, about this time tomorrow I will cause very heavy hail to fall, such as has never been seen in Egypt from the day it was founded until now.' Announcement of the 7th Plague: unprecedented cosmic hail.
historicalContext: The 7th Plague targeted **Nut** (goddess of the sky/heaven), **Shu** (god of the atmosphere), and **Set** (god of storms).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Hinneh anokhi mamthir ka-eth machar barad kaved me'od asher lo-hayah khamohu be-Mitzrayim mi-l-yom hivvassdah ve-ad-attah*: *mamthir* ('causing rain of'). *barad* (hail).
historicalTrivia: Egypt normally receives almost zero rainfall; catastrophic ice-hail (*barad*) was completely alien to Egyptian experience.

dominicalIntent: 'Now therefore send, get your livestock and all that you have in the field into safe shelter, for every man and beast that is in the field and is not brought home will die when the hail falls on them.' MERCIFUL WARNING TO SAVE LIVES! God mercifully warns Egyptians to bring their livestock and servants indoors to escape death from the hail.
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (God's mercy offering salvation even to Egyptians who heed His word).
historicalContext: Merciful 24-hour grace period allowing Egyptians to shelter cattle indoors.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-attah shelach he'ez eth-miqnekha ve-eth kol-asher lekha ba-ssadeh kol-ha-adam ve-ha-bhemah asher-yimmatze ba-ssadeh ve-lo ye'assaph ha-bbeythah ve-yarad alehem ha-barad va-methu*: *he'ez* ('bring to safety / shelter', root *oz*).
historicalTrivia: This is the first plague where God offers a way of salvation to any individual Egyptian who fears His word!

dominicalIntent: Then whoever feared the word of the Lord among the servants of Pharaoh hurried his slaves and his livestock into the houses (*Ha-yare eth-dvar YHVH me-avdey Par'oh he'niyss eth-avadav ve-eth-miqnehu el-ha-bbattim*). EGYPTIANS WHO FEARED THE WORD OF YAHWEH SAVED! Scripture records: **'THOSE WHO FEARED THE WORD OF YAHWEH AMONG PHARAOH'S SERVANTS HURRIED THEIR SLAVES AND LIVESTOCK INTO HOUSES!'** Faithful Egyptians are saved by believing God's word!
cccReferences: CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Acts 10:35 ('In every nation anyone who fears him is acceptable to him').
historicalContext: First instance of Gentiles believing and obeying Yahweh's word to escape judgment.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ha-yare eth-dvar YHVH me-avdey Par'oh he'niyss eth-avadav ve-eth-miqnehu el-ha-bbattim*: *Ha-yare* ('He who feared'). *he'niyss* ('caused to flee/hurried').
historicalTrivia: These god-fearing Egyptians formed the core of the 'mixed multitude' (*erev rav*) that marched out with Moses (Exod 12:38)!

dominicalIntent: but whoever did not pay attention to the word of the Lord left his slaves and his livestock in the field (*Ve-asher lo-sam libbo el-dvar YHVH...*). Foolish Egyptians who ignored God's word leave their servants and cattle exposed to death.
historicalContext: The fatal consequence of ignoring divine warnings.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-asher lo-sam libbo el-dvar YHVH vayya'azov eth-avadav ve-eth-miqnehu ba-ssadeh*: *lo-sam libbo* ('did not set his heart / pay attention').
historicalTrivia: Proverbs 22:3 describes this: 'The prudent sees danger and hides himself, but the simple go on and suffer for it'.

dominicalIntent: Then the Lord said to Moses: 'Stretch out your hand toward heaven, so that there may be hail in all the land of Egypt, on man and beast and every plant of the field, in the land of Egypt.' Command to stretch out the hand for the 7th Plague.
historicalContext: Moses executing the cosmic hail plague.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe nteh eth-yadkha al-ha-ssamayim ve-yihi varad be-khol-eretz Mitzrayim al-ha-adam ve-al-ha-bhemah ve-al kol-essv ha-ssadeh be-eretz Mitzrayim*.
historicalTrivia: Moses himself (not Aaron) stretches out his hand toward heaven.

dominicalIntent: Then Moses stretched out his staff toward heaven, and the Lord sent thunder and hail, and fire ran down to the earth. And the Lord rained hail upon the land of Egypt (*...V-YHVH nathan qoloth u-varad vat-thilah esh artzah...*). THUNDER, HAIL, AND FIRE RUSHING TO THE EARTH! Moses stretches his staff; **YAHWEH SENDS THUNDER (*QOLOTH*), HAIL (*BARAD*), AND FIRE RUSHING DOWN TO THE EARTH (*esh artzah*)!** Lightning bolts interwoven with ice blocks!
historicalContext: Apocalyptic storm combining ice-hail and sheet-lightning (*esh*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyet Moshe eth-matthu al-ha-ssamayim V-YHVH nathan qoloth u-varad vat-thilah esh artzah vayyamther YHVH barad al-eretz Mitzrayim*: *qoloth* (thunders/voices). *vat-thilah esh artzah* ('and fire ran/darted down to the earth').
historicalTrivia: Revelation 8:7 quotes Exodus 9:23 for the 1st Trumpet judgment: 'there followed hail and fire, mixed with blood, and these were thrown upon the earth'.

dominicalIntent: There was hail and fire flashing continually in the midst of the hail, very heavy hail, such as had never been in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation (*...u-mithlaqachath bi-thokh ha-barad...*). FIRE FLASHING CONTINUALLY INSIDE THE HAIL! Supernatural phenomenon: **FIRE FLASHING CONTINUALLY INSIDE BLOCKS OF ICE (*esh mithlaqachath bi-thokh ha-barad*)**! Fire and ice co-existing without destroying each other!
cccReferences: CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Ezek 1:4.
historicalContext: Miraculous co-existence of fire (*esh*) and ice (*barad*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi varad ve-esh mithlaqachath bi-thokh ha-barad kaved me'od asher lo-hayah khamohu be-khol-eretz Mitzrayim me-az haythah le-ghoy*: *mithlaqachath* ('flashing continually / infolding itself', root *laqach*).
crossReferences: Ezekiel 1:4 ('a great cloud, with brightness around it, and fire flashing forth continually'); Psalm 148:8.
historicalTrivia: Ezekiel 1:4 uses this exact word *mithlaqachath* ('infolding fire') to describe the divine chariot vision!

dominicalIntent: The hail struck down everything that was in the field in all the land of Egypt, both man and beast. And the hail struck down every plant of the field and broke every tree of the field. TOTAL DESTRUCTION OF CROPS AND TREES! The cosmic hail destroys all outdoor life, breaking every tree and shattering flax and barley crops.
historicalContext: Agricultural catastrophe destroying Egypt's spring harvest.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyakh ha-barad be-khol-eretz Mitzrayim eth kol-asher ba-ssadeh me-adam ve-ad-bhemah ve-eth kol-essev ha-ssadeh hikkah ha-barad ve-eth-kol-etz ha-ssadeh Shibber*.
crossReferences: Psalm 78:47 ('He destroyed their vines with hail and their sycamores with frost'); Psalm 105:33.
historicalTrivia: Sycamore fig trees (*etz ha-ssadeh*) took decades to grow; breaking them decimated timber and fruit supplies.

dominicalIntent: Only in the land of Goshen, where the people of Israel were, was there no hail (*Raq be-eretz Goshen... lo hayah barad*). GOSHEN UNTOUCHED BY HAIL! Scripture records: **'ONLY IN THE LAND OF GOSHEN, WHERE THE PEOPLE OF ISRAEL WERE, WAS THERE NO HAIL!'** (*lo hayah barad*). Perfect divine protection.
cccReferences: CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Exod 8:22; Exod 10:23.
historicalContext: Complete atmospheric shield over Goshen.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Raq be-eretz Goshen asher-sham bney Yisra'el lo hayah barad*.
historicalTrivia: While fire and ice rained down just miles away, the skies over Goshen remained clear and serene!

dominicalIntent: Then Pharaoh sent and called Moses and Aaron and said to them: 'This time I have sinned; the Lord is in the right, and I and my people are in the wrong' (*...Chatathi ha-ppa'am YHVH ha-tzaddiq va-ani ve-ammi ha-rrsha'im*). PHARAOH'S CONFESSION: 'I HAVE SINNED! YAHWEH IS RIGHT, AND I AM WRONG!' Terrified by the thunder and hail, Pharaoh summons Moses and Aaron, confessing: **'THIS TIME I HAVE SINNED! YAHWEH IS IN THE RIGHT (*YHVH ha-tzaddiq*), AND I AND MY PEOPLE ARE IN THE WRONG (*ha-rrsha'im*)!'**
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Pharaoh's desperate, forced confession under terror); Exod 10:16; 1 Sam 15:24; Matt 27:4.
historicalContext: Royal confession of guilt under catastrophic divine judgment.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyishlach Par'oh vayyiqra le-Moshe u-le-Aaron vayyo'mer alehem chatathi ha-ppa'am YHVH ha-tzaddiq va-ani ve-ammi ha-rrsha'im*: *YHVH ha-tzaddiq* ('Yahweh is the Righteous One'). *ha-rrsha'im* ('the wicked ones').
crossReferences: Exodus 10:16; 1 Samuel 15:24; Matthew 27:4 (Judas: 'I have sinned'); Psalm 119:137.
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh uses formal legal language: *YHVH ha-tzaddiq* ('Yahweh is innocent/righteous') and *ha-rrsha'im* ('we are the guilty/wicked')!

dominicalIntent: 'Plead with the Lord, for there has been enough of God's thunder and hail. I will let you go, and you shall stay no longer.' Pharaoh begs for intercession, promising immediate release.
historicalContext: Begging for cessation of thunder (*qoloth Elohim*) and hail.
translationNuances: Hebrew *H'athiru el-YHVH ve-rav mi-heyoth qoloth Elohim u-varad va-ashallchah ethkhem ve-lo thossiphun la-amod*: *qoloth Elohim* ('voices/thunders of God').
crossReferences: Exodus 8:8; Exodus 9:33; Psalm 29:3 ('The voice of the Lord is upon the waters').
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh refers to the thunder as 'the voices of God' (*qoloth Elohim*).

dominicalIntent: Moses said to him: 'As soon as I have gone out of the city, I will stretch out my hands to the Lord. The thunder will cease, and there will be no more hail, so that you may know that the earth is the Lord's' (*...le-ma'an teda ki la-YHVH ha-aretz*). STRETCHING OUT HANDS IN PRAYER—'THAT YOU MAY KNOW THE EARTH IS YAHWEH'S!' Moses promises to pray outside the city: **'THAT YOU MAY KNOW THAT THE EARTH IS YAHWEH'S!'** (*ki la-YHVH ha-aretz*). CITED IN PSALM 24:1!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Moses lifting up hands in intercessory prayer outside the city); Ps 24:1; 1 Cor 10:26.
historicalContext: Extending hands in liturgical intercession (*phressath kappayim*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer elav Moshe ke-tze'thi eth-ha-ir ephros eth-kappai el-YHVH ha-qqoloth yikhdathun ve-ha-barad lo yihyeh-od le-ma'an teda ki la-YHVH ha-aretz*: *ki la-YHVH ha-aretz* ('that the earth is Yahweh's').
crossReferences: Psalm 24:1 ('The earth is the Lord's and the fullness thereof'); 1 Corinthians 10:26; 1 Kings 8:22.
historicalTrivia: St. Paul in 1 Corinthians 10:26 quotes Exodus 9:29 / Psalm 24:1 (*tou gar kyriou hē gē kai to plērōma autēs*) to justify eating all wholesome foods!

dominicalIntent: 'But as for you and your servants, I know that you do not yet fear the Lord God' (*Ve-attha ve-avadeykha yada'ti ki terem thiyre'un mi-ppney YHVH Elohim*). PROPHETIC DISCERNMENT: 'I KNOW YOU DO NOT YET FEAR YAHWEH!' Moses sees right through Pharaoh's superficial confession, knowing his repentance is born of terror, not true fear of God.
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Prophetic discernment seeing through superficial contrition).
historicalContext: Prophetic evaluation of insincere court repentance.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-attha ve-avadeykha yada'ti ki terem thiyre'un mi-ppney YHVH Elohim*: *terem thiyre'un* ('you do not yet fear/revere').
historicalTrivia: This is the only place in the Pentateuch where the combined title **YHVH Elohim** ('The LORD God') appears outside Genesis 2-3!

dominicalIntent: The flax and the barley were struck down, for the barley was in the ear and the flax was in bud. Agricultural breakdown: flax (*pishtah*) and barley (*ss'orah*) destroyed in the February/March harvest.
historicalContext: Egyptian agricultural calendar: Barley (*ss'orah*) headed out and flax (*pishtah*) budding in late winter (February/March).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-ha-ppishtah ve-ha-ss'orah hukkathah ki ha-ss'orah aviv ve-ha-ppishtah giv'ol*: *aviv* (in the ear/heading). *giv'ol* (in bud/boll).
historicalTrivia: Flax was used for fine Egyptian linen (*sshesh*) and barley for bread and beer; their destruction crippled Egyptian textiles and brewing!

dominicalIntent: But the wheat and the emmer were not struck down, for they are late in coming up. Wheat (*chittah*) and emmer-spelt (*kussemath*) spared because they ripen later in April/May (setting up the 8th Plague of Locusts!).
historicalContext: Late-ripening winter crops (wheat and emmer) surviving the hail to be consumed by locusts in Exodus 10.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-ha-chittah ve-ha-kkussemath lo hukku ki aphiloth henah*: *kussemath* (emmer wheat / spelt). *aphiloth* (late-ripening).
historicalTrivia: Emmer wheat (*kussemath*) was the primary grain used for Egyptian bread production.

dominicalIntent: So Moses went out of the city from Pharaoh and stretched out his hands to the Lord, and the thunder and the hail ceased, and the rain no longer poured upon the earth (*Vayyetze Moshe me-eth Par'oh... vayyiphros kappav... vayyikhdlun ha-qqoloth...*). MOSES PRAYS WITH OUTSTRETCHED HANDS—HAIL CEASES! Moses leaves the city, stretches out his hands (*kappav*) in prayer to Yahweh; the thunder, hail, and rain **instantly cease**!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The instant efficacy of Moses' intercessory prayer); Jas 5:17-18.
historicalContext: Intercessory prayer posture with palms turned upward (*phressath kappayim*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyetze Moshe me-eth Par'oh eth-ha-ir vayyiphros kappav el-YHVH vayyikhdlun ha-qqoloth ve-ha-barad u-matar lo-nathakh artzah*: *vayyiphros kappav* ('and he spread out his palms').
historicalTrivia: Spreading out the palms (*kappayim*) was the classic ancient posture of supplication, seeking divine grace.

dominicalIntent: But when Pharaoh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunder had ceased, he sinned yet again and hardened his heart, he and his servants (*Vayyar Par'oh ki-chadal ha-matar... vayyosseph la-chato vayyakhbed libbo...*). RELIEF BRINGS RENEWED SIN: PHARAOH HARDENS HIS HEART AGAIN! As soon as the danger passes, Pharaoh **sins yet again (*vayyosseph la-chato*)** and hardens his heart!
cccReferences: CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Exod 8:15; Exod 8:32.
historicalContext: Recidivism of the unrepentant sinner following relief.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyar Par'oh ki-chadal ha-matar ve-ha-barad ve-ha-qqoloth vayyosseph la-chato vayyakhbed libbo hu ve-avadav*: *vayyosseph la-chato* ('and he added to sin').
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh and his court officials (*hu ve-avadav*) act in joint obduracy.

dominicalIntent: So the heart of Pharaoh was hardened, and he would not let the people of Israel go, just as the Lord had spoken through Moses. Conclusion of Chapter 9: Pharaoh's heart hardened as foretold by Yahweh.
cccReferences: CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Exod 4:21; Exod 7:3.
historicalContext: Setting the stage for the final two plagues before the Passover.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyechazaq lev Par'oh ve-lo shillach eth-bney Yisra'el ka-asher dibber YHVH be-yad-Moshe*.
historicalTrivia: Exodus 9 closes with Pharaoh's heart locked in obduracy, setting up Exodus 10!

dominicalIntent: Then the Lord said to Moses: 'Go in to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and the heart of his servants, that I may show these signs of mine among them...' GOD HARDENING PHARAOH'S HEART TO SHOW HIS SIGNS! Yahweh explains: He has allowed Pharaoh's heart to become heavy (*hikhbaddeti*) to display His signs (*othoth*) among them.
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Divine signs demonstrating Yahweh's glory); CCC 2575; Rom 9:17-18.
historicalContext: Preparation for the 8th Plague (Locusts).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe bo el-Par'oh ki-anokhi hikhbaddeti eth-libbo ve-eth-lev avadav le-ma'an shithi othothai elleh be-qirbo*: *hikhbaddeti* (I have made heavy/hardened).
historicalTrivia: The verb *hikhbad* means making the heart heavy like lead.

dominicalIntent: '...and that you may tell in the hearing of your son and of your grandson how I have dealt harshly with the Egyptians and what signs I have done among them, that you may know that I am the Lord.' PASSED DOWN TO CHILDREN AND GRANDCHILDREN! God reveals a primary purpose of the Exodus: **'THAT YOU MAY TELL IN THE HEARING OF YOUR SON AND GRANDSON WHAT SIGNS I HAVE DONE, THAT YOU MAY KNOW THAT I AM YAHWEH!'** Grounding the Passover tradition (*Haggadah*).
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Passing down the saving history of the Exodus to future generations); CCC 2575; Deut 6:6-7; Ps 78:3-6.
historicalContext: Establishing the oral catechetical obligation to teach children the mighty deeds of Yahweh.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-le-ma'an tssapper be-ozney vinkha u-ven-binkha eth asher hith'allalti be-Mitzrayim ve-eth-othothai asher-samti vahem vi-yda'them ki-ani YHVH*: *hith'allalti* ('how I made sport of / dealt severely with').
historicalTrivia: This verse is the foundational commandment for the Passover Seder *Haggadah* ('Telling the Story' to sons and grandsons)!

dominicalIntent: So Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh and said to him: 'Thus says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews, "How long will you refuse to humble yourself before me? Let my people go, that they may serve me."' 'HOW LONG WILL YOU REFUSE TO HUMBLE YOURSELF?!' Moses and Aaron issue a direct rebuke: **'HOW LONG WILL YOU REFUSE TO HUMBLE YOURSELF (*le-anoth*) BEFORE ME?!'**
cccReferences: CCC 2086 (The sin of pride refusing to humble oneself before God); CCC 2575; Jas 4:10.
historicalContext: Rebuking royal pharaonic pride.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyavo Moshe ve-Aaron el-Par'oh vayyo'mru elav koh-amar YHVH Elohey ha-Ivriyyim ad-mathai me'antha le-anoth mi-ppanai shallach eth-ammi ve-ya'avduni*: *le-anoth* (to humble yourself / bow down).
historicalTrivia: True repentance requires humbling oneself (*le-anoth*) before God.

dominicalIntent: 'Else, if you refuse to let my people go, behold, tomorrow I will bring locusts into your country...' ANNOUNCEMENT OF THE 8TH PLAGUE: SWARMS OF LOCUSTS (*ARBEH*)! Moses warns: if Pharaoh refuses, tomorrow God will bring catastrophic **locust swarms (*arbeh*)**. Targets **Senehem** (Egyptian locust-god) and **Osiris** (god of agriculture)!
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Dismantling Osiris and Senehem); CCC 2575; Ps 78:46; Rev 9:3.
historicalContext: The 8th Plague targeted **Senehem** (locust deity) and **Osiris** (crop protector).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ki im-ma'en attha le-shallach eth-ammi hineni mevi machar arbeh bi-gvulakha*: *arbeh* (swarming desert locust, *Schistocerca gregaria*).
historicalTrivia: Desert locust swarms (*arbeh*) can contain up to 80 million locusts per square kilometer, eating their weight in food every day!

dominicalIntent: 'and they shall cover the face of the land, so that no one can see the land. And they shall eat what is left to you after the hail, and they shall eat every tree of yours that grows in the field...' LOCUSTS DEVOURING ALL SURVIVING VEGETATION! The locusts will cover the eye of the earth (*eyan ha-aretz*) and devour every remaining plant and tree left by the hail.
cccReferences: CCC 2575; Joel 1:4.
historicalContext: Complete agricultural denudation.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-khissah eth-eyan ha-aretz ve-lo yukhal lir'oth eth-ha-aretz ve-akhal eth-yether ha-ppelaytah ha-nnish'ereth lakhem min-ha-barad ve-akhal eth-kol-ha-etz ha-tzome'ach lakhem min-ha-ssadeh*: *eyan ha-aretz* ('the eye/surface of the earth').
crossReferences: Joel 1:4 ('What the cutting locust left, the swarming locust has eaten'); Psalm 105:35.
historicalTrivia: The phrase *eyan ha-aretz* ('eye of the earth') means the visible ground surface.

dominicalIntent: '...and they shall fill your houses and the houses of all your servants and of all the Egyptians, as neither your fathers nor your grandfathers have seen, from the day they came on the earth to this day.' Then he turned and went out from Pharaoh. Unprecedented locust invasion filling all homes. Moses turns and exits.
historicalContext: Locusts penetrating indoor living quarters.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-mal'u vatteykha u-vattey khol-avadeykha u-vattey khol-Mitzrayim asher lo-ra'u avotheykha va-avoth avotheykha mi-yom heyotham al-ha-adamah ad ha-yom ha-zeh vayyiphen vayyetze me-eth Par'oh*.
historicalTrivia: Joel 2:9 describes locusts: 'They leap upon the city, they run upon the walls, they climb up into the houses, they enter through the windows like a thief'.

dominicalIntent: Then Pharaoh's servants said to him: 'How long shall this man be a snare to us? Let the men go, that they may serve the Lord their God.
