Do you not yet understand that Egypt is ruined?' PHARAOH'S COURTIERS REBEL: 'DO YOU NOT YET UNDERSTAND THAT EGYPT IS RUINED?!' For the first time, Pharaoh's own royal courtiers (*avdey Par'oh*) revolt against Pharaoh's stubbornness: **'HOW LONG SHALL THIS MAN BE A SNARE (*le-mowqesh*) TO US?! DO YOU NOT YET UNDERSTAND THAT EGYPT IS RUINED (*ha-terem teda ki avdhah Mitzrayim*)?!'**
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Total economic ruin of Egypt causing internal palace rebellion).
historicalContext: Palace officials panicking over the total destruction of Egypt's food supply.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mru avdey Par'oh elav ad-mathai yihyeh zeh lanu le-mowqesh shallach eth-ha-anashim ve-ya'avdu eth-YHVH Eloheyhem ha-terem teda ki avdhah Mitzrayim*: *le-mowqesh* ('for a snare/trap'). *avdhah* ('is ruined / destroyed / lost').
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh's advisors realize what Pharaoh refuses to see: Egypt is economically ruined (*avdhah Mitzrayim*)!

dominicalIntent: So Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh. And he said to them: 'Go, serve the Lord your God. But which ones are to go?' Pharaoh recalls Moses and Aaron, offering a conditional negotiation.
historicalContext: Royal recall under court pressure.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyushed eth-Moshe ve-eth-Aaron el-Par'oh vayyo'mer alehem lekhu ivdu eth-YHVH Eloheykhem mi u-mi ha-holkhim*: *mi u-mi* ('who and who? / exactly which ones?').
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh attempts to negotiate a partial departure.

dominicalIntent: Moses said: 'We will go with our young and our old. We will go with our sons and our daughters, with our flocks and our herds, for we must hold a feast to the Lord' (*...be-n'areynu u-vi-zqeneynu nelakh... ki chag-YHVH lanu*). MOSES DEMANDS TOTAL EXODUS FOR ALL GENERATIONS AND ALL POSSESSIONS! Moses refuses any partial departure: **'WE WILL GO WITH OUR YOUNG AND OUR OLD, WITH OUR SONS AND DAUGHTERS, WITH OUR FLOCKS AND HERDS, FOR WE MUST HOLD A FEAST TO YAHWEH!'** (*chag-YHVH lanu*). ALL GENERATIONS MUST WORSHIP TOGETHER!
cccReferences: CCC 2060 (Total family dedication in divine worship); CCC 2575; Josh 24:15 ('As for me and my house, we will serve the Lord').
historicalContext: Demanding that every man, woman, child, and animal depart for the feast (*Chag*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Moshe be-n'areynu u-vi-zqeneynu nelakh bi-vneynu u-vi-vnothaynu be-tzonenu u-vi-vqarernu nelakh ki chag-YHVH lanu*: *chag-YHVH* ('a feast/pilgrimage of Yahweh').
crossReferences: Joshua 24:15; Acts 2:39 ('the promise is for you and for your children'); Exodus 12:37.
historicalTrivia: Moses insists that children (*bneynu u-vi-vnothaynu*) are essential members of the worshipping covenant assembly.

dominicalIntent: But he said to them: 'The Lord be with you, if ever I let you go with your little ones! Look, you have some evil purpose in mind.' PHARAOH'S MOCKERY! Pharaoh mocks them sarcastically: 'May Yahweh be with you if I ever let your children go! See, evil is before your face!'
historicalContext: Cynical royal mockery rejecting the departure of women and children.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer alehem yehi khen YHVH immakhem ka-asher ashalleach ethkhem ve-eth-tappkhem re'u ki ra'ah neged pneykhem*: *ra'ah* (evil/disaster).
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh accuses Moses of using a religious feast as a cover for political escape.

dominicalIntent: 'No! Go the men among you and serve the Lord, for that is what you are asking.' And they were driven out from Pharaoh's presence (*...vayghoresh otham mi-ppney Phar'oh*). PHARAOH'S 3RD COMPROMISE OFFER: 'ONLY THE MEN MAY GO!' Pharaoh offers his 3rd compromise: **'ONLY THE MEN MAY GO!'** (*ha-ggvarim*). He then **drives Moses and Aaron out of his presence (*vayghoresh otham*)**! Moses rejects leaving the children behind.
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Rejection of Satan's attempt to separate children from worship).
historicalContext: Pharaoh attempting to hold women and children hostage to guarantee the men's return.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Lo khen lekhu-na ha-ggvarim ve-ivdu eth-YHVH ki othah athem mvaqshim vayghoresh otham mi-ppney Phar'oh*: *vayghoresh* (and they were driven/expelled out, root *garash*).
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh drives them out (*vayghoresh*); soon Pharaoh himself will be driven out by the plagues!

dominicalIntent: Then the Lord said to Moses: 'Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts, that they may come up over the land of Egypt and devour every plant in the land, all that the hail has left.' Command for the 8th Plague.
historicalContext: Executing the locust invasion.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe nteh yadkha al-eretz Mitzrayim ba-arbeh ve-ya'al al-eretz Mitzrayim ve-yo'khal eth-kol-essev ha-aretz eth kol-asher hish'ir ha-barad*.
historicalTrivia: Moses stretches his hand over all Egypt.

dominicalIntent: So Moses stretched out his staff over the land of Egypt, and the Lord brought an east wind upon the land all that day and all that night. When it was morning, the east wind had brought the locusts (*...v-YHVH nihag ruach qadim ba-aretz...*). THE EAST WIND (*RUACH QADIM*) BRINGS THE LOCUSTS! Moses stretches his staff; Yahweh drives a powerful **East Wind (*ruach qadim*)** across Egypt all day and night. By morning, the East Wind brings billions of locusts!
historicalContext: Supernatural East Wind (*ruach qadim*) blowing across Sinai/Arabia bringing locust swarms.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyet Moshe eth-matthu al-eretz Mitzrayim v-YHVH nihag ruach qadim ba-aretz kol-ha-yom ha-hu ve-khol-ha-laylah ha-boqer hayah u-ruach ha-qqadim nassah eth-ha-arbeh*: *ruach qadim* ('east wind').
crossReferences: Exodus 14:21 (East Wind parting the Red Sea!); Psalm 78:46; Psalm 105:34; Ezekiel 27:26.
historicalTrivia: The East Wind (*ruach qadim*) is God's instrument of judgment in Exodus: here bringing locusts, later parting the Red Sea (Exod 14:21)!

dominicalIntent: The locusts came up over all the land of Egypt and settled on the whole country of Egypt, such a dense swarm of locusts as had never been before, nor ever shall be again (*...be-khovad me'od le-phanav lo-hayah khen arbeh khamohu...*). UNPRECEDENTED DENSE SWARM OF LOCUSTS! The locust swarm covers all Egypt with catastrophic density (*be-khovad me'od*). Never was there such a swarm before or after!
historicalContext: Apocalyptic swarm blocking out the sun.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vaya'al ha-arbeh al kol-eretz Mitzrayim vayyanach be-khol gvul Mitzrayim kaved me'od le-phanav lo-hayah khen arbeh khamohu ve-acharav lo yihyeh-khen*: *kaved me'od* ('exceedingly heavy/dense').
crossReferences: Joel 2:2 ('a great and powerful people; their like has never been from of old, nor will be again after them'); Revelation 9:3-10.
historicalTrivia: Joel 2:2 quotes Exodus 10:14 to describe the apocalyptic Day of the Lord!

dominicalIntent: They covered the face of the whole land, so that the land was darkened, and they ate all the plants in the land and all the fruit of the trees that the hail had left. Not a green thing remained, neither tree nor plant of the field, through all the land of Egypt (*...lo-nothar kol-yereq ba-etz u-ve-essev ha-ssadeh...*). TOTAL STRIPPING OF ALL GREENERY: NOT A GREEN THING REMAINED! The locusts darken the sky (*vat-thekhshakh ha-aretz*) and devour every leaf: **'NOT A GREEN THING REMAINED (*lo-nothar kol-yereq*), NEITHER TREE NOR PLANT, THROUGH ALL THE LAND OF EGYPT!'** Total ecological death.
historicalContext: Complete denudation of all crops, trees, and gardens across Egypt.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vaykhass eth-eyan kol-ha-aretz vat-thekhshakh ha-aretz vayyo'khal eth-kol-essev ha-aretz ve-eth kol-peri ha-etz asher hish'ir ha-barad ve-lo-nothar kol-yereq ba-etz u-ve-essev ha-ssadeh be-khol-eretz Mitzrayim*: *lo-nothar kol-yereq* ('not any green thing was left').
crossReferences: Psalm 105:35 ('and ate up all the vegetation in their land and ate up the fruit of their ground'); Revelation 9:4.
historicalTrivia: In a few hours, millions of acres of fertile Nile greenery were reduced to bare dirt and stripped branches.

dominicalIntent: Then Pharaoh hastily called Moses and Aaron and said: 'I have sinned against the Lord your God, and against you' (*Vaymaher Par'oh li-qra le-Moshe u-le-Aaron vayyo'mer chatathi le-YHVH Eloheykhem ve-lakhem*). PHARAOH'S HASTY CONFESSION OF SIN! Terrified, Pharaoh hastily summons Moses and Aaron: **'I HAVE SINNED AGAINST YAHWEH YOUR GOD, AND AGAINST YOU!'** (*chatathi le-YHVH... ve-lakhem*).
cccReferences: CCC 2575; Exod 9:27; Matt 27:4.
historicalContext: Hasty royal panic under total famine threat.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vaymaher Par'oh li-qra le-Moshe u-le-Aaron vayyo'mer chatathi le-YHVH Eloheykhem ve-lakhem*: *Vaymaher* (and he hurried/hastened). *chatathi* ('I have sinned').
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh confesses 'against Yahweh... and against you', echoing Judas Iscariot's confession in Matthew 27:4.

dominicalIntent: 'Now therefore, forgive my sin, please, only this once, and plead with the Lord your God only to remove this death from me' (*...ve-h'athiru le-YHVH Eloheykhem ve-yasser me-alai raq eth-ha-mmaveth ha-zeh*). 'REMOVE THIS DEATH FROM ME!' Pharaoh begs: **'Forgive my sin, I pray, only this once, AND PLEAD WITH YAHWEH TO REMOVE THIS DEATH (*ha-mmaveth*) FROM ME!'** He titles the locust plague 'this death' (*ha-mmaveth*).
historicalContext: Begging for intercession to remove starvation death (*ha-mmaveth*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-attah ssa na chattathi aq ha-ppa'am ve-h'athiru le-YHVH Eloheykhem ve-yasser me-alai raq eth-ha-mmaveth ha-zeh*: *eth-ha-mmaveth ha-zeh* ('this death').
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh calls the locust plague 'death' (*mmaveth*) because total crop destruction meant nationwide mass starvation.

dominicalIntent: So he went out from Pharaoh and prayed to the Lord. Moses intercedes again.
historicalContext: Patriarchal intercession.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyetze me-eth Par'oh vayye'thar el-YHVH*.
historicalTrivia: Moses repeatedly prays for his persecutor.

dominicalIntent: And the Lord turned the wind into a very strong west wind, which lifted the locusts and drove them into the Red Sea. Not a single locust was left in all the country of Egypt (*...ruach yam chazaq me'od... vayyithqa'ehu Yammah-Suph lo nish'ar arbeh echad*). THE WEST WIND BLOWS THE LOCUSTS INTO THE RED SEA (*YAM SUPH*)! Yahweh turns the wind into a powerful **West Wind / Sea Wind (*ruach yam*)**, carrying all the locusts into the **RED SEA (*YAM SUPH*)**! **NOT A SINGLE LOCUST WAS LEFT (*lo nish'ar arbeh echad*)**! FIRST BIBLICAL MENTION OF THE RED SEA (**YAM SUPH**)!
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (The miraculous removal of locusts into the Red Sea); CCC 2575; Exod 13:18; Exod 14:2.
historicalContext: Strong West Wind driving the locusts eastward into the Red Sea (*Yam Suph* = Sea of Reeds / Red Sea).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyaphokh YHVH ruach-yam chazaq me'od vayyissa eth-ha-arbeh vayyithqa'ehu Yammah-Suph lo nish'ar arbeh echad be-khol gvul Mitzrayim*: *ruach-yam* ('sea/west wind'). *Yammah-Suph* ('into the Sea of Reeds / Red Sea'). *lo nish'ar... echad* ('not one remained').
historicalTrivia: This is the very first mention of the **Red Sea (*Yam Suph*)** in Sacred Scripture! The same sea that swallowed the locusts will later swallow Pharaoh's army (Exod 14:28)!

dominicalIntent: But the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not let the people of Israel go (*Vayyechazzeq YHVH eth-lev Par'oh...*). Yahweh hardens Pharaoh's heart; he breaks his pledge.
historicalContext: Judicial hardening following the 8th Plague.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyechazzeq YHVH eth-lev Par'oh ve-lo shillach eth-bney Yisra'el*.
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh's heart is locked in obduracy setting up the 9th Plague of Darkness.

dominicalIntent: Then the Lord said to Moses: 'Stretch out your hand toward heaven, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, a darkness to be felt' (*...ve-vihi choshekh al-eretz Mitzrayim ve-yamesh choshekh*). THE 9TH PLAGUE (UNANNOUNCED): SUPERNATURAL DARKNESS THAT CAN BE FELT (*YAMESH CHOSHEKH*)! Without warning, Yahweh commands Moses to stretch his hand toward heaven to bring **DARKNESS THAT CAN BE FELT (*ve-yamesh choshekh*)** over Egypt! Targets **Re / Amun-Re** (the supreme sun-god of Egypt), **Horus**, and **Aton**!
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Dismantling Re/Amun-Re, the supreme sun-god of Egypt); CCC 2575; Ps 105:28; Rev 16:10.
historicalContext: The 9th Plague targeted **Re / Amun-Re** (the supreme Egyptian Sun God). Pharaoh was regarded as the physical son of Re; blotting out the sun destroyed the supreme god of Egypt!
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe nteh yadkha al-ha-ssamayim ve-vihi choshekh al-eretz Mitzrayim ve-yamesh choshekh*: *ve-yamesh choshekh* ('and darkness may be felt / grope in darkness', root *mashash*).
crossReferences: Psalm 105:28 ('He sent darkness, and made the land dark'); Revelation 16:10; Matthew 27:45 (Darkness at the Crucifixion!).
historicalTrivia: The 3 hours of darkness at Christ's Crucifixion (Matt 27:45) is the New Testament fulfillment of the 3 days of darkness in Egypt!

dominicalIntent: So Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and there was pitch darkness in all the land of Egypt three days (*...vayyehi choshekh-aphelah be-khol-eretz Mitzrayim shelosheth yamim*). THREE DAYS OF PITCH DARKNESS (*CHOSHEKH-APHELAH*)! Moses stretches his hand; **PITCH DARKNESS (*choshekh-aphelah*)** covers all Egypt for **THREE DAYS (*shelosheth yamim*)**! PREFIGURING THE THREE HOURS OF DARKNESS AT CHRIST'S CRUCIFIXION AND THE THREE DAYS IN THE TOMB!
cccReferences: CCC 600 (Darkness at the Crucifixion prefigured by Egypt's darkness); CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Matt 27:45; Mark 15:33; Luke 23:44-45.
historicalContext: Supernatural thick gloom (*aphelah*) shutting down all light, sun, and fire across Egypt for 3 days.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyet Moshe eth-yado al-ha-ssamayim vayyehi choshekh-aphelah be-khol-eretz Mitzrayim shelosheth yamim*: *choshekh-aphelah* ('darkness of thick gloom/blackness'). *shelosheth yamim* ('three days').
historicalTrivia: Wisdom 17:2-21 gives a breathtaking description of this plague: 'bound by a chain of darkness... terrified by phantoms... shut up in a prison without iron bars'!

dominicalIntent: They did not see one another, nor did anyone rise from his place for three days, but all the people of Israel had light in their dwellings (*...u-le-khol-bney Yisra'el hayah or be-moshvotham*). ISRAEL HAS LIGHT IN THEIR DWELLINGS! Total paralysis in Egypt: no one could see or rise from his place for 3 days. **'BUT ALL THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL HAD LIGHT IN THEIR DWELLINGS!'** (*u-le-khol-bney Yisra'el hayah or*). CHRISTIANS ARE CHILDREN OF LIGHT DWELLING IN A WORLD OF DARKNESS (EPH 5:8; 1 PET 2:9)!
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Believers as Children of Light shielded from worldly darkness); CCC 2575; Eph 5:8; 1 Pet 2:9; John 8:12.
historicalContext: Supernatural illumination over Goshen while all Egypt lay in paralyzing blackness.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Lo-ra'u ish eth-achiv ve-lo-qamu ish mi-thachtav shelosheth yamim u-le-khol-bney Yisra'el hayah or be-moshvotham*: *hayah or* ('there was light').
crossReferences: Ephesians 5:8 ('For once you were darkness, but now you are light in the Lord'); 1 Peter 2:9; John 8:12 ('I am the light of the world'); Wisdom 18:1.
historicalTrivia: Wisdom 18:1 describes Goshen during the 9th Plague: 'But for your holy ones there was a very great light'!

dominicalIntent: Then Pharaoh called Moses and said: 'Go, serve the Lord; your little ones also may go with you; only let your flocks and your herds be stayed behind.' PHARAOH'S 4TH COMPROMISE OFFER: 'LEAVE YOUR FLOCKS BEHIND!' Paralyzed by darkness, Pharaoh summons Moses, offering his 4th and final compromise: 'Go, take your children; **only let your flocks and herds be left behind (*raq tzonkhem u-vqararkhem yutztzav*)**!' Pharaoh tries to strip Israel of their sacrificial animals.
cccReferences: CCC 2060 (Rejection of compromises that withhold sacrificial offerings from God); CCC 2575.
historicalContext: Pharaoh trying to retain Israel's wealth (livestock) to force their return.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vyiqra Par'oh el-Moshe vayyo'mer lekhu ivdu eth-YHVH raq tzonkhem u-vqararkhem yutztzav gam-tappkhem yelekh immakhem*: *yutztzav* ('shall be detained/stayed behind').
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh's 4th compromise: 'Serve God, but leave your wealth/property in Egypt!' Moses refuses.

dominicalIntent: But Moses said: 'You must also let us have sacrifices and burnt offerings, that we may sacrifice to the Lord our God.' Moses demands full sacrificial freedom: Pharaoh must provide animals for sacrifices (*zvachim*) and burnt offerings (*oloth*).
cccReferences: CCC 2099 (Burnt offerings and sacrifices belonging to God alone); CCC 2575.
historicalContext: Demanding animals for *zvachim* (peace offerings) and *oloth* (total burnt offerings).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Moshe gam-attha thitten be-yadenu zvachim ve-oloth ve-assinu le-YHVH Eloheynu*: *zvachim ve-oloth* ('sacrifices and whole-burnt offerings').
historicalTrivia: Moses insists Pharaoh himself must contribute to Yahweh's sacrifices!

dominicalIntent: 'Our livestock also must go with us; not a hoof shall be left behind, for we must take of them to serve the Lord our God, and we do not know with what we must serve the Lord until we arrive there' (*...lo-thishsha'er parssah...*). 'NOT A HOOF SHALL BE LEFT BEHIND!' SUPREME FAITHFULNESS! Moses utters the famous declaration of total consecration: **'OUR LIVESTOCK ALSO MUST GO WITH US; NOT A HOOF SHALL BE LEFT BEHIND! (*lo-thishsha'er parssah*)'** Total separation from Egypt!
cccReferences: CCC 2060 (Total, unreserved consecration of all possessions to divine service); CCC 2575; Rom 12:1.
historicalContext: Refusing to leave a single hoof (*parssah*) of cattle in Pharaoh's territory.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-gham-miqnenu yelekh immanu lo-thishsha'er parssah ki mimmennu niqqach la-avod eth-YHVH Eloheynu va-anachnu lo-neda mah-n'avod eth-YHVH ad-bo'enu shammah*: *parssah* (hoof/cloven foot).
crossReferences: Romans 12:1 ('present your bodies as a living sacrifice'); Exodus 12:32.
historicalTrivia: The idiom 'not a hoof left behind' (*lo-thishsha'er parssah*) became a proverbial expression for total, unreserved commitment.

dominicalIntent: But the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he would not let them go (*Vayyechazzeq YHVH eth-lev Par'oh...*). Yahweh hardens Pharaoh's heart; he rejects Moses' terms.
historicalContext: Final hardening before the 10th Plague.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyechazzeq YHVH eth-lev Par'oh ve-lo avah le-shallcham*: *lo avah* ('was not willing / refused').
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh reaches the point of total spiritual blindness.

dominicalIntent: Then Pharaoh said to him: 'Get away from me; take care never to see my face again, for on the day you see my face you shall die' (*...hi-ssaver lekha al-thosseph re'oth phanai ki be-yom re'othkha phanai thamuth*). PHARAOH'S DEATH THREAT: 'SEE MY FACE NO MORE, FOR ON THAT DAY YOU SHALL DIE!' Enraged Pharaoh threatens Moses with immediate execution: **'GET AWAY FROM ME! TAKE CARE NEVER TO SEE MY FACE AGAIN, FOR ON THE DAY YOU SEE MY FACE YOU SHALL DIE!'**
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The tyrant issuing his final death threat against God's prophet).
historicalContext: Pharaoh breaking diplomatic relations under penalty of death.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer-lo Phar'oh lekh me-alai hi-ssaver lekha al-thosseph re'oth phanai ki be-yom re'othkha phanai thamuth*: *hi-ssaver lekha* ('take heed to yourself / beware!').
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh threatens Moses with death (*thamuth*); within 24 hours, Pharaoh's own firstborn son will die instead!

dominicalIntent: Moses said: 'As you say! I will never see your face again' (*...Ken dibbartaha lo-ossiph od re'oth phaneykha*). MOSES' PROPHETIC FAREWELL: 'AS YOU SAY! I WILL NEVER SEE YOUR FACE AGAIN!' Moses accepts the verdict: **'AS YOU SAY! I WILL NEVER SEE YOUR FACE AGAIN!'** Moses leaves Pharaoh's presence forever, preparing for the 10th Plague and the Passover!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The final prophetic parting before the Passover and the 10th Plague); Heb 11:27 ('By faith he left Egypt, not being afraid of the anger of the king').
historicalContext: Final break between Moses and Pharaoh before the midnight of Passover.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Moshe ken dibbartaha lo-ossiph od re'oth phaneykha*: *lo-ossiph od* ('I will not add again').
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 11:27 praises Moses: 'By faith he left Egypt, not being afraid of the anger of the king; for he endured as seeing him who is invisible'!

dominicalIntent: The Lord said to Moses: 'Yet one plague more I will bring upon Pharaoh and upon Egypt. Afterward he will let you go from here; when he lets you go, he will drive you away completely' (*...Odh negh'a echad avi al-Par'oh... kashallecho kalah garesh yegharesh ethkhem mi-zzeh*). ANNOUNCEMENT OF THE FINAL 10TH PLAGUE! Yahweh announces to Moses: **'YET ONE PLAGUE MORE I WILL BRING UPON PHARAOH AND EGYPT! AFTERWARD HE WILL DRIVE YOU AWAY COMPLETELY!'** (*kalah garesh yegharesh*). The final climax of the Exodus plagues.
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (The final plague of liberation); CCC 2575; Exod 3:19-20; Exod 12:31.
historicalContext: The prelude to the 10th Plague (Death of the Firstborn) and the Passover Night.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe odh negh'a echad avi al-Par'oh ve-al-Mitzrayim achar ken yeshallach ethkhem mi-zzeh kashallecho kalah garesh yegharesh ethkhem mi-zzeh*: *negh打击/plague/stroke). *kalah garesh yegharesh* (infinitive absolute: 'driving he will completely drive you out!').
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh who tried to hold Israel will now force them out completely (*kalah garesh*)!

dominicalIntent: 'Speak now in the hearing of the people, that they ask, every man of his neighbor and every woman of her neighbor, for silver and gold jewelry.' DIRECTIVE TO REQUEST GOLD AND SILVER! God instructs the Hebrews to ask their Egyptian neighbors for silver (*khesseph*) and gold (*zahav*) articles.
cccReferences: CCC 2413 (Just back-pay for centuries of slave labor); CCC 2575; Gen 15:14; Exod 3:21-22.
historicalContext: Collection of just retroactive wages from Egyptian neighbors prior to departure.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Dabber-na be-ozney ha-am ve-yish'lu ish me-eth re'ehu ve-ishah me-eth re'uthah kley-khesseph u-khley zahav*: *yish'lu* (let them ask/request).
historicalTrivia: These requested gold and silver items were later consecrated to build the Tabernacle (Exod 25:2-8).

dominicalIntent: And the Lord gave the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians. Moreover, the man Moses was very great in the land of Egypt, in the sight of Pharaoh's servants and in the sight of the people (*...Ve-gham ha-ish Moshe gadol me'od be-eretz Mitzrayim...*). MOSES VERY GREAT IN THE LAND OF EGYPT! Yahweh grants Israel favor in Egyptian eyes. Scripture notes: **'MOREOVER, THE MAN MOSES WAS VERY GREAT (*gadol me'od*) IN THE LAND OF EGYPT, IN THE SIGHT OF PHARAOH'S SERVANTS AND IN THE SIGHT OF THE PEOPLE!'** The humble shepherd elevated to supreme international stature.
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The exaltation of God's humble prophet in the sight of nations); Exod 3:21; Acts 7:22.
historicalContext: Reverence accorded to Moses by Egyptian palace officials and common citizens.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyitten YHVH eth-chen ha-am be-eyney Mitzrayim ve-gham ha-ish Moshe gadol me'od be-eretz Mitzrayim be-eyney avdey-Phar'oh u-ve-eyney ha-am*: *gadol me'od* ('exceedingly great').
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh's own court servants respected Moses far more than they respected their own stubborn king!

dominicalIntent: So Moses said: 'Thus says the Lord, "About midnight I will go out in the midst of Egypt..."' (*...Koh amar YHVH ka-chatzoth ha-llaylah anokhi yotze be-thokh Mitzrayim*). ANNOUNCEMENT OF MIDNIGHT JUDGMENT: 'ABOUT MIDNIGHT I WILL GO OUT!' Moses delivers his final warning to Pharaoh: **'THUS SAYS YAHWEH: ABOUT MIDNIGHT (*ka-chatzoth ha-llaylah*) I WILL GO OUT INTO THE MIDST OF EGYPT!'** THE MIDNIGHT HOUR OF PASSOVER REDEMPTION!
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (The midnight stroke of divine liberation); CCC 2575; Exod 12:29; Wis 18:14-15; Matt 25:6.
historicalContext: The prophetic announcement of the midnight Passover judgment (*ka-chatzoth ha-llaylah*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Moshe koh amar YHVH ka-chatzoth ha-llaylah anokhi yotze be-thokh Mitzrayim*: *ka-chatzoth ha-llaylah* ('about the middle of the night / midnight').
crossReferences: Exodus 12:29; Wisdom 18:14-15 ('For while gentle silence enveloped all things, and night in its swift course was half gone, your all-powerful word leaped from heaven'); Matthew 25:6 ('At midnight there was a cry').
historicalTrivia: Wisdom 18:14-15 describes the midnight stroke (*ka-chatzoth*) as the **All-Powerful Word of God (*Logos*)** leaping down from heaven like a stern warrior carrying a sharp sword!

dominicalIntent: '...and every firstborn in the land of Egypt shall die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits on his throne, even to the firstborn of the slave girl who is behind the handmill, and all the firstborn of the cattle.' THE DEATH OF THE FIRSTBORN ANNOUNCED! Moses prophesies: **'EVERY FIRSTBORN IN THE LAND OF EGYPT SHALL DIE'** (*v-meth kol-bekhor be-eretz Mitzrayim*), from Pharaoh's heir down to the captive slave girl and cattle! TALIONIC JUSTICE: Pharaoh tried to drown God's firstborn son Israel (Exod 1:22; 4:22-23); now Egypt loses its firstborn!
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Divine talionic justice against state infanticide); CCC 2575; Exod 4:22-23; Exod 12:29; Ps 78:51.
historicalContext: The 10th Plague targeted **Pharaoh's heir** (considered the incarnate son of Re) and **Min/Osiris** (gods of fertility and royal succession).
translationNuances: Hebrew *V-meth kol-bekhor be-eretz Mitzrayim mi-bekhor Phar'oh ha-yoshev al-kisso ad bekhor ha-shiphchah asher achar ha-rrechayim ve-khol bekhor bhemah*: *v-meth kol-bekhor* ('and every firstborn shall die'). *ha-rrechayim* (the handmill).
historicalTrivia: In ancient Egypt, the firstborn son (*bekhor*) was sacred, possessing total inheritance and priestly rights to conduct mortuary rituals for the father.

dominicalIntent: 'There shall be a great cry throughout all the land of Egypt, such as there has never been, nor ever will be again' (*Ve-haythah tza'aqah ghedolah be-khol-eretz Mitzrayim...*). UNPRECEDENTED GREAT CRY IN EGYPT! Moses prophesies a **great cry of lamentation (*tza'aqah ghedolah*)** across Egypt, matching the cry of Hebrew mothers whose infants were thrown into the Nile!
historicalContext: National lamentation across all Egyptian homes.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-haythah tza'aqah ghedolah be-khol-eretz Mitzrayim asher kamohu lo haythah ve-khamohu lo thossiph*: *tza'aqah ghedolah* ('a great cry/outcry').
crossReferences: Exodus 12:30 ('and there was a great cry in Egypt'); Genesis 27:34; Revelation 18:19.
historicalTrivia: The word *tza'aqah* ('cry') is the exact word used for Israel's cry under slavery in Exodus 2:23 and 3:7!

dominicalIntent: 'But not a dog shall growl against any of the people of Israel, either man or beast, that you may know that the Lord makes a distinction between Egypt and Israel' (*...le-kol bney Yisra'el lo yecheratz-kelev lashono... le-ma'an teda'un asher yaphleh YHVH...*). NOT A DOG SHALL GROWL AGAINST ISRAEL! SUPREME COVENANT IMMUNITY! Moses decrees: **'BUT AGAINST ANY OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL, NOT A DOG SHALL GROWL HIS TONGUE (*lo yecheratz-kelev lashono*)!'** — so quiet and peaceful will be Goshen's protection! **'THAT YOU MAY KNOW THAT YAHWEH MAKES A MIRACULOUS DISTINCTION (*yaphleh*) BETWEEN EGYPT AND ISRAEL!'**
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (The miraculous distinction protecting the faithful); CCC 2575; Exod 8:22; Exod 9:4; Mal 3:18.
historicalContext: Absolute supernatural peace over Goshen during the midnight judgment.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-le-khol bney Yisra'el lo yecheratz-kelev lashono le-me-adam ve-ad-bhemah le-ma'an teda'un asher yaphleh YHVH beyn Mitzrayim u-veyn Yisra'el*: *lo yecheratz-kelev lashono* ('not a dog shall sharpen/move his tongue'). *yaphleh* ('makes a miraculous distinction').
crossReferences: Joshua 10:21 ('no one moved his tongue against any of the people of Israel'); Exodus 8:22; Malachi 3:18.
historicalTrivia: The idiom 'not a dog shall growl' (*lo yecheratz kelev*) signifies total immunity, safety, and tranquil peace.

dominicalIntent: 'And all these your servants shall come down to me and bow down to me, saying, "Get out, you and all the people who follow you." And after that I will go out.' And he went out from Pharaoh in hot anger (*...Vayyetze me-eth Par'oh bo-chori-aph*). PHARAOH'S COURTIERS BOW BEFORE MOSES! MOSES EXITS IN HOT ANGER! Moses prophesies that Pharaoh's own high officials will come and **bow down before him** (*ve-hishtachavu-li*), begging Israel to leave. Moses then turns and **exits Pharaoh's presence in hot anger (*bo-chori-aph*)**!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Righteous anger of the prophet against unrepentant tyranny); Exod 10:29; Mark 3:5.
historicalContext: Final departure of Moses from Pharaoh's palace.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-yardu khol-avadeykha elleh elai ve-hishtachavu-li le'mor tze attha ve-khol-ha-am asher-be-ragleykha ve-acharey-khen etze vayyetze me-eth Par'oh bo-chori-aph*: *bo-chori-aph* ('in burning heat of anger').
crossReferences: Exodus 10:29; Mark 3:5 (Jesus' holy anger at hardness of heart); Exodus 12:31-33.
historicalTrivia: Moses' 'hot anger' (*chori-aph*) mirrors divine holy wrath against Pharaoh's persistent rejection of truth.

dominicalIntent: Then the Lord said to Moses: 'Pharaoh will not listen to you, that my wonders may be multiplied in the land of Egypt.' Yahweh confirms that Pharaoh's refusal fulfills the plan to multiply wonders.
cccReferences: CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Exod 7:3.
historicalContext: Divine explanation of Pharaoh's obstinacy.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe lo-yishma alehkhem Par'oh le-ma'an revoth mophthai be-eretz Mitzrayim*: *revoth mophthai* ('multiplying my wonders').
historicalTrivia: Every refusal of Pharaoh provided the stage for a greater manifestation of God's power.

dominicalIntent: Moses and Aaron did all these wonders before Pharaoh, and the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not let the people of Israel go out of his land. Summary conclusion of the 9 plagues before the Passover.
cccReferences: CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Exod 4:21; Exod 10:27.
historicalContext: Final summary statement closing the 9-plague cycle.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-Moshe ve-Aaron assu eth-kol-ha-mophthim ha-elleh liphney Phar'oh vayyechazzeq YHVH eth-lev Par'oh ve-lo-shillach eth-bney-Yisra'el me-artzo*.
historicalTrivia: Exodus 11:10 closes the first major division of Exodus, leading directly into the Paschal Ordinance of Exodus 12!

dominicalIntent: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt... Yahweh addresses Moses and Aaron in Egypt to institute the perpetual Paschal liturgy.
cccReferences: CCC 1334 (The institution of the Passover liturgy prefiguring the Eucharist); CCC 1362-1372; CCC 2575.
historicalContext: Nisan (Abib) 1446 BC: Divine institution of the Passover (*Pesach*) liturgy.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe ve-el-Aaron be-eretz Mitzrayim le'mor*.
historicalTrivia: The Paschal liturgy of Exodus 12 is the foundational liturgical charter of the Old Covenant.

dominicalIntent: 'This month shall be for you the beginning of months. It shall be the first month of the year for you' (*Ha-chodesh ha-zeh lakhem rosh chodashim...*). RE-CALIBRATION OF THE CALENDAR: NISAN BECOMES THE FIRST MONTH! God re-orders time itself around Redemption: **'THIS MONTH SHALL BE FOR YOU THE HEAD OF MONTHS (*rosh chodashim*)!'** The month of Abib/Nisan (spring) becomes Month 1 of Israel's sacred calendar. **NEW CREATION RE-CALIBRATES TIME AROUND REDEMPTION!**
cccReferences: CCC 1168 (The liturgical year and sacred time centered on Christ's Paschal Mystery); CCC 1334; Exod 13:4; Deut 16:1.
historicalContext: Re-setting Israel's civil calendar (Rosh Hashanah in 7th month Tishrei) to make spring month Abib/Nisan Month 1 of the religious calendar.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ha-chodesh ha-zeh lakhem rosh chodashim rishon hu lakhem le-chodshey ha-shanah*: *rosh chodashim* ('head/beginning of months'). *Nisan* (Abib = March/April).
historicalTrivia: Redemption in Exodus 12 re-started time for Israel, just as the Resurrection of Christ re-started human history with BC/AD!

dominicalIntent: 'Tell all the congregation of Israel that on the tenth day of this month every man shall take a lamb according to their fathers' houses, a lamb for a household' (*...be-assor la-chodesh ha-zeh ve-yiqchu lahem ish seh le-veyth-avoth seh la-bayith*). SELECTING THE PASCHAL LAMB ON NISAN 10—PALM SUNDAY FULFILLMENT! On **Nisan 10 (*be-assor la-chodesh*)**, each household selects **a lamb (*seh*)**. **JESUS ENTERED JERUSALEM ON PALM SUNDAY ON THIS EXACT DAY (NISAN 10), OFFERING HIMSELF AS THE TRUE PASCHAL LAMB TO BE INSPECTED FOR 4 DAYS BEFORE CRUCIFIXION!**
cccReferences: CCC 608 (JESUS THE LAMB OF GOD: 'Behold the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world', prefigured by the Passover lamb of Nisan 10); CCC 1334; John 1:29; John 12:1-12; 1 Pet 1:19.
historicalContext: Selecting the lamb on Nisan 10 and tethering it to the bedpost for 4 days of inspection until sacrifice on Nisan 14.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Dabru el-kol-adath Yisra'el le'mor be-assor la-chodesh ha-zeh ve-yiqchu lahem ish seh le-veyth-avoth seh la-bayith*: *seh* (a young lamb or goat). *be-assor* ('on the tenth day').
historicalTrivia: On Nisan 10, as Jewish families tethered their Passover lambs in Jerusalem, Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a donkey (John 12:1-12) as the divine Lamb!

dominicalIntent: 'And if the household is too small for a lamb, then he and his nearest neighbor shall take according to the number of persons; according to what each can eat you shall make your count for the lamb.' Neighbors sharing a single Paschal lamb so no portion of the lamb is wasted. Communion in unity.
cccReferences: CCC 1334 (Community sharing in the Paschal banquet); CCC 1329.
historicalContext: Neighbourhood fellowship groups (*chavuroth*) formed to consume the lamb completely.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-im-yim'at ha-bayith mi-heyoth mi-sseh ve-laqach hu u-shekheno ha-qqarov el-beytho be-mikhssath nephashoth ish le-phi okhlung thakhossu al-ha-ssseh*: *mikhssath* (number/tally).
historicalTrivia: Rabbinic law specified that a Paschal company (*chavurah*) must consist of at least 10 people.

dominicalIntent: 'Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male a year old. You may take it from the sheep or from the goats' (*Seh thamim zakhar ben-shanah yihyeh lakhem...*). A LAMB WITHOUT BLEMISH, MALE A YEAR OLD—PREFIGURING CHRIST THE UNBLEMISHED VICTIM! The requirements: (1) **Without blemish (*seh thamim*)** = Spotless/perfect, (2) **Male (*zakhar*)**, (3) **One year old (*ben-shanah*)**. **CITED IN 1 PETER 1:19 AS THE EXACT TYPE OF JESUS CHRIST: 'REDEEMED WITH THE PRECIOUS BLOOD OF CHRIST, LIKE THAT OF A LAMB WITHOUT BLEMISH OR SPOT!'**
cccReferences: CCC 608 (Christ the unblemished Lamb of God); CCC 1334; 1 Pet 1:19 ('without blemish or spot'); Heb 9:14; Lev 22:19-21.
historicalContext: Rigorous 4-day inspection to ensure zero physical flaw, broken bone, or disease.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Seh thamim zakhar ben-shanah yihyeh lakhem min-ha-khvasim u-min-ha-izzim tiqqachu*: *thamim* (perfect / unblemished / blameless). *zakhar* (male).
historicalTrivia: 1 Peter 1:18-19 explicitly quotes Exodus 12:5: 'You were ransomed... not with perishable things... but with the precious blood of Christ, like that of a lamb without blemish (*amōmou*) or spot (*aspilou*)'!

dominicalIntent: 'and you shall keep it until the fourteenth day of this month, when the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill their lambs at twilight' (*...ve-shachatu otho kol qahal adath-YISRA'EL beyn ha-arbayim*). SLAUGHTER AT TWILIGHT ON NISAN 14—THE EXACT HOUR OF CHRIST'S DEATH ON THE CROSS! The lamb is kept until **Nisan 14**; then **the whole assembly of Israel slaughters it AT TWILIGHT (*beyn ha-arbayim* = 3:00 PM!)**. **JESUS CHRIST WAS CRUCIFIED AND DIED ON THE CROSS ON NISAN 14 AT THE EXACT 9TH HOUR (3:00 PM), THE PRECISE HOUR THE PASCHAL LAMBS WERE SLAUGHTERED IN THE TEMPLE!**
cccReferences: CCC 608 (Christ dying at 3:00 PM on Nisan 14 as the true Paschal Lamb); CCC 1334; Mark 15:34-37; John 19:14; 1 Cor 5:7.
historicalContext: Slaughter at *beyn ha-arbayim* ('between the two evenings' = 3:00 PM to sunset). All families slaughtering in unison.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-hayah lakhem le-mishmereth ad arba'ah assar yom la-chodesh ha-zeh ve-shachatu otho kol qahal adath-YISRA'EL beyn ha-arbayim*: *beyn ha-arbayim* ('between the two evenings' / 3:00 PM afternoon).
crossReferences: Mark 15:34-37; John 19:14; 1 Corinthians 5:7 ('Christ, our Paschal Lamb, has been sacrificed'); Matthew 27:46-50.
historicalTrivia: Josephus (*Jewish War* VI.9.3) records that during Passover in Jerusalem, over 256,000 lambs were slaughtered at the Temple between 3:00 PM and 5:00 PM (*beyn ha-arbayim*)!

dominicalIntent: 'Then they shall take some of the blood and put it on the two doorposts and the lintel of the houses in which they eat it' (*...ve-nathnu al-shteney ha-mmezuzoth ve-al-ha-mashqoph...*). THE BLOOD ON THE DOORPOSTS AND LINTEL—THE SIGN OF THE CROSS! The blood of the slain lamb must be applied using hyssop to: (1) The **two doorposts (*shteney ha-mmezuzoth*)**, (2) The **lintel (*ha-mashqoph*)**. **PATRISTIC EXEGESIS (ST. JOHN CHRYSOSTOM, ST. AUGUSTINE) HIGHLIGHTS THAT THE BLOOD STAINED UPON LINTEL AND POSTS FORMED THE SIGN OF THE CROSS, SIGNIFYING THAT REDEMPTION FLOWS FROM CHRIST'S BLOOD ON THE CROSS!**
cccReferences: CCC 1219 (The Blood of the Lamb on doorposts prefiguring the cleansing Blood of Christ applied in Baptism); CCC 1334; CCC 617; Heb 9:22; Rev 7:14.
historicalContext: Blood applied to the wooden frame of the home entrance.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-laqchu min-ha-ddam ve-nathnu al-shteney ha-mmezuzoth ve-al-ha-mashqoph al ha-bbattim asher-yoklu otho bahem*: *mezuzoth* (doorposts). *mashqoph* (top lintel).
crossReferences: Hebrews 9:22 ('Without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness'); Revelation 7:14; Exodus 12:13; 1 Peter 1:2.
historicalTrivia: Dipping hyssop into the basin and striking lintel and posts formed a vertical and horizontal cross pattern upon the doorway!

dominicalIntent: 'They shall eat the flesh that night, roasted on the fire; with unleavened bread and bitter herbs they shall eat it' (*Ve-aklu eth-ha-basar ba-llaylah ha-hu tzli-esh u-matzoth al-mrorim yo'kluhu*). EATING THE FLESH OF THE LAMB—THE MANDATORY EUCHARISTIC BANQUET! IT WAS NOT ENOUGH TO KILL THE LAMB; **THEY HAD TO EAT THE FLESH (*Ve-aklu eth-ha-basar*)**! (1) **Flesh roasted on fire (*tzli-esh*)**, (2) **Unleavened bread (*matzoth*)**, (3) **Bitter herbs (*mrorim*)**. **JESUS FULFILLS THIS IN JOHN 6:53: 'UNLESS YOU EAT THE FLESH OF THE SON OF MAN AND DRINK HIS BLOOD, YOU HAVE NO LIFE IN YOU!'**
cccReferences: CCC 1334 (The Paschal meal of lamb and unleavened bread fulfilled in the Holy Mass); CCC 1384 ('Take and eat'); John 6:53-56; 1 Cor 11:23-26.
historicalContext: The sacred sacrificial banquet: consuming the roasted lamb whole along with *matzoth* (unleavened bread) and *maror* (bitter herbs like lettuce/horseradish).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-aklu eth-ha-basar ba-llaylah ha-hu tzli-esh u-matzoth al-mrorim yo'kluhu*: *basar* (flesh). *matzoth* (unleavened bread). *mrorim* (bitter herbs).
historicalTrivia: Catholic theology emphasizes: slaying the lamb without eating its flesh brought no protection; receiving Holy Communion (*eating the Flesh of Christ*) is essential for Paschal salvation!

dominicalIntent: 'Do not eat any of it raw or boiled in water, but roasted, its head with its legs and its inner parts.' The lamb must be roasted whole (*tzli-esh*) over fire, keeping all organs intact.
historicalContext: Fire-roasting on a spit preserved the whole lamb structure.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Al-thokhlu mimmennu na u-vashal mevushal ba-mmayim ki im-tzli-esh rosho al-kera'av ve-al-qirbo*.
historicalTrivia: Roasting on a pomegranate-wood spit held the lamb upright in the fire.

dominicalIntent: 'And you shall let none of it remain until the morning; anything that remains until the morning you shall burn' (*Ve-lo thothiru mimmennu ad-boqer... ba-esh tishrophu*). NO REMNANT UNTIL MORNING! The lamb must be completely consumed; any unconsumed flesh must be burned with fire before morning. Sacred sacrificial food must not undergo decay.
cccReferences: CCC 1334 (Reverence for the consecrated sacrificial victim); Lev 7:15; Acts 2:27.
historicalContext: Sacrificial law preventing corruption or profane desecration.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-lo thothiru mimmennu ad-boqer ve-ha-nothar mimmennu ad-boqer ba-esh tishrophu*: *lo thothiru* ('you shall leave nothing over').
crossReferences: Exodus 23:18; Leviticus 7:15; Acts 2:27 ('nor let your Holy One see corruption').
historicalTrivia: The prohibition against leaving remnants prefigures Christ's Body in the tomb, which saw no corruption (Acts 2:27).

dominicalIntent: 'In this manner you shall eat it: with your belt fastened, your sandals on your feet, and your staff in your hand. And you shall eat it in haste. It is the Lord's Passover' (*...ve-akhaltem otho be-chippazon PESACH hu le-YHVH*). EATING IN HASTE WITH BELT GIRT—THIS IS YAHWEH'S PASSOVER (*PESACH*)! The posture of readiness for immediate exodus: (1) **Loins girt (*chagureykhem*)**, (2) **Sandals on feet**, (3) **Staff in hand**, (4) **EAT IT IN HASTE (*be-chippazon*)**! **FIRST APPEARANCE OF THE SACRED WORD PASSOVER (**PESACH** = 'To Leap / Pass Over')!**
cccReferences: CCC 1334 (The Passover *Pesach* as the transition from slavery to freedom); CCC 2575; Luke 12:35 ('Let your loins be girt'); Eph 6:14.
historicalContext: The pilgrim posture of imminent departure.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-khakhab thokhlu otho mothneykhem chagurim na'aleykhem be-ragleykhem u-mmattekhem be-yadhkhem ve-akhaltem otho be-chippazon PESACH hu le-YHVH*: *be-chippazon* ('in hurried haste'). *PESACH* (Passover, root *passach* = to leap/pass over/protect).
historicalTrivia: The Hebrew verb *passach* means both 'to leap/pass over' and 'to hover over in protection' (cf. Isa 31:5)!

dominicalIntent: 'For I will pass through the land of Egypt that night, and I will strike all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and beast; and on all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgments: I am the Lord' (*...u-ve-khol-elohey Mitzrayim e'esseh shphatim Anokhi YHVH*). JUDGMENT ON ALL THE DEMON-GODS OF EGYPT! Yahweh announces: **'ON ALL THE GODS OF EGYPT I WILL EXECUTE JUDGMENTS (*u-ve-khol-elohey Mitzrayim e'esseh shphatim*): I AM YAHWEH!'** The 10th Plague systematically overthrew the entire Egyptian pantheon!
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (THE DEFEAT OF PAGAN DEMON-GODS: The 10 Plagues and Passover as Yahweh's victory over idols); CCC 2575; Num 33:4; 1 Cor 10:20.
historicalContext: Numbers 33:4 confirms: 'Upon their gods also the Lord executed judgments'.

dominicalIntent: 'The blood shall be a sign for you, on the houses where you are. And when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague will befall you to destroy you, when I strike the land of Egypt' (*Ve-hayah ha-ddam lakhem le-oth... u-ra'ithi eth-ha-ddam u-phasachti alehkhem...*). THE BLOOD AS THE SAVING SIGN: 'WHEN I SEE THE BLOOD, I WILL PASS OVER YOU!' Yahweh decrees: **'THE BLOOD SHALL BE A SIGN FOR YOU! AND WHEN I SEE THE BLOOD, I WILL PASS OVER / PROTECT YOU (*u-phasachti alehkhem*)!'** THE BLOOD OF CHRIST SAVES US FROM ETERNAL DEATH!
cccReferences: CCC 1219 (The Blood of Christ prefigured by the Passover blood saving from the Angel of Death); CCC 1334; Heb 11:28; Rev 12:11.
historicalContext: The blood of the slain lamb acting as the divine covenant shield.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-hayah ha-ddam lakhem le-oth al ha-bbattim asher athem sham ve-ra'ithi eth-ha-ddam u-phasachti alehkhem ve-lo-yihyeh vakhem negh'aph le-mashchith be-hikkothi be-eretz Mitzrayim*: *u-phasachti* ('and I will pass over / shelter / protect').
crossReferences: Hebrews 11:28 ('By faith he kept the Passover and sprinkled the blood, so that the Destroyer of the firstborn might not touch them'); Revelation 12:11; 1 John 1:7.
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 11:28 praises Moses for instituting this blood sprinkling (*proschysin tou haimatos*) to halt the Destroyer (*ho olothreuōn*)!

dominicalIntent: 'This day shall be for you a memorial day, and you shall keep it as a feast to the Lord; throughout your generations, as a statute forever, you shall keep it as a feast' (*Ve-hayah ha-yom ha-zeh lakhem le-zikkaron... chuqqath olam*). A MEMORIAL DAY (*ZIKKARON*) FOREVER! Yahweh institutes the Passover as an everlasting **Memorial Day (*Zikkaron*)**! **ZIKKARON IS NOT MERE RECOLLECTION, BUT SACRAMENTAL RE-PRESENTATION (*ANAMNESIS*), EXACTLY AS CHRIST INSTITUTED THE EUCHARIST: 'DO THIS IN MEMORY OF ME' (*ANAMNESIS*)!**
cccReferences: CCC 1363 (THE CATECHISM DEFINITION OF MEMORIAL / ANAMNESIS: In the liturgy, *Zikkaron/Anamnesis* makes the past saving event present now!); CCC 1362-1372; CCC 1167; Luke 22:19; 1 Cor 11:24.
historicalContext: Instituting the perpetual Passover memorial (*Zikkaron* / *Anamnesis*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-hayah ha-yom ha-zeh lakhem le-zikkaron ve-chaggothem otho chag le-YHVH le-dorotheykhem chuqqath olam techagghuhu*: *le-zikkaron* (for a memorial / re-presentation, Greek *eis anamnesin*!). *chuqqath olam* ('statute forever').
crossReferences: Luke 22:19 ('Do this in remembrance / *anamnesin* of me'); 1 Corinthians 11:24-25; Exodus 13:9.
historicalTrivia: CCC 1363 explains: 'In the sense of Sacred Scripture, the memorial (*zikkaron*) is not merely the recollection of past events... these events become in a certain way present and real'!

dominicalIntent: 'Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread. On the first day you shall remove leaven out of your houses, for if anyone eats what is leavened, from the first day until the seventh day, that person shall be cut off from Israel.' FEAST OF UNLEAVENED BREAD (*MATZOTH*)! 7 days of eating **unleavened bread (*matzoth*)**. All leaven (*se'or* = symbol of sin and corruption, 1 Cor 5:6-8) must be purged from every house.
cccReferences: CCC 1334 (Unleavened bread as symbol of purity and sincerity); 1 Cor 5:6-8 ('Cleanse out the old leaven'); Lev 23:6.
historicalContext: Purging all leavened dough (*se'or*) from homes before sunset on Nisan 14.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Shiv'ath yamim matzoth thokhlu akh ba-yom ha-rishon thashbithu s'or mi-bbattheykhem ki kol-okhel chometz ve-nikhrthah ha-nnephesh ha-hi mi-Yisra'el*: *s'or* (leaven/yeast). *chometz* (leavened bread). *nikhrthah* ('shall be cut off').
historicalTrivia: St. Paul in 1 Corinthians 5:7-8 applies this directly: 'Cleanse out the old leaven... Let us therefore celebrate the festival, not with the old leaven of malice and evil, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth'!

dominicalIntent: 'On the first day you shall hold a holy assembly, and on the seventh day a holy assembly. No work shall be done on those days, except what everyone needs to eat, that alone may be prepared by you.' Holy convocations (*miqra-qodesh*) opening and closing the 7-day feast.
cccReferences: CCC 2172 (Holy assemblies and rest during sacred feasts); Lev 23:7-8.
historicalContext: Sacred assembly (*miqra-qodesh*) with rest from ordinary labor.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-va-yom ha-rishon miqra-qodesh u-va-yom ha-shvi'i miqra-qodesh yihyeh lakhem kol-melakhav lo-ye'asseh vahem...*: *miqra-qodesh* ('convocation of holiness / sacred assembly').
historicalTrivia: The term *miqra-qodesh* ('holy convocation') is the root of the word *Ecclesia* (Church = Called-out Assembly)!

dominicalIntent: 'And you shall observe the Feast of Unleavened Bread, for on this very day I brought your hosts out of the land of Egypt. Therefore you shall observe this day, throughout your generations, as a statute forever.' Mandate for perpetual annual observance of Unleavened Bread.
historicalContext: Commemorating the exact day Israel's hosts (*tzva'oth*) marched out.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-shmarthem eth-ha-mmatzoth ki be-etzem ha-yom ha-zeh hotzethi eth-tzva'othkhem mi-eretz Mitzrayim u-shmarthem eth-ha-yom ha-zeh le-dorotheykhem chuqqath olam*.
historicalTrivia: The phrase *be-etzem ha-yom ha-zeh* means 'on the self-same/exact day'.

dominicalIntent: 'In the first month, from the fourteenth day of the month at evening, you shall eat unleavened bread until the twenty-first day of the month at evening.' Specifying the exact 7-day timeframe: Nisan 14 evening to Nisan 21 evening.
historicalContext: Calendar boundaries for the 7-day feast.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ba-rishon be-arba'ah assar yom la-chodesh ba-erev thokhlu matzoth ad yom ha-echad u-voshrim la-chodesh ba-arev*.
historicalTrivia: Dating: March/April spring equinox period.

dominicalIntent: 'For seven days no leaven is to be found in your houses. If anyone eats what is leavened, that person will be cut off from the congregation of Israel, whether he is a sojourner or a native of the land.' Strict penalty for eating leaven, applying equally to native Israelites and resident aliens (*ger*).
historicalContext: Total purging of leaven (*se'or*) from all homes.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Shiv'ath yamim s'or lo yimmatze be-vatteykhem ki kol-okhel machmetz ve-nikhrthah ha-nnephesh ha-hi me-adath Yisra'el ba-gger u-ve-ezrach ha-aretz*: *ba-gger* (in the resident alien/sojourner). *be-ezrach* (in the native-born).
historicalTrivia: Resident aliens (*ger*) who lived among Israel were required to keep the purity of Unleavened Bread.

dominicalIntent: 'You shall eat nothing leavened; in all your dwelling places you shall eat unleavened bread.' Final re-iteration of unleavened bread.
historicalContext: Universal household mandate across all Israelite dwellings.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Kol-machmetz lo thokhlu be-khol moshvotheykhem thokhlu matzoth*.
historicalTrivia: To this day, Jewish homes perform *Bedikat Chametz* (searching for leaven with a candle) on the night before Passover!

dominicalIntent: Then Moses called all the elders of Israel and said to them: 'Go and select lambs for yourselves according to your clans, and kill the Passover lamb' (*Vyiqra Moshe le-khol-ziqney Yisra'el... mishkhu u-qchu lakhem tzon... ve-shachtu ha-PPESACH*). MOSES MANDATES THE PASSOVER TO THE ELDERS! Moses convenes the elders of Israel: **'DRAW OUT AND TAKE LAMBS FOR YOUR FAMILIES, AND SLAUGHTER THE PASSOVER LAMB (*ha-Ppesach*)!'**
historicalContext: Moses executing the divine Paschal ordinance through the 12-tribe elders.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vyiqra Moshe le-khol-ziqney Yisra'el vayyo'mer alehem mishkhu u-qchu lakhem tzon le-mishpchotheykhem ve-shachtu ha-PPESACH*: *mishkhu* ('draw out / select'). *ha-PPESACH* ('the Passover [Lamb]').
historicalTrivia: Notice the lamb itself is called **The Passover** (*ha-Ppesach*), just as Christ Himself is called **our Passover** in 1 Cor 5:7!

dominicalIntent: 'Take a bunch of hyssop and dip it in the blood that is in the basin, and touch the lintel and the two doorposts with the blood that is in the basin. None of you shall go out of the door of his house until the morning.' THE HYSSOP AND THE BLOOD! Moses commands: (1) Take **a bunch of hyssop (*ezov*)**, (2) Dip it in the blood in the basin (*saph*), (3) Touch lintel and doorposts, (4) **DO NOT GO OUT OF THE DOOR UNTIL MORNING!** **HYSSOP IS THE EXACT PLANT USED ON CALVARY TO OFFER VINEGAR TO JESUS ON THE CROSS (JOHN 19:29)!**
cccReferences: CCC 1219 (Hyssop and blood prefiguring Baptism and the Cross); CCC 1334; Ps 51:7 ('Purge me with hyssop'); John 19:29; Heb 9:19.
historicalContext: Hyssop (*Origanum syriacum*), a bushy aromatic plant with cleansing properties used for ritual blood sprinkling.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-llaqachtem agudath ezov u-tvaltham ba-ddam asher-ba-ssaph ve-higga'them el-ha-mashqoph ve-el-shteney ha-mmezuzoth min-ha-ddam asher ba-ssaph ve-athem lo thetze'u ish mi-ppethach-beytho ad-boqer*: *ezov* (hyssop). *saph* (basin/threshold).
crossReferences: John 19:29 ('They put a sponge full of the sour wine on a hyssop branch and held it to his mouth'); Psalm 51:7; Hebrews 9:19; Leviticus 14:4.
historicalTrivia: At the Crucifixion, St. John specifically records that the sponge of wine was placed on a branch of **hyssop** (*hyssōpō*), explicitly connecting Christ's Death to Exodus 12:22!

dominicalIntent: 'For the Lord will pass through to strike the Egyptians, and when he sees the blood on the lintel and on the two doorposts, the Lord will pass over the door and will not allow the Destroyer to enter your houses to strike you' (*...ve-lo yitten ha-mmashchith la-vo...*). THE DESTROYER (*HA-M MASHCHITH*) BLOCKED BY THE BLOOD! Yahweh promises: when He sees the blood, He will pass over / shield the door, **'AND WILL NOT ALLOW THE DESTROYER (*ha-mmashchith*) TO ENTER YOUR HOUSES TO STRIKE YOU!'** (Heb 11:28).
cccReferences: CCC 1219; CCC 2575; Heb 11:28 ('so that the Destroyer of the firstborn might not touch them'); 1 Cor 10:10.
historicalContext: The Angel of Death / Destroyer (*ha-mmashchith*) executing divine judgment on Egypt.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-avar YHVH li-ngoph eth-Mitzrayim ve-ra'ah eth-ha-ddam al-ha-mashqoph ve-al shteney ha-mmezuzoth u-phassach YHVH al-ha-ppethach ve-lo yitten ha-mmashchith la-vo el-battheykhem li-ngoph*: *ha-mmashchith* (the Destroyer / Destroying Angel, LXX *ho olothreuvōn*).
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 11:28 cites *ho olothreuvōn* ('the Destroyer'): the Blood of the Lamb is the only shield that halts the Destroyer.

dominicalIntent: 'You shall observe this rite as a statute for you and for your sons forever' (*U-shmarthem eth-ha-davar ha-zeh le-choq-lekha u-le-vaneykha ad-olam*). Mandate for perpetual observance across all generations (*ad-olam*).
historicalContext: Perpetual liturgical ordinance.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-shmarthem eth-ha-davar ha-zeh le-choq-lekha u-le-vaneykha ad-olam*: *ad-olam* ('forever / unto eternity').
historicalTrivia: The Paschal liturgy continues in its fulfilled Eucharistic form in the Catholic Church into eternity!

dominicalIntent: 'And when you come to the land that the Lord will give you, as he has promised, you shall keep this service' (*...u-shmarthem eth-ha-avodah ha-zoth*). Mandate to continue the Paschal Service (*avodah*) upon entering Canaan.
historicalContext: Preserving the Paschal liturgy in the Promised Land (fulfilled in Joshua 5:10 at Gilgal!).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-hayah ki-thavo'u el-ha-aretz asher yitten YHVH lakhem ka-asher dibber u-shmarthem eth-ha-avodah ha-zoth*: *ha-avodah* ('this service / liturgy / rite').
historicalTrivia: The word *avodah* means divine service / liturgy.

dominicalIntent: 'And when your children say to you, "What do you mean by this service?"' THE CHILDREN'S QUESTION AT THE PASSOVER TABLE! Prophesying that future children will ask at the Seder table: **'WHAT DOES THIS LITURGY MEAN TO YOU?!'** (*Mah ha-avodah ha-zoth lakhem*).
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Liturgical catechesis of children); CCC 2575; Exod 13:14; Deut 6:20.
historicalContext: The formal 4 Questions (*Ma Nishtana*) asked by the youngest child at the Seder table.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-hayah ki-yo'mru alehkhem bneykhem mah ha-avodah ha-zoth lakhem*: *mah ha-avodah ha-zoth lakhem* ('What is this service to you?').
historicalTrivia: This verse is the direct biblical source for the 4 Questions (*Ma Nishtana*) asked by the youngest child at every Jewish Passover Seder!

dominicalIntent: 'you shall say, "It is the sacrifice of the Lord's Passover, for he passed over the houses of the people of Israel in Egypt, when he struck the Egyptians but spared our houses." And the people bowed their heads and worshiped' (*...Zevach-PESACH hu le-YHVH... vayyiqqad ha-am vayyishtachavvu*). THE LITURGICAL ANSWER AND WORSHIP! The father answers: **'IT IS THE SACRIFICE OF YAHWEH'S PASSOVER (*Zevach-PESACH hu le-YHVH*)!'** Hearing this, **the people bowed their heads and worshiped (*vayyiqqad ha-am vayyishtachavvu*)**!
cccReferences: CCC 1334 (The Paschal sacrifice of praise and worship); CCC 2575; Exod 4:31.
historicalContext: Liturgical formula of the Seder father, followed by solemn prostration.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-amarthem zevach-PESACH hu le-YHVH asher passach al-batthey vney-Yisra'el be-Mitzrayim be-naghpo eth-Mitzrayim ve-eth-battheynu hitzil vayyiqqad ha-am vayyishtachavvu*: *Zevach-PESACH* ('Sacrifice of Passover'). *vayyiqqad... vayyishtachavvu* ('bowed their heads and prostrated').
historicalTrivia: The assembly responds to the Paschal ordinance with profound liturgical adoration (*vayyiqqad ha-am vayyishtachavvu*).

dominicalIntent: Then the people of Israel went and did so; as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron, so they did (*Vayyelkhu vayya'assu bney Yisra'el...*). FAITHFUL EXECUTION! Israel goes forth and executes every detail of the Paschal ordinance in perfect obedience.
historicalContext: Total 12-tribe compliance on the afternoon of Nisan 14.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyelkhu vayya'assu bney Yisra'el ka-asher tzivvah YHVH eth-Moshe ve-Aaron ken assu*.
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 11:28 attributes this obedience to faith: 'By faith he kept the Passover and sprinkled the blood'.

dominicalIntent: At midnight the Lord struck down all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat on his throne to the firstborn of the captive who was in the dungeon, and all the firstborn of the livestock (*Vayehi bi-chatzith ha-llaylah v-YHVH hikkah khol-bekhor be-eretz Mitzrayim...*). THE MIDNIGHT STRIKE ON THE FIRSTBORN! At midnight (*bi-chatzith ha-llaylah*), Yahweh strikes all the firstborn in Egypt, from Pharaoh's heir down to the captive in the dungeon and the cattle! FULFILLMENT OF THE 10TH PLAGUE AND DIVINE TALIONIC JUSTICE!
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (The midnight destruction of Egypt's firstborn liberating Israel); CCC 2575; Wis 18:14-15; Heb 11:28.
historicalContext: Midnight on Nisan 15, 1446 BC.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi bi-chatzith ha-llaylah v-YHVH hikkah khol-bekhor be-eretz Mitzrayim mi-bkor Phar'oh ha-yoshev al-kisso ad bekhor ha-shvi asher be-veyth ha-bor ve-khol bekhor bhemah*: *bi-chatzith ha-llaylah* ('in the middle of the night').
historicalTrivia: Wisdom 18:14-15 describes the midnight strike as the divine **Logos** leaping down from heaven's royal throne!

dominicalIntent: And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he and all his servants and all the Egyptians. And there was a great cry in Egypt, for there was not a house where someone was not dead (*...ki-eyn bayith asher eyn-sham meth*). NOT A HOUSE WITHOUT A DEAD BODY! Pharaoh and all Egypt awaken at midnight: **THERE WAS NOT A SINGLE EGYPTIAN HOUSE WHERE SOMEONE WAS NOT DEAD!** A great cry (*tza'aqah ghedolah*) fills Egypt.
cccReferences: CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Exod 11:6.
historicalContext: Universal death of firstborn males in every non-blood-protected Egyptian home.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyaqam Par'oh laylah hu ve-khol-avadav ve-khol-Mitzrayim vat-tehi tza'aqah ghedolah be-Mitzrayim ki-eyn bayith asher eyn-sham meth*: *eyn-sham meth* ('there was not there one dead').
historicalTrivia: Every non-covenant family in Egypt suffered the loss of its eldest male.

dominicalIntent: Then he summoned Moses and Aaron by night and said: 'Up, go out from among my people, both you and the people of Israel; and go, serve the Lord, as you have said.' PHARAOH SURRENDERS AT MIDNIGHT: 'UP, GO OUT FROM MY PEOPLE!' In total panic, Pharaoh summons Moses and Aaron in the middle of the night, pleading: **'UP, GO OUT FROM AMONG MY PEOPLE, BOTH YOU AND ISRAEL; GO, SERVE YAHWEH AS YOU HAVE SAID!'** Total unconditional surrender!
cccReferences: CCC 2060; CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Exod 6:1; Exod 11:1.
historicalContext: Midnight royal summons expelling Israel from Egypt.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vyiqra le-Moshe u-le-Aaron laylah vayyo'mer qumu tze'u mi-thokh ammi gam-athem gam-bney Yisra'el u-lekhu ivdu eth-YHVH ke-dhabberkhem*: *qumu tze'u* ('Arise! Get out!').
crossReferences: Exodus 6:1; Exodus 11:1; Psalm 105:38 ('Egypt was glad when they departed').
historicalTrivia: Psalm 105:38 notes: 'Egypt was glad when they departed, for dread of them had fallen upon them'.

dominicalIntent: 'Take your flocks and your herds, as you have said, and be gone; and bless me also!' PHARAOH BEGS FOR MOSES' BLESSING! Pharaoh surrenders all conditions: 'Take your flocks and herds and go; **AND BLESS ME ALSO (*u-verakhtem gam-othi*)**!' The world's supreme god-king begs the humble Hebrew prophet for his blessing!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The absolute humiliation of Pharaoh begging the prophet for a blessing); Heb 7:7.
historicalContext: Pharaoh begging the prophet for intercessory blessing to avert further death.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Gam-tzonkhem gam-bveqarkhem qchu ka-asher dibbarthem ve-lekhu u-verakhtem gam-othi*: *u-verakhtem gam-othi* ('and bless also me!').
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh who asked 'Who is Yahweh?' (Exod 5:2) now begs for Yahweh's blessing through Moses!

dominicalIntent: The Egyptians were urgent with the people to send them out of the land in haste. For they said: 'We shall all be dead' (*...Ki amru kullanu methim*). EGYPTIAN URGENCY: 'WE SHALL ALL BE DEAD!' The Egyptian populace pressures the Hebrews to leave in extreme haste (*be-chippazon*), crying: **'WE SHALL ALL BE DEAD!'**
historicalContext: Public panic driving the immediate expulsion of the Hebrews.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vat-thechazaq Mitzrayim al-ha-am le-maher le-shallcham min-ha-aretz ki amru kullanu methim*: *kullanu methim* ('we are all dead men!').
historicalTrivia: The Egyptians themselves forced the Hebrews to depart without even waiting for dough to rise.

dominicalIntent: So the people took their dough before it was leavened, their kneading bowls being bound up in their cloaks on their shoulders (*...mish'arotham tzruroth be-ssimlosham...*). UNLEAVENED DOUGH ON THEIR SHOULDERS! Israel carries their unleavened dough (*batzekh*) in their **kneading bowls (*mish'aroth*) wrapped in their cloaks** on their shoulders. The physical origin of Unleavened Bread!
cccReferences: CCC 1334 (Unleavened bread carried out in haste as the perpetual Paschal food); Exod 12:15; Exod 12:39.
historicalContext: Carrying unbaked, unleavened dough bowls wrapped in outer garments (*smloth*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyissa ha-am eth-btzeko terem yechmatz mish'arotham tzruroth be-ssimlosham al-shikhmam*: *btzeko* (their dough). *mish'arotham* (their kneading troughs/bowls).
historicalTrivia: Deuteronomy 16:3 calls Unleavened Bread **'the bread of affliction' (*lechem oni*)**, because they came out of Egypt in haste!

dominicalIntent: The people of Israel had also done as Moses told them, for they had asked the Egyptians for silver and gold jewelry and for clothing. The Hebrews ask the Egyptians for gold, silver, and fine garments.
historicalContext: Execution of the divine instruction to receive back-pay from Egyptians.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-vney-Yisra'el assu ki-dvar Moshe vayyish'lu mi-Mitzrayim kley-khesseph u-khley zahav u-ssmaloth*.
historicalTrivia: Psalm 105:37 summarizes: 'Then he brought out Israel with silver and gold, and there was none among his tribes who stumbled'.

dominicalIntent: And the Lord had given the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they let them have what they asked. Thus they plundered the Egyptians (*...Vayyatznilu eth-Mitzrayim*). PLUNDERING THE EGYPTIANS (*VAYYATZNILU ETH-MITZRAYIM*)! Yahweh grants Israel favor; Egyptians gladly hand over their wealth to speed their departure: **'THUS THEY PLUSTERED THE EGYPTIANS!'** Fulfilling Genesis 15:14!
cccReferences: CCC 2413 (Just compensation for centuries of forced labor); CCC 2575; Gen 15:14; Exod 3:22.
historicalContext: Receiving state wealth as just divine restitution for 400 years of uncompensated slave labor.
translationNuances: Hebrew *V-YHVH nathan eth-chen ha-am be-eyney Mitzrayim vayyash'ilum vayyatznilu eth-Mitzrayim*: *vayyatznilu* (and they stripped/plundered/rescued, root *natzal*).
crossReferences: Genesis 15:14 ('afterward they shall come out with great possessions'); Exodus 3:22; Psalm 105:37.
historicalTrivia: The gold and silver stripped (*vayyatznilu*) from Egypt supplied the materials for the Ark of the Covenant, the Tabernacle, and the Golden Calf!

dominicalIntent: And the people of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand men on foot, besides women and children (*...ke-shes-me'oth eleph ragli ha-ggvarim mi-l-vadh mi-ttaph*). THE EXODUS MARCH: 600,000 MEN ON FOOT! Israel marches from **Rameses** (Avaris) to **Succoth** ('Shelters/Booths'). Total population tally: **ABOUT 600,000 MEN ON FOOT (*shes-me'oth eleph ragli*)**, besides women and children (totaling ~2 to 2.5 million souls!).
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The massive exodus of the 12-tribe nation); Exod 38:26; Num 1:46; Num 11:21.
historicalContext: The 1st leg of the Exodus journey: Rameses (Tell el-Dab'a) to Succoth (Tell el-Maskhuta). 600,000 adult males aged 20+.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiss'u vney-Yisra'el mi-R'amses Succothah ke-shes-me'oth eleph ragli ha-ggvarim mi-l-vadh mi-ttaph*: *R'amses* (Rameses/Avaris). *Succothah* (to Succoth = booths). *shes-me'oth eleph* (600,000).
historicalTrivia: Numbers 1:46 records the precise census 1 year later: 603,550 adult men aged 20 and older!

dominicalIntent: A mixed multitude also went up with them, and very much livestock, both flocks and herds (*Ve-gham erev rav alah ittham...*). THE MIXED MULTITUDE (*EREV RAV*) JOINS THE EXODUS! A **mixed multitude (*erev rav*)** of non-Israelite foreigners (believing Egyptians, Asiatics, and foreign slaves converted by the plagues) joins the Exodus march! **THE UNIVERSAL CHURCH OPEN TO ALL NATIONS PREFIGURED!**
cccReferences: CCC 781 (The People of God gathered from all nations prefigured by the mixed multitude); CCC 2575; Num 11:4; Zech 8:23.
historicalContext: Gentiles, Egyptians, and foreign slaves who believed Yahweh joining Israel's exodus.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-gham erev rav alah ittham ve-tzon u-vqarar miqneh kaved me'od*: *erev rav* ('a mixed multitude / diverse crowd', root *arav* = to mix).
historicalTrivia: The *erev rav* ('mixed multitude') proves that Israel was never an exclusive ethnic enclave, but a covenant community open to all who fear Yahweh!

dominicalIntent: And they baked unleavened cakes of the dough that they had brought out of Egypt, for it was not leavened, because they were driven out of Egypt and could not delay, nor had they prepared any provisions for themselves (*...uggoth matzoth ki lo chametz...*). BAKING UNLEAVENED CAKES (*UGGOTH MATZOTH*) AT SUCCOTH! At Succoth, they bake **unleavened cakes (*uggoth matzoth*)** from the dough brought out of Egypt, for they were expelled in haste (*ki ghurshu mi-Mitzrayim*).
cccReferences: CCC 1334 (Unleavened bread of haste); Deut 16:3.
historicalContext: First meal baked on the Exodus journey at Succoth.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyaphu eth-ha-bhatzeq asher hotzi'u mi-Mitzrayim uggoth matzoth ki lo chametz ki ghurshu mi-Mitzrayim ve-lo yakhalu li-thmahme'ah ve-gham-tzedah lo-assu lahem*: *uggoth matzoth* ('unleavened round cakes'). *ghurshu* ('they were driven out').
historicalTrivia: Because they were driven out (*ghurshu*), they had no time to prepare travel provisions (*tzedah*), relying entirely on God's manna!

dominicalIntent: The time that the people of Israel lived in Egypt was four hundred and thirty years (*U-moshav bney Yisra'el asher yashvu be-Mitzrayim sheloshim shanah ve-arba me'oth shanah*). THE 430 YEARS IN EGYPT! Scripture records the exact duration of the sojourn: **FOUR HUNDRED AND THIRTY YEARS (*sheloshim shanah ve-arba me'oth shanah*)**! **ST. PAUL CITES THIS EXACT 430-YEAR TIMELINE IN GALATIANS 3:17!**
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The fulfillment of the 430-year covenant timeline cited by St. Paul); Gal 3:17; Gen 15:13; Acts 7:6.
historicalContext: Historical duration from Abraham's covenant promise / Jacob's entry to the Exodus (1876 BC to 1446 BC = 430 years!).
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-moshav bney Yisra'el asher yashvu be-Mitzrayim sheloshim shanah ve-arba me'oth shanah*: *sheloshim... ve-arba me'oth* (430 years).
crossReferences: Galatians 3:17 ('The law, which came 430 years afterward, does not annul a covenant previously ratified by God'); Genesis 15:13; Acts 7:6.
historicalTrivia: Galatians 3:17 explicitly calculates 430 years between God's covenant promise to Abraham and the giving of the Law at Sinai!

dominicalIntent: At the end of four hundred and thirty years, on that very day, all the hosts of the Lord went out from the land of Egypt (*...be-etzem ha-yom ha-zeh yatze'u kol-tzva'oth YHVH me-eretz Mitzrayim*). ON THAT VERY DAY ALL THE HOSTS OF YAHWEH MARCHED OUT! At the end of the 430 years to the exact day (**be-etzem ha-yom ha-zeh**), **ALL THE HOSTS OF YAHWEH (*kol-tzva'oth YHVH*) MARCHED OUT OF EGYPT!** Divine precision.
historicalContext: Exact calendar fulfillment on Nisan 15.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi mi-qqetz sheloshim shanah ve-arba me'oth shanah vayehi be-etzem ha-yom ha-zeh yatze'u kol-tzva'oth YHVH me-eretz Mitzrayim*: *be-etzem ha-yom ha-zeh* ('on the self-same / exact day'). *tzva'oth YHVH* ('armies/hosts of Yahweh').
historicalTrivia: Israel is titled for the first time **The Armies/Hosts of Yahweh (*Tzva'oth YHVH*)**!

dominicalIntent: It was a night of watching by the Lord, to bring them out of the land of Egypt; so this same night is a night of watching kept to the Lord by all the people of Israel throughout their generations (*Leil shimmurim hu le-YHVH... leil shimmurim le-khol-bney Yisra'el...*). A NIGHT OF WATCHING FOR YAHWEH (*LEIL SHIMMURIM*)! The Passover night is titled **LEIL SHIMMURIM ('A Night of Vigil / Watching for Yahweh')**! **THIS IS THE FOUNDATION FOR THE HOLY SATURDAY EASTER VIGIL (*LUCERNARIUM / VIGILIA PASCHALIS*), THE MOTHER OF ALL HOLY VIGILS IN THE CATHOLIC CHURCH!**
cccReferences: CCC 1168 (The Easter Vigil as the Supreme Night of Watching prefigured by *Leil Shimmurim*); CCC 1334; CCC 2575; Mark 14:38; Luke 12:37.
historicalContext: The sacred night vigil (*Leil Shimmurim*) kept by God watching over Israel, and Israel keeping vigil for God.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Leil shimmurim hu le-YHVH le-hotzi'am me-eretz Mitzrayim hu-ha-llaylah ha-zeh le-YHVH shimmurim le-khol-bney Yisra'el le-dorotheyhem*: *Leil shimmurim* ('Night of Vigils / Keeping Watch / Protection').
crossReferences: Luke 12:37 ('Blessed are those servants whom the master finds awake when he comes'); Mark 14:38; Exodus 14:24.
historicalTrivia: In Catholic liturgy, the Easter Vigil (*Vigilia Paschalis*) on Holy Saturday night directly fulfills Exodus 12:42's *Leil Shimmurim*!

dominicalIntent: And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron: 'This is the statute of the Passover: no foreigner shall eat of it' (*...Zoth chuqqath ha-PPESACH kol-ben-nekhar lo-yo'khal bo*). REGULATION FOR THE PASSOVER BANQUET: NO UNCOVENANTED FOREIGNER! Yahweh institutes the Paschal ordinance: **'NO FOREIGNER / UNCOVENANTED PERSON (*ben-nekhar*) SHALL EAT OF IT!'** PREFIGURING SACRAMENTAL COMMUNION: ONLY THE BAPTIZED IN THE STATE OF GRACE MAY RECEIVE THE EUCHARIST!
cccReferences: CCC 1355 (Sacramental admission to the Eucharist restricted to the baptized faithful); CCC 1385; 1 Cor 11:27-29.
historicalContext: Excluding uncircumcised, uncovenanted Gentiles (*ben-nekhar*) from consuming the sacred Paschal victim.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe ve-Aaron zoth chuqqath ha-PPESACH kol-ben-nekhar lo-yo'khal bo*: *ben-nekhar* ('son of a foreigner / stranger').
historicalTrivia: Just as no uncircumcised foreigner could eat the Passover lamb, so no unbaptized person may receive the Holy Eucharist (Didache 9.5)!

dominicalIntent: 'but every slave that is bought for money may eat of it after you have circumcised him.' A slave bought for money may partake once he enters the covenant through circumcision.
cccReferences: CCC 1150 (Circumcision as initiation into covenant communion); CCC 1334.
historicalContext: Covenant inclusion through household circumcision.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-khol-eved ish miqnath-khesseph u-malthah otho az yo'khal bo*: *u-malthah otho* ('and you shall circumcise him').
historicalTrivia: Circumcision incorporated slaves into full spiritual equality at the Seder table.

dominicalIntent: 'No foreigner or hired servant may eat of it.' Temporary day-laborers (*thoshav ve-sakhir*) who are not part of the covenant household are excluded.
historicalContext: Distinction between a permanent household member and a hired day-laborer (*sakhir*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Thoshav ve-sakhir lo-yo'khal bo*: *thoshav* (temporary resident). *sakhir* (hired hand).
historicalTrivia: Membership in the covenant household, not employment status, determined access to the sacrament.

dominicalIntent: 'In one house it shall be eaten; you shall not take any of the flesh outside the house, and you shall not break one of its bones' (*...ve-etzem lo thishbru-vo*). NOT A BONE OF THE LAMB SHALL BE BROKEN—FULFILLED AT THE CRUCIFIXION OF JESUS! Two crucial mandates: (1) Eaten in one house (Unity of the Church!), (2) **'YOU SHALL NOT BREAK ONE OF ITS BONES (*ve-etzem lo thishbru-vo*)!'** **ST. JOHN IN JOHN 19:36 EXPLICITLY DECLARES THAT WHEN THE SOLDIERS REFRAINED FROM BREAKING JESUS' LEGS ON THE CROSS, THIS EXACT PASCHAL MANDATE WAS FULFILLED!**
cccReferences: CCC 608 (JESUS THE PASCHAL LAMB: John 19:36 citing Exod 12:46: 'Not a bone of him shall be broken'); CCC 813 (Unity of the Church eating in one house); John 19:36; Ps 34:20; Num 9:12.
historicalContext: Preserving the structural integrity of the Paschal lamb; fulfilled at Golgotha.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Be-veyth echad ye'akhel lo-thotzi min-ha-bayith min-ha-bbasar chutzah ve-etzem lo thishbru-vo*: *etzem* (bone). *lo thishbru-vo* ('you shall not break in it').
crossReferences: John 19:36 ('For these things took place that the Scripture might be fulfilled: "Not one of his bones will be broken"'); Psalm 34:20; Numbers 9:12.
historicalTrivia: On Golgotha, the Roman soldiers broke the legs of the two thieves, but when they came to Jesus and saw He was already dead, they broke NOT ONE OF HIS BONES (John 19:33-36)!

dominicalIntent: 'All the congregation of Israel shall keep it' (*Kol-adath Yisra'el ya'assu otho*). UNIVERSAL OBLIGATION! Every member of the congregation of Israel (*Kol-adath Yisra'el*) is bound to keep the Passover.
cccReferences: CCC 1388 (Universal obligation of the faithful to participate in the Paschal banquet); CCC 2575.
historicalContext: Total 12-tribe liturgical obligation.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Kol-adath Yisra'el ya'assu otho*: *adath* (congregation/assembly).
historicalTrivia: Neglecting the Passover without valid excuse resulted in being cut off (*kareth*) from Israel (Num 9:13).

dominicalIntent: 'If a stranger shall sojourn with you and would keep the Passover to the Lord, let all his males be circumcised. Then he may come near and keep it; he shall be as a native of the land. But no uncircumcised person shall eat of it' (*...ve-hayah ke-ezrach ha-aretz ve-khol-arel lo-yo'khal bo*). CONVERSION AND COVENANT INCLUSION FOR GENTILES! Any resident alien (*ger*) who undergoes circumcision for all his males becomes **'AS A NATIVE OF THE LAND (*ke-ezrach ha-aretz*)'** and may eat the Passover! But no uncircumcised person (*arel*) may eat it.
cccReferences: CCC 1267 (Baptism incorporating Gentiles into the one People of God as full native citizens); CCC 1355; Gal 3:28.
historicalContext: Full conversion protocol for Gentiles seeking entry into Israel's covenant.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-khi-yagur ittakh ger ve-assah phesach le-YHVH himmol lo khol-zakhar ve-az yiqrav la-assotho ve-hayah ke-ezrach ha-aretz ve-khol-arel lo-yo'khal bo*: *ke-ezrach* ('as a native citizen'). *arel* (uncircumcised person).
historicalTrivia: Circumcision erased the Gentile-Israelite national boundary, making the converted Gentile a full *ezrach* (native citizen)!

dominicalIntent: 'There shall be one law for the native and for the stranger who sojourns among you' (*Torah achath yihyeh la-ezrach u-la-gger ha-ggar be-thokhkhhem*). ONE LAW FOR NATIVE AND STRANGER! Yahweh decrees absolute legal and spiritual equality: **'THERE SHALL BE ONE LAW (*TORAH ACHATH*) FOR THE NATIVE AND FOR THE STRANGER WHO SOJOURNS AMONG YOU!'**
cccReferences: CCC 1934 (Equal dignity of all human beings before God's law); CCC 2575; Lev 24:22; Num 15:15-16.
historicalContext: The foundational principle of equal justice under divine law (*Torah achath*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Torah achath yihyeh la-ezrach u-la-gger ha-ggar be-thokhkhhem*: *Torah achath* ('one law/instruction').
crossReferences: Leviticus 24:22 ('You shall have one law for the sojourner and for the native'); Numbers 15:15-16; Galatians 3:28.
historicalTrivia: This is the first time the phrase **Torah Achath** ('One Law') appears in the Bible, establishing universal equality under God's law.

dominicalIntent: Thus all the people of Israel did; just as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron, so they did. Universal obedience of Israel to the Paschal regulations.
historicalContext: Full 12-tribe adherence.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'assu kol-bney Yisra'el ka-asher tzivvah YHVH eth-Moshe ve-eth-Aaron ken assu*.
historicalTrivia: Re-iterates the total compliance of the community.

dominicalIntent: And on that very day the Lord brought the people of Israel out of the land of Egypt by their hosts (*Vayehi be-etzem ha-yom ha-zeh hotzi YHVH eth-bney Yisra'el me-eretz Mitzrayim al-tziv'otham*). GRAND CONCLUSION OF EXODUS 12: MARCHING OUT BY THEIR HOSTS! On that self-same day (**be-etzem ha-yom ha-zeh**), **YAHWEH BROUGHT THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL OUT OF THE LAND OF EGYPT BY THEIR HOSTS / ARMIES (*al-tziv'otham*)!** THE EXODUS IS ACCOMPLISHED!
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (The triumphant climax of the Exodus liberation); CCC 2575; Ps 105:37; Acts 7:36.
historicalContext: Historical completion of the Exodus on Nisan 15, 1446 BC.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi be-etzem ha-yom ha-zeh hotzi YHVH eth-bney Yisra'el me-eretz Mitzrayim al-tziv'otham*: *be-etzem ha-yom ha-zeh* ('on the exact/self-same day'). *al-tziv'otham* ('by their armies/hosts').
historicalTrivia: Exodus 12 closes with Israel marching out as a victorious, organized holy army (*tzva'oth*) under the Banner of Yahweh!

dominicalIntent: The Lord said to Moses... Yahweh introduces the divine mandate for the consecration of the firstborn.
cccReferences: CCC 529 (The Presentation of the Lord in the Temple prefigured by the consecration of the firstborn); CCC 2063; CCC 2575.
historicalContext: Nisan 15, 1446 BC: Post-Passover divine instructions at Succoth.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayydabber YHVH el-Moshe le'mor*.
historicalTrivia: The consecration of the firstborn is the direct foundation for the Catholic Feast of the Presentation of the Lord (Candlemas, Feb 2).

dominicalIntent: 'Consecrate to me all the firstborn.
