Whatever is the first to open the womb among the people of Israel, both of man and of beast, is mine' (*Qaddesh-li khol-bekhor peter kol-rechem... li hu*). CONSECRATION OF THE FIRSTBORN—CITED IN LUKE 2:23 FOR THE PRESENTATION OF JESUS IN THE TEMPLE! God commands: **'CONSECRATE TO ME ALL THE FIRSTBORN (*Qaddesh-li khol-bekhor*); WHATEVER OPENS THE WOMB (*peter kol-rechem*)... IS MINE!'** **ST. LUKE IN LUKE 2:23 EXPLICITLY QUOTES THIS VERSE WHEN MARY AND JOSEPH PRESENT THE INFANT JESUS IN THE TEMPLE!**
cccReferences: CCC 529 (THE PRESENTATION OF JESUS IN THE TEMPLE: Luke 2:23 citing Exod 13:2: 'Every male who opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord'); CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Luke 2:22-23; Num 3:13.
historicalContext: Divine ownership of all firstborn males in Israel in exchange for sparing them on Passover night.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Qaddesh-li khol-bekhor peter kol-rechem bi-vney Yisra'el ba-adam u-va-bhemah li hu*: *Qaddesh-li* ('sanctify / set apart as holy to Me'). *peter kol-rechem* ('opener of all womb', LXX *dianoigon pasan mētran*).
crossReferences: Luke 2:22-23 ('As it is written in the Law of the Lord, "Every male who first opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord"'); Exodus 13:12; Numbers 3:13; Numbers 8:16.
historicalTrivia: Luke 2:23 translates *peter kol-rechem* into Greek as *pan dianoigon mētran* ('every opener of the womb'), establishing Jesus as the Supreme Firstborn!

dominicalIntent: Moses said to the people: 'Remember this day in which you came out from Egypt, out of the house of slavery, for by a strong hand the Lord brought you out from this place. No leavened bread shall be eaten' (*Zakhor eth-ha-yom ha-zeh... ki be-chazaq yad hotzi YHVH ethkhem mi-zzeh...*). REMEMBER THIS DAY! BY A STRONG HAND (*CHAZAQ YAD*) YAHWEH BROUGHT YOU OUT! Moses commands Israel to remember (*Zakhor*) the day of exodus accomplished by God's **strong hand (*be-chazaq yad*)**.
cccReferences: CCC 1363 (Liturgical remembrance *Zikkaron*); CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Deut 16:3.
historicalContext: First address of Moses to the assembled 600,000 men at Succoth.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Moshe el-ha-am zakhor eth-ha-yom ha-zeh asher yetza'them mi-Mitzrayim mi-bbeyth avadim ki be-chazaq yad hotzi YHVH ethkhem mi-zzeh ve-lo ye'akhel chametz*: *zakhor* (infinitive absolute: 'remember continuously!'). *be-chazaq yad* ('with strength of hand').
historicalTrivia: The phrase *beyth avadim* ('house of slaves/bondage') became the standard prophetic summary for Egypt.

dominicalIntent: 'Today, in the month of Abib, you are going out.' Dating the departure in the spring month of Abib (Nisan).
cccReferences: CCC 1168 (Sacred spring season of redemption); Deut 16:1.
historicalContext: Month of Abib ('young ear of grain' / March-April equinox).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ha-yom athem yotz'im be-chodesh ha-Aviv*: *be-chodesh ha-Aviv* ('in the month of Abib/spring').
historicalTrivia: Abib means 'green ear of grain', indicating the barley harvest season.

dominicalIntent: 'And when the Lord brings you into the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, which he swore to your fathers to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, you shall keep this service in this month.' Re-affirming the perpetual Paschal liturgy in the Promised Land.
cccReferences: CCC 1334; CCC 2575; Exod 3:8; Exod 3:17.
historicalContext: Covenant oath (*nishba*) to the Patriarchs giving the land flowing with milk and honey (*zavath chalav u-dvash*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-hayah ki-yevi'akha YHVH el-eretz ha-Kna'ani... asher nishba la-avotheykha la-theth lakh eretz zavath chalav u-dvash ve-avadtha eth-ha-avodah ha-zoth ba-chodesh ha-zeh*.
historicalTrivia: Milk (*chalav*) and honey (*dvash*) symbolized pastoral abundance and wild date-syrup richness.

dominicalIntent: 'Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a feast to the Lord.' Re-iterating the 7-day feast ending in a solemn festival (*Chag*).
historicalContext: The 7-day festival of Unleavened Bread.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Shiv'ath yamim thokhal matzoth u-va-yom ha-shvi'i chag le-YHVH*.
historicalTrivia: The 7th day (Nisan 21) was the day Israel crossed the Red Sea!

dominicalIntent: 'Unleavened bread shall be eaten for seven days; no leavened bread shall be seen with you, and no leaven shall be seen with you in all your territory.' Total territorial ban on leaven.
historicalContext: Complete purging of yeast/leaven (*s'or*) across all Israelite territory.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Matzoth ye'akhel eth shiv'ath ha-yyamim ve-lo-yera'eh lekha chametz ve-lo-yera'eh lekha s'or be-khol-gvulekha*.
historicalTrivia: Not only inside houses, but throughout all territorial boundaries (*gvulekha*), leaven is banned.

dominicalIntent: 'You shall tell your son on that day, "It is because of what the Lord did for me when I came out of Egypt."' THE PERSONAL FIRST-PERSON PASSOVER TESTIMONY! The father instructs his son in the first person: **'IT IS BECAUSE OF WHAT YAHWEH DID FOR ME (*LI*) WHEN I CAME OUT OF EGYPT!'** EVERY GENERATION MUST VIEW ITSELF AS PERSONALLY LIBERATED FROM EGYPT!
cccReferences: CCC 1363 (Every generation personally present to the saving Exodus event through liturgy); CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Exod 10:2; Deut 6:21.
historicalContext: The core Rabbinic principle of the Seder *Haggadah*: 'In every generation, a person is obligated to see himself as though he personally went out from Egypt'!
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-higgadtha le-vinkha ba-yom ha-hu le'mor ba'avur zeh assah YHVH LI be-tze'thi mi-Mitzrayim*: *LI* ('for ME personally!'). *Ve-higgadtha* (and you shall tell/recount -> *Haggadah*!).
historicalTrivia: The verb *Ve-higgadtha* ('and you shall tell') gives its name to the Passover book: the **Haggadah**!

dominicalIntent: 'And it shall be to you as a sign on your hand and as a memorial between your eyes, that the law of the Lord may be in your mouth. For with a strong hand the Lord has brought you out of Egypt' (*Ve-hayah lekha le-oth al-yadkha u-le-zikkaron beyn eyneykha...*). THE SIGN ON THE HAND AND FRONTLET BETWEEN THE EYES—ORIGIN OF TEFILLIN / PHYLACTERIES! God institutes a visible covenant sign: **'IT SHALL BE TO YOU AS A SIGN ON YOUR HAND (*le-oth al-yadkha*) AND AS A MEMORIAL BETWEEN YOUR EYES (*u-le-zikkaron beyn eyneykha*)!'** THE DIRECT BIBLICAL ORIGIN OF TEFILLIN (PHYLACTERIES) WORN IN PRAYER!
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (External physical signs reminding believers of God's Law); CCC 2575; Deut 6:8; Deut 11:18; Matt 23:5.
historicalContext: Wearing leather phylactery boxes (*Tefillin*) containing Exodus 13:1-10 on the left arm and forehead during morning prayer.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-hayah lekha le-oth al-yadkha u-le-zikkaron beyn eyneykha le-ma'an thihyeh Torath YHVH be-phikha ki be-yad chazaqah hotzi'akha YHVH mi-Mitzrayim*: *le-oth al-yadkha* ('for a sign on your hand'). *beyn eyneykha* ('between your eyes' = forehead).
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 6:8; Deuteronomy 11:18; Matthew 23:5 ('They make their phylacteries broad'); Proverbs 3:3.
historicalTrivia: Tefillin (phylacteries) contain 4 parchment scrolls, including Exodus 13:1-10 and Exodus 13:11-16!

dominicalIntent: 'You shall therefore keep this statute at its appointed time from year to year' (*...mi-yamim yamimah*). Perpetual annual observance (*mi-yamim yamimah* = year to year).
cccReferences: CCC 1168 (The annual liturgical cycle); Exod 12:14.
historicalContext: Annual recurrence of the Paschal feast.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-shamartha eth-ha-chuqqah ha-zoth le-mo'adah mi-yamim yamimah*: *mi-yamim yamimah* ('from days to days' = year by year).
historicalTrivia: The idiom *mi-yamim yamimah* means an annual recurring anniversary.

dominicalIntent: 'When the Lord brings you into the land of the Canaanites, as he swore to you and your fathers, and shall give it to you...' Repeating the entry into Canaan.
historicalContext: Patriarchal land oath.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-hayah ki-yevi'akha YHVH el-eretz ha-Kna'ani ka-asher nishba lekha u-la-avotheykha u-nthanah lakh*.
historicalTrivia: Re-affirming the divine oath (*nishba*) to Abraham.

dominicalIntent: 'you shall set apart to the Lord all that first opens the womb. All firstlings of your livestock that are males shall be the Lord's' (*...ve-ha me'avartha kol-peter-rechem le-YHVH... ha-zzkharim le-YHVH*). SETTING APART ALL FIRSTBORN MALES FOR YAHWEH! God commands: **'YOU SHALL PASS OVER / SET APART (*ve-ha'avartha*) ALL THAT FIRST OPENS THE WOMB TO YAHWEH!'** Every firstborn male belongs exclusively to God.
cccReferences: CCC 529 (The consecration of firstborn males); CCC 2575; Luke 2:23; Exod 13:2.
historicalContext: Solemn transfer of ownership (*ha'avarah*) of firstborn males to God.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-ha'avartha kol-peter-rechem le-YHVH ve-khol-peter sheger bhemah asher yihyeh lekha ha-zzkharim le-YHVH*: *ve-ha'avartha* ('you shall cause to pass over / consecrate', root *avar*). *ha-zzkharim* (the males).
historicalTrivia: The verb *ha'avarah* ('cause to pass over') echoes the Passover *Pesach*!

dominicalIntent: 'Every firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb, or if you will not redeem it you shall break its neck. Every firstborn of man among your sons you shall redeem' (*...ve-khol bekhor adam be-vaneykha thiphdeh*). REDEEMING THE DONKEY AND REDEEMING THE HUMAN FIRSTBORN (*PIDYON HA-BEN*)! Two laws: (1) An unclean donkey must be redeemed (*thiphdeh*) with a lamb or have its neck broken, (2) **EVERY FIRSTBORN HUMAN SON MUST BE REDEEMED (*thiphdeh*)!** **FOUNDATION FOR THE SACRED RITE OF REDEMPTION OF THE FIRSTBORN (*PIDYON HA-BEN*), PERFORMED FOR JESUS IN LUKE 2:22-24!**
cccReferences: CCC 529 (PIDYON HA-BEN: Redemption of the Firstborn Son fulfilled in Jesus Christ); CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Luke 2:22-24; Num 18:15-16.
historicalContext: The 5-shekel redemption rite (*Pidyon Ha-Ben*) redeeming the 31-day-old firstborn son from a Priest (*Kohen*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-khol-peter chamor thiphdeh ve-seh ve-im-lo thiphdeh va-araphto ve-khol bekhor adam be-vaneykha thiphdeh*: *thiphdeh* (you shall redeem / ransom, root *padah*). *va-araphto* ('you shall break its neck').
historicalTrivia: To this day, observant Jewish families perform the *Pidyon Ha-Ben* ceremony on the 31st day after a firstborn son's birth, giving 5 silver coins to a Kohen!

dominicalIntent: 'And when in time to come your son asks you, "What does this mean?" you shall say to him, "By a strong hand the Lord brought us out of Egypt, from the house of slavery."' FATHER'S CATECHETICAL ANSWER TO HIS SON! When the son asks 'What does this mean?', the father answers: **'BY A STRONG HAND (*BE-CHAZAQ YAD*) YAHWEH BROUGHT US OUT OF EGYPT, FROM THE HOUSE OF SLAVERY!'**
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Parental catechesis teaching salvation history); CCC 2575; Exod 12:26; Deut 6:20.
historicalContext: Parental obligation to transmit the historical truth of the Exodus to children.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-hayah ki-yish'alkha vinkha machar le'mor mah-zoth ve-amartha elav be-chazaq yad hotzi'anu YHVH mi-Mitzrayim mi-bbeyth avadim*: *mah-zoth* ('What is this?').
historicalTrivia: This is one of the 4 classic child scenarios in the Passover Seder *Haggadah* (The Simple Son who asks 'What is this?').

dominicalIntent: 'For when Pharaoh stubbornly refused to let us go, the Lord killed all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both the firstborn of man and the firstborn of livestock. Therefore I sacrifice to the Lord all the males that first open the womb, but all the firstborn of my sons I redeem.' Explaining the divine rationale for the firstborn sacrifice and redemption.
historicalContext: Recounting the 10th Plague midnight execution as the basis for *Pidyon Ha-Ben*.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi ki-hiqshah Phar'oh le-shallchenu vayyaharogh YHVH kol-bekhor be-eretz Mitzrayim mi-bkor adam ve-ad-bekhor bhemah al-ken ani zove'ach le-YHVH kol-peter rechem ha-zzkharim ve-khol-bekhor banai ephdeh*: *hiqshah* ('made hard/stubborn').
historicalTrivia: The redemption of human firstborns (*ephdeh*) honors God's sparing of Israel's firstborn.

dominicalIntent: 'It shall be as a mark on your hand and frontlets between your eyes, for by a strong hand the Lord brought us out of Egypt' (*Ve-hayah le-oth al-yadkhah u-le-totaphoth beyn eyneykha...*). FRONTLETS BETWEEN THE EYES (*TOTAPHOTH*)! The sign reinstated: **'IT SHALL BE AS A MARK ON YOUR HAND AND AS FRONTLETS BETWEEN YOUR EYES (*u-le-totaphoth beyn eyneykha*)!'** THE BIBLICAL NOUN **TOTAPHOTH** (PHYLACTERIES / TEFILLIN)!
cccReferences: CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Deut 6:8; Deut 11:18; Matt 23:5.
historicalContext: The second key verse mandating head-phylacteries (*Tefillin shel rosh*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-hayah le-oth al-yadkhah u-le-totaphoth beyn eyneykha ki be-chazaq yad hotzi'anu YHVH mi-Mitzrayim*: *totaphoth* (head-frontlets / phylacteries, root *tatap* = headband/pendant).
historicalTrivia: The word *totaphoth* is used 3 times in the Bible (Exod 13:16; Deut 6:8; Deut 11:18) to denote the head-phylactery box worn on the forehead!

dominicalIntent: When Pharaoh let the people go, God did not lead them by way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near. For God said: 'Lest the people change their minds when they see war and return to Egypt' (*...ki amar Elohim pen-yinnahem ha-am bi-r'otham milchamah ve-shavu Mitzraymah*). GOD'S DIVINE PEDAGOGY: BYPASSING THE SHORT COASTAL ROUTE! God deliberately bypasses the short coastal military road ('The Way of the Philistines' / *Via Maris*) to protect fragile Israel: **'LEST THE PEOPLE CHANGE THEIR MINDS WHEN THEY SEE WAR AND RETURN TO EGYPT!'**
cccReferences: CCC 305 (Divine Providence guiding His people with gentle pedagogical wisdom); CCC 2575; Ps 107:7; 1 Cor 10:13.
historicalContext: The Northern coastal route (*Via Maris*) was heavily fortified with Egyptian fortresses and garrisoned by Philistine/Canaanite armies. Israel was unprepared for battle.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi be-shallach Par'oh eth-ha-am ve-lo-nacham Elohim derekh eretz Plishtim ki qarov hu ki amar Elohim pen-yinnahem ha-am bi-r'otham milchamah ve-shavu Mitzraymah*: *pen-yinnahem* ('lest they repent/regret/change mind').
crossReferences: Numbers 14:1-4; 1 Corinthians 10:13 ('God will not let you be tempted beyond your strength'); Psalm 107:7.
historicalTrivia: The *Via Maris* (coastal road) took only 10 days to reach Canaan, but Egyptian forts along the way would have crushed a civilian refugee march.

dominicalIntent: But God led the people around by the way of the wilderness toward the Red Sea. And the people of Israel went up out of the land of Egypt equipped for battle (*Vayyassev Elohim eth-ha-am derekh ha-midbar YAM-SUPH u-chamushim alu vney-YISRA'EL mi-eretz Mitzrayim*). LEADING TOWARD THE RED SEA (*YAM SUPH*)—MARCHING IN BATTLE ARRAY (*CHAMUSHIM*)! God detours Israel through the wilderness toward the **RED SEA (*YAM SUPH*)**. Israel marches out **equipped for battle / in 5-rank formation (*chamushim*)**!
cccReferences: CCC 1221 (The passage through the Red Sea prefiguring Holy Baptism); CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Exod 14:2; 1 Cor 10:1-2.
historicalContext: Leading Israel southeast toward the Red Sea. *Chamushim* means organized into 5 military divisions / ranks.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyassev Elohim eth-ha-am derekh ha-midbar YAM-SUPH u-chamushim alu vney-YISRA'EL mi-eretz Mitzrayim*: *YAM-SUPH* (Red Sea / Sea of Reeds). *chamushim* (in ranks of five / marshaled for battle, root *chamesh* = five).
crossReferences: Exodus 14:2; Joshua 1:14 ('equipped for battle' / *chamushim*); Joshua 4:12; 1 Corinthians 10:1-2.
historicalTrivia: The military term *chamushim* indicates Israel marched not as a chaotic rabble, but as a disciplined 5-column military host!

dominicalIntent: Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, for Joseph had made the sons of Israel solemnly swear, saying: 'God will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones with you from here' (*...ve-ha'althem eth-atzmothai mi-zzeh itthakhem*). MOSES CARRIES THE BONES OF JOSEPH—FULFILLING THE 400-YEAR OATH! Moses personally carries the mummified **bones of Joseph (*atzmoth Yoseph*)** out of Egypt, fulfilling Joseph's dying prophecy and oath in Genesis 50:25!
historicalContext: Carrying Joseph's coffin throughout the 40-year wilderness wanderings until his burial at Shechem (Josh 24:32).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vyiqach Moshe eth-atzmoth Yoseph immo ki hashbea hishbi'a eth-bney Yisra'el le'mor paqodh yiphqodh Elohim ethkhem ve-ha'althem eth-atzmothai mi-zzeh itthakhem*: *atzmoth Yoseph* ('bones of Joseph'). *paqodh yiphqodh* ('visiting He will surely visit!').
crossReferences: Genesis 50:25; Joshua 24:32; Hebrews 11:22 ('By faith Joseph, at the end of his life, made mention of the exodus... and gave directions concerning his bones').
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 11:22 highlights Joseph's command regarding his bones as one of the supreme acts of Old Testament faith!

dominicalIntent: And they moved on from Succoth and encamped at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness. Station 2 of the Exodus journey: Etham ('Fortress').
historicalContext: Etham (*Atuma*), a desert border outpost on the edge of the Egyptian wilderness barrier.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiss'u mi-Ssuccoth vayyachanu v-Etham bi-qtzeh ha-midbar*: *Etham* (border fortress on wilderness edge).
historicalTrivia: Etham lay at the boundary of the Egyptian border fortification system (*Shur*).

dominicalIntent: And the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of cloud to lead them along the way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, that they might travel by day and by night (*V-YHVH holekh liphneyhem yomam be-ammud anan... ve-laylah be-ammud esh...*). THE PILLAR OF CLOUD BY DAY AND THE PILLAR OF FIRE BY NIGHT! Yahweh Himself goes before Israel: (1) **By day in a PILLAR OF CLOUD (*be-ammud anan*)** to shade and guide them, (2) **By night in a PILLAR OF FIRE (*be-ammud esh*)** to give light! **THE VISIBLE SHEKINAH PRESENCE OF GOD GUARDING HIS CHURCH!**
cccReferences: CCC 697 (THE CLOUD AND THE LIGHT: The Holy Spirit manifested in the Pillar of Cloud and Fire guiding God's People); CCC 2575; Ps 78:14; Ps 105:39; 1 Cor 10:1-2.
historicalContext: The supernatural *Shekinah* column of cloud and fire moving continuously ahead of Israel's march.
translationNuances: Hebrew *V-YHVH holekh liphneyhem yomam be-ammud anan la-nchotham ha-dderekh ve-laylah be-ammud esh le-ha'ir lahem la-lekheth yomam va-laylah*: *ammud anan* ('pillar of cloud'). *ammud esh* ('pillar of fire').
crossReferences: Exodus 14:19-24; Psalm 78:14 ('In the daytime he led them with a cloud, and all the night with a fiery light'); Psalm 105:39; 1 Corinthians 10:1-2; Nehemiah 9:12.
historicalTrivia: CCC 697 teaches that the Pillar of Cloud and Fire was the Old Testament manifestation of the Holy Spirit leading the Church!

dominicalIntent: The pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night did not depart from before the people (*Lo-yamish ammud ha-anan yomam ve-ammud ha-esh laylah liphney ha-am*). UNFAILING DIVINE PRESENCE! The Pillar of Cloud by day and Pillar of Fire by night **NEVER DEPARTED (*Lo-yamish*)** from before the people throughout their 40-year journey! PREFIGURING CHRIST'S PROMISE: 'LO, I AM WITH YOU ALWAYS, EVEN TO THE END OF THE AGE' (MATT 28:20)!
cccReferences: CCC 697 (The permanent presence of the Holy Spirit); CCC 2575; Matt 28:20; Neh 9:19.
historicalContext: Unbroken 40-year manifestation of Yahweh's guiding presence.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Lo-yamish ammud ha-anan yomam ve-ammud ha-esh laylah liphney ha-am*: *Lo-yamish* ('did not remove / did not depart / did not cease', root *mush*).
crossReferences: Matthew 28:20 ('I am with you always, to the end of the age'); Nehemiah 9:19 ('The pillar of cloud... did not depart from them'); Psalm 121:5-8.
historicalTrivia: Nehemiah 9:19 marvels: 'In your great mercies you did not forsake them in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud... did not depart from them by day, nor the pillar of fire by night'!

dominicalIntent: The Lord said to Moses... Yahweh issues strategic military directives for encamping before the Red Sea.
cccReferences: CCC 1221 (The Red Sea passage prefiguring Baptismal liberation); CCC 2575.
historicalContext: Nisan 17, 1446 BC: Strategic divine trap set for Pharaoh's army.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayydabber YHVH el-Moshe le'mor*.
historicalTrivia: The crossing of the Red Sea is the central saving miracle of the Old Testament.

dominicalIntent: 'Tell the people of Israel to turn back and encamp in front of Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, in front of Baal-zephon; you shall encamp opposite it, by the sea.' THE DIVINE TRAP: ENCAMPING AT PI-HAHIROTH BEFORE BAAL-ZEPHON! Yahweh orders a tactical backtrack: Israel turns back and encamps at **Pi-hahiroth ('Mouth of Gorges')**, between **Migdol ('Watchtower')** and the Red Sea, facing **Baal-zephon ('Lord of the North')**! Creating a humanly inescapable cul-de-sac to lure Pharaoh into God's trap!
historicalContext: Pi-hahiroth (Egyptian *Pr-Hwt-Hrt*), Migdol (fortress line), and Baal-zephon (shrine to the Canaanite sea/storm god). Israel trapped between mountains, sea, and fortresses.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Dabber el-bney Yisra'el ve-yashuvu ve-yachanu liphney Pi ha-Chiroth beyn Migdol u-veyn ha-yyam liphney Ba'al Tzephon nikhto thachanu al-ha-yyam*: *yashuvu* ('let them turn back / reverse course').
historicalTrivia: Baal-zephon was worshipped by sailors as the master of sea storms; Yahweh deliberately crushed Pharaoh in front of Baal-zephon's sanctuary to prove Baal's powerlessness!

dominicalIntent: 'For Pharaoh will say of the people of Israel, "They are wandering aimslessly in the land; the wilderness has shut them in."' DIVINE STRATEGY: MAKING PHARAOH THINK ISRAEL IS TRAPPED! God explains His tactic: Pharaoh will conclude Israel is hopelessly lost (*nevukhim*) and hemmed in by the desert (*ssagar alehem ha-midbar*).
cccReferences: CCC 305 (God using the arrogance of tyrants for divine victory); CCC 2575.
historicalContext: Military reconnaissance reporting to Pharaoh that Israel had turned back into a dead-end coastal terrain.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-amar Par'oh li-vney Yisra'el nevukhim hem ba-aretz ssagar alehem ha-midbar*: *nevukhim* (tangled/confused/aimless). *ssagar* ('has closed/shut them in').
historicalTrivia: The verb *nevukhim* means wandering in confusion like cattle trapped in a ravine.

dominicalIntent: 'And I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and he will pursue them, and I will get glory over Pharaoh and all his host, and the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord.' And they did so. 'I WILL GET GLORY OVER PHARAOH!' Yahweh declares His ultimate purpose: **'I WILL GET GLORY OVER PHARAOH AND ALL HIS ARMY (*ve-ikkavdhah be-Phar'oh u-ve-khol-cheylo*), AND THE EGYPTIANS SHALL KNOW THAT I AM YAHWEH!'**
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (God's glory manifested in the destruction of tyranny); CCC 2575; Rom 9:17; Exod 14:18.
historicalContext: The definitive manifestation of Yahweh's glory (*kavod*) destroying Egypt's military superpower.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-chizqaqti eth-lev-Par'oh ve-radeph achareyhem ve-ikkavdhah be-Phar'oh u-ve-khol-cheylo ve-yadh'u Mitzrayim ki-ani YHVH vayya'assu-khen*: *ve-ikkavdhah* ('and I will be glorified / gain honor').
historicalTrivia: The noun *kavod* (glory) implies heavy, undeniable weight and majesty.

dominicalIntent: When the king of Egypt was told that the people had fled, the mind of Pharaoh and his servants was changed toward the people, and they said: 'What is this we have done, that we have let Israel go from serving us?' PHARAOH'S REGRET: 'WHAT HAVE WE DONE?!' Pharaoh and his courtiers regret releasing Israel, realizing their economic empire has lost its entire slave labor force.
historicalContext: Royal palace reaction when reports confirm Israel is not returning after 3 days.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyuggad le-melekh Mitzrayim ki varach ha-am vayyehaphekh levav Par'oh ve-avadav el-ha-am vayyo'mru mah-zoth assinu ki-shillachnu eth-Yisra'el me-ovdenu*: *vayyehaphekh* ('and was turned around / reversed').
historicalTrivia: Pharaoh realizes 600,000 adult male slaves have walked out with Egypt's gold!

dominicalIntent: So he made ready his chariot and took his army with him. Pharaoh personally hitches his war chariot and mobilizes the elite Egyptian army.
historicalContext: Mobilization of the royal Egyptian war chariot corps.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayye'ssor eth-rikhto ve-eth-ammo laqach immo*: *rikhto* (his war chariot/chariotry).
historicalTrivia: Egyptian war chariots were the most advanced military technology of the Bronze Age.

dominicalIntent: and took six hundred chosen chariots and all the other chariots of Egypt with officers over all of them (*...shes-me'oth rekhev bachur... ve-shalishim al-kullo*). PHARAOH'S CHARIOT ARMY: 600 CHOSEN WAR CHARIOTS! Pharaoh deploys: (1) **600 chosen elite chariots (*shes-me'oth rekhev bachur*)**, (2) All the remaining chariots of Egypt, (3) **Captains/officers (*shalishim*)** over every chariot!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The overwhelming worldly military power arrayed against God's defenseless people).
historicalContext: The 18th Dynasty royal chariot corps. A *shalish* was a 3rd man in the chariot (driver, shield-bearer, bowman/captain).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vyyiqach shes-me'oth rekhev bachur ve-khol rekhev Mitzrayim ve-shalishim al-kullo*: *rekhev bachur* ('chosen/select chariots'). *shalishim* (captains / 3rd-man chariot commanders).
crossReferences: Exodus 15:4 ('his chosen officers / *shalishav* were sunk in the Red Sea'); 2 Kings 7:2; 1 Kings 9:22.
historicalTrivia: The *shalish* ('three-man officer') was the elite chariot warrior of New Kingdom Egypt!

dominicalIntent: And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued the people of Israel while the people of Israel were going out defiantly (*...u-vney YISRA'EL yotz'im be-yad ramah*). ISRAEL MARCHING OUT WITH A HIGH HAND (*BE-YAD RAMAH*)! Pharaoh pursues Israel, while Israel marches out **with a high hand / triumphant confidence (*be-yad ramah*)**!
historicalContext: Marching under royal banners with defiant joy (*be-yad ramah*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyechazzeq YHVH eth-lev Par'oh melekh Mitzrayim vayyirdoph acharey bney Yisra'el u-vney Yisra'el yotz'im be-yad ramah*: *be-yad ramah* ('with a high/upraised hand' = boldly, triumphantly).
crossReferences: Numbers 33:3 ('the people of Israel went out boldly in the sight of all the Egyptians'); Numbers 15:30.
historicalTrivia: The idiom *be-yad ramah* ('with a high hand') signifies triumphant victory without fear.

dominicalIntent: The Egyptians pursued them, all Pharaoh's horses and chariots and his horsemen and his army, and overtook them encamped by the sea, by Pi-hahiroth, in front of Baal-zephon. Pharaoh's army overtakes Israel trapped against the sea at Pi-hahiroth.
historicalContext: The Egyptian army cornering Israel between the sea and the desert mountains.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyirdphu Mitzrayim achareyhem vayyassigu otham chanim al-ha-yyam kol-ssuss rekhev Phar'oh u-pharashav ve-cheylo al-Pi ha-Chiroth liphney Ba'al Tzephon*.
historicalTrivia: Israel is completely boxed in: open sea in front, mountains on flanks, 600 chariots behind.

dominicalIntent: When Pharaoh drew near, the people of Israel lifted up their eyes, and behold, the Egyptians were marching after them, and they feared greatly. And the people of Israel cried out to the Lord (*...vayyiyr'u me'od vayyitz'aqu bney-YISRA'EL el-YHVH*). PANIC AT THE RED SEA: ISRAEL CRIES OUT TO GOD! Israel sees Pharaoh's chariot army advancing; terror strikes: **they feared greatly (*vayyiyr'u me'od*) and cried out to Yahweh (*vayyitz'aqu... el-YHVH*)**!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The desperate cry of faith in the face of human impossibility); Ps 107:6.
historicalContext: Unarmed civilian refugees seeing 600 war chariots charging toward them.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-Phar'oh hiqriv vayyiss'u vney-Yisra'el eth-eyneyhem ve-hinneh Mitzrayim nosse'a achareyhem vayyiyr'u me'od vayyitz'aqu bney-Yisra'el el-YHVH*: *vayyitz'aqu* ('and they cried out loudly').
historicalTrivia: Israel's panic reveals how quickly human fear returns when physical eyes replace eyes of faith.

dominicalIntent: They said to Moses: 'Is it because there are no graves in Egypt that you have taken us away to die in the wilderness? What have you done to us in bringing us out of Egypt?' THE FIRST OF ISRAEL'S 10 DESERT COMPLAINTS: 'WERE THERE NO GRAVES IN EGYPT?!' In bitter sarcasm, Israel rebels against Moses: **'IS IT BECAUSE THERE ARE NO GRAVES IN EGYPT THAT YOU HAVE TAKEN US AWAY TO DIE IN THE WILDERNESS?!'**
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (The sin of murmuring and testing God); CCC 2575; Ps 106:7-8; 1 Cor 10:9-10.
historicalContext: Egypt was world-famous for its massive tombs, pyramids, and necropolises; Israel's sarcasm was razor-sharp.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mru el-Moshe ha-mi-bbli eyn-qvarim be-Mitzrayim leqachthanu la-muth ba-midbar mah-zoth assitha lanu le-hotzi'anu mi-Mitzrayim*: *ha-mi-bbli eyn-qvarim* ('is it from lack of graves?').
historicalTrivia: This is the very 1st of Israel's 10 rebellions/murmurings in the wilderness (cf. Num 14:22)!

dominicalIntent: 'Is not this what we said to you in Egypt, "Leave us alone that we may serve the Egyptians"? For it would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness.' Preference for slave security over divine freedom.
historicalContext: Slave mentality choosing comfortable bondage over faith-filled struggle.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ha-lo-zeh ha-davar asher dibbarnu eleykha be-Mitzrayim le'mor chadal mimmennu ve-na'avdhah eth-Mitzrayim ki tov lanu avodh eth-Mitzrayim mi-mmuthenu ba-midbar*.
historicalTrivia: Acts 7:39 notes: 'Our fathers refused to obey him, but thrust him aside, and in their hearts turned back to Egypt'.

dominicalIntent: And Moses said to the people: 'Fear not, stand firm, and see the salvation of the Lord, which he will work for you today. For the Egyptians whom you see today, you shall never see again' (*...Al-thiyr'u hithyatzvu u-r'u eth-YESHU'ATH YHVH...*). MOSES' IMMORTAL COMMAND: 'FEAR NOT, STAND FIRM, AND SEE THE SALVATION (*YESHU'AH*) OF YAHWEH!' Moses utters the supreme rallying cry of faith: **'FEAR NOT! STAND FIRM, AND SEE THE SALVATION (*YESHU'ATH / JESUS*) OF YAHWEH WHICH HE WILL WORK FOR YOU TODAY! FOR THE EGYPTIANS YOU SEE TODAY, YOU SHALL NEVER SEE AGAIN FOREVER!'**
cccReferences: CCC 1221 (The Red Sea passage as the definitive manifestation of divine Salvation *Yeshu'ah*); CCC 169 (Faith standing firm); CCC 2575; 2 Chron 20:17.
historicalContext: Prophetic command to stand still (*hithyatzvu*) and watch God fight.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Moshe el-ha-am al-thiyr'u hithyatzvu u-r'u eth-YESHU'ATH YHVH asher-ya'asseh lakhem ha-yom ki asher re'ithem eth-Mitzrayim ha-yom lo thossiphu lir'otham od ad-olam*: *hithyatzvu* ('stand firm / take your stand'). *YESHU'ATH* (salvation/deliverance, root *Yasha* -> **JESUS**!).
crossReferences: 2 Chronicles 20:17 ('Stand firm, hold your position, and see the salvation / *yeshu'ah* of the Lord'); Isaiah 30:15; Psalm 46:10.
historicalTrivia: The Hebrew word for salvation here is **YESHU'ATH** (*Yeshu'ah*), the exact Hebrew name of **JESUS**!

dominicalIntent: 'The Lord will fight for you, and you have only to be silent' (*YHVH yillachem lakhem ve-athem thacharishun*). 'YAHWEH WILL FIGHT FOR YOU; YOU HAVE ONLY TO BE SILENT!' Moses declares: **'YAHWEH WILL FIGHT FOR YOU (*YHVH yillachem lakhem*), AND YOU HAVE ONLY TO BE SILENT (*ve-athem thacharishun*)!'** GOD FIGHTS THE BATTLE!
historicalContext: The Divine Warrior (*YHVH Ish Milchamah*, Exod 15:3) fighting on behalf of His helpless people.
translationNuances: Hebrew *YHVH yillachem lakhem ve-athem thacharishun*: *thacharishun* ('you shall hold your peace / be silent / keep still', root *charash*).
historicalTrivia: Isaiah 30:15 echoes this: 'In returning and rest you shall be saved; in quietness and in trust shall be your strength'.

dominicalIntent: The Lord said to Moses: 'Why do you cry to me? Tell the people of Israel to go forward' (*...mah-titz'aq elai dabber el-bney-YISRA'EL ve-yiss'u*). GOD COMMANDS: 'GO FORWARD!' Yahweh instructs Moses: **'WHY DO YOU CRY TO ME?! TELL THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL TO GO FORWARD (*ve-yiss'u*)!'** MARCH DIRECTLY TOWARD THE SEA!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Prayer issuing into immediate decisive action).
historicalContext: The divine command to march directly toward the crashing waves of the Red Sea.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe mah-titz'aq elai dabber el-bney-YISRA'EL ve-yiss'u*: *ve-yiss'u* ('and let them march / pull up tent pegs / go forward!').
historicalTrivia: Rabbinic tradition records that the prince of Judah, **Nahshon son of Amminadab**, stepped into the sea up to his neck before the waters split!

dominicalIntent: 'Lift up your staff, and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it, that the people of Israel may go through the sea on dry ground' (*...u-vqa'ehu ve-yavo'u vney-YISRA'EL be-thokh ha-yyam ba-yyabashah*). COMMAND TO DIVIDE THE SEA (*U-VQA'EHU*)! Yahweh commands Moses: (1) **Lift up your staff (*ha-rem eth-mattekha*)**, (2) **Stretch out your hand over the sea**, (3) **DIVIDE IT (*u-vqa'ehu*)**, (4) Israel shall walk through on **DRY GROUND (*ba-yyabashah*)**!
cccReferences: CCC 1221 (The sea divided allowing Israel to pass on dry ground, prefiguring Baptism); CCC 2575; Ps 66:6; Ps 78:13.
historicalContext: Moses extending the Staff of God over the Red Sea.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-attha ha-rem eth-mattekha u-nteh eth-yadkha al-ha-yyam u-vqa'ehu ve-yavo'u vney-YISRA'EL be-thokh ha-yyam ba-yyabashah*: *u-vqa'ehu* ('and split/divide it', root *baqa*). *ba-yyabashah* ('on dry ground').
crossReferences: Psalm 66:6; Psalm 78:13 ('He divided the sea and let them pass through it'); Isaiah 63:12; 1 Corinthians 10:1-2.
historicalTrivia: The root *baqa* ('split/cleave') is used for splitting rocks to gush water and splitting the sea!

dominicalIntent: 'And I will harden the hearts of the Egyptians so that they shall go in after them, and I will get glory over Pharaoh and all his host, his chariots, and his horsemen.' Divine trap luring Pharaoh's army into the seabed.
historicalContext: Blinded Egyptian army driving full speed onto the dry seabed in pursuit of Israel.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-ani hineni mechazzeq eth-lev Mitzrayim ve-yavo'u achareyhem ve-ikkavdhah be-Phar'oh u-ve-khol-cheylo be-rikhto u-v-pharashav*.
historicalTrivia: Blinded by fury and hubris, the Egyptians charge directly into the sea canyon.

dominicalIntent: 'And the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord, when I have gotten glory over Pharaoh, his chariots, and his horsemen.' Re-iterating the supreme purpose: all Egypt knowing Yahweh is Lord.
cccReferences: CCC 2086; CCC 2575; Exod 7:5; Exod 14:4.
historicalContext: Universal divine recognition through the overthrow of Egypt's military.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-yad'u Mitzrayim ki-ani YHVH be-ikkavdhi be-Phar'oh be-rikhto u-v-pharashav*.
historicalTrivia: The 10th Plague and Red Sea combined to dismantle all Egyptian pagan theology.

dominicalIntent: Then the angel of God who was going before the host of Israel moved and went behind them, and the pillar of cloud moved from before them and stood behind them (*Vayyissa Mal'akh ha-Elohim... vayyavol mi-ppneyhem vayya'amod mi-a-chareyhem*). THE ANGEL OF GOD AND THE PILLAR OF CLOUD SHIFT REARWARD! The **Angel of God (*Mal'akh ha-Elohim*)** and the **Pillar of Cloud (*ammud ha-anan*)** move from the front to the rear, standing between Israel and Pharaoh's charging army as a protective divine shield!
cccReferences: CCC 336 (Angelic protection shielding God's People); CCC 697; CCC 2575; Exod 23:20; Isa 63:9.
historicalContext: The Angel of Yahweh placing Himself as a defensive wall between Egyptian chariots and Israel's rear guard.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyissa Mal'akh ha-Elohim ha-holekh liphney machaneh Yisra'el vayyelekhi mi-a-chareyhem vayyissa ammud ha-anan mi-ppneyhem vayya'amod mi-a-chareyhem*: *Mal'akh ha-Elohim* ('Angel of God').
crossReferences: Exodus 23:20; Isaiah 63:9 ('The Angel of his presence saved them'); Psalm 34:7; Genesis 48:16.
historicalTrivia: Isaiah 63:9 identifies this Angel of God (*Mal'akh ha-Elohim*) as the **Angel of His Presence** (*Mal'akh Panav*)!

dominicalIntent: coming between the host of Egypt and the host of Israel. And there was the cloud and the darkness, and it lit up the night without one coming near the other all night (*...vayyehi ha-anan ve-ha-choshekh vayya'er eth-ha-llaylah...*). DOUBLE-EFFECT CLOUD: DARKNESS TO EGYPTIANS, LIGHT TO ISRAEL! Miracle of the Cloud: (1) To Egypt, it was **pitch darkness (*ha-choshekh*)**, blocking their advance, (2) To Israel, **IT LIT UP THE NIGHT (*vayya'er eth-ha-llaylah*)**! Neither army came near the other all night!
cccReferences: CCC 697 (The divine Cloud bringing light to the faithful and darkness to the proud); CCC 2575; Ps 105:39; Wis 18:3.
historicalContext: Supernatural cloud wall providing illumination to Israel while blinding Egyptian charioteers.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyavo beyn machaneh Mitzrayim u-veyn machaneh Yisra'el vayyehi ha-anan ve-ha-choshekh vayya'er eth-ha-llaylah ve-lo-qarav zeh el-zeh kol-ha-llaylah*: *vayya'er* ('and it illuminated/lit up').
crossReferences: Wisdom 18:3; Psalm 105:39; Joshua 24:7 ('he put darkness between you and the Egyptians').
historicalTrivia: Wisdom 18:3 notes: 'You provided a flaming pillar of fire as a guide for your people's unknown journey'!

dominicalIntent: Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the Lord drove the sea back by a strong east wind all night and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided (*...v-YHVH nihag eth-ha-yyam be-ruach qadim azzah kol-ha-llaylah vayyassem eth-ha-yyam le-charavah vayyibbaq'u ha-mmayim*). THE STRONG EAST WIND SPLITS THE RED SEA (*VAYYIBBAQ'U HA-M MAYIM*)! Moses stretches his hand; **YAHWEH DRIVES THE SEA BACK WITH A POWERFUL EAST WIND (*be-ruach qadim azzah*) ALL NIGHT, MAKING THE SEA DRY LAND, AND THE WATERS WERE DIVIDED!**
cccReferences: CCC 1221 (THE RED SEA DIVIDED: The foundational Old Testament type of Holy Baptism); CCC 697; CCC 2575; Ps 78:13; Ps 136:13; 1 Cor 10:1-2.
historicalContext: All-night supernatural gale-force East Wind (*ruach qadim*) blasting a dry highway through the Red Sea waters.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyet Moshe eth-yado al-ha-yyam v-YHVH nihag eth-ha-yyam be-ruach qadim azzah kol-ha-llaylah vayyassem eth-ha-yyam le-charavah vayyibbaq'u ha-mmayim*: *le-charavah* ('into dry land'). *vayyibbaq'u* ('and were split/cleaved').
crossReferences: Psalm 78:13; Psalm 106:9; Psalm 136:13 ('who divided the Red Sea in two'); Isaiah 51:10; 1 Corinthians 10:1-2.
historicalTrivia: 1 Corinthians 10:1-2 explicitly interprets this: 'Our fathers were all under the cloud, and all passed through the sea, and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea'!

dominicalIntent: And the people of Israel went into the midst of the sea on dry ground, the waters being a wall to them on their right hand and on their left (*...ve-ha-mmayim lahem chomah mi-yminam u-mi-ssmo'lam*). WATERS A WALL ON RIGHT AND LEFT! ISRAEL MARCHES THROUGH ON DRY GROUND! Israel walks into the sea canyon: **THE WATERS WERE A LIQUID WALL (*chomah*) TO THEM ON THEIR RIGHT HAND AND ON THEIR LEFT!** PREFIGURING THE BAPTISMAL FONTS!
cccReferences: CCC 1221 (Passing through the waters of Baptism); CCC 2575; Heb 11:29; 1 Cor 10:1-2.
historicalContext: Israel walking through the seabed with vertical walls of water on both flanks.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyavo'u vney-Yisra'el be-thokh ha-yyam ba-yyabashah ve-ha-mmayim lahem chomah mi-yminam u-mi-ssmo'lam*: *chomah* (a defensive wall/rampart).
crossReferences: Hebrews 11:29 ('By faith the people crossed the Red Sea as on dry land'); Exodus 15:8; Nahum 3:8.
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 11:29 contrasts Israel's faith with Egypt's presumption: 'when the Egyptians attempted to do the same, they were drowned'!

dominicalIntent: The Egyptians pursued and went in after them into the midst of the sea, all Pharaoh's horses, his chariots, and his horsemen. The Egyptian army pursues blindly into the seabed canyon.
historicalContext: Pharaoh's cavalry charging down the dry seabed path in the dark.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyirdphu Mitzrayim vayyavo'u achareyhem kol ssuss Phar'oh rikhto u-pharashav el-thokh ha-yyam*.
historicalTrivia: Driven by fury, 600 war chariots plunge into the sea corridor.

dominicalIntent: And in the morning watch the Lord in the pillar of fire and of cloud looked down on the Egyptian forces and threw the Egyptian forces into a panic (*...Vayehi be-ashmorith ha-bboqer vayyashqeph YHVH... vayyaham eth machaneh Mitzrayim*). THE MORNING WATCH: YAHWEH LOOKS DOWN FROM THE PILLAR OF FIRE! In the **morning watch (*ashmorith ha-bboqer*)** (3:00 AM - 6:00 AM), Yahweh looks down from the Pillar of Fire and Cloud and **throws Pharaoh's army into terrifying panic (*vayyaham*)**!
historicalContext: The 4th/last watch of the night (3:00 AM to 6:00 AM sunrise). Thunder, lightning, and divine terror striking the Egyptians.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi be-ashmorith ha-bboqer vayyashqeph YHVH el-machaneh Mitzrayim be-ammud esh ve-anan vayyaham eth machaneh Mitzrayim*: *ashmorith ha-bboqer* ('morning watch'). *vayyashqeph* ('looked down / bent down'). *vayyaham* ('threw into panic/confusion').
crossReferences: Psalm 77:16-19 ('The clouds poured out water; the skies gave forth thunder... your lightning lighted up the world'); Psalm 18:14; Exodus 23:27.
historicalTrivia: Psalm 77:16-19 records that during this morning watch, Yahweh sent massive thunder, torrential rain, and lightning bolts directly into the seabed!

dominicalIntent: clogging their chariot wheels so that they drove heavily. And the Egyptians said: 'Let us flee from before Israel, for the Lord fights for them against the Egyptians' (*...Vayyo'mer Mitzrayim anussah mi-ppney YISRA'EL ki YHVH nillcham lahem be-Mitzrayim*). CHARIOT WHEELS CLOGGED! EGYPTIANS FLEE CRYING: 'YAHWEH FIGHTS FOR ISRAEL!' Yahweh twists/clogs their chariot wheels (*vayasasar eth ophan marchevothav*); the mud traps them. Panic-stricken, the Egyptians cry: **'LET US FLEE FROM ISRAEL, FOR YAHWEH FIGHTS FOR THEM AGAINST EGYPT!'**
cccReferences: CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Exod 14:14; Deut 20:4.
historicalContext: Chariot axles snapping and wheels sinking into the mud; Egyptian army in full retreat.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayassar eth ophan marchevothav vaynehaghehu bi-khveduth vayyo'mer Mitzrayim anussah mi-ppney Yisra'el ki YHVH nillcham lahem be-Mitzrayim*: *Vayassar* ('and he removed/swerved/clogged'). *bi-khveduth* ('with heaviness/difficulty').
historicalTrivia: Iron/bronze chariot wheels sank into the wet sea mud; horses panicked, breaking axles and trapping the entire Egyptian army!

dominicalIntent: Then the Lord said to Moses: 'Stretch out your hand over the sea, that the water may come back upon the Egyptians, upon their chariots, and upon their horsemen.' Command to return the waters upon Egypt.
historicalContext: Moses standing on the Eastern shore extending his rod to collapse the water walls.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe nteh eth-yadkha al-ha-yyam ve-yashuvu ha-mmayim al-Mitzrayim al-rikhto ve-al-pharashav*.
historicalTrivia: The collapse of the water walls marks the total destruction of Pharaoh's power.

dominicalIntent: So Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to its normal course when the morning appeared. And as the Egyptians fled into it, the Lord threw the Egyptians into the midst of the sea (*...vayna'er YHVH eth-Mitzrayim be-thokh ha-yyam*). THE COLLAPSE OF THE RED SEA! YAHWEH OVERTHROWS EGYPT! Moses stretches his hand; at daybreak, the sea crashes back with full force! As Egyptians try to flee into the returning wall, **YAHWEH SHOOK / OVERTHREW THE EGYPTIANS INTO THE MIDST OF THE SEA (*vayna'er YHVH eth-Mitzrayim*)**!
cccReferences: CCC 1221 (The drowning of Pharaoh's army as the type of Sin washed away in Baptism); CCC 2575; Ps 136:15.
historicalContext: Dawn collapse of the sea walls drowning the entire Egyptian chariot force.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyet Moshe eth-yado al-ha-yyam vayyashav ha-yyam li-phnoth boqer le-eythano u-Mitzrayim nassim li-qra'tho vayna'er YHVH eth-Mitzrayim be-thokh ha-yyam*: *li-phnoth boqer* ('at the turning of morning / dawn'). *vayna'er* ('and he shook off / overthrown', root *na'ar*).
crossReferences: Psalm 136:15 ('and overthrew / *shi'er* Pharaoh and his host in the Red Sea'); Nehemiah 9:11; Jude 1:5.
historicalTrivia: The verb *vayna'er* means 'to shake off like dust from a rug'; God shook off the Egyptian empire into the depths of the sea!

dominicalIntent: The waters returned and covered the chariots and the horsemen; of all the host of Pharaoh that had followed them into the sea, not one of them remained (*...lo-nish'ar bahem ad-echad*). NOT ONE EGYPTIAN SURVIVED! The crashing sea covers all chariots and horsemen: **'NOT A SINGLE ONE OF THEM REMAINED (*lo-nish'ar bahem ad-echad*)!'** TOTAL ANNIHILATION OF EGYPT'S ARMY!
cccReferences: CCC 1221 (Total destruction of the power of Satan and Sin in the waters of Baptism); CCC 2575; Ps 106:11.
historicalContext: Complete destruction of the 18th Dynasty royal chariot corps.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyashuvu ha-mmayim vaykhassu eth-ha-rrekhev ve-eth-ha-pparashim le-khol cheyl Phar'oh ha-bba'im achareyhem ba-yyam lo-nish'ar bahem ad-echad*: *lo-nish'ar... ad-echad* ('not remained among them even one!').
crossReferences: Psalm 106:11 ('The waters covered their adversaries; not one of them was left'); Exodus 15:5.
historicalTrivia: Psalm 106:11 quotes Exodus 14:28 word for word: *lo nish'ar mehem echad* ('not one of them was left')!

dominicalIntent: But the people of Israel walked on dry ground through the sea, the waters being a wall to them on their right hand and on their left. Contrast: Israel safe on dry ground (*ba-yyabashah*).
historicalContext: Israel standing safe on the Eastern shore of the Red Sea.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-vney Yisra'el halkhu va-yyabashah be-thokh ha-yyam ve-ha-mmayim lahem chomah mi-yminam u-mi-ssmo'lam*.
historicalTrivia: Re-iterates the miraculous dry ground path (*ba-yyabashah*).

dominicalIntent: Thus the Lord saved Israel that day from the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the seashore (*Vayyosha YHVH ba-yom ha-hu eth-YISRA'EL... vayyar YISRA'EL eth-Mitzrayim meth al-ssphath ha-yyam*). YAHWEH SAVED ISRAEL THAT DAY! EGYPTIANS DEAD ON THE SEASHORE! Scripture summarizes: **'THUS YAHWEH SAVED ISRAEL THAT DAY (*Vayyosha YHVH*) FROM THE HAND OF THE EGYPTIANS, AND ISRAEL SAW THE EGYPTIANS DEAD UPON THE SEASHORE!'**
cccReferences: CCC 1221 (The definitive act of Old Testament salvation); CCC 2575; Ps 106:10; Acts 7:36.
historicalContext: The morning after the crossing: bodies of Egyptian soldiers and broken chariots washed onto the Sinai shore.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyosha YHVH ba-yom ha-hu eth-Yisra'el mi-yad Mitzrayim vayyar Yisra'el eth-Mitzrayim meth al-ssphath ha-yyam*: *Vayyosha* (and He saved/delivered, root *yasha* -> **JESUS**!).
crossReferences: Psalm 106:10 ('So he saved them from the hand of the foe and redeemed them from the power of the enemy'); Jude 1:5.
historicalTrivia: Jude 1:5 explicitly attributes this salvation to Jesus: 'Jesus, who saved a people out of the land of Egypt'!

dominicalIntent: Israel saw the great power that the Lord used against the Egyptians, so the people feared the Lord, and they believed in the Lord and in his servant Moses (*...vayyiyr'u ha-am eth-YHVH vayya'aminu ba-YHVH u-v-Moshe avdo*). THEY BELIEVED IN YAHWEH AND IN HIS SERVANT MOSES! GRAND CLIMAX OF EXODUS 14: Israel sees the great hand (*ha-yyad ha-ggedolah*) of Yahweh: **'SO THE PEOPLE FEARED YAHWEH, AND THEY BELIEVED IN YAHWEH AND IN HIS SERVANT MOSES (*vayya'aminu ba-YHVH u-v-Moshe avdo*)!'**
cccReferences: CCC 1221 (Faith in God born from experiencing the baptismal victory); CCC 2575 (Moses recognized as God's faithful servant); John 5:46; Heb 3:5.
historicalContext: Total national conversion to faith in Yahweh and submission to Moses.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyar Yisra'el eth-ha-yyad ha-ggedolah asher assah YHVH be-Mitzrayim vayyiyr'u ha-am eth-YHVH vayya'aminu ba-YHVH u-v-Moshe avdo*: *ha-yyad ha-ggedolah* ('the great hand/power'). *vayya'aminu* ('and they believed/trusted', root *aman* = Amen!).
crossReferences: John 5:46 ('If you believed Moses, you would believe me; for he wrote of me'); Hebrews 3:5 ('Moses was faithful in all God's house as a servant'); Psalm 106:12.
historicalTrivia: Psalm 106:12 summarizes this moment: 'Then they believed his words; they sang his praise' (leading directly into the Song of Moses in Exodus 15)!

dominicalIntent: Then Moses and the people of Israel sang this song to the Lord, saying: 'I will sing to the Lord, for he has triumphed gloriously; the horse and his rider he has thrown into the sea' (*...Ashirah l-YHVH ki-gha'oh ga'ah suss ve-rokhevo ramah va-yyam*). THE SONG OF MOSES / SONG OF THE SEA (*SHIRAT HA-YAM*)! Moses and Israel sing the fundamental hymn of redemption: **'I WILL SING TO YAHWEH, FOR HE HAS TRIUMPHED GLORIOUSLY (*ki-gha'oh ga'ah*); THE HORSE AND HIS RIDER HE HAS THROWN INTO THE SEA!'** **SUNG AT EVERY EASTER VIGIL MASS AS THE 3RD RESPONSORIAL PSALM, AND IN REVELATION 15:3 BY THE REDEEMED SAINTS IN HEAVEN!**
cccReferences: CCC 1167 (The Song of Moses *Shirat Ha-Yam* as the archetype of Christian liturgical praise); CCC 1221; CCC 2575; CCC 2619; Rev 15:3.
historicalContext: Nisan 17, 1446 BC: The victory hymn sung on the Eastern shore of the Red Sea. One of the oldest poetic texts in the Hebrew Bible.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Az yashir-Moshe u-vney Yisra'el eth-ha-shirah ha-zoth le-YHVH vayyo'mru le'mor ashirah l-YHVH ki-gha'oh ga'ah suss ve-rokhevo ramah va-yyam*: *ki-gha'oh ga'ah* ('for in exalting He has exalted / triumphed gloriously'). *Shirat Ha-Yam* ('Song of the Sea').
crossReferences: Revelation 15:3 ('And they sing the Song of Moses, the servant of God, and the Song of the Lamb'); Psalm 106:12; Judges 5:1; 2 Samuel 22:1.
historicalTrivia: Revelation 15:3 reveals that in Heaven, all redeemed martyrs sing the **Song of Moses and the Song of the Lamb**!

dominicalIntent: 'The Lord is my strength and my song, and he has become my salvation; this is my God, and I will praise him, my father's God, and I will exalt him' (*Ozzi ve-zimrath YAH vayyehi-li li-YESHU'AH zeh Eli ve-anvehu Elohey avi va-arommenhu*). YAHWEH IS MY STRENGTH, SONG, AND SALVATION (*YESHU'AH*)! THE TRINITARIAN CONFESSION! The song proclaims: **'YAH IS MY STRENGTH AND SONG, AND HE HAS BECOME MY SALVATION (*YESHU'AH*)! THIS IS MY GOD (*ZEH ELI*), AND I WILL PREPARE HIM A DWELLING PLACE (*ve-anvehu*)!'**
historicalContext: Confessing Yahweh as personal God (*Eli*) and Father's God (*Elohey avi*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ozzi ve-zimrath YAH vayyehi-li li-YESHU'AH zeh Eli ve-anvehu Elohey avi va-arommenhu*: *Ozzi* (my strength). *YESHU'AH* (salvation -> **JESUS**!). *ve-anvehu* ('I will glorify Him / build Him a sanctuary/home', root *navah*).
crossReferences: Psalm 118:14; Isaiah 12:2 ('God is my salvation; I will trust and not be afraid; for the Lord God is my strength and my song'); Matthew 1:21.
historicalTrivia: Isaiah 12:2 and Psalm 118:14 quote Exodus 15:2 word for word! The Targum Onkelos translates *ve-anvehu* as 'I will build Him a Sanctuary'.

dominicalIntent: 'The Lord is a man of war; the Lord is his name' (*YHVH ISH MILCHAMAH YHVH SHEMO*). THE DIVINE WARRIOR! The Song proclaims: **'YAHWEH IS A MAN OF WAR (*YHVH Ish Milchamah*); YAHWEH IS HIS NAME!'** God revealed as the invincible Divine Warrior who crushes demonic tyranny.
cccReferences: CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Rev 19:11-16 (Christ the Divine Warrior riding on a white horse).
historicalContext: Yahweh defeating Pharaoh's armies without Israel lifting a sword.
translationNuances: Hebrew *YHVH ish milchamah YHVH shemo*: *ish milchamah* ('man of war / warrior').
crossReferences: Revelation 19:11-16; Isaiah 42:13 ('The Lord goes forth like a mighty man, like a man of war he stirs up his zeal'); Psalm 24:8.
historicalTrivia: Psalm 24:8 echoes this: 'Who is this King of glory? The Lord, strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle!'

dominicalIntent: 'Pharaoh's chariots and his host he cast into the sea, and his chosen officers are sunk in the Red Sea' (*...u-mivchar shalishav tubb'u ve-YAM-SUPH*). Overthrow of Pharaoh's elite: his chosen 3rd-man officers (*mivchar shalishav*) are drowned in the Red Sea (*Yam Suph*).
historicalContext: Sinking of Egypt's elite chariot commanders (*shalishim*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Marchevoth Phar'oh ve-cheylo yarah va-yyam u-mivchar shalishav tubb'u ve-YAM-SUPH*: *tubb'u* ('were drowned / plunged into mud/depths').
historicalTrivia: The verb *tubb'u* means sinking into deep mud (*tobha*).

dominicalIntent: 'The floods covered them; they went down into the depths like a stone' (*...yarhu vi-mtzoloth khemow-aven*). SINKING LIKE A STONE (*KHEMOW-AVEN*)! The heavy bronze-armored Egyptian soldiers sink into the ocean depths (*metzoloth*) like stones.
historicalContext: Heavy armor pulling soldiers down into the sea floor.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Tehomoth yekhasyumu yarhu vi-mtzoloth khemow-aven*: *tehomoth* (oceanic deeps). *metzoloth* (depths/abysses). *khemow-aven* ('like a stone').
crossReferences: Nehemiah 9:11 ('their pursuers you cast into the depths, as a stone into mighty waters'); Exodus 15:10.
historicalTrivia: Nehemiah 9:11 directly quotes Exodus 15:5!

dominicalIntent: 'Your right hand, O Lord, glorious in power, your right hand, O Lord, shatters the enemy' (*Yemin-kha YHVH ne'edari ba-kkoach yemin-kha YHVH tir'atz oyev*). THE ALMIGHTY RIGHT HAND OF YAHWEH! Exalting the Right Hand (*Yemin*) of Yahweh: **'YOUR RIGHT HAND, O YAHWEH, GLORIOUS IN POWER; YOUR RIGHT HAND SHATTERS THE ENEMY!'** PREFIGURING CHRIST SEATED AT THE RIGHT HAND OF GOD!
cccReferences: CCC 659 (Christ seated at the Right Hand of the Father); CCC 2575; Ps 118:15-16; Acts 2:33.
historicalContext: The Right Hand (*Yemin*) as the symbol of divine omnipotence and messianic power.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Yemin-kha YHVH ne'edari ba-kkoach yemin-kha YHVH tir'atz oyev*: *yemin-kha* ('your right hand'). *tir'atz* ('shatters / smashes to pieces').
crossReferences: Psalm 118:15-16 ('The right hand of the Lord does valiantly, the right hand of the Lord exalts'); Acts 2:33; Hebrews 1:3.
historicalTrivia: In Catholic theology, the Right Hand of God (*Yemin YHVH*) is a title for the Son of God, through whom all things were created and saved.

dominicalIntent: 'In the greatness of your majesty you overthrow your adversaries; you send out your fury; it consumes them like stubble' (*...thashallach charonkha yo'khlemo ka-qqash*). DIVINE WRATH CONSUMING IDOLATRY LIKE STUBBLE (*KA-QQASH*)! God's burning wrath (*charonkha*) consumes the proud persecutors like dry straw/stubble.
cccReferences: CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Heb 12:29 ('Our God is a consuming fire').
historicalContext: Fire imagery depicting divine judgment destroying human pride.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-v-rov ge'onkha thaharos qameykha thashallach charonkha yo'khlemo ka-qqash*: *ge'onkha* (your majesty/exaltation). *ka-qqash* ('like stubble/straw').
historicalTrivia: Malachi 4:1 uses *ka-qqash* ('like stubble') for the day of judgment.

dominicalIntent: 'At the blast of your nostrils the waters piled up; the floods stood up in a heap; the deeps congealed in the heart of the sea' (*U-ve-ruach appeykha ne'ermu mayim nitzvu khmo-ned nozlim qaph'u thehomoth be-lev-yam*). THE BLAST OF GOD'S NOSTRILS CONGEALS THE DEEPS! Poetic description: at the breath/blast of Yahweh's nostrils (*ruach appeykha*), the flowing waters stood up like a solid wall/heap (*ned*), and the ocean deeps **congealed/froze solid (*qaph'u*)** in the heart of the sea!
historicalContext: The East Wind depicted as the mighty breath of Yahweh's nostrils.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-ve-ruach appeykha ne'ermu mayim nitzvu khmo-ned nozlim qaph'u thehomoth be-lev-yam*: *ruach appeykha* ('breath of your nostrils/anger'). *qaph'u* ('congealed / curdled / turned solid').
crossReferences: Psalm 78:13 ('He made the waters stand like a heap / *ned*'); Exodus 14:22; 2 Samuel 22:16.
historicalTrivia: The verb *qapha* means to curdle like cheese or freeze solid like ice!

dominicalIntent: 'The enemy said, "I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide the spoil, my desire shall have its fill of them. I will draw my sword, my hand shall destroy them."' THE HUBRIS OF THE PERSECUTOR! Mimicking Pharaoh's arrogant staccato boasts: 'I will pursue (*ardoph*), I will overtake (*assigh*), I will divide spoil (*achalleq shalal*), my soul shall be satisfied (*thimla'emo naphshi*)!'
cccReferences: CCC 2086 (The pride of tyrants claiming self-sufficiency); CCC 2575; Ps 10:2-4.
historicalContext: Poetic mimicry of Pharaoh's arrogant battle speeches.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Amar oyev ardoph assigh achalleq shalal thimla'emo naphshi ariq charbi thorishemo yadi*: 5 rapid staccato verbs expressing blind hubris.
historicalTrivia: The 5 rapid verbs without conjunctions (*ardoph, assigh, achalleq, thimla'emo, ariq*) create a breathless sense of arrogant urgency.

dominicalIntent: 'You blew with your wind; the sea covered them; they sank like lead in the mighty waters' (*Nashaphtha ve-ruchakha kissamo yam tzalalu ka-ofereth be-mayim addirim*). SINKING LIKE LEAD IN THE MIGHTY WATERS! One breath of God (*Nashaphtha ve-ruchakha*) undoes all human military arrogance: **'THEY SANK LIKE LEAD (*tzalalu ka-ofereth*) IN THE MIGHTY WATERS!'**
historicalContext: Instant destruction of the Egyptian force.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Nashaphtha ve-ruchakha kissamo yam tzalalu ka-ofereth be-mayim addirim*: *tzalalu* ('they plunged/sank into the abyss'). *ka-ofereth* ('like heavy lead').
historicalTrivia: Lead (*ofereth*) was the heaviest common metal known in antiquity.

dominicalIntent: 'Who is like you, O Lord, among the gods? Who is like you, majestic in holiness, awesome in glorious deeds, doing wonders?' (*Mi-khamokhah ba-elim YHVH mi kamokhah ne'edar ba-qqodesh nora thehilloth ossheh phele*). 'WHO IS LIKE YOU O YAHWEH AMONG THE GODS?!' THE SUPREME HYMNIC DECLARATION OF DIVINE INCOMPARABILITY! The Song acclaims: **'WHO IS LIKE YOU, O YAHWEH, AMONG THE GODS (*Mi-khamokhah ba-elim YHVH*)?! WHO IS LIKE YOU, MAJESTIC IN HOLINESS (*ne'edar ba-qqodesh*), AWESOME IN PRAISES (*nora thehilloth*), DOING WONDERS (*ossheh phele*)?!'**
cccReferences: CCC 2086 (THE UNCONTAINABLE HOLINESS AND UNICITY OF GOD: 'Who is like Yahweh?'); CCC 2575; Ps 86:8; Ps 89:6-8; Mic 7:18.
historicalContext: Liturgical climax proclaiming Yahweh's absolute transcendence over all pagan idols.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Mi-khamokhah ba-elim YHVH mi kamokhah ne'edar ba-qqodesh nora thehilloth ossheh phele*: *Mi-khamokhah* ('Who is like You?'). *ne'edar ba-qqodesh* ('glorious/majestic in holiness'). *ossheh phele* ('doing wonder/miracle').
crossReferences: Psalm 86:8 ('There is none like you among the gods, O Lord'); Psalm 89:6-8; Micah 7:18 ('Who is a God like you, pardoning iniquity?'); 1 Samuel 2:2.
historicalTrivia: The Hebrew acronym for **M**i-**kh**amokhah **b**a-elim **Y**HVH forms the name **MACCABEE** (*Makkabi* = 'Who is like You among the gods, Yahweh?'), adopted by the heroic Jewish martyrs in 167 BC!

dominicalIntent: 'You stretched out your right hand; the earth swallowed them.' God extending His right hand; the abyss/earth swallows the persecutors.
historicalContext: Poetic imagery of the sea floor consuming Egypt's army.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Natitha yemin-kha thivla me-mo eretz*: *thivla me-mo eretz* ('the earth/underworld swallowed them').
historicalTrivia: The seabed is poetically called *eretz* (the underworld/abyss).

dominicalIntent: 'You have led in your steadfast love the people whom you have redeemed; you have guided them by your strength to your holy abode' (*Nachitha ve-chasdkha am-zu ga'altha nehaltha ve-ozkha el-neveh qodshekha*). COVENANT LOVE (*CHESED*) AND REDEMPTION (*GE'ULLAH*) GUIDING TO GOD'S HOLY ABODE! Proclaiming God's covenant love: **'YOU HAVE LED IN YOUR STEADFAST LOVE (*Chesed*) THE PEOPLE WHOM YOU HAVE REDEEMED (*ga'altha*); YOU HAVE GUIDED THEM BY YOUR STRENGTH TO YOUR HOLY ABODE (*neveh qodshekha*)!'**
cccReferences: CCC 2063; CCC 2575 (God's *Chesed* leading redeemed believers to the heavenly sanctuary); Ps 77:15; Ps 78:54.
historicalContext: Predicting the march to Mount Sinai and the Promised Land / Mount Zion (*neveh qodshekha*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Nachitha ve-chasdkha am-zu ga'altha nehaltha ve-ozkha el-neveh qodshekha*: *ve-chasdkha* ('in your covenant love/mercy'). *ga'altha* ('you have redeemed as Kinsman-Redeemer', root *ga'al*). *neveh qodshekha* ('your holy dwelling/pasture').
crossReferences: Psalm 77:15 ('You with your arm redeemed your people'); Psalm 78:54; Isaiah 63:9; Psalm 23:2.
historicalTrivia: The verb *ga'al* identifies Yahweh as Israel's *Go'el* (Kinsman-Redeemer who ransoms His family).

dominicalIntent: 'The peoples have heard; they tremble; pangs have seized the inhabitants of Philistia.' SURROUNDING PAGAN NATIONS TREMBLING WITH TERROR! The report of the Red Sea crossing strikes terror into Philistia (*Pelesheth*).
historicalContext: The international impact of the Red Sea miracle across Canaan.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Sham'u ammim yirgazun chil achaz yoshtvey Pelesheth*: *yirgazun* ('they quake/tremble'). *chil* ('writhing labor pangs').
crossReferences: Joshua 2:9-11 (Rahab confirming this terror 40 years later!); Psalm 48:6.
historicalTrivia: Rahab in Joshua 2:9 confirms this exact prophecy: 'terror of you has fallen upon us... our hearts melted'!

dominicalIntent: 'Now are the chiefs of Edom dismayed; trembling seizes the leaders of Moab; all the inhabitants of Canaan have melted away' (*...namogu kol yoshtvey Kna'an*). THE CANAANITES MELT AWAY IN FEAR! Prophesying that the chiefs of **Edom**, the leaders of **Moab**, and **all the inhabitants of Canaan have melted away (*namogu*)** in terror before Israel's advance!
cccReferences: CCC 2575; Josh 2:11; Josh 5:1.
historicalContext: International dread paralyzing Edom, Moab, and Canaanite kings.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Az nivhalu alluphey Edom eyley Mo'av yo'chazemo ra'adh namogu kol yoshtvey Kna'an*: *namogu* ('have melted away / dissolved', root *mug*).
crossReferences: Joshua 2:11 ('as soon as we heard it, our hearts melted'); Joshua 5:1 ('their hearts melted and there was no longer any spirit in them'); Psalm 107:26.
historicalTrivia: Joshua 5:1 records the fulfillment when Israel crossed the Jordan: the hearts of all Canaanite kings melted (*namog*)!

dominicalIntent: 'Terror and dread fall upon them; because of the greatness of your arm, they are as still as a stone, till your people, O Lord, pass by, till the people pass by whom you have purchased' (*...ad-ya'avor am-zu qanitha*). UNTIL THE PEOPLE PASS BY WHOM YOU PURCHASED (*QANITHA*)! God's mighty arm freezes pagan nations like stones until **the people whom You purchased (*am-zu qanitha*)** pass through! CITED IN ACTS 20:28 AND 1 CORINTHIANS 6:20!
cccReferences: CCC 608 (The Church purchased by the Blood of Christ); CCC 2575; Acts 20:28 ('the Church of God which he obtained with his own blood'); 1 Cor 6:20 ('you were bought with a price').
historicalContext: The covenant acquisition (*qanitha*) of Israel as God's purchased possession.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Tippol alehem eymatha va-phachadh bi-gdol zro'akha yiddmu ka-aven ad-ya'avor amkha YHVH ad-ya'avor am-zu qanitha*: *qanitha* ('you have acquired / purchased / created').
crossReferences: Acts 20:28; 1 Corinthians 6:20; Psalm 74:2 ('Remember your congregation, which you have purchased of old'); Isaiah 43:21.
historicalTrivia: St. Paul's phrase 'bought with a price' (*ēgorasthēte timēs*, 1 Cor 6:20) directly draws from Exodus 15:16's *am-zu qanitha*!

dominicalIntent: 'You will bring them in and plant them on your own mountain, the place, O Lord, which you have made for your abode, the sanctuary, O Lord, which your hands have established' (*Thvi'emo ve-thitta'emo be-har nachalathkha... miqqedash Adonai konnu yadeykha*). PLANTING ISRAEL ON GOD'S HOLY MOUNTAIN AND SANCTUARY! Prophesying the entry into Canaan: **'YOU WILL BRING THEM IN AND PLANT THEM ON YOUR MOUNTAIN OF INHERITANCE (*be-har nachalathkha*), THE SANCTUARY (*MIQQEDASH*), O LORD, WHICH YOUR HANDS HAVE ESTABLISHED!'** PROPHESYING MOUNT ZION AND THE JERUSALEM TEMPLE!
cccReferences: CCC 1197 (The Temple and Holy Mountain as the sanctuary established by God); CCC 2575; Ps 78:54-55; Heb 9:11; Rev 21:2.
historicalContext: Prophetic vision of Mount Zion and the Sanctuary (*Miqqedash*) established by God.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Thvi'emo ve-thitta'emo be-har nachalathkha makhon le-shivthakaha pha'altha YHVH miqqedash Adonai konnu yadeykha*: *har nachalathkha* ('mountain of your inheritance'). *miqqedash* (sanctuary/temple). *konnu* ('have established/founded').
historicalTrivia: This is the very first time the word **Miqqedash** (Sanctuary / Temple) appears in Sacred Scripture!

dominicalIntent: 'The Lord will reign forever and ever' (*YHVH YIMLOKH LE-OLAM VA-ED*). GRAND DOXOLOGICAL CLIMAX: 'YAHWEH WILL REIGN FOREVER AND EVER!' The Song of Moses concludes with the eternal kingdom proclamation: **'YAHWEH SHALL REIGN FOREVER AND EVER (*YHVH yimlokh le-olam va-ed*)!'** **CITED IN REVELATION 11:15 AT THE 7TH TRUMPET: 'THE KINGDOM OF THE WORLD HAS BECOME THE KINGDOM OF OUR LORD AND OF HIS CHRIST, AND HE SHALL REIGN FOREVER AND EVER!'**
cccReferences: CCC 2816 (THE KINGDOM OF GOD: 'Yahweh shall reign forever and ever' fulfilled in the eternal Kingdom of Christ); CCC 2575; Rev 11:15; Ps 146:10.
historicalContext: Eternal enthronement acclamation of Yahweh as Sovereign King of the Universe.
translationNuances: Hebrew *YHVH yimlokh le-olam va-ed*: *yimlokh* ('shall reign as King'). *le-olam va-ed* ('forever and unto eternity').
crossReferences: Revelation 11:15 ('and he shall reign forever and ever / *basileusei eis tous aiōnas tōn aiōnōn*'); Psalm 146:10; Psalm 10:16; Micah 4:7.
historicalTrivia: Revelation 11:15 translates Exodus 15:18 into Greek as *basileusei eis tous aiōnas tōn aiōnōn* ('He shall reign for ages of ages')!

dominicalIntent: For when the horses of Pharaoh with his chariots and his horsemen went into the sea, the Lord brought back the waters of the sea upon them, but the people of Israel walked on dry ground through the midst of the sea. Prose narrative summary connecting the Song back to the historical event.
historicalContext: Historical prose summary of the Red Sea overthrow.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ki ba ssuss Phar'oh be-rikhto u-v-pharashav ba-yyam vayyashav YHVH alehem eth-mey ha-yyam u-vney Yisra'el halkhu va-yyabashah be-thokh ha-yyam*.
historicalTrivia: Prose hook bridging the Song of Moses (vv. 1-18) to Miriam's antiphonal response (vv. 20-21).

dominicalIntent: Then Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a tambourine in her hand, and all the women went out after her with tambourines and dancing (*Vattiqach Miryam ha-nnevi'ah achoth Aaron eth-ha-ttoph be-yadah...*). MIRIAM THE PROPHETESS LEADS THE WOMEN IN TAMBOURINE DANCE! **Miriam the Prophetess (*Miryam ha-nnevi'ah*)**, Aaron's sister, takes a tambourine/timbrel (*toph*) in hand; all the women follow her with **tambourines and liturgical dancing (*be-thuppim u-vi-mcholoth*)**! FIRST WOMAN TITLED PROPHETESS IN SCRIPTURE!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Miriam leading liturgical song of praise); CCC 2619; Judg 11:34; 1 Sam 18:6; Ps 150:4.
historicalContext: Liturgical victory dance (*machol*) accompanied by frame drums / tambourines (*thuppim*). Miriam is the 1st woman given the title *Nevi'ah* (Prophetess).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vattiqach Miryam ha-nnevi'ah achoth Aaron eth-ha-ttoph be-yadah vat-tetzenah khol-ha-nashim achareha be-thuppim u-vi-mcholoth*: *Miryam ha-nnevi'ah* ('Miriam the Prophetess'). *thuppim* (frame drums / tambourines). *mcholoth* (choral round-dances).
crossReferences: Judges 11:34; 1 Samuel 18:6; Psalm 68:25 ('in the midpoint the maidens playing tambourines'); Psalm 150:4; Luke 1:46-55 (Magnificat!).
historicalTrivia: Miriam's song prefigures the Virgin Mary's **Magnificat** (Luke 1:46-55); both prophetesses lead God's people in exultant praise for divine liberation!

dominicalIntent: And Miriam sang to them: 'Sing to the Lord, for he has triumphed gloriously; the horse and his rider he has thrown into the sea' (*Vatta'an lahem Miryam Shiru l-YHVH ki-gha'oh ga'ah...*). MIRIAM'S ANTIPHONAL RESPONSE! Miriam leads the women in the roaring antiphonal refrain: **'SING TO YAHWEH, FOR HE HAS TRIUMPHED GLORIOUSLY; THE HORSE AND HIS RIDER HE HAS THROWN INTO THE SEA!'**
cccReferences: CCC 2575; CCC 2619; Exod 15:1.
historicalContext: Antiphonal call-and-response liturgy (*Vatta'an lahem* = 'And Miriam sang responsively to them').
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vatta'an lahem Miryam shiru l-YHVH ki-gha'oh ga'ah suss ve-rokhevo ramah va-yyam*: *Vatta'an* ('and she answered/responded antiphonally').
historicalTrivia: Antiphonal singing (choirs responding back and forth) originated with Miriam's chorus at the Red Sea!

dominicalIntent: Then Moses led Israel onward from the Red Sea, and they went into the wilderness of Shur. They went three days in the wilderness and found no water (*...vayyelkhu shelosheth yamim ba-midbar ve-lo-matz'u mayim*). MARCH INTO THE WILDERNESS OF SHUR: 3 DAYS WITHOUT WATER! Moses leads Israel away from the Red Sea into the **Wilderness of Shur**. They march for **3 days (*shelosheth yamim*)** into the burning desert without finding water! TRIAL OF FAITH FOLLOWING TRIUMPH!
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (The wilderness testing purifying Israel's faith); CCC 2575; Exod 17:1; Num 33:8.
historicalContext: Entering the northwestern Sinai desert (*Shur* = 'Wall', referring to the border fortresses). 3-day desert march to Marah.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyassa Moshe eth-Yisra'el mi-YAM-SUPH vayyetze'u el-midbar-Shur vayyelkhu shelosheth yamim ba-midbar ve-lo-matz'u mayim*: *midbar-Shur* ('Wilderness of Shur/Wall').
historicalTrivia: Notice: 3 days after the glorious Red Sea triumph, Israel faces severe thirst in the desert, teaching that trials immediately follow spiritual breakthroughs.

dominicalIntent: When they came to Marah, they could not drink the water of Marah because it was bitter; therefore it was named Marah (*...ki marim hem al-ken qara-shmah Marah*). THE BITTER WATERS OF MARAH! They reach an oasis, but the water is undrinkable because it is **bitter (*marim*)**; therefore the place is named **MARAH ('BITTERNESS')**!
cccReferences: CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Ruth 1:20.
historicalContext: Marah (*Ain Hawarah*), a desert spring saturated with bitter magnesium sulfate (Epsom salts).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyavo'u Marathah ve-lo yakhalu li-shthoth mayim mi-Mmarah ki marim hem al-ken qara-shmah Marah*: *Marah* (bitter/bitterness).
crossReferences: Ruth 1:20 ('Call me Marah, for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me'); Numbers 33:8-9.
historicalTrivia: The spring *Ain Hawarah* in Sinai is still known today for its bitter, saline waters.

dominicalIntent: And the people murmured against Moses, saying: 'What shall we drink?' (*Vayyillonu ha-am al-Moshe le'mor mah-nishtheh*). MURMURING AT MARAH! The people murmur/complain against Moses: **'WHAT SHALL WE DRINK?!'** (*mah-nishtheh*).
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (The sin of murmuring against God's appointed shepherd); CCC 2575; 1 Cor 10:10; Phil 2:14.
historicalContext: Rebellion born of physical thirst and lack of trust in God.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyillonu ha-am al-Moshe le'mor mah-nishtheh*: *Vayyillonu* ('and they grumbled/murmured', root *lun*).
crossReferences: 1 Corinthians 10:10 ('nor grumble, as some of them did and were destroyed by the Destroyer'); Philippians 2:14; Exodus 16:2.
historicalTrivia: 1 Corinthians 10:10 warns Christians against following Israel's example of grumbling (*gongyzō*).

dominicalIntent: And he cried to the Lord, and the Lord showed him a log, and he threw it into the water, and the water became sweet. There the Lord made for them a statute and a rule, and there he tested them (*...vayyorehu YHVH etz vayyashlekh el-ha-mmayim vayyimthqu ha-mmayim...*). THE TREE THAT SWEETENED THE BITTER WATERS—PREFIGURING THE WOOD OF THE CROSS! Moses cries to Yahweh; Yahweh shows him **a tree/log (*etz*)**; Moses throws the tree into the bitter water, and **THE WATER BECOMES SWEET (*vayyimthqu ha-mmayim*)**! **PATRISTIC EXEGESIS (ST. AMBROSE, ST. AUGUSTINE, ST. CYRIL) UNANIMOUSLY IDENTIFIES THIS TREE (*ETZ*) AS THE WOOD OF THE CROSS OF CHRIST (*LIGNUM CRUCIS*), WHICH SWEETENS ALL BITTER SUFFERING AND MAKES SALVATION FLOW!**
cccReferences: CCC 617 (THE WOOD OF THE CROSS: The Tree of Marah prefiguring the Cross *Lignum Crucis* sweetening the bitterness of sin and death); CCC 1221; CCC 2575; Gal 3:13; 1 Pet 2:24.
historicalContext: Throwing the wood of a specific desert shrub/tree (*etz*) into the mineralized pool to sweeten it. Instituting a divine statute (*choq ve-mishpat*) at Marah.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyitz'aq el-YHVH vayyorehu YHVH etz vayyashlekh el-ha-mmayim vayyimthqu ha-mmayim sham sam lo choq u-mishpat ve-sham nissahu*: *etz* (tree / wood / timber). *vayyimthqu* ('and they became sweet'). *nissahu* ('he tested him/them').
crossReferences: 1 Peter 2:24 ('He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree / *xylon*'); Galatians 3:13; Sirach 38:5 ('Was not water made sweet with a tree in order that his power might be known?').
historicalTrivia: Sirach 38:5 explicitly cites Exodus 15:25: 'Was not water made sweet with a tree (*xylon*) in order that his power might be known?'!

dominicalIntent: saying: 'If you will diligently listen to the voice of the Lord your God, and do that which is right in his eyes, and give ear to his commandments and keep all his statutes, I will put none of the diseases on you that I put on the Egyptians, for I am the Lord, your healer' (*...KI ANI YHVH ROPHE'EKHA*). 'FOR I AM YAHWEH YOUR HEALER (*YHVH ROPHE'EKHA*)!' THE GREAT DIVINE COVENANT OF HEALING! Yahweh promises: if Israel obeys, He will inflict none of Egypt's diseases on them, **'FOR I AM YAHWEH YOUR HEALER (*Ki Ani YHVH Rophe'ekha*)!'**
cccReferences: CCC 1502 (GOD THE HEALER: Yahweh *Rophe'ekha* as the source of physical and spiritual healing, fulfilled in Jesus Christ the Divine Physician); CCC 1503; CCC 2063; CCC 2575; Ps 103:3; Matt 8:17.
historicalContext: Covenant declaration at Marah introducing Yahweh's divine title as Healer (*Rophe*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer im-shamoa tishma qol YHVH Eloheykha ve-ha-yashar be-eynav ta'asseh ve-ha'azantha le-mitzvothav ve-shamartha kol-chuqqav kol-ha-mmachalah asher-samti ve-Mitzrayim lo-asim aleykha KI ANI YHVH ROPHE'EKHA*: *YHVH Rophe'ekha* ('Yahweh your Physician / Healer', root *rapha*).
crossReferences: Psalm 103:3 ('Who heals all your diseases'); Matthew 8:17 ('He took our infirmities and bore our diseases'); Isaiah 53:5 ('By his wounds we are healed'); Exodus 23:25.
historicalTrivia: This is the revelation of one of the fundamental Covenant Names of God: **YAHWEH-RAPHA / YHVH ROPHE'EKHA** ('Yahweh Who Heals You')!

dominicalIntent: Then they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they encamped there by the water (*...shethem assar eynoth mayim ve-shiv'im thmarim...*). THE OASIS OF ELIM: 12 SPRINGS AND 70 PALM TREES! TYPOLOGY OF THE 12 APOSTLES AND 70 DISCIPLES! Israel reaches **Elim ('Terebinths/Oasis')**, finding **12 SPRINGS OF WATER (*shethem assar eynoth mayim*)** and **70 PALM TREES (*shiv'im thmarim*)**! **PATRISTIC EXEGESIS (ST. JEROME, ST. AMBROSE) HIGHLIGHTS THAT THE 12 SPRINGS PREFIGURE THE 12 APOSTLES GUSHING LIVING WATER, AND THE 70 PALMS PREFIGURE THE 70 DISCIPLES SENT BY CHRIST (LUKE 10:1)!**
cccReferences: CCC 1221 (The 12 springs of Elim prefiguring the 12 Apostles spreading Baptismal waters); CCC 858 (The 12 Apostles and 70 Disciples); Luke 9:1; Luke 10:1; Rev 7:9.
historicalContext: Elim (*Wadi Gharandal*), a lush tropical palm oasis in Sinai with 12 natural springs and 70 date palms.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyavo'u Elimah ve-sham shethem assar eynoth mayim ve-shiv'im thmarim vayyachanu-sham al-ha-mmayim*: *Elimah* (to Elim = giant trees/oases). *eynoth* (springs/fountains). *thmarim* (date palm trees).
crossReferences: Luke 9:1 (The 12 Apostles); Luke 10:1 (The 70 Disciples); Numbers 33:9; Revelation 7:9 ('holding palm branches in their hands').
historicalTrivia: St. Jerome in his *Epistle to Fabiola* marvels: '12 springs of water representing the 12 Apostles, and 70 palm trees representing the 70 disciples sent out by the Savior'!

dominicalIntent: They set out from Elim, and all the congregation of the people of Israel came to the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after they had departed from the land of Egypt. STATION 3: THE WILDERNESS OF SIN! Exactly 1 month after departing Egypt (Iyar 15, 1446 BC), Israel arrives in the **Wilderness of Sin (*Midbar-Sin*)**, located between Elim and Mount Sinai.
cccReferences: CCC 1334 (The journey through the desert prefiguring the pilgrim Church nourished by heavenly bread); CCC 2575.
historicalContext: Iyar 15, 1446 BC (30 days after the Passover Exodus). Travel provisions brought from Egypt (*tzedah*) run out completely.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiss'u me-Elim vayyavo'u kol-adath bney-Yisra'el el-midbar-Sin asher beyn-Elim u-veyn Sinai be-chamishah assar yom la-chodesh ha-sheni le-tze'tham me-eretz Mitzrayim*: *midbar-Sin* ('Wilderness of Sin/Thorn').
historicalTrivia: The Wilderness of Sin is distinct from the Wilderness of Zin (Kadesh-barnea); Sin lies along the southwestern Sinai coast.

dominicalIntent: And the whole congregation of the people of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness (*Vayyillonu kol-adath bney Yisra'el...*). NATIONAL MURMURING FOR FOOD! Deprived of food, the entire 12-tribe assembly grumbles against Moses and Aaron.
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Sin of grumbling against divine providence); CCC 2575; 1 Cor 10:10.
historicalContext: Widespread panic when home-baked unleavened bread runs out completely after 30 days.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyillonu kol-adath bney Yisra'el al-Moshe ve-al-Aaron ba-midbar*: *Vayyillonu* ('and they grumbled/murmured').
historicalTrivia: 1 Corinthians 10:10 warns against this exact grumbling.

dominicalIntent: and the people of Israel said to them: 'Would that we had died by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the meat pots and ate bread to the full, for you have brought us out into this wilderness to kill this whole assembly with hunger' (*...be-shivthenu al-ssir ha-bassar...*). LUSTING FOR EGYPT'S MEAT POTS (*SIR HA-BASSAR*)! The assembly romanticizes their Egyptian slavery: **'WOULD THAT WE HAD DIED IN EGYPT WHEN WE SAT BY THE MEAT POTS (*sir ha-bassar*) AND ATE BREAD TO THE FULL!'** Accusing Moses of orchestrating mass starvation.
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Slavish attachment to worldly comfort over spiritual freedom); CCC 2575; Num 11:4-6.
