historicalContext: Rebel memory distorting Egyptian forced labor into a culinary paradise.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mru alehem bney Yisra'el mi-yitten muthenu ve-yad-YHVH be-eretz Mitzrayim be-shivthenu al-ssir ha-bassar be-okhlenu lechem la-ssovah ki-hotze'them othanu el-ha-midbar ha-zeh le-hamith eth-kol-ha-qqahal ha-zeh ba-rra'av*: *ssir ha-bassar* ('pot/cauldron of meat').
crossReferences: Numbers 11:4-6 ('O that we had meat to eat!'); Psalm 78:19-20; Acts 7:39.
historicalTrivia: The idiom 'fleshpots of Egypt' (*sir ha-bassar*) originated with this verse.

dominicalIntent: Then the Lord said to Moses: 'Behold, I am about to rain bread from heaven for you, and the people shall go out and gather a day's portion every day, that I may test them, whether they will walk in my law or not' (*...Hineni mamthir lakhem lechem min-ha-ssamayim...*). BREAD FROM HEAVEN (*LECHEM MIN-HA-SSAMAYIM*) ANNOUNCED—JOHN 6 EUCHARISTIC DISCOURSE! Yahweh promises: **'BEHOLD, I AM ABOUT TO RAIN BREAD FROM HEAVEN FOR YOU (*Hineni mamthir... lechem min-ha-ssamayim*)!'** **JESUS EXPLICITLY CITATION OF THIS VERSE IN JOHN 6:31-35, 51 TO REVEAL HIMSELF AS THE TRUE BREAD FROM HEAVEN IN THE HOLY EUCHARIST!**
cccReferences: CCC 1334 (MANNA THE EUCHARISTIC TYPE: The bread from heaven prefiguring the Holy Eucharist); CCC 1093; CCC 2835 ('Give us this day our daily bread'); John 6:31-35; John 6:51; 1 Cor 10:3.
historicalContext: Daily gift of heavenly bread given to test (*l-nassotho*) Israel's obedience to divine instructions.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe hineni mamthir lakhem lechem min-ha-ssamayim ve-yatza ha-am ve-laqchu devar-yom be-yomo le-ma'an anassennu ha-yelekh be-thorathi im-lo*: *lechem min-ha-ssamayim* ('bread from the heavens'). *devar-yom be-yomo* ('portion of a day in its day' -> 'Our daily bread'!).
crossReferences: John 6:31-35 ('Our fathers ate the manna... My Father gives you the true bread from heaven'); John 6:51; Psalm 78:24-25; Matthew 6:11; 1 Corinthians 10:3.
historicalTrivia: The phrase *devar-yom be-yomo* ('a day's portion every day') is the direct Old Testament source for the 4th petition of the Lord's Prayer: **'Give us this day our daily bread'** (*panem nostrum cotidianum*)!

dominicalIntent: 'On the sixth day, when they prepare what they bring in, it will be twice as much as they gather daily.' THE DOUBLE PORTION ON THE 6TH DAY! God institutes the 6th-day miracle: a **double portion (*mishneh*)** gathered and prepared on Friday to preserve the 7th-day Sabbath rest.
cccReferences: CCC 2172 (The Sabbath rest sanctified by God); CCC 1334.
historicalContext: Preparing food on the 6th day (Friday) to refrain from all cooking labor on the Sabbath.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-hayah ba-yom ha-shishshi ve-hekhinu eth asher-yavi'u ve-hayah mishneh al asher-yilqchu yom yom*: *mishneh* (double amount/portion).
crossReferences: Exodus 16:22; Leviticus 25:21 (Triple crop yield before Sabbatical year!).
historicalTrivia: To this day, Jewish Sabbath tables feature 2 braided *Challah* loaves (*Mishneh*) to commemorate the double portion of manna on Friday!

dominicalIntent: So Moses and Aaron said to all the people of Israel: 'At evening you shall know that the Lord has brought you out of the land of Egypt...' Prophesying the evening manifestation of divine power.
historicalContext: Announcing the evening arrival of the quail army.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Moshe ve-Aaron el-kol-bney Yisra'el erev vi-yda'them ki YHVH hotzi ethkhem mi-eretz Mitzrayim*.
historicalTrivia: The evening revelation (*erev*) answered Israel's complaint for meat.

dominicalIntent: 'and in the morning you shall see the glory of the Lord, because he has heard your grumbling against the Lord. For what are we, that you grumble against us?' MORNING GLORY OF YAHWEH (*KAVOD YHVH*)! Moses promises: **'IN THE MORNING YOU SHALL SEE THE GLORY OF YAHWEH (*u-voqer u-re'ithem eth-kavod YHVH*)!'** Explaining that murmuring against God's ministers is murmuring against God Himself.
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Grumbling against church leadership targeted at God); CCC 2575; Num 14:27; Luke 10:16.
historicalContext: The manifestation of the *Kavod YHVH* (Glory of the Lord) in the desert cloud.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-voqer u-re'ithem eth-kavod YHVH be-shom'o eth-tlunnatheykhem al-YHVH ve-nachnu mah ki thallinu alenu*: *kavod YHVH* ('Glory of Yahweh'). *tlunnatheykhem* ('your grumblings/complaints').
crossReferences: Exodus 16:10; Numbers 14:27; Luke 10:16 ('He who hears you hears me, and he who rejects you rejects me'); 1 Thessalonians 4:8.
historicalTrivia: Jesus in Luke 10:16 echoes Exodus 16:7: rejecting God's shepherd is rejecting God Himself.

dominicalIntent: And Moses said: 'When the Lord gives you in the evening meat to eat and in the morning bread to the full, because the Lord has heard your grumbling that you grumble against him—what are we? Your grumbling is not against us but against the Lord.' Re-iterating: meat in the evening (*bassar ba-erev*), bread to the full in the morning (*lechem ba-bboqer le-ssova*).
historicalContext: Evening quail (*Slav*) and morning manna (*Man*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Moshe be-theth YHVH lakhem ba-erev bassar le-ekhol u-lechem ba-bboqer li-ssova be-shoma YHVH eth-tlunnatheykhem asher-athem mallinim alav ve-nachnu mah lo-alenu thlunnatheykhem ki al-YHVH*.
historicalTrivia: Meat in evening, bread in morning: complete physical fulfillment.

dominicalIntent: Then Moses said to Aaron: 'Say to the whole congregation of the people of Israel, "Come near before the Lord, for he has heard your grumbling."' Aaron calling the 12 tribes to assemble before Yahweh.
historicalContext: Formal liturgical assembly before the Shekinah Cloud.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Moshe el-Aaron emor el-kol-adath bney Yisra'el qirvu liphney YHVH ki shama eth tlunnatheykhem*: *qirvu* ('draw near / approach').
historicalTrivia: The verb *qarev* is the root for *Qorban* (Sacrifice/Offering drawn near to God).

dominicalIntent: And as soon as Aaron spoke to the whole congregation of the people of Israel, they looked toward the wilderness, and behold, the glory of the Lord appeared in the cloud (*...ve-hinneh kavod YHVH nir'ah ba-anan*). THE GLORY OF YAHWEH APPEARS IN THE CLOUD! As Aaron speaks, the 600,000 men turn toward the desert: **BEHOLD, THE GLORY OF YAHWEH (*kavod YHVH*) APPEARED BLAZING IN THE CLOUD!**
cccReferences: CCC 697 (THE CLOUD OF GLORY: The Holy Spirit manifested in the radiant Cloud of Glory *Kavod*); CCC 2575; Exod 24:16; Matt 17:5.
historicalContext: Supernatural blazing manifestation of the *Shekinah* within the desert Cloud.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi ke-dhabber Aaron el-kol-adath bney-Yisra'el vayyiphnu el-ha-midbar ve-hinneh kavod YHVH nir'ah ba-anan*: *kavod YHVH* ('Glory of Yahweh').
crossReferences: Exodus 24:16; Exodus 40:34-35; Matthew 17:5 (The Cloud at the Transfiguration!); Luke 9:34-35.
historicalTrivia: This same Cloud of Glory (*Kavod*) overshadowed the Apostles at Christ's Transfiguration (Matt 17:5)!

dominicalIntent: And the Lord said to Moses... Divine response confirming the provision.
historicalContext: Direct Yahweh speech to Moses.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayydabber YHVH el-Moshe le'mor*.
historicalTrivia: Formal divine oracle.

dominicalIntent: 'I have heard the grumbling of the people of Israel. Say to them, "At twilight you shall eat meat, and in the morning you shall be filled with bread. Then you shall know that I am the Lord your God."' Divine decree: evening quail (*beyn ha-arbayim*), morning bread (*lechem*).
historicalContext: Evening quail arrival matching the Passover slaughter hour (*beyn ha-arbayim*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Shama'ti eth-tlunnoth bney Yisra'el dabber alehem le'mor beyn ha-arbayim thokhu bassar u-va-bboqer tishb'u-lechem vi-yda'them ki ani YHVH Eloheykhem*: *beyn ha-arbayim* ('between the two evenings' / 3:00 PM - twilight).
historicalTrivia: Notice the phrase *beyn ha-arbayim* is the exact time set for the Passover lamb slaughter (Exod 12:6)!

dominicalIntent: In the evening quail came up and covered the camp, and in the morning dew lay around the camp (*...vat-ta'al ha-sslav vat-thekhas eth-ha-mmachaneh...*). EVENING QUAIL (*SLAV*) COVER THE CAMP! At evening, massive flocks of migratory **quail (*slav*)** land across the camp; in the morning, a layer of dew (*shikhvath ha-ttal*) surrounds the camp.
historicalContext: Migratory European quail (*Coturnix coturnix*) flying across the Mediterranean and dropping exhausted in Sinai desert camps.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi va-erev vat-ta'al ha-sslav vat-thekhas eth-ha-mmachaneh u-va-bboqer haythah shikhvath ha-ttal ssaviv la-mmachaneh*: *ha-sslav* (quail). *shikhvath ha-ttal* ('layer of dew').
crossReferences: Numbers 11:31-32; Psalm 78:27-28 ('He rained meat on them like dust, winged birds like the sand of the seas'); Psalm 105:40.
historicalTrivia: Quail migrate annually between Europe and Africa; exhausted by the sea flight, millions land on Sinai beaches so low they can be picked up by hand!

dominicalIntent: And when the dew had gone up, there was on the face of the wilderness a fine, flake-like thing, fine as frost on the ground (*...ve-hinneh al-pney ha-midbar daq me-chusphas daq ka-khor ba-aretz*). THE MANNA APPEARS: FINE, FLAKE-LIKE AS FROST (*DAQ ME-CHUSPHAS*)! The dew evaporates, leaving on the desert surface a **fine, flake-like, scale-like substance (*daq me-chusphas*)**, fine as hoarfrost (*khor*) on the ground!
cccReferences: CCC 1334 (The miraculous appearance of Manna); 1 Cor 10:3.
historicalContext: Supernatural morning deposit left when desert dew evaporated.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vat-ta'al shikhvath ha-ttal ve-hinneh al-pney ha-midbar daq me-chusphas daq ka-khor ba-aretz*: *daq* (fine/thin/powdery). *me-chusphas* (flake-like / scale-like / encrusted). *khor* (hoarfrost).
historicalTrivia: Wisdom 16:20-21 describes the manna: 'You gave them food of angels (*angelōrun broma*)... suited to every taste'!

dominicalIntent: When the people of Israel saw it, they said to one another: 'What is it?' for they did not know what it was. And Moses said to them: 'It is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat' (*...MAN HU... Hu ha-llechem asher nathan YHVH lakhem le-okhlah*). 'MAN NA?' ('WHAT IS IT?')—NAME OF THE MANNA! THE BREAD GIVEN BY YAHWEH! Israel sees the substance, asking in astonishment: **'MAN HU?!' ('WHAT IS IT?!')**—hence its name **MANNA (*MAN*)**! Moses responds: **'THIS IS THE BREAD THAT YAHWEH HAS GIVEN YOU TO EAT!'**
cccReferences: CCC 1334 (MANNA THE BREAD OF HEAVEN FULFILLED IN THE EUCHARIST); CCC 1093; John 6:31-32; John 6:48-51 ('I am the Bread of Life').
historicalContext: The naming of the heavenly bread *Man* (from Aramaic/Hebrew *Man hu* = 'What is it?').
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyir'u vney-Yisra'el vayyo'mru ish el-achiv MAN HU ki lo yadh'u mah-hu vayyo'mer Moshe alehem hu ha-llechem asher nathan YHVH lakhem le-okhlah*: *MAN HU* ('What is it? / What is this?').
crossReferences: John 6:31-35; John 6:48-51 ('Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness and died; I am the living bread that came down from heaven'); 1 Corinthians 10:3; Nehemiah 9:15.
historicalTrivia: In John 6:48-51, Jesus contrasts the Old Manna (which nourished physical life temporarily) with the New Manna of the Eucharist (which gives eternal life)!

dominicalIntent: 'This is what the Lord has commanded: "Gather of it, each one of you, as much as he can eat. You shall each take an omer, according to the number of the persons that each of you has in his tent."' RATION MANDATE: ONE OMER PER PERSON (*OMER LA-GGULGOLETH*)! God commands: gather **one omer (*omer* ~ 2.2 liters / 2 quarts) per head/person (*la-ggulgoleth*)** for every member in the tent.
cccReferences: CCC 1334; CCC 2835 ('Our daily bread').
historicalContext: An *Omer* (~2.2 liters) was the standard daily grain ration for an adult human being.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Zeh ha-davar asher tzivvah YHVH liqthu mimmennu ish le-phi okhlo omer la-ggulgoleth mi-sspar nephashotheykhem ish le-asher be-ohalo tiqqachu*: *omer* (~2.2 liters / 1/10th Ephah). *la-ggulgoleth* ('per skull/head' -> Golgotha!).
historicalTrivia: The Hebrew word *gulgholeth* ('skull/head') is the exact root of **GOLGOTHA** (*place of the skull*, Matt 27:33)!

dominicalIntent: And the people of Israel did so: they gathered, some more, some less. Gathering according to family size and capacity.
historicalContext: Daily morning collection before sunrise.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'assu-khen bney Yisra'el vayyilqthu ha-mmarbeh ve-ha-mm'at*.
historicalTrivia: Some collected large baskets, others small bowls.

dominicalIntent: But when they measured it with an omer, whoever gathered much had nothing left over, and whoever gathered little had no lack. Each gathered as much as he could eat (*...ve-lo he'ediph ha-mmarbeh ve-ha-mm'at lo hechsir...*). THE MIRACLE OF EQUALIZATION—CITED BY ST. PAUL IN 2 CORINTHIANS 8:15! A supernatural miracle of measurement: **'HE WHO GATHERED MUCH HAD NOTHING LEFT OVER, AND HE WHO GATHERED LITTLE HAD NO LACK!'** **ST. PAUL IN 2 CORINTHIANS 8:15 QUOTES THIS VERSE AS THE CHRISTIAN PRINCIPLE OF CHARITABLE SHARING AND EQUALITY!**
cccReferences: CCC 2407 (Economic justice and charitable sharing cited by St. Paul from Exod 16:18); CCC 2835; 2 Cor 8:13-15 ('As it is written, "He who gathered much had nothing over, and he who gathered little had no lack"').
historicalContext: Supernatural redistribution: when poured into an omer measure, every individual's portion equaled exactly 1 omer!
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyammudhu va-omer ve-lo he'ediph ha-mmarbeh ve-ha-mm'at lo hechsir ish le-phi okhlo laqachu*: *lo he'ediph* ('had no surplus'). *lo hechsir* ('had no lack/deficit').
historicalTrivia: St. Paul in 2 Corinthians 8:14-15 uses Exodus 16:18 to urge wealthy Christians to give alms so that 'your abundance at the present time may supply their need... as it is written: He who gathered much had nothing over'!

dominicalIntent: And Moses said to them: 'Let no one leave any of it over till the morning.' Command against hoarding manna overnight.
cccReferences: CCC 2835 ('Give us this day our daily bread' trusting God for tomorrow).
historicalContext: Daily dependence on God without hoarding.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Moshe alehem ish al-yothar mimmennu ad-boqer*: *al-yothar* ('let no one leave over').
crossReferences: Matthew 6:11; Matthew 6:34 ('Do not be anxious about tomorrow').
historicalTrivia: Hoarding manna revealed a lack of faith in God's promise to provide tomorrow.

dominicalIntent: But they did not listen to Moses. Some left part of it till the morning, and it bred worms and stank. And Moses was angry with them (*...vayyarum thola'im vayyiv'as vayyiqtzoph alehem Moshe*). HOARDED MANNA ROT-WORMS AND STENCH! Disobedient Israelites hoard manna overnight; by morning **it bred worms (*thola'im*) and stank (*vayyiv'as*)**! Moses is rightly angry with them.
historicalContext: Supernatural rotting of hoarded weekday manna into maggots (*thola'im*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-lo-sham'u el-Moshe vayyothiru anashim mimmennu ad-boqer vayyarum thola'im vayyiv'as vayyiqtzoph alehem Moshe*: *thola'im* (maggots/worms). *vayyiv'as* ('and it stank/rotted').
crossReferences: James 5:2-3 ('Your riches have rotted... your gold and silver have rusted'); Exodus 16:24.
historicalTrivia: James 5:2-3 echoes Exodus 16:20: hoarded wealth rots into worms and judgment.

dominicalIntent: Morning by morning they gathered it, each as much as he could eat; but when the sun grew hot, it melted (*...u-cham ha-sshemesh ve-namas*). THE MANNA MELTS IN THE MORNING SUN (*VE-NAMAS*)! Daily morning routine: gathered early; **as soon as the desert sun grew hot, the ungathered manna melted away (*ve-namas*)**!
historicalContext: Sunlight dissolving ungathered manna on the desert floor to keep the camp clean.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyilqthu otho ba-bboqer ba-bboqer ish le-phi okhlo u-cham ha-sshemesh ve-namas*: *ve-namas* ('and it melted/dissolved').
crossReferences: Wisdom 16:27 ('For that which was not destroyed by fire, being warmed by a little sunbeam, melted away'); Psalm 68:2.
historicalTrivia: Wisdom 16:27 explains that manna melted in the sun to teach believers to rise before sunrise to pray to God!

dominicalIntent: On the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread, two omers each. And when all the leaders of the congregation came and told Moses... FRIDAY DOUBLE PORTION GATHERED! On the 6th day (Friday), Israel gathers **two omers per person (*shteney ha-omer la-echad*)**; leaders report the miracle to Moses.
cccReferences: CCC 2172 (Sanctifying the Sabbath); CCC 1334.
historicalContext: Friday double collection (4.4 liters per person).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi ba-yom ha-shishshi laqchu lechem mishneh shteney ha-omer la-echad vayyavo'u kol-nssi'ey ha-edah vayyaggidu le-Moshe*: *lechem mishneh* ('double bread').
historicalTrivia: The 2 loaves of Challah baked for Friday night dinner directly commemorate *lechem mishneh*!

dominicalIntent: he said to them: 'This is what the Lord has commanded: "Tomorrow is a day of solemn rest, a holy Sabbath to the Lord; bake what you will bake and boil what you will boil, and all that is left over lay aside to be kept till the morning."' THE HOLY SABBATH TO YAHWEH (*SHABBATH QODESH LE-YHVH*) DECLARED! Moses declares: **'TOMORROW IS A DAY OF SOLEMN REST, A HOLY SABBATH TO YAHWEH (*SHABBATHON SHABBATH-QODESH LE-YHVH*)!'** FIRST EXPLICIT LEGISLATION OF SABBATH REST IN THE BIBLE!
cccReferences: CCC 2168 (THE SABBATH REST INSTITUTED: The 7th day as God's holy rest prefiguring the Lord's Day / Sunday Resurrection); CCC 2172; CCC 2173; Gen 2:2-3; Mark 2:27-28.
historicalContext: First formal command to observe the 7th-day Sabbath (*Shabbath*) prior to the 10 Commandments at Sinai.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer alehem hu asher dibber YHVH SHABBATHON SHABBATH-QODESH LE-YHVH machar eth asher-tho'phu epho ve-eth asher-thevashlu bashlu ve-eth kol-ha-nothar hinichu lakhem le-mishmereth ad-ha-bboqer*: *SHABBATHON* (cessation / solemn rest). *SHABBATH-QODESH* ('holy Sabbath').
crossReferences: Genesis 2:2-3; Exodus 20:8-11; Mark 2:27-28 ('The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath'); Hebrews 4:9-10.
historicalTrivia: This is the very first time the word **SHABBATH** (Sabbath) appears as a noun and commandment in Sacred Scripture!

dominicalIntent: So they laid it aside till the morning, as Moses commanded them, and it did not stink, and there were no worms in it (*...ve-lo hiv'as ve-rrimmah lo haythah bo*). THE FRIDAY NIGHT SABBATH MIRACLE: NO WORMS OR STENCH! The double portion stored on Friday night remains **completely fresh, without stench (*lo hiv'as*) or worms (*rimmah*)**! Supernatural preservation of Sabbath food.
historicalContext: Weekly miracle testifying to the sanctity of the Sabbath.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyinichu otho ad-ha-bboqer ka-asher tzivvah Moshe ve-lo hiv'as ve-rrimmah lo haythah bo*: *hiv'as* (stank). *rimmah* (worm/maggot).
crossReferences: Exodus 16:20; Psalm 16:10 ('nor will you let your Holy One see corruption').
historicalTrivia: While weekday manna rotted in 12 hours (v. 20), Sabbath manna stayed fresh for 36 hours!

dominicalIntent: Moses said: 'Eat it today, for today is a Sabbath to the Lord; today you will not find it in the field.' Eating the Friday-collected manna on the Sabbath day.
historicalContext: Refraining from all foraging labor on Sabbath morning.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Moshe ikhluhu ha-yom ki-shabbath ha-yom le-YHVH ha-yom lo thimtza'uhu ba-ssadeh*.
historicalTrivia: The 3-fold repetition of *ha-yom* ('today') is the Rabbinic source for eating 3 meals (*Shalosh Seudot*) on the Sabbath!

dominicalIntent: 'Six days you shall gather it, but on the seventh day, which is a Sabbath, there will be none.' Establishing the 6-day cycle: 6 days of manna, zero on Sabbath.
historicalContext: The 6-day work, 1-day rest rhythm.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Shesheth yamim thilqthu-hu u-va-yom ha-shvi'i shabbath lo yihyeh-bo*.
historicalTrivia: For 40 years (~2,080 consecutive weeks), no manna ever fell on Sabbath morning!

dominicalIntent: On the seventh day some of the people went out to gather, but they found none (*...ve-lo matza'u*). SABBATH VIOLATION: SEARCHING FOR MANNA ON SABBATH! Disobedient Israelites go out on Sabbath morning to gather manna, **BUT THEY FOUND NONE (*ve-lo matza'u*)**!
historicalContext: First violation of the Sabbath rest.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi ba-yom ha-shvi'i yatze'u min-ha-am li-lqoth ve-lo matza'u*: *ve-lo matza'u* ('and they found nothing').
historicalTrivia: Demonstrates the futility of seeking worldly gain in violation of holy rest.

dominicalIntent: And the Lord said to Moses: 'How long will you refuse to keep my commandments and my laws?' GOD'S REBUKE: 'HOW LONG WILL YOU REFUSE TO KEEP MY LAWS?!' Yahweh rebukes Israel's persistent disobedience.
historicalContext: Divine grief over Israel's chronic lawlessness.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe ad-anathi me'anthem li-shmor mitzvothai ve-thorothai*: *ad-anathi* ('until when? / how long?').
historicalTrivia: God treats the disobedience of a few as a warning to the whole covenant nation.

dominicalIntent: 'See! The Lord has given you the Sabbath; therefore on the sixth day he gives you bread for two days. Remain each of you in his place; let no one go out of his place on the seventh day.' SABBATH REST IN ONE'S PLACE! God emphasizes: 'Yahweh has given you the Sabbath... **REMAIN EACH IN HIS PLACE (*shevu ish thachtav*); LET NO ONE GO OUT ON THE SEVENTH DAY!**'
historicalContext: Restricting long-distance travel on the Sabbath (origin of the *Techum Shabbat* / Sabbath day's journey, Acts 1:12).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Re'u ki-YHVH nathan lakhem ha-shabbath al-ken hu nothen lakhem ba-yom ha-shishshi lechem yomayim shevu ish thachtav al-yetze ish mi-mmeqomo ba-yom ha-shvi'i*: *shevu ish thachtav* ('sit/remain each man under himself / in his place').
crossReferences: Acts 1:12 ('a Sabbath day's journey away'); Jeremiah 17:21-22.
historicalTrivia: Acts 1:12 mentions 'a Sabbath day's journey' (*sabbatou echon hodos* = 2,000 cubits / ~0.6 miles), derived from Exodus 16:29!

dominicalIntent: So the people rested on the seventh day (*Vayyishbthu ha-am ba-yom ha-shvi'i*). NATIONAL SABBATH REST COMPLIED WITH! Israel observes the 7th-day Sabbath rest (*Vayyishbthu*).
historicalContext: First universal national observance of the Sabbath.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyishbthu ha-am ba-yom ha-shvi'i*: *Vayyishbthu* ('and they rested/ceased', root *shabath*).
historicalTrivia: The verb *shabath* means to cease from work and enter holy delight.

dominicalIntent: Now the house of Israel called its name Manna. It was like coriander seed, white, and the taste of it was like wafers made with honey (*...va-yo'khlo k-tzaphichith bi-dvash*). THE APPEARANCE AND SWEET TASTE OF MANNA! Israel names the bread **MANNA (*MAN*)**. Description: (1) Like **white coriander seed (*zera gad lavan*)**, (2) Taste like **wafers made with honey (*tzaphichith bi-dvash*)**!
cccReferences: CCC 1334 (The sweetness of the Eucharistic Manna); Wis 16:20-21; Rev 2:17 ('the hidden manna').
historicalContext: Physical characteristics: small white round seeds tasting like honey-sweetened pastry (*tzaphichith bi-dvash*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiqra veyth-Yisra'el eth-shemo MAN ve-hu ke-zera gad lavan ve-ta'mo k-tzaphichith bi-dvash*: *tzaphichith bi-dvash* ('pastry/wafer in honey').
crossReferences: Numbers 11:7-8 ('like bdellium... taste like cakes baked with oil'); Wisdom 16:20-21; Revelation 2:17 ('hidden manna').
historicalTrivia: Revelation 2:17 promises the victorious Christian: 'I will give him some of the **hidden manna** (*tou manna tou kekrymmenou*)'!

dominicalIntent: Moses said: 'This is what the Lord has commanded: "Let an omer of it be kept throughout your generations, so that they may see the bread with which I fed you in the wilderness, when I brought you out of the land of Egypt."' PRESERVING AN OMER OF MANNA FOR FUTURE GENERATIONS! God commands Moses to preserve 1 omer of manna in a jar so future generations can see the heavenly bread.
cccReferences: CCC 1334; Heb 9:4.
historicalContext: Creating a perpetual sanctuary relic of the Manna.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Moshe zeh ha-davar asher tzivvah YHVH mlo ha-omer mimmennu le-mishmereth le-dorotheykhem le-ma'an yir'u eth-ha-llechem asher he'ekhalti ethkhem ba-midbar be-hotzi'i ethkhem me-eretz Mitzrayim*.
crossReferences: Hebrews 9:4 ('having a golden urn holding the manna'); Exodus 16:33-34.
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 9:4 confirms that a **Golden Pot of Manna** was preserved inside the Ark of the Covenant!

dominicalIntent: And Moses said to Aaron: 'Take a jar, and put an omer of manna in it, and place it before the Lord, to be kept throughout your generations' (*...Qach tzintzeneth achath ve-then-shammah mlo-ha-omer MAN...*). THE GOLDEN JAR OF MANNA (*TZINTZENETH*)! Moses commands Aaron: **'TAKE A GOLDEN JAR (*tzintzeneth*), AND PUT AN OMER OF MANNA IN IT, AND PLACE IT BEFORE YAHWEH!'** **CITED IN HEBREWS 9:4 AS THE GOLDEN URN OF MANNA (*CHRYSOUS STAMNOS*) KEPT INSIDE THE ARK OF THE COVENANT!**
cccReferences: CCC 1334 (The Golden Pot of Manna in the Ark prefiguring the Blessed Sacrament preserved in the Tabernacle); CCC 2676 (Mary as the Golden Ark of the Covenant carrying the Living Manna Jesus); Heb 9:4 ('the golden urn holding the manna').
historicalContext: Placing the clay/golden jar (*tzintzeneth*) containing 1 omer of uncorrupted manna before the Testimony (*Eduth*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Moshe el-Aaron qach tzintzeneth achath ve-then-shammah mlo-ha-omer MAN ve-hannach otho liphney YHVH le-mishmereth le-dorotheykhem*: *tzintzeneth* (jar/pot/urn, LXX *stamnos*, Vulgate *vas*).
crossReferences: Hebrews 9:4 ('in which was a golden urn holding the manna'); Revelation 2:17; Exodus 25:16.
historicalTrivia: In Catholic Litany of Loreto, Mary is invoked as **Ark of the Covenant** (*Foederis Arca*) because she carried Jesus, the Living Manna, inside her womb!

dominicalIntent: As the Lord commanded Moses, so Aaron placed it before the Testimony to be kept (*Liphney ha-Eduth le-mishmereth*). PLACED BEFORE THE TESTIMONY (*HA-EDUTH*)! Aaron places the Jar of Manna before the **Testimony / Ark of the Covenant (*Liphney ha-Eduth*)**.
cccReferences: CCC 1334; Heb 9:4.
historicalContext: Depositing the Manna Jar in front of the 2 Stone Tablets (*Eduth*) inside the Holy of Holies.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ka-asher tzivvah YHVH el-Moshe vayyanichehu Aaron liphney ha-Eduth le-mishmereth*: *ha-Eduth* ('the Testimony / Covenant Tablets').
historicalTrivia: The 3 items inside the Ark of the Covenant: (1) Golden Jar of Manna, (2) Aaron's Rod that budded, (3) The 2 Stone Tablets of the Law (Heb 9:4)!

dominicalIntent: The people of Israel ate the manna forty years, till they came to a habitable land. They ate the manna till they came to the border of the land of Canaan (*...aklu eth-ha-man arba'im shanah... ad-bo'am el-qtzeh eretz Kna'an*). FORTY YEARS OF DAILY MANNA! Scripture records: **ISRAEL ATE THE MANNA FOR FORTY YEARS (*arba'im shanah*)**, until the day they crossed Gilgal into Canaan (Joshua 5:12)!
cccReferences: CCC 1334 (Unbroken 40-year Eucharistic nourishment throughout the desert pilgrimage); Josh 5:12; Neh 9:20-21.
historicalContext: Continuous 40-year daily miracle (1446 BC to 1406 BC = ~14,600 consecutive days of manna!).
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-vney Yisra'el aklu eth-ha-man arba'im shanah ad-bo'am el-eretz noshaveth eth-ha-man aklu ad-bo'am el-qtzeh eretz Kna'an*: *noshaveth* ('habitable / settled').
crossReferences: Joshua 5:12 ('And the manna ceased on the day after they ate of the produce of the land'); Nehemiah 9:20-21; Deuteronomy 8:2-3.
historicalTrivia: Joshua 5:12 records that the manna ceased on Nisan 16, 1406 BC, the day after Israel ate the first produce of Canaan at Gilgal!

dominicalIntent: An omer is the tenth part of an ephah (*Ve-ha-omer assirith ha-ephah hu*). Metric note: 1 Omer = 1/10th of an Ephah (~2.2 liters).
historicalContext: Standard ancient Hebrew dry measure equivalent (~2.2 liters).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-ha-omer assirith ha-ephah hu*: *assirith ha-ephah* ('tenth of an ephah').
historicalTrivia: An Ephah was ~22 liters; an Omer was 1/10th of an Ephah (~2.2 liters).

dominicalIntent: All the congregation of the people of Israel moved on from the wilderness of Sin by stages, according to the commandment of the Lord, and encamped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink. STATION 4: REPHIDIM! Israel marches by stages (*le-massa'eyhem*) to **Rephidim ('Resting Places')**, near Horeb/Sinai. Severe drought: no water to drink.
cccReferences: CCC 1221 (Water from the Rock prefiguring Baptism and the Holy Spirit flowing from Christ's pierced side); CCC 2575.
historicalContext: Rephidim (*Wadi Feiran* / *Wadi esh-Sheikh*), a dry desert valley near Mount Sinai.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiss'u kol-adath bney-Yisra'el mi-midbar-Sin le-massa'eyhem al-pi YHVH vayyachanu bi-Rphidim ve-eyn mayim li-shthoth ha-am*: *le-massa'eyhem* ('by their stages/marches').
historicalTrivia: Rephidim means 'resting places' or 'refreshment', making the lack of water ironic.

dominicalIntent: Therefore the people quarreled with Moses and said: 'Give us water to drink.' And Moses said to them: 'Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test the Lord?' REPHIDIM REBELLION: 'WHY DO YOU TEST YAHWEH?!' Israel fiercely quarrels (*vayyarev*) with Moses. Moses rebukes them: **'WHY DO YOU TEST YAHWEH (*Mah-thnassun eth-YHVH*)?!'**
cccReferences: CCC 2119 (THE SIN OF TESTING GOD: 'You shall not put the Lord your God to the test'); CCC 2575; Deut 6:16; Matt 4:7.
historicalContext: Hostile quarrel threatening Moses' life.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyarev ha-am im-Moshe vayyo'mru tnu-lanu mayim ve-nishtheh vayyo'mer lahem Moshe mah-thrivun immadi mah-thnassun eth-YHVH*: *vayyarev* (and they strove/quarreled, root *riv*). *thnassun* (test/tempt, root *nasa*).
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 6:16 ('You shall not put the Lord your God to the test, as you tested him at Massah'); Matthew 4:7; Luke 4:12; Psalm 95:8-9.
historicalTrivia: Jesus quotes Deuteronomy 6:16 (referencing Exodus 17:2) to defeat Satan in the wilderness temptation (Matt 4:7)!

dominicalIntent: But the people thirsted there for water, and the people murmured against Moses and said: 'Why did you bring us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our livestock with thirst?' Thirst driving the people to murmur again.
historicalContext: Severe physical dehydration in the scorching Sinai heat.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyutzma sham ha-am la-mmayim vayyallon ha-am al-Moshe vayyo'mer lamah zeh he'elithanu mi-Mitzrayim le-hamith othi ve-eth-banai ve-eth-miqnai ba-tzama*: *Vayyutzma* ('and thirsted').
historicalTrivia: Dehydration in 100°F+ desert temperatures caused rapid psychological breakdown.

dominicalIntent: So Moses cried to the Lord: 'What shall I do with this people? They are almost ready to stone me' (*...od m'at u-ssqaluni*). MOSES' CRY: 'THEY ARE ALMOST READY TO STONE ME!' Moses cries to Yahweh: **'WHAT SHALL I DO WITH THIS PEOPLE?! THEY ARE ALMOST READY TO STONE ME (*od m'at u-ssqaluni*)!'** Patriarchal intercession under threat of martyrdom.
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Moses interceding for his persecutors even when facing stoning); Exod 14:15; Num 14:10; John 10:31.
historicalContext: Threat of mob stoning (*seqilah*) by desperate, dehydrated elders.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyitz'aq Moshe el-YHVH le'mor mah a'asseh la-am ha-zeh od m'at u-ssqaluni*: *od m'at u-ssqaluni* ('a little more and they will stone me!').
historicalTrivia: Jesus experienced this exact threat of stoning in John 10:31!

dominicalIntent: And the Lord said to Moses: 'Pass on before the people, taking with you some of the elders of Israel, and take in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.' Divine command to take the Staff of God and elders to Mount Horeb.
historicalContext: Selecting official witnesses (*ziqney Yisra'el*) for the miracle at Horeb.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe avor liphney ha-am ve-qach ittakh mi-ziqney Yisra'el u-mattekha asher hikkitha bo eth-ha-Ye'or qach be-yadkha ve-halakhta*.
historicalTrivia: The staff that struck the Nile in judgment now brings forth life-giving water!

dominicalIntent: 'Behold, I will stand before you there on the rock at Horeb, and you shall strike the rock, and water shall come out of it, that the people may drink.' And Moses did so, in the sight of the elders of Israel (*...ve-hikkitha va-tzur ve-yatz'u mimmennu mayim...*). WATER FROM THE STRUCK ROCK AT HOREB—1 CORINTHIANS 10:4 CHRIST THE ROCK! Yahweh promises: **'BEHOLD, I WILL STAND BEFORE YOU THERE ON THE ROCK AT HOREB (*al-ha-tzur be-Chorev*); AND YOU SHALL STRIKE THE ROCK, AND WATER SHALL COME OUT OF IT!'** **ST. PAUL EXPLICITLY DECLARES IN 1 CORINTHIANS 10:4: 'THEY DRANK FROM THE SPIRITUAL ROCK THAT FOLLOWED THEM, AND THE ROCK WAS CHRIST!'**
cccReferences: CCC 1221 (WATER FROM THE PIERCED ROCK: The water gushing from Horeb's struck rock prefiguring the Holy Spirit flowing from Christ's pierced side); CCC 694; CCC 2575; 1 Cor 10:4; John 7:37-38; John 19:34.
historicalContext: Striking the granite cliff of Mount Horeb in the presence of Israel's elders, gushing rivers of water in the desert.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Hineni omad liphneykha sham al-ha-tzur be-Chorev ve-hikkitha va-tzur ve-yatz'u mimmennu mayim ve-shathah ha-am vayya'as ken Moshe le-eyney ziqney Yisra'el*: *ha-tzur* (the massive flint rock/cliff). *be-Chorev* (at Mount Horeb/Sinai).
crossReferences: 1 Corinthians 10:4 ('and all drank the same spiritual drink... and the Rock was Christ'); John 7:37-38; John 19:34; Psalm 78:15-16 ('He split rocks in the wilderness and gave them drink abundant as the deep'); Psalm 105:41.
historicalTrivia: The Greek of 1 Corinthians 10:4 translates *ha-tzur* as *hē petra de ēn ho Christos* ('and the Rock was Christ')! St. John Chrysostom notes that Christ was struck on the Cross to gush forth the waters of Baptism!

dominicalIntent: And he called the name of the place Massah and Meribah, because of the quarreling of the people of Israel, and because they tested the Lord by saying: 'Is the Lord among us or not?' (*...MASSAH u-MERIBAH... Ha-yesh YHVH be-qirbenu im-ayin*). NAMING THE PLACE MASSAH ('TESTING') AND MERIBAH ('QUARRELING')! Moses names the place **MASSAH ('Testing')** and **MERIBAH ('Quarreling')**, for their blasphemous question: **'IS YAHWEH AMONG US OR NOT (*Ha-yesh YHVH be-qirbenu im-ayin*)?!'** CITED IN PSALM 95 AND HEBREWS 3-4!
cccReferences: CCC 2119 (THE SIN OF TEMPTING GOD AT MASSAH AND MERIBAH); CCC 2575; Ps 95:7-9 ('Harden not your hearts as at Meribah, as on the day at Massah'); Heb 3:7-9; Heb 4:7.
historicalContext: The double naming of the location to memorialize Israel's sin of testing God's presence.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiqra shem ha-mmaqom MASSAH u-MERIBAH al-riv bney Yisra'el ve-al nassotham eth-YHVH le'mor ha-yesh YHVH be-qirbenu im-ayin*: *MASSAH* (Testing/Trial, root *nasa*). *MERIBAH* (Quarreling/Strife, root *riv*).
historicalTrivia: Psalm 95 (*Venite Adoremus*), sung every single morning in the Catholic Liturgy of the Hours (Invitatory), warns: 'Today if you hear his voice, harden not your hearts as at Meribah, as on the day at Massah in the wilderness'!

dominicalIntent: Then Amalek came and fought with Israel at Rephidim (*Vayyavo Amaleq vayyillachem im-YISRA'EL bi-Rphidim*). THE ATTACK OF AMALEK AT REPHIDIM! The nomadic nation of **Amalek (*Amaleq*)**, descendants of Esau (Gen 36:12), launches a treacherous ambush attack against Israel at Rephidim, attacking the faint and weary rear guard (Deut 25:17-18).
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Amalek as the archetype of satanic assault against God's pilgrim Church); CCC 2575; Deut 25:17-19; 1 Sam 15:2.
historicalContext: Amalekites (fierce desert bandits operating out of the Negev/Sinai) attacking the exhausted rear guard of Israel without cause.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyavo Amaleq vayyillachem im-Yisra'el bi-Rphidim*: *Amaleq* (Amalek, grandson of Esau).
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 25:17-19 ('Remember what Amalek did to you... he attacked your rear, when you were faint and weary'); 1 Samuel 15:2-3; 1 Samuel 30:1.
historicalTrivia: Deuteronomy 25:17-18 records that Amalek acted with utter godlessness, striking down the vulnerable elderly, women, and children marching in the rear!

dominicalIntent: So Moses said to Joshua: 'Choose for us men, and go out and fight with Amalek. Tomorrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the staff of God in my hand.' FIRST APPEARANCE OF JOSHUA (*YEHOSHUA / JESUS*)! Moses commissions **Joshua (*Yehoshua*)** to lead Israel's army into battle, while Moses ascends the hill holding the **Staff of God (*matteh ha-Elohim*)**! **JOSHUA (HEBREW *YEHOSHUA*) IS THE EXACT HEBREW NAME OF JESUS!**
cccReferences: CCC 430 (JESUS THE DIVINE COMMANDER: Joshua *Yehoshua* prefiguring Jesus *Yeshua* leading God's people to victory over demonic forces); CCC 2575.
historicalContext: Joshua son of Nun (Ephraimite general) leading the army while Moses intercedes on the mountain peak.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Moshe el-Yehoshua bchar-lanu anashim ve-tze illachem ba-Amaleq machar anokhi nitzav al-rosh ha-ggiv'ah u-matteh ha-Elohim be-yadi*: *Yehoshua* (Yahweh is Salvation -> **JESUS**!). *matteh ha-Elohim* ('staff of God').
crossReferences: Numbers 13:16; Joshua 1:1; Acts 7:45; Hebrews 4:8 (Translating Joshua as *Iēsous*!).
historicalTrivia: In the Septuagint and New Testament Greek, the name **Joshua** is written **IĒSOUS** (JESUS)! Joshua leading Israel to victory is a direct type of Jesus defeating Satan!

dominicalIntent: So Joshua did as Moses told him, and fought with Amalek, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill. Joshua leads the military charge; Moses, Aaron, and **Hur** (of Judah, grandfather of Bezalel) ascend the mountain top.
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The dual dimension of Christian warfare: action on the battlefield and intercession on the mountain).
historicalContext: Moses, Aaron, and Hur establishing the mountain intercessory command post.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'as Yehoshua ka-asher amar-lo Moshe le-hillachem ba-Amaleq u-Moshe Aaron ve-Chur alu rosh ha-ggiv'ah*: *Chur* (Hur, leader of Judah, Exod 24:14; 31:2).
historicalTrivia: Hur (*Chur*) was the husband of Miriam (according to Josephus, *Antiq.* III.2.4) and prince of the tribe of Judah!

dominicalIntent: Whenever Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed, and whenever he lowered his hand, Amalek prevailed (*Ve-hayah ka-asher yarim Moshe yado ve-gavar YISRA'EL...*). MOSES' OUTSTRETCHED ARMS FORMING THE CROSS! Whenever Moses raises his hands in prayer, Israel prevails; when his hands droop, Amalek prevails! **PATRISTIC EXEGESIS (ST. JUSTIN MARTYR, TERTULLIAN, ST. CYPRIAN) UNANIMOUSLY DECLARES THAT MOSES STANDING ON THE MOUNTAIN WITH ARMS EXTENDED FORMED THE SIGN OF THE CROSS, PROVING THAT VICTORY OVER SATAN COMES ONLY THROUGH THE CROSS OF CHRIST!**
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (MOSES AS THE INTERCESSOR WITH ARMS EXTENDED FORMING THE CROSS: Intercessory prayer sustaining spiritual battle); CCC 2619; Gal 6:14; Col 2:14-15.
historicalContext: Continuous intercessory prayer posture (*phressath kappayim*) determining physical battle outcomes.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-hayah ka-asher yarim Moshe yado ve-gavar Yisra'el ve-kha-asher yaniach yado ve-gavar Amaleq*: *yarim... yado* ('lifted up his hands'). *ve-gavar* ('and prevailed/overcame').
crossReferences: Justin Martyr (*Dialogue with Trypho* 90); Tertullian (*An-Marcion* III.18); Galatians 6:14; Colossians 2:14-15.
historicalTrivia: St. Justin Martyr (AD 150) writes: 'Moses prayed to God with his arms extended on either side in the form of a cross; while this posture was maintained, Amalek was defeated'!

dominicalIntent: But Moses' hands grew weary, so they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it, while Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on one side, and the other on the other side. So his hands were steady until the going down of the sun (*...ve-Aaron ve-Chur thamkhu ve-yadav... ad-bo ha-sshemesh*). AARON AND HUR SUPPORT MOSES' HANDS IN THE CROSS FORMATION! Moses grows weary; Aaron and Hur place a stone seat under him and **hold up his hands on either side (*thamkhu ve-yadav*)**, keeping his arms extended in the Cross formation **until sunset (*ad-bo ha-sshemesh*)**!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The necessity of communal support for the priest/intercessor in spiritual warfare); Exod 24:14; 1 Thess 5:11.
historicalContext: Aaron (Priesthood) and Hur (Royalty/Judah) supporting the Prophet Moses.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-yedhey Moshe kvedim vayyiqchu-even vayyasimu thachtav vayyeshev aleha ve-Aaron ve-Chur thamkhu ve-yadav mi-zzeh echad u-mi-zzeh echad vayehi yadav emunah ad-bo ha-sshemesh*: *emunah* ('steadfast / faithful / firm').
crossReferences: 1 Thessalonians 5:11 ('encourage one another and build one another up'); Galatians 6:2; Hebrews 12:12.
historicalTrivia: Aaron represents the Priesthood, Hur represents the Royal Line of Judah; together they uphold the Prophet Moses, symbolizing Priesthood, Royalty, and Prophecy supporting the Cross!

dominicalIntent: And Joshua overwhelmed Amalek and his people with the sword (*Vayyachalosh Yehoshua eth-Amaleq ve-eth-ammo le-phi-charev*). JOSHUA DEFEATS AMALEK WITH THE SWORD! Through Moses' intercession and Joshua's leadership, **Joshua overwhelms Amalek (*Vayyachalosh Yehoshua eth-Amaleq*)** with the edge of the sword!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The victory of Christ *Yehoshua* over demonic powers through the Cross); Rev 19:15.
historicalContext: Complete military routing of Amalek's invading force at Rephidim.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyachalosh Yehoshua eth-Amaleq ve-eth-ammo le-phi-charev*: *Vayyachalosh* ('and he mowed down / prostrated / overwhelmed', root *chalash*). *le-phi-charev* ('by the mouth/edge of the sword').
historicalTrivia: The verb *chalash* means mowing down like wheat harvest.

dominicalIntent: Then the Lord said to Moses: 'Write this as a memorial in a book and recite it in the ears of Joshua, that I will utterly blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven' (*Kethov zoth zikkaron ba-ssepher... ki-machoh emcheh eth-zekher Amaleq...*). 'WRITE THIS IN A BOOK! I WILL UTTERLY BLOT OUT AMALEK!' God commands Moses: **'WRITE THIS AS A MEMORIAL IN A BOOK (*ba-ssepher*) AND RECITE IT IN THE EARS OF JOSHUA, FOR I WILL UTTERLY BLOT OUT THE REMEMBRANCE OF AMALEK FROM UNDER HEAVEN!'** FIRST DIRECT COMMAND TO WRITE HOLY SCRIPTURE IN A BOOK!
cccReferences: CCC 105 (GOD THE AUTHOR OF SACRED SCRIPTURE: Divine command to write divine revelations in a Book *Sepher*); CCC 2575; Deut 25:19; 1 Sam 15:3.
historicalContext: First explicit mention of Moses writing the Pentateuch into a formal scroll/book (*Sepher*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe kethov zoth zikkaron ba-ssepher ve-sim be-ozney Yehoshua ki-machoh emcheh eth-zekher Amaleq mi-thachath ha-ssamayim*: *ba-ssepher* ('in the Book/Scroll'). *machoh emcheh* ('wiping out I will wipe out!').
historicalTrivia: This is the very first time in the Bible that God commands the writing of Sacred Scripture in a Book (*ba-ssepher*)!

dominicalIntent: And Moses built an altar and called the name of it, The Lord Is My Banner (*...Vayyiqra shemo YHVH-NISSI*). THE ALTAR OF YAHWEH-NISSI ('YAHWEH IS MY BANNER')! Moses builds an altar of Thanksgiving, naming it **YAHWEH-NISSI ('YAHWEH IS MY BANNER / MY RALLYING STANDARD')**!
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Yahweh our Banner prefiguring the Cross as the victorious standard of Christ); CCC 2575; Isa 11:10; John 12:32.
historicalContext: Building a stone victory altar at the foot of the Rephidim hill.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiven Moshe mizbe'ach vayyiqra shemo YHVH-NISSI*: *YHVH-NISSI* ('Yahweh is my Banner / Standard / Signal-pole', root *ness* = banner/flag/standard).
crossReferences: Isaiah 11:10 ('In that day the root of Jesse shall stand as a signal/banner /*ness* for the peoples'); John 3:14; John 12:32.
historicalTrivia: The Hebrew word *Ness* means a military banner or signal-pole elevated on a hill. In Isaiah 11:10, Christ on the Cross is the ultimate *Ness*!

dominicalIntent: saying: 'A hand upon the throne of the Lord! The Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation' (*...Ki-yad al-kes YAH milchamah le-YHVH ba-Amaleq mi-ddor dor*). PERPETUAL WAR AGAINST AMALEK! Moses proclaims: **'A HAND UPON THE THRONE OF YAH! (*Ki-yad al-kes YAH*) YAHWEH WILL HAVE WAR WITH AMALEK FROM GENERATION TO GENERATION!'** Continuous warfare against satanic opposition.
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (Perpetual spiritual warfare against Satan throughout generations); CCC 2575; 1 Sam 15:2-3; Eph 6:12.
historicalContext: Solemn oath: Yahweh's hand resting upon His heavenly throne (*kes YAH*) swearing perpetual warfare against Amalek until final destruction.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer ki-yad al-kes YAH milchamah le-YHVH ba-Amaleq mi-ddor dor*: *kes YAH* ('throne of Yah'). *mi-ddor dor* ('from generation to generation').
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 25:19; 1 Samuel 15:2-3 (King Saul's war with Agag/Amalek); 1 Samuel 30:17; Esther 3:1 (Haman the Agagite/Amalekite!); Ephesians 6:12.
historicalTrivia: Haman in the Book of Esther was an Agagite (a royal descendant of Amalek)! Mordecai (a Benjamite descendant of Saul) defeated Haman, fulfilling Exodus 17:16!

dominicalIntent: Jethro, the priest of Midian, Moses' father-in-law, heard of all that God had done for Moses and for Israel his people, how the Lord had brought Israel out of Egypt. JETHRO THE MIDIANITE PRIEST HEARS OF YAHWEH'S VICTORY! **Jethro (*Yithro*)**, Midianite Priest and father-in-law (*chothen*) of Moses, hears the international report of the Exodus.
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Gentile recognition of Yahweh's saving deeds); Exod 2:16; Exod 3:1.
historicalContext: Reunion of Moses' family at Mount Horeb/Sinai.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyishma Yithro khohen Midyan chothen Moshe eth kol-asher assah Elohim le-Moshe u-le-Yisra'el ammo ki-hotzi YHVH eth-Yisra'el mi-Mitzrayim*: *chothen* (father-in-law).
historicalTrivia: Jethro is also called Reuel (Exod 2:18) and Hobab (Num 10:29; Judg 4:11).

dominicalIntent: Now Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, had taken Zipporah, Moses' wife, after he had sent her home, Jethro brings Zipporah back to Moses.
historicalContext: Rejoining of Moses' family circle.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vyyiqach Yithro chothen Moshe eth-Tzipporah esheth Moshe achar shillucheha*: *shillucheha* ('after her sending back / dismissal').
historicalTrivia: Zipporah had been sent back to Midian for safety during the dangerous 10 Plagues conflict in Egypt.

dominicalIntent: and her two sons, of whom the name of the one was Gershom (for he said, 'I have been a sojourner in a foreign land'), Naming of Moses' 1st son: **Gershom ('Sojourner there')**.
historicalContext: Etymology of Moses' firstborn son.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-eth shney vaneha asher shem ha-echad Gershom ki amar ger hayithi be-eretz nokhriyyah*: *Gershom* ('sojourner/stranger there').
historicalTrivia: Acts 7:29 notes: 'At this retort Moses fled and became an exile in the land of Midian, where he became the father of two sons'.

dominicalIntent: and the name of the other, Eliezer (for he said, 'The God of my father was my help, and delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh'). NAMING OF MOSES' 2ND SON: ELIEZER ('MY GOD IS HELP')! Etymology of **Eliezer ('My God is Help')**: celebrating God's deliverance from Pharaoh's sword (*mi-cherev Phar'oh*).
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The testimony of divine help embodied in family naming).
historicalContext: Etymology of Moses' second son born in Midian.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-shem ha-echad Eliezer ki-Elohey avi be-ezri vayyatzileni mi-cherev Phar'oh*: *Eliezer* ('God is my help', *Eli* + *ezer*).
historicalTrivia: 1 Chronicles 23:17 notes that the descendants of Eliezer were very numerous.

dominicalIntent: Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, came with his sons and his wife to Moses in the wilderness where he was encamped at the mountain of God. Arrival at Mount Horeb/Sinai ('the Mountain of God' / *Har ha-Elohim*).
historicalContext: Israel encamped at the base of Mount Sinai.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyavo Yithro chothen Moshe u-vanav ve-ishto el-Moshe el-ha-midbar asher-hu choneh sham HAR HA-ELOHIM*: *Har ha-Elohim* ('Mountain of God' = Mount Sinai).
historicalTrivia: This fulfills God's promise in Exodus 3:12: 'When you have brought the people out of Egypt, you shall serve God upon this mountain'!

dominicalIntent: And when he sent word to Moses, 'I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you with your wife and her two sons with her,' Formal heraldic announcement of Jethro's arrival.
historicalContext: Nomadic desert courtesy.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer el-Moshe ani chothenkha Yithro ba eleykha ve-ishtkha u-shney vaneha immah*.
historicalTrivia: Protocol required declaring oneself before entering a desert camp.

dominicalIntent: Moses went out to meet his father-in-law and bowed down and kissed him. And they asked each other of their welfare and went into the tent. MOSES' HUMBLE ORIENTAL RESPECT! The leader of 2 million people goes out, bows down (*vayyishtachu*), kisses his father-in-law, and inquires of his peace (*shalom*).
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Filial piety and humility of God's prophet); Gen 29:13; Gen 33:4.
historicalContext: Eastern oriental greeting of honor (*proskynesis* and kiss).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyetze Moshe li-qrath chothno vayyishtachu vayyissaq-lo vayyish'lu ish-le-re'ehu le-shalom vayyavo'u ha-ohelah*: *vayyishtachu* ('and he bowed low'). *le-shalom* ('for peace/welfare').
historicalTrivia: Despite his supreme international status (Exod 11:3), Moses displays profound humility before his elder father-in-law.

dominicalIntent: Then Moses told his father-in-law all that the Lord had done to Pharaoh and to the Egyptians for Israel's sake, all the hardship that had come upon them in the way, and how the Lord had delivered them (*...vayyatzilemo YHVH*). MOSES' TESTIMONY TO JETHRO! Moses recounts the detailed eyewitness testimony of the Plagues, Red Sea, and wilderness deliverances.
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Personal evangelistic witness converting Gentiles to true worship).
historicalContext: Tent-side narration of Yahweh's saving deeds.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyessapper Moshe le-chothno eth kol-asher assah YHVH le-Phar'oh u-le-Mitzrayim al odoth Yisra'el eth kol-ha-ttla'ah asher matza'atham ba-dderekh vayyatzilemo YHVH*: *ha-ttla'ah* ('the hardship/toil/trouble').
historicalTrivia: Personal testimony (*vayyessapper*) is God's primary instrument for converting the nations.

dominicalIntent: And Jethro rejoiced for all the good that the Lord had done to Israel, in that he had delivered them out of the hand of the Egyptians (*Vayyichad Yithro...*). JETHRO REJOICES IN YAHWEH'S GOODNESS! Jethro experiences deep joy (*Vayyichad Yithro*) over Yahweh's salvation of Israel.
historicalContext: Gentile conversion joy.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyichad Yithro al kol-ha-ttovah asher-assah YHVH le-Yisra'el asher hitzilo mi-yad Mitzrayim*: *Vayyichad* ('and he rejoiced / felt gladness', root *chadah*).
crossReferences: Romans 12:15 ('Rejoice with those who rejoice'); Luke 15:6; Acts 11:23.
historicalTrivia: The verb *chadah* means inner heart-rejoicing.

dominicalIntent: Jethro said: 'Blessed be the Lord, who has delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians and out of the hand of Pharaoh and has delivered the people from under the hand of the Egyptians' (*...Barukh YHVH asher hitzil ethkhem...*). JETHRO'S SOLEMN DOXOLOGY: 'BLESSED BE YAHWEH!' The Gentile priest erupts in formal covenant praise: **'BLESSED BE YAHWEH (*Barukh YHVH*), WHO HAS DELIVERED YOU FROM EGYPT AND PHARAOH!'**
cccReferences: CCC 2086 (Gentile profession of praise to Yahweh); CCC 2575; Gen 14:20; Luke 1:68.
historicalContext: Gentile priest blessing Yahweh (*Barukh YHVH*), mirroring Melchizedek's blessing of Abraham in Genesis 14:20!
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Yithro barukh YHVH asher hitzil ethkhem mi-yad Mitzrayim u-mi-yad Phar'oh asher hitzil eth-ha-am mi-thachath yad-Mitzrayim*: *barukh YHVH* ('Blessed be Yahweh').
crossReferences: Genesis 14:20 (Melchizedek: 'Blessed be God Most High'); 1 Kings 8:56; Luke 1:68 ('Blessed be the Lord God of Israel').
historicalTrivia: Jethro is the 2nd Gentile priest in Genesis-Exodus (after Melchizedek, Gen 14) to pronounce a solemn blessing upon Yahweh!

dominicalIntent: 'Now I know that the Lord is greater than all gods, because in this affair they dealt arrogantly with the people' (*Attah yada'ti ki-ghadol YHVH mi-kol-ha-elohim...*). JETHRO'S CONFESSION OF FAITH: 'NOW I KNOW YAHWEH IS GREATER THAN ALL GODS!' Jethro utters his decisive confession of faith: **'NOW I KNOW THAT YAHWEH IS GREATER THAN ALL GODS (*Attah yada'ti ki-ghadol YHVH mi-kol-ha-elohim*)!'**
cccReferences: CCC 2086 (THE SOVEREIGNTY OF GOD OVER ALL PAGAN DEITIES: Gentile conversion confessing Yahweh's supreme unicity); CCC 2575; 2 Kings 5:15; Ps 135:5.
historicalContext: Gentile priest abandoning polytheism to acknowledge Yahweh's supreme unicity.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Attah yada'ti ki-ghadol YHVH mi-kol-ha-elohim ki va-dhavar asher zadhu alehem*: *Attah yada'ti* ('Now I know!'). *gadol YHVH mi-kol-ha-elohim* ('Yahweh is greater than all the gods').
crossReferences: 2 Kings 5:15 (Naaman: 'Now I know that there is no God in all the earth but in Israel!'); Psalm 135:5; 2 Chronicles 2:5.
historicalTrivia: Jethro's *Attah yada'ti* ('Now I know!') parallels Naaman the Syrian's confession in 2 Kings 5:15!

dominicalIntent: And Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought a burnt offering and sacrifices to God; and Aaron came with all the elders of Israel to eat bread with Moses' father-in-law before God (*...Vyiqach Yithro... olah u-zvachim l-Elohim...*). JETHRO OFFERS BURNT OFFERINGS AND CELEBRATES COVENANT SACRAMENTAL BANQUET! Jethro offers a **burnt offering (*olah*)** and **sacrifices (*zvachim*)** to God; **Aaron and all the elders of Israel come to eat bread with Jethro BEFORE GOD (*liphney ha-Elohim*)**!
cccReferences: CCC 2099 (Sacrifice of whole burnt offerings *olah* and communion banquet prefiguring the Eucharist); CCC 2575; Gen 31:54; 1 Cor 10:18.
historicalContext: Sacrificial communion feast celebrating Jethro's entry into covenant fellowship before the divine presence (*liphney ha-Elohim*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vyiqra Yithro chothen Moshe olah u-zvachim l-Elohim vayyavo Aaron ve-khol ziqney Yisra'el le-ekhol-lechem im-chothen Moshe liphney ha-Elohim*: *olah* (holocaust / whole-burnt offering). *zvachim* (peace offerings/sacrifices). *liphney ha-Elohim* ('in the presence of God').
historicalTrivia: Gentile priest Jethro acts as the officiant offering sacrifices, and High Priest Aaron and the elders eat the sacred meal with him (*liphney ha-Elohim*)!

dominicalIntent: The next day Moses sat to judge the people, and the people stood around Moses from morning till evening (*...vayyeshev Moshe li-shpot eth-ha-am... min-ha-boqer ad-ha-arev*). MOSES' EXHAUSTING JUDICIAL BURDEN! Next morning, Moses sits to judge all disputes solo from morning till evening (*min-ha-boqer ad-ha-arev*).
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The crushing burden of pastoral and judicial governance).
historicalContext: Moses sitting as sole magistrate for 600,000 men and their families.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi mi-mmachrath vayyeshev Moshe li-shpot eth-ha-am vayya'amod ha-am al-Moshe min-ha-boqer ad-ha-arev*: *li-shpot* ('to judge/adjudicate').
historicalTrivia: Deciding thousands of civil, marital, and property disputes single-handedly created an unsustainable pastoral bottleneck.

dominicalIntent: When Moses' father-in-law saw all that he was doing for the people, he said: 'What is this that you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone, and all the people stand around you from morning till evening?' Jethro questions Moses' inefficient administrative model.
historicalContext: Jethro's keen administrative observation.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyar chothen Moshe eth kol-asher-hu ossheh la-am vayyo'mer mah-ha-davar ha-zeh asher attha ossheh la-am maddua attha yoshev le-vaddkha ve-khol-ha-am nitzav aleykha min-boqer ad-arev*: *le-vaddkha* ('by yourself alone').
historicalTrivia: Jethro recognizes that solo leadership leads to burnout for both leader and people.

dominicalIntent: And Moses said to his father-in-law: 'Because the people come to me to inquire of God...' Moses explains his pastoral duty: seeking God's divine will (*lidros Elohim*).
historicalContext: Moses acting as oracle and supreme judge.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Moshe le-chothno ki-yavo elai ha-am li-dros Elohim*: *li-dros Elohim* ('to seek/inquire of God').
historicalTrivia: Inquiring of God (*lidros Elohim*) meant seeking divine judicial decisions.

dominicalIntent: 'when they have a dispute, they come to me and I judge between one man and another, and I make them know the statutes of God and his laws.' Teaching God's statutes (*choqoth*) and laws (*toroth*).
historicalContext: Instruction in divine law prior to the formal Sinai Code.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ki-yihyeh lahem davar ba elai ve-shaphathti beyn ish u-veyn re'ehu ve-hoda'ti eth-choqey ha-Elohim ve-eth-thorothav*: *choqey* (statutes). *thorothav* (his laws/instructions).
historicalTrivia: Moses was already teaching core Torah principles (*thoroth*) before Sinai!

dominicalIntent: Moses' father-in-law said to him: 'What you are doing is not good.' Jethro's honest rebuke: 'Lo tov ha-davar' ('This thing is not good!').
historicalContext: Fraternal correction of the prophet by his father-in-law.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer chothen Moshe elav lo-tov ha-davar asher attha ossheh*: *lo-tov* ('not good!').
crossReferences: Genesis 2:18 ('It is not good that man should be alone'); Numbers 11:14.
historicalTrivia: This is one of the rare places in Scripture where a human tells Moses that his action is 'not good' (*lo-tov*)!

dominicalIntent: 'You and the people with you will certainly wear yourselves out, for the thing is too heavy for you. You are not able to do it alone' (*Navol thivvol gam-attha... ki-khaved mimmenkha ha-davar lo-thukhal assho le-vaddkha*). BURNOUT WARNING: 'YOU WILL WEAR YOURSELF OUT!' Jethro warns: **'YOU WILL CERTAINLY WEAR YOURSELF OUT (*Navol thivvol*), FOR THE TASK IS TOO HEAVY FOR YOU (*khaved mimmenkha*)!'**
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The wisdom of shared governance and delegation in the Church).
historicalContext: Administrative diagnosis of pastoral exhaustion and exhaustion of the populace.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Navol thivvol gam-attha gam-ha-am ha-zeh asher immakh ki-khaved mimmenkha ha-davar lo-thukhal assho le-vaddkha*: *Navol thivvol* (infinitive absolute: 'fading/wither you will certainly wither/wear out!').
crossReferences: Numbers 11:14 ('I am not able to carry all this people alone, the burden is too heavy for me'); Deuteronomy 1:9.
historicalTrivia: The verb *navol* means to wither like a fading leaf in drought.

dominicalIntent: 'Now obey my voice; I will give you advice, and God be with you! You shall represent the people before God and bring their cases to God' (*...Heyeh attha la-am mul ha-Elohim...*). JETHRO'S PLAN: MOSES STANDS BEFORE GOD AS INTERCESSOR! Jethro outlines the primary role of the prophet: Moses focuses on standing before God (*mul ha-Elohim*) in prayer and bringing hard cases to Him.
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The primary duty of spiritual leaders: prayer and intercession); Acts 6:4 ('We will devote ourselves to prayer and to the ministry of the word').
historicalContext: Dividing spiritual leadership (intercession/teaching) from civil administration (judging minor cases).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Attah shma be-qoli i'atzkha ve-yihi Elohim immakh heyeh attha la-am mul ha-Elohim ve-heve'tha attha eth-ha-ddevarim el-ha-Elohim*: *mul ha-Elohim* ('opposite / before God').
crossReferences: Acts 6:4 ('But we will devote ourselves to prayer and to the ministry of the word'); Exodus 24:2.
historicalTrivia: Acts 6:2-4 (appointing Deacons so the Apostles could focus on prayer) directly fulfills Jethro's advice in Exodus 18:19!

dominicalIntent: 'and you shall warn them about the statutes and the laws, and make them know the way in which they must walk and what they must do.' Moses' core task: teaching the way (*ha-dderekh*) and the work (*ha-mma'asseh*).
historicalContext: Catechetical instruction of the whole nation.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-hizhartha eth-hem eth-ha-cchoqim ve-eth-ha-thoroth ve-hoda'tha lahem eth-ha-dderekh yelkhu vah ve-eth-ha-mma'asseh asher ya'assun*: *ha-dderekh* ('the way' -> 'The Way' Acts 9:2!). *ha-mma'asseh* ('the work/deed').
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 5:33; Psalm 143:8; Acts 9:2 ('belonging to The Way').
historicalTrivia: The term *ha-dderekh* ('the way') became the title for early Christianity in the Book of Acts (Acts 9:2; 19:9)!

dominicalIntent: 'Moreover, look for able men from all the people, men who fear God, who are trustworthy and hate a bribe, and place such men over the people as chiefs of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens' (*...anshey-chayil yir'ey Elohim anshey emeth ssone'ey vetza...*). QUALIFICATIONS FOR JUDGES & DELEGATED HIERARCHY! Jethro's 4 moral qualifications for leaders: (1) **Able men (*anshey-chayil*)**, (2) **God-fearing (*yir'ey Elohim*)**, (3) **Trustworthy (*anshey emeth*)**, (4) **Hating dishonest gain (*ssone'ey vetza*)**! Appointing chiefs of **thousands (*alaphim*)**, **hundreds (*me'oth*)**, **fifties (*chamishim*)**, and **tens (*asaroth*)**! FOUNDATION OF CHURCH HIERARCHY & DEACONATE!
cccReferences: CCC 874-896 (THE HIERARCHICAL CONSTITUTION OF THE CHURCH: Delegated authority in the Church prefigured by Jethro's judicial hierarchy); CCC 1536; CCC 2575; Acts 6:3; 1 Tim 3:1-13; Tit 1:5-9.
historicalContext: Organizing 600,000 men into a 4-tier judicial hierarchy (78,600 judges total!).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-attha thechezeh mi-kol-ha-am anshey-chayil yir'ey Elohim anshey emeth ssone'ey vetza ve-samtha alehem ssarey alaphim ssarey me'oth ssarey chamishim ve-ssarey asaroth*: *anshey-chayil* ('men of valor/character'). *ssone'ey vetza* ('haters of bribes/unjust gain').
crossReferences: Acts 6:3 ('pick out from among you seven men of good repute, full of the Spirit and of wisdom'); 1 Timothy 3:1-13; Titus 1:5-9; Deuteronomy 1:13-17.
historicalTrivia: Math check: for 600,000 men, appointing chiefs of 1000s (600), 100s (6,000), 50s (12,000), and 10s (60,000) created exactly **78,600 local judges**!

dominicalIntent: 'And let them judge the people at all times. Every great matter they shall bring to you, but any small matter they shall decide themselves. So it will be easier for you, and they will bear the burden with you.' DELEGATION AND SUBSIDIARITY! Minor cases decided at local 10-man court levels; major appellate cases brought to Moses. **THE CATHOLIC PRINCIPLE OF SUBSIDIARITY PREFIGURED!**
cccReferences: CCC 1883 (THE PRINCIPLE OF SUBSIDIARITY: Decisions made at the lowest competent level, prefigured by Jethro's system); CCC 2575; Gal 6:2.
historicalContext: Creation of lower courts of first instance and a supreme appellate court.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-shaphtu eth-ha-am be-khol-eth ve-hayah kol-ha-davar ha-ggadol yavi'u eleykha ve-khol-ha-davar ha-qqaton yishptu-hem ve-ha-qel me-aleykha ve-nass'u itthakh*: *ha-davar ha-ggadol* ('the great matter'). *ha-davar ha-qqaton* ('the small matter'). *ve-ha-qel* ('make it lighter').
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 1:17 ('The case that is too hard for you, you shall bring to me'); Galatians 6:2 ('Bear one another's burdens'); Acts 6:2-4.
historicalTrivia: CCC 1883 defines Subsidiarity: 'Neither the state nor any larger society should substitute itself for the initiative and responsibility of individuals and intermediary bodies'!

dominicalIntent: 'If you do this, God will direct you, you will be able to endure, and all this people also will go to their place in peace.' Results of delegation: pastoral endurance and national peace (*shalom*).
historicalContext: Promising stability and peace for the whole assembly.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Im eth-ha-davar ha-zeh ta'asseh ve-tzivvkha Elohim ve-yakhaltha amod ve-gham kol-ha-am ha-zeh al-meqomo yavo be-shalom*: *be-shalom* ('in peace/wholeness').
crossReferences: Numbers 11:17; 1 Corinthians 14:33 ('God is not a God of confusion but of peace').
historicalTrivia: Orderly delegation creates communal peace (*shalom*).

dominicalIntent: So Moses listened to the voice of his father-in-law and did all that he had said (*Vayyishma Moshe le-qol chothno...*). MOSES' SUPREME HUMILITY IN OBEYING ADVICE! Moses (who spoke face-to-face with God!) humbly listens to and implements the advice of his Midianite father-in-law!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Moses' docility and humility accepting wise counsel).
historicalContext: The supreme prophet accepting administrative counsel from a Gentile elder.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyishma Moshe le-qol chothno vayya'as kol asher amar*.
historicalTrivia: Moses' willingness to learn from Jethro demonstrates true meekness (*anav*, Num 12:3).

dominicalIntent: Moses chose able men out of all Israel and made them heads over the people, chiefs of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens. Moses selects and ordains 78,600 judges across all 12 tribes.
cccReferences: CCC 874; CCC 2575; Deut 1:15.
historicalContext: Implementation of the 4-tier judicial hierarchy.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyivchar Moshe anshey-chayil mi-kol-Yisra'el vayyitten otham rashim al-ha-am ssarey alaphim ssarey me'oth ssarey chamishim ve-ssarey asaroth*: *anshey-chayil* ('men of character/strength').
historicalTrivia: Deuteronomy 1:13 adds that the 12 tribes themselves chose these men from their own clans!

dominicalIntent: And they judged the people at all times. Hard cases they brought to Moses, but any small matter they decided themselves. Functioning of the judicial system.
historicalContext: Daily operation of lower courts and Supreme Court.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-shaphtu eth-ha-am be-khol-eth eth-ha-davar ha-qqasheh yevi'un el-Moshe ve-khol-ha-davar ha-qqaton yishptu hem*: *ha-davar ha-qqasheh* ('the hard matter').
historicalTrivia: Moses presided over the Supreme Court for constitutional and divine oracle cases.

dominicalIntent: Then Moses let his father-in-law depart, and he went his way to his own country (*Vayyashallach Moshe eth-chothno vayyelekh lo el-artzo*). Moses sends Jethro back to Midian with blessing.
historicalContext: Jethro returning to Midian (while his son Hobab stayed to guide Israel, Num 10:29-32).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyashallach Moshe eth-chothno vayyelekh lo el-artzo*.
historicalTrivia: Jethro's clan (the Kenites) accompanied Israel into Canaan and settled near Jericho and Hebron (Judg 1:16)!

dominicalIntent: On the third new moon after the people of Israel had gone out of the land of Egypt, on that day they came into the wilderness of Sinai. ARRIVAL AT MOUNT SINAI! Exactly on Sivan 1 (3rd month, 45 days after Passover), Israel enters the **Wilderness of Sinai (*Midbar-Sinai*)**.
cccReferences: CCC 62 (The Sinai Covenant establishing Israel as God's holy nation); CCC 2060; CCC 2575.
historicalContext: Sivan 1, 1446 BC: Israel arrives at Mount Sinai, where they will remain for 11 months and 19 days (until Numbers 10:11).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ba-chodesh ha-shlishi le-tze'th bney-Yisra'el me-eretz Mitzrayim ba-yom ha-zeh ba'u midbar Sinai*: *midbar Sinai* ('Wilderness of Sinai').
historicalTrivia: This date is the foundation for the Feast of Pentecost (*Shavuot*), celebrated 50 days after Passover!

dominicalIntent: They set out from Rephidim and came into the wilderness of Sinai, and they encamped in the wilderness. There Israel encamped before the mountain (*...vayyichan-sham YISRA'EL neged ha-har*). ENCAMPING BEFORE THE HOLY MOUNTAIN! Israel encamps in the plain directly facing Mount Sinai (*neged ha-har*).
historicalContext: The plain of *Er-Raha* at the foot of Mount Sinai (*Jebel Musa*), capable of accommodating over 2 million people.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiss'u mi-Rphidim vayyavo'u midbar Sinai vayyachanu ba-midbar vayyichan-sham Yisra'el neged ha-har*: *vayyichan* (singular verb: 'and Israel encamped as ONE MAN!').
historicalTrivia: Rashi notes that the singular verb *vayyichan* ('and he encamped') signifies that all 12 tribes were united 'as one man with one heart'!

dominicalIntent: while Moses went up to God. The Lord called to him out of the mountain, saying: 'Thus you shall say to the house of Jacob, and tell the people of Israel...' Moses ascends the mountain; Yahweh addresses him out of the mountain peak.
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Moses ascending the mountain as mediator of the Covenant); Acts 7:38.
historicalContext: Moses' 1st mountain ascent at Sinai.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-Moshe alah el-ha-Elohim vayyiqra elav YHVH min-ha-har le'mor koh thomar le-veyth Ya'aqov ve-thagged li-vney Yisra'el*.
crossReferences: Acts 7:38 ('This is the one who was in the congregation in the wilderness with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai'); Exodus 24:15-18.
historicalTrivia: Moses made 7 distinct ascents up Mount Sinai during his time at the holy mountain.

dominicalIntent: 'You yourselves have seen what I did to the Egyptians, and how I bore you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself' (*...va-essa ethkhem al-khanphey nesharim va-avi ethkhem elai*). 'I BORE YOU ON EAGLES' WINGS (*AL-KHANPHEY NESHARIM*) AND BROUGHT YOU TO MYSELF!' God describes His tender saving love: **'I BORE YOU ON EAGLES' WINGS AND BROUGHT YOU TO MYSELF!'**
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (God's fatherly love raising up His people); CCC 2575; Deut 32:11; Rev 12:14.
historicalContext: The mother eagle training her eaglets, catching them on her wings if they fall.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Athem re'ithem asher assithi le-Mitzrayim va-essa ethkhem al-khanphey nesharim va-avi ethkhem elai*: *nesharim* (eagles/griffon vultures).
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 32:11 ('Like an eagle that stirs up its nest... bearing them on its pinions'); Revelation 12:14 ('the woman was given the two wings of the great eagle').
historicalTrivia: Revelation 12:14 quotes Exodus 19:4: the Woman clothed with the sun is given 'the two wings of the great eagle' to fly into the wilderness!

dominicalIntent: 'Now therefore, if you will indeed obey my voice and keep my covenant, you shall be my treasured possession among all peoples, for all the earth is mine' (*...ve-hiyithem li sghullah mi-kol-ha-ammim...*). ISRAEL AS GOD'S TREASURED POSSESSION (*SGHULLAH*)! Yahweh offers the Covenant terms: **'IF YOU OBEY MY VOICE AND KEEP MY COVENANT, YOU SHALL BE MY TREASURED POSSESSION (*Sghullah*) AMONG ALL PEOPLES!'** CITED IN 1 PETER 2:9!
cccReferences: CCC 781 (THE PEOPLE OF GOD: 1 Peter 2:9 citing Exod 19:5-6: 'a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's own special possession'); CCC 2063; CCC 2575; 1 Pet 2:9; Deut 7:6.
historicalContext: The term *Sghullah* refers to a king's private, priceless royal jewel/treasury.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-attah im-shamoa tishm'u be-qoli u-shmarthem eth-brithi ve-hiyithem li sghullah mi-kol-ha-ammim ki-li kol-ha-aretz*: *sghullah* (treasured personal jewel/possession).
historicalTrivia: 1 Peter 2:9 translates *sghullah* into Greek as *laos eis peripoiēsin* ('a people for God's own possession')!

dominicalIntent: 'and you shall be to me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. These are the words that you shall speak to the people of Israel' (*...MAMLEKHETH KOHANIM VE-GOY QADOSH...*). KINGDOM OF PRIESTS AND A HOLY NATION—CITED IN 1 PETER 2:9 AND REVELATION 1:6! GOD'S SUPREME CHARTER FOR HIS PEOPLE! Yahweh decrees: **'YOU SHALL BE TO ME A KINGDOM OF PRIESTS (*Mamlekheth Kohanim*) AND A HOLY NATION (*Goy Qadosh*)!'** **THIS IS THE DIRECT OLD TESTAMENT FOUNDATION FOR THE COMMON PRIESTHOOD OF ALL BAPTIZED CHRISTIANS IN 1 PETER 2:9 AND REVELATION 1:6!**
cccReferences: CCC 784 (THE COMMON PRIESTHOOD OF THE FAITHFUL: 1 Peter 2:9 and Rev 1:6 citing Exod 19:6: 'made us a kingdom, priests to his God and Father'); CCC 1546 (The royal priesthood of all believers); CCC 2063; CCC 2575; 1 Pet 2:9; Rev 1:6; Rev 5:10.
historicalContext: The original divine plan: the entire nation of Israel to act as royal priests (*Kohanim*) mediating God's blessing to all Gentile nations.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-athem thihyu-li mamlekheth kohanim ve-goy qadosh elleh ha-ddevarim asher tdabber el-bney Yisra'el*: *mamlekheth kohanim* (a kingdom of priests, LXX *basileion hierateuma*). *goy qadosh* (a holy nation, LXX *ethnos hagion*).
crossReferences: 1 Peter 2:9 ('you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood / *basileion hierateuma*, a holy nation / *ethnos hagion*'); Revelation 1:6; Revelation 5:10; Isaiah 61:6.
historicalTrivia: CCC 1546 cites Exodus 19:6 to teach that through Baptism, every Christian is anointed into the **Common Priesthood of the Faithful** (*hierateuma basileion*)!

dominicalIntent: So Moses came and called the elders of the people and set before them all these words that the Lord had commanded him. Moses presents the Covenant charter to the elders of Israel.
historicalContext: Moses descending to present God's proposal to the 70 elders of the 12 tribes.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyavo Moshe vayyiqra le-ziqney ha-am vayyassem liphneyhem eth kol-ha-ddevarim ha-elleh asher tzivvahu YHVH*.
historicalTrivia: The elders act as representatives of the 12-tribe nation.

dominicalIntent: All the people answered together and said: 'All that the Lord has spoken we will do.' And Moses reported the words of the people to the Lord (*...Kol asher-dibber YHVH na'asseh...*). ISRAEL'S COVENANT ACCLAMATION: 'ALL THAT YAHWEH HAS SPOKEN WE WILL DO!' All the people answer in unanimous liturgical consent: **'ALL THAT YAHWEH HAS SPOKEN WE WILL DO (*Kol asher-dibber YHVH na'asseh*)!'**
cccReferences: CCC 2060 (Liturgical covenant consent of the assembly); CCC 2575; Exod 24:3; Exod 24:7.
historicalContext: The 12 tribes unanimously accepting Yahweh's proposal to enter the Sinai Covenant.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'anu khol-ha-am yachdav vayyo'mru kol asher-dibber YHVH na'asseh vayyashev Moshe eth-divrey ha-am el-YHVH*: *na'asseh* ('we will do / execute').
crossReferences: Exodus 24:3; Exodus 24:7 ('All that the Lord has spoken we will do, and we will be obedient'); Deuteronomy 5:27.
historicalTrivia: The phrase *na'asseh ve-nishma* ('we will do and we will hear/obey', Exod 24:7) became Israel's pledge of total covenant trust.

dominicalIntent: And the Lord said to Moses: 'Behold, I am coming to you in a thick cloud, that the people may hear when I speak with you, and may also believe you forever.' When Moses told the words of the people to the Lord... THE THICK CLOUD (*AV HA-ANAN*) ANNOUNCED! Yahweh announces He will descend in a **thick, dense cloud (*be-av ha-anan*)** so all Israel hears God's voice speaking with Moses.
cccReferences: CCC 697 (THE CLOUD OF THE SPIRIT: God approaching His people in the thick cloud of divine mystery); CCC 2575; Deut 4:11; Matt 17:5.
historicalContext: Preparing the assembly for the audible, public divine voice at Sinai.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe hinneh anokhi ba eleykha be-av ha-anan le-ma'an yishma ha-am be-dhabberi immakh ve-gham-bakha ya'aminu le-olam vayyagged Moshe eth-divrey ha-am el-YHVH*: *be-av ha-anan* ('in the thickness/density of the cloud').
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 4:11; Psalm 18:11; Matthew 17:5; 1 Kings 8:12 ('The Lord has said that he would dwell in thick darkness').
historicalTrivia: At the Transfiguration, the Father spoke from the same Cloud (*av ha-anan*): 'This is my beloved Son... listen to him' (Matt 17:5)!

dominicalIntent: the Lord said to Moses: 'Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their garments...' THREE-DAY SANCTIFICATION: CONSECRATE AND WASH GARMENTS! Yahweh commands a 3-day ritual purification: (1) **Consecrate the people (*ve-qiddashtam*)** today and tomorrow, (2) **Washing of garments (*vi-khivssu simlotham*)**.
cccReferences: CCC 1152 (Ritual washings prefiguring the interior cleansing of Baptism); CCC 2575; Heb 10:22.
historicalContext: 3-day preparation for encountering God's real presence on the 3rd day.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe lekh el-ha-am ve-qiddashtam ha-yom u-machar vi-khivssu simlotham*: *ve-qiddashtam* ('and sanctify/consecrate them'). *vi-khivssu* ('and let them wash/launder').
crossReferences: Genesis 35:2; Leviticus 15:5; Hebrews 10:22 ('our bodies washed with pure water'); Revelation 7:14.
historicalTrivia: Washing garments (*khivssu simlotham*) symbolized purging all Egyptian pollution from body and soul.

dominicalIntent: 'and be ready for the third day. For on the third day the Lord will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people' (*...ki ba-yom ha-shlishi yerhed YHVH le-eyney khol-ha-am al-har Sinai*). 'ON THE THIRD DAY YAHWEH WILL COME DOWN!' PREFIGURING THE RESURRECTION ON THE THIRD DAY! God promises: **'ON THE THIRD DAY YAHWEH WILL COME DOWN (*ba-yom ha-shlishi yerhed YHVH*) ON MOUNT SINAI IN THE SIGHT OF ALL THE PEOPLE!'**
cccReferences: CCC 1167 (THE THIRD DAY MYSTERY: God's ultimate revelation and victory occurring on the 3rd day, prefiguring the Resurrection of Jesus Christ); CCC 2575; Hos 6:2; 1 Cor 15:4.
historicalContext: The 3rd day of consecration (Sivan 6) when the Law was given at Sinai.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-hayu nkhonim la-yom ha-shlishi ki ba-yom ha-shlishi yerhed YHVH le-eyney khol-ha-am al-har Sinai*: *ba-yom ha-shlishi* ('on the third day').
crossReferences: Hosea 6:2 ('On the third day he will raise us up'); 1 Corinthians 15:4 ('raised on the third day in accordance with the Scriptures'); Luke 24:46.
historicalTrivia: In Jewish tradition, Sivan 6 (the 3rd day of Sinai) is the exact date of **Shavuot / Pentecost**, the day the Holy Spirit descended on the Church (Acts 2:1)!

dominicalIntent: 'And you shall set limits for the people all around, saying, "Take care not to go up into the mountain or touch the edge of it. Whoever touches the mountain shall be put to death."' STRICT BOUNDARIES AROUND THE MOUNTAIN! God commands Moses to set boundaries (*higgbaltha*); anyone who touches the mountain shall die (*moth yumath*).
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (The overwhelming holiness of God inspiring sacred fear); CCC 2575; Heb 12:18-20.
historicalContext: Physical boundary line fence surrounding the base of Mount Sinai.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-higgbaltha eth-ha-am ssaviv le'mor hi-ssavru lakhem aloth ba-har u-n-gho'a be-qatzehu kol-ha-nno'ghe'a ba-har moth yumath*: *higgbaltha* ('you shall set a boundary/limit'). *moth yumath* ('dying he shall die').
crossReferences: Hebrews 12:18-20 ('For you have not come to what may be touched, a blazing fire... for they could not bear the order that was given, "If even a beast touches the mountain, it shall be stoned"'); Exodus 19:23.
