historicalTrivia: Hebrews 12:18-24 contrasts the terrifying, untouchable Mount Sinai with the approachable grace of Mount Zion and the Heavenly Jerusalem!

dominicalIntent: 'No hand shall touch him, but he shall be stoned or shot; whether beast or man, he shall not live. When the trumpet sounds a long blast, they shall come up to the mountain.' Penalty of stoning (*ssaqol yissaqel*) or archery shooting for boundary violators. Long blast of the ram's horn (*Yovel*) signals permission to approach.
historicalContext: Executing boundary violators without physical contact (stoning or shooting from afar). The long *Yovel* (ram's horn blast).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Lo-thigga bo yad ki-ssaqol yissaqel o-yaroh yiyareh im-bhemah im-ish lo yichyeh bi-mshokh ha-yovel hemah ya'alu va-har*: *ha-yovel* (the ram's horn / Jubilee trumpet).
historicalTrivia: The word *Yovel* (ram's horn) is the root of the word **JUBILEE**!

dominicalIntent: So Moses went down from the mountain to the people and consecrated the people; and they washed their garments. Moses executes the 3-day consecration.
historicalContext: Moses descending to oversee ritual washings.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyerhed Moshe min-ha-har el-ha-am vayqaddesh eth-ha-am vaykhavssu simlotham*.
historicalTrivia: All 2 million Israelites washed their outer cloaks.

dominicalIntent: And he said to the people: 'Be ready for the third day; do not go near a woman.' Conjugal abstinence for 3 days to maintain maximal ritual purity.
historicalContext: Conjugal abstinence (*al-thiggshu el-ishah*) commanded for total focus on divine encounter.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer el-ha-am heyu nkhonim li-shlosheth yamim al-thiggshu el-ishah*: *al-thiggshu* ('do not approach').
historicalTrivia: 1 Corinthians 7:5 cites temporary abstinence by mutual consent for devoted prayer, rooted in Exodus 19:15.

dominicalIntent: On the morning of the third day there were thunders and lightnings and a thick cloud on the mountain and a very loud trumpet blast, so that all the people in the camp trembled (*Vayehi ba-yom ha-shlishi... qoloth u-vraqim ve-anan kaved... ve-qol shophar chazaq me'od...*). THE APOCALYPTIC THEOPHANY OF SINAI! On the 3rd day morning (Sivan 6): (1) **THUNDERS (*Qoloth*) AND LIGHTNINGS (*Vraqim*)**, (2) **THICK CLOUD (*Anan Kaved*)**, (3) **A VERY LOUD TRUMPET BLAST (*Qol Shophar Chazaq Me'od*)**! **ALL THE PEOPLE IN THE CAMP TREMBLED (*Vayyecheradh kol-ha-am*)!**
cccReferences: CCC 696 (Fire, smoke, and trumpet sound manifesting divine holiness); CCC 2575; Heb 12:18-21; Rev 4:5.
historicalContext: The cosmic divine descent (*Theophany*) on Mount Sinai. The supernatural *Shophar* (ram's horn blast) blaring from heaven.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi ba-yom ha-shlishi bi-yoth ha-bboqer vayehi qoloth u-vraqim ve-anan kaved al-ha-har ve-qol shophar chazaq me'od vayyecheradh kol-ha-am asher ba-mmachaneh*: *qoloth* (thunders/voices). *vraqim* (lightnings). *qol shophar* ('voice/sound of the shofar').
crossReferences: Hebrews 12:18-21; Revelation 4:5 ('From the throne came flashes of lightning, and rumblings and peals of thunder'); Revelation 8:5; Psalm 77:18.
historicalTrivia: Revelation 4:5 and 8:5 use Exodus 19:16's thunder, lightning, and trumpet blasts to describe God's heavenly throne!

dominicalIntent: Then Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet God, and they took their stand at the foot of the mountain (*...li-qrath ha-Elohim... be-thachthith ha-har*). STANDING AT THE FOOT OF THE MOUNTAIN! Moses leads the terrified assembly out of the camp to meet God (*li-qrath ha-Elohim*); they stand at the base of the mountain (*be-thachthith ha-har*).
cccReferences: CCC 2575; Deut 4:11.
historicalContext: The entire nation standing in the plain of Er-Raha directly below the roaring, burning mountain peak.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyotze Moshe eth-ha-am li-qrath ha-Elohim min-ha-mmachaneh vayyithyatzvu be-thachthith ha-har*: *li-qrath ha-Elohim* ('to meet / encounter God'). *be-thachthith* ('at the lowest part / base').
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 4:11 ('You came near and stood at the foot of the mountain, while the mountain burned with fire to the heart of heaven'); Deuteronomy 5:5.
historicalTrivia: Deuteronomy 4:11 notes that Mount Sinai burned with fire 'to the heart of heaven' (*ad-lev ha-ssamayim*)!

dominicalIntent: Now Mount Sinai was wrapped in smoke because the Lord had descended on it in fire. The smoke of it went up like the smoke of a kiln, and the whole mountain trembled greatly (*Ve-har Sinai ashan kullo mi-ppney asher yarad alav YHVH ba-esh... vayyecheradh kol-ha-har me'od*). MOUNT SINAI ENVELOPED IN FIRE AND SMOKE! THE WHOLE MOUNTAIN SHAKES VIOLENTLY! **MOUNT SINAI WAS WRAPPED ENTIRELY IN SMOKE BECAUSE YAHWEH DESCENDED ON IT IN FIRE (*ba-esh*)**! Smoke rose like a smelting furnace (*kivshan*), and **THE WHOLE MOUNTAIN SHHOOK VIOLENTLY (*vayyecheradh kol-ha-har me'od*)**!
cccReferences: CCC 696 (FIRE AS THE SIGN OF THE HOLY SPIRIT: Yahweh descending in fire on Sinai, fulfilled in the tongues of fire at Pentecost, Acts 2:3); CCC 2575; Heb 12:18; Ps 68:8; Acts 2:3.
historicalContext: Volcanic-like divine fire (*esh*) engulfing the granite peak of Mount Sinai; massive seismic quaking (*vayyecheradh*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-har Sinai ashan kullo mi-ppney asher yarad alav YHVH ba-esh vayya'al ashano ke-eshan ha-kkivshan vayyecheradh kol-ha-har me'od*: *ba-esh* ('in fire'). *kivshan* (smelting kiln/furnace). *vayyecheradh* ('trembled/quaked violently').
crossReferences: Acts 2:3 (Tongues of fire at Pentecost!); Hebrews 12:18; Psalm 68:8 ('the earth quaked, the heavens poured down rain, before God, the One of Sinai'); Psalm 104:32.
historicalTrivia: The divine fire on Sinai (*ba-esh*) is the direct Old Testament type of the **Tongues of Fire** that descended on the 120 disciples at Pentecost in Acts 2:3!

dominicalIntent: And as the sound of the trumpet grew louder and louder, Moses spoke, and God answered him in thunder (*...ve-ha-Elohim ya'anennu ve-qol*). THE CRESCENDO TRUMPET BLAST AND GOD ANSWERING IN THUNDER! The heavenly Shophar blast grows louder and louder (*hōlēkh ve-chazaq me'od*); Moses speaks, and **GOD ANSWERS HIM IN AN AUDIBLE THUNDER-VOICE (*ve-ha-Elohim ya'anennu ve-qol*)**!
cccReferences: CCC 2575; Heb 12:19 ('the sound of a trumpet and a voice whose words made the hearers beg that no further messages be spoken to them'); John 12:28-29.
historicalContext: The crescendo blast of the divine Shophar, accompanied by God's thunder-voice (*Qol*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi qol ha-shophar holekh ve-chazaq me'od Moshe yedabber ve-ha-Elohim ya'anennu ve-qol*: *holekh ve-chazaq me'od* ('going and getting exceedingly louder'). *ve-qol* ('in a voice / thunder').
crossReferences: Hebrews 12:19; John 12:28-29 ('The crowd that stood there and heard it said that it had thundered'); Psalm 29:3.
historicalTrivia: John 12:28-29 records that when the Father spoke to Jesus from heaven, the crowd thought it was thunder (*brontē*), echoing Sinai!

dominicalIntent: The Lord came down on Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain. And the Lord called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up. Yahweh descends on Mount Sinai's peak and summons Moses to ascend alone.
historicalContext: Moses' 2nd mountain ascent into the divine fire and cloud.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyerhed YHVH al-har Sinai el-rosh ha-har vayyiqra YHVH le-Moshe el-rosh ha-har vayya'al Moshe*.
historicalTrivia: Moses ascends into the blazing summit.

dominicalIntent: And the Lord said to Moses: 'Go down and warn the people, lest they break through to the Lord to look and many of them perish.' God commands Moses to warn the people against unholy curiosity.
historicalContext: Warning against breaking the boundary line to gaze upon the divine glory.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe red ha'ed ba-am pen-yeherssu el-YHVH lir'oth ve-naphal mimmennu rav*: *yeherssu* ('break through / burst past').
crossReferences: Exodus 3:5; 1 Samuel 6:19 (50,070 men of Beth-shemesh struck down for gazing into the Ark!).
historicalTrivia: 1 Samuel 6:19 proves this principle: 50,070 men died at Beth-shemesh for looking inside the Ark of the Covenant!

dominicalIntent: 'Also let the priests who come near to the Lord consecrate themselves, lest the Lord break out against them' (*...ve-gham ha-kkohanim ha-nniggashim el-YHVH yithqaddashu pen-yiphrotz bahem YHVH*). CONSECRATION OF THE PRIESTS! The firstborn priests (*Kohanim*) who approach Yahweh must undergo special sanctification lest Yahweh break out against them (*pen-yiphrotz*).
cccReferences: CCC 1536 (Sanctification required for sacred ministers); CCC 2575; 2 Sam 6:7.
historicalContext: Pre-Levitical firstborn priests who served before the golden calf apostasy.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-gham ha-kkohanim ha-nniggashim el-YHVH yithqaddashu pen-yiphrotz bahem YHVH*: *pen-yiphrotz* ('lest He burst/break out in judgment', root *paratz* -> Perez!).
crossReferences: 2 Samuel 6:7 (Uzzah struck down when God broke out / *paratz*); Exodus 24:5; Leviticus 10:1-3.
historicalTrivia: The verb *paratz* ('break out') is used in 2 Samuel 6:8 for Perez-uzzah when Uzzah touched the Ark!

dominicalIntent: Moses said to the Lord: 'The people cannot come up to Mount Sinai, for you yourself warned us, saying, "Set limits around the mountain and consecrate it."' Moses confirms that boundary lines have been set.
historicalContext: Moses reporting full boundary enforcement.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Moshe el-YHVH lo-yukhal ha-am la-aloth el-har Sinai ki-attha ha'edothah banu le'mor haghbel eth-ha-har ve-qiddashto*.
historicalTrivia: Moses assures God that the boundary fence is secure.

dominicalIntent: And the Lord said to him: 'Go down, and come up bringing Aaron with you. But do not let the priests and the people break through to come up to the Lord, lest he break out against them.' God instructs Moses to descend and bring Aaron up with him.
historicalContext: Aaron selected to accompany Moses for the 20 Commandments revelation.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer elav YHVH lekh-red ve-alitha attha ve-Aaron immakh ve-ha-kkohanim ve-ha-am al-yeherssu la-aloth el-YHVH pen-yiphrotz-bam*.
historicalTrivia: Aaron is granted unique privilege alongside Moses.

dominicalIntent: So Moses went down to the people and told them. Moses descends and delivers the final warnings before the 10 Commandments.
cccReferences: CCC 2056 (The preparation for the 10 Commandments); CCC 2575.
historicalContext: Moses standing before the silent, trembling 12-tribe assembly as the 10 Commandments are about to be spoken.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyerhed Moshe el-ha-am vayyo'mer alehem*.
historicalTrivia: Exodus 19 closes with Moses standing among the people, setting the stage for Exodus 20!

dominicalIntent: And God spoke all these words, saying (*Vayyedabber Elohim eth kol-ha-ddevarim ha-elleh le'mor*). GOD HIMSELF SPEAKS THE TEN COMMANDMENTS DIRECTLY! For the first and only time in all of Scripture, **GOD HIMSELF SPEAKS DIRECTLY AND AUDIBLY TO THE ENTIRE ASSEMBLED NATION** without a human intermediary! (Deut 4:12-13; CCC 2056).
cccReferences: CCC 2056 (The Ten Words spoken by God Himself directly to the whole people); CCC 2058; CCC 2059.
historicalContext: Sivan 6, 1446 BC: The divine voice thundering the Decalogue directly at the 12-tribe assembly standing at the base of burning Sinai.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyedabber Elohim eth kol-ha-ddevarim ha-elleh le'mor*: *Vayyedabber Elohim* ('And God spoke'). *kol-ha-ddevarim* ('all these words'). The rabbis call the Decalogue the *Assereth ha-Ddevarim* ('The Ten Words').
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 4:12-13; Deuteronomy 5:4 ('The Lord spoke with you face to face at the mountain'); Acts 7:38; Hebrews 12:18-19.
historicalTrivia: Deuteronomy 5:4 records: 'Yahweh spoke with you FACE TO FACE (*panim be-phanim*) at the mountain out of the fire.' An event of utterly unparalleled cosmic magnitude!

dominicalIntent: 'I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.' (*ANOKHI YHVH ELOHEKHA ASHER HOTZETHIKHA ME-ERETZ MITZRAYIM MI-BETH AVADIM*). THE DIVINE PROLOGUE: THE COVENANT IDENTITY OF GOD! **'I AM YAHWEH YOUR GOD (*ANOKHI YHVH ELOHEKHA*)!'** — God establishes His identity as REDEEMER before giving commandments. **THE COMMANDMENTS ARE THE RESPONSE OF LOVE TO THE GRACE OF THE EXODUS, NOT THE CONDITION FOR IT!** (CCC 2061).
cccReferences: CCC 2057 (The Decalogue as response to the gift of liberation, not the condition for it); CCC 2061 (The 10 Commandments as expressions of covenant love); CCC 2084 (THE FIRST COMMANDMENT: 'I am the Lord your God').
historicalContext: The divine self-identification (*Anokhi YHVH*) anchors all 10 Commandments in the grace of the Exodus liberation.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Anokhi YHVH Elohekha asher hotzethikha me-eretz Mitzrayim mi-beth avadim*: *Anokhi* (emphatic 'I', self-assertion). *YHVH* (the sacred Tetragrammaton). *hotzethikha* ('who brought you out'). *beth avadim* ('house of slaves/bondage').
historicalTrivia: The Catechism (CCC 2057) teaches: God's first word to Israel is NOT a command but a GIFT — 'I freed you'! The 10 Commandments are the GRATEFUL RESPONSE of a freed people, not a ladder to earn freedom.

dominicalIntent: 'You shall have no other gods before me.' (*LO YIHYEH LEKHA ELOHIM ACHERIM AL-PANAI*). THE FIRST COMMANDMENT: NO OTHER GODS! **'YOU SHALL HAVE NO OTHER GODS BEFORE MY FACE (*AL-PANAI*)!'** — The absolute uniqueness and jealous love of Yahweh. CCC 2084-2132.
cccReferences: CCC 2084 (The First Commandment: 'I am the Lord your God, you shall have no other gods before me'); CCC 2086 (Faith, hope, charity as responses to the First Commandment); CCC 2110-2128 (Sins against the First Commandment: idolatry, divination, superstition).
historicalContext: The First Commandment is the foundation of the entire Covenant; all other commandments flow from it.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Lo yihyeh lekha Elohim acherim al-panai*: *al-panai* ('before my face/presence' — in my sight, in my presence, above me, beside me — all options excluded!).
historicalTrivia: The phrase *al-panai* ('before my face') implies that Israel must not tolerate any other god even in God's very presence — an absolute exclusivity.

dominicalIntent: 'You shall not make for yourself a carved image (*PESEL*), or any likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth.' THE SECOND COMMANDMENT: NO CARVED IMAGES! Prohibition of the *PESEL* (carved/graven idol).
cccReferences: CCC 2129-2132 (The Second Commandment forbids idols that replace the living God); CCC 2112 (Idolatry as worshipping a creature instead of the Creator).
historicalContext: The prohibition covers all three cosmological zones: heaven, earth, and the underworld sea — leaving no creative sphere where idols may be fashioned.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Lo tha'asseh lekha pesel ve-khol temunah asher ba-shsamayim mi-ma'al va'asher ba-aretz mi-ttachath va'asher ba-mmayim mi-ttachath la-aretz*: *pesel* (carved idol from *pashal* 'to cut/carve'). *temunah* ('likeness/form').
historicalTrivia: The Catechism (CCC 2130) carefully distinguishes: the prohibition is against IDOLS that replace God, NOT against all sacred images — the Tabernacle itself was filled with cherubim, pomegranates, and artistic imagery!

dominicalIntent: 'You shall not bow down to them or serve them, for I the Lord your God am a jealous God (*EL QANNA*), visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me...' GOD AS EL QANNA — JEALOUS GOD! God reveals Himself as **EL QANNA** ('Jealous God') — a God of burning, consuming passion for His people's fidelity! Visiting iniquity to 3rd-4th generation.
cccReferences: CCC 2086 (God as 'jealous God' meaning His love cannot tolerate idolatrous rivals); CCC 2114 (Idolatry perverts the innate sense of God and violates the dignity of the person).
historicalContext: God's 'jealousy' (*qin'ah*) is the Covenant passion of a faithful Husband who cannot endure His Bride's infidelity.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Lo thishtachavveh lahem ve-lo tha'avdem ki anokhi YHVH Elohekha El Qanna poqed avon avoth al-banim al-shileshim ve-al-ribbe'im le-ssone'ai*: *El Qanna* ('Jealous God', from *qin'ah* = zeal/jealousy/passion). *poqed avon avoth* ('visiting the iniquity of fathers').
crossReferences: Exodus 34:14 ('Yahweh, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God'); Nahum 1:2; 2 Corinthians 11:2.
historicalTrivia: The visiting of iniquity to 3rd-4th generations refers to systemic social consequences of sin in families and cultures, not to God punishing innocent descendants.

dominicalIntent: 'but showing steadfast love (*CHESED*) to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments.' THE INFINITE ASYMMETRY OF DIVINE MERCY! While punishment extends to 3-4 generations, **GOD'S COVENANT LOVE (*CHESED*) EXTENDS TO THOUSANDS (*LAALPHAIM*)!** — an asymmetric grace overwhelming!
cccReferences: CCC 2086 (God's mercy infinitely exceeds His judgment: to thousands of those who love Him); CCC 214 (God as faithful love *chesed*).
historicalContext: The ratio is staggering: judgment to 3-4 generations; mercy to THOUSANDS of generations.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-osseh chesed la-alaphim le-ohavai u-le-shomrey mitzvothai*: *chesed* (covenantal steadfast love/mercy). *la-alaphim* ('to thousands' — possibly 'thousands of generations'!).
crossReferences: Psalm 103:8-11; Micah 7:18-20; Luke 1:50; Romans 5:20 ('where sin increased, grace abounded all the more').
historicalTrivia: 3-4 generations vs. thousands = roughly 1:250 ratio of judgment to mercy. God's mercy VASTLY and infinitely overwhelms His punishment!

dominicalIntent: 'You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain (*LO TISSA ETH-SHEM YHVH ELOHEKHA LA-SHAV*), for the Lord will not hold him guiltless who takes his name in vain.' THE THIRD COMMANDMENT: DO NOT TAKE YAHWEH'S NAME IN VAIN! The prohibition covers: false oaths, magic use of the divine Name, blasphemy, disrespectful use. CCC 2142-2167.
cccReferences: CCC 2142 (The Third Commandment: respecting the Lord's name); CCC 2150 (False oaths in God's name); CCC 2162 (Blasphemy as grave sin); CCC 2163 (Christian duty to praise God's name).
historicalContext: *La-shav* means 'for emptiness/vanity/falsehood' — using God's name for worthless, deceptive, or magical purposes.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Lo tissa eth-shem YHVH Elohekha la-shav ki lo yenaqqeh YHVH eth asher-yissa eth-shmo la-shav*: *tissa* (from *nasa* = 'to carry/lift up/bear'). *la-shav* ('for vanity/emptiness/falsehood'). *lo yenaqqeh* ('will not hold guiltless/innocent').
historicalTrivia: The Third Commandment is violated not just by profanity but by: false oaths invoking God's name, empty religious formulas, using God's name in magic spells or occult practices.

dominicalIntent: 'Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy (*ZAKHOR ETH-YOM HA-SHABBATH LE-QADDSHO*).' THE FOURTH COMMANDMENT: REMEMBER THE SABBATH! *ZAKHOR* — REMEMBER! The Sabbath as memorial of Creation AND liberation. CCC 2168-2188.
cccReferences: CCC 2168 (The Fourth Commandment: 'Remember the sabbath day to keep it holy'); CCC 2170 (The sabbath at the heart of Israel's law); CCC 2175 (Sunday as the Day of the Lord, fulfilling and surpassing the Sabbath).
historicalContext: The Sabbath (*Shabbath*) rooted in the 7th day of creation rest (Gen 2:1-3) and the Exodus liberation.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Zakhor eth-yom ha-Shabbath le-qadddsho*: *Zakhor* ('Remember!' — active memorial participation). *le-qaddsho* ('to sanctify/make holy it'). Deut 5:12 uses *Shamor* ('Observe/Guard') — both words implying different aspects.
historicalTrivia: Exodus grounds the Sabbath in CREATION (Gen 2:3); Deuteronomy 5:15 grounds it in the EXODUS LIBERATION — two dimensions perfectly united in the Lord's Day (Sunday)!

dominicalIntent: 'Six days you shall labor, and do all your work...' Work is a positive value; 6 days of purposeful labor mirror God's 6 days of creative work (CCC 2184).
cccReferences: CCC 2184 (The dignity of human work in the pattern of God's creative activity); CCC 2427 (Work as participation in God's creative action).
historicalContext: The 6-day work week as the God-ordained rhythm of human existence.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Shesheth yamim tha'avod ve-assitha kol-mela'khteykha*: *tha'avod* ('you shall work/serve'). *mela'khah* ('work/craft/skilled labor').
crossReferences: Genesis 2:15 (God put man in the garden to work and keep it); Psalm 90:17; 2 Thessalonians 3:10.
historicalTrivia: The very word for 'work' (*mela'khah*) is cognate with the word for 'angel/messenger' (*malakh*), implying that purposeful work has a sacred, angelic dignity.

dominicalIntent: 'but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the Lord your God. On it you shall not do any work, you, or your son, or your daughter, your male servant, or your female servant, or your livestock, or the sojourner who is within your gates.' THE SABBATH REST EXTENDS TO ALL: SERVANTS, ANIMALS, STRANGERS! The Sabbath is a profound social leveler — even slaves and animals rest! CCC 2172.
cccReferences: CCC 2172 (The Sabbath rest includes servants, animals, and sojourners — a model of social justice); CCC 2185 (The Sabbath as protest against servitude to work and money).
historicalContext: The universal application of Sabbath rest was revolutionary — no other ancient culture legislated rest for slaves and animals.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-yom ha-shvi'i Shabbath la-YHVH Elohekha lo-tha'asseh khol-mela'khah attah u-vinkha u-vitttekha avdekha va-amathekha u-vhemteykha ve-gherkhha asher bi-sha'areykha*: *la-YHVH* ('belonging to Yahweh'). *bi-sha'areykha* ('within your gates' = your city/jurisdiction).
historicalTrivia: The Sabbath rest for animals (Exodus 23:12) is one of the earliest animal welfare laws in human history!

dominicalIntent: 'For in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and rested on the seventh day. Therefore the Lord blessed the Sabbath day and made it holy.' THE SABBATH ROOTED IN THE CREATION WEEK! The 7-day rhythm of human life mirrors God's 6+1 creative rhythm in Genesis 1-2. CCC 345.
cccReferences: CCC 345 (The Sabbath as memorial of creation and God's rest); CCC 2169 (The Sabbath day blessed and consecrated by God).
historicalContext: Genesis 2:1-3 established the cosmic Sabbath that the Decalogue now legislates.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ki shesheth yamim assah YHVH eth ha-ssamayim ve-eth ha-aretz eth ha-yam ve-eth-kol-asher-bam vayyanaach ba-yom ha-shvi'i al-ken berakh YHVH eth-yom ha-Shabbath vayyeqadeshehu*: *vayyanaach* ('and He rested'). *berakh* ('He blessed'). *vayyeqadeshehu* ('and He sanctified it').
crossReferences: Genesis 2:1-3; Exodus 31:17; Hebrews 4:3-11 (The eternal Sabbath rest of God fulfilled in Christ).
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 4:9-10 announces: 'There remains a Sabbath rest for the people of God — for whoever has entered God's rest has also rested from his works.' The ultimate Sabbath is ETERNAL LIFE in God!

dominicalIntent: 'Honor your father and your mother (*KABBED ETH-AVIKHA VE-ETH-IMMEKHA*), that your days may be long in the land that the Lord your God is giving you.' THE FIFTH COMMANDMENT: HONOR YOUR PARENTS! **THE FIRST COMMANDMENT WITH A PROMISE** (Eph 6:2-3)! *KABBED* ('honor') — same root as *KAVOD* (glory/weight). CCC 2197-2257.
cccReferences: CCC 2197 (The Fifth Commandment: Honor your father and mother); CCC 2214 (Parents participating in God's Fatherhood); CCC 2248 (The duties of children including honor, gratitude, and filial obedience).
historicalContext: Honoring parents (*kabbed*) includes financial support in old age, obedience in youth, and respect always.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Kabbed eth-avikha ve-eth-immekha le-ma'an ya'arikhu yamekha al ha-adamah asher-YHVH Elohekha noten lakh*: *kabbed* ('honor/give weight to' from *kavad* = to be heavy/weighty/glorious). *ya'arikhu yamekha* ('your days will be long').
crossReferences: Ephesians 6:2-3 ('Honor your father and mother — this is the first commandment with a promise'); Proverbs 1:8; Sirach 3:3-7; Mark 7:10; Luke 2:51.
historicalTrivia: St. Paul in Ephesians 6:2-3 explicitly calls this 'THE FIRST COMMANDMENT WITH A PROMISE' (*entolē prōtē en epangeliai*)!

dominicalIntent: 'You shall not murder (*LO TIRTZACH*).' THE SIXTH COMMANDMENT (Catholic/Lutheran: 5th): NO MURDER! The prohibition covers deliberate, premeditated homicide (*ratzach* = murder as distinct from killing in war or execution). **JESUS EXPANDS THIS TO INCLUDE ANGER IN MATT 5:21-22!** CCC 2258-2330.
cccReferences: CCC 2258 (Human life is sacred because it is created in the image of God); CCC 2268 (The Fifth Commandment forbids murder); CCC 2302 (Jesus condemns anger as the root of murder).
historicalContext: The Hebrew *tirtzach* specifically refers to culpable homicide, not all killing (war and capital punishment used different words).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Lo tirtzach*: *ratzach* ('to murder/slay unjustly', distinct from *harag* = to kill generally, or *hemath* = to put to death legally).
historicalTrivia: Jesus in Matt 5:21-22: 'You have heard it said *lo tirtzach*... but I say to you, **everyone who is angry with his brother will be liable to judgment**'! Jesus pushes the commandment from the external act to the internal root — anger!

dominicalIntent: 'You shall not commit adultery (*LO TINAF*).' THE SEVENTH COMMANDMENT (Catholic: 6th): NO ADULTERY! **JESUS EXPANDS THIS TO INCLUDE LUSTFUL LOOKING IN MATT 5:27-28!** CCC 2331-2400.
cccReferences: CCC 2331 (The Sixth Commandment: 'You shall not commit adultery'); CCC 2336 (Chastity as integrating sexuality into the person); CCC 2380 (Adultery as injustice against spouse and children).
historicalContext: Adultery (*na'aph*) specifically referred to sexual relations with another man's wife — a violation of the covenant bond of marriage.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Lo tinaf*: *na'aph* ('to commit adultery' — specifically against a marriage covenant). Jesus quotes this commandment in LXX Greek *moicheuseis*.
historicalTrivia: Jesus in Matt 5:28: 'But I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman with lustful intent has already committed adultery with her in his heart.' Jesus interiorizes the 6th Commandment from the body to the heart!

dominicalIntent: 'You shall not steal (*LO TIGNOV*).' THE EIGHTH COMMANDMENT (Catholic: 7th): NO THEFT! CCC 2401-2463. Covers theft, fraud, unjust wages, slavery — all violations of another's property and dignity.
cccReferences: CCC 2401 (The Seventh Commandment: 'You shall not steal'); CCC 2408 (Theft is taking another's goods against the reasonable will of the owner); CCC 2411 (Contracts and promises must be honored in justice).
historicalContext: The scope of *tignov* (theft) includes: robbery, fraud, deceptive business practices, and even kidnapping (Exod 21:16).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Lo tignov*: *ganav* ('to steal/take stealthily'). Some Rabbis interpret the 8th Commandment as specifically forbidding KIDNAPPING (theft of persons), since ordinary theft was covered by civil law.
historicalTrivia: St. Paul in Ephesians 4:28 inverts the commandment positively: 'Let the thief no longer steal, but rather let him labor, doing honest work with his own hands, so that he may have something to share with anyone in need.'

dominicalIntent: 'You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor (*LO TA'ANEH VE-RE'AKHA ED SHAQER*).' THE NINTH COMMANDMENT (Catholic: 8th): NO FALSE TESTIMONY! Covers perjury, slander, defamation, lying in court. CCC 2464-2513.
cccReferences: CCC 2464 (The Eighth Commandment: 'You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor'); CCC 2476 (False witness and perjury as grave sins); CCC 2505 (Beauty of truth and the duty to witness).
historicalContext: The commandment arose from the judicial context: bearing false testimony (*ed shaqer*) in a capital court case could cost an innocent person their life.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Lo tha'aneh ve-re'akha ed shaqer*: *tha'aneh* ('you shall not answer/testify'). *ed shaqer* ('a false/lying witness'). *re'akha* ('your neighbor' = fellow covenant member).
crossReferences: Proverbs 6:19; Proverbs 12:17; Matthew 19:18; John 14:6 ('I am the Way, the TRUTH, and the Life').
historicalTrivia: Jesus was condemned to death in large part because of **false witnesses** (*pseudomartyres*) in Matt 26:60-61 — a direct violation of the 8th Commandment at the supreme level!

dominicalIntent: 'You shall not covet your neighbor's house; you shall not covet your neighbor's wife, or his male servant, or his female servant, or his ox, or his donkey, or anything that is your neighbor's (*LO TACHMOD*).' THE TENTH COMMANDMENT (Catholic: 9th & 10th): NO COVETING! **THE COMMANDMENT THAT PENETRATES FROM EXTERNAL ACTS TO INTERIOR DESIRE! CITED BY ST. PAUL IN ROMANS 7:7!** CCC 2514-2557.
cccReferences: CCC 2514 (The Ninth Commandment: 'You shall not covet your neighbor's wife'); CCC 2534 (The Tenth Commandment: 'You shall not covet your neighbor's goods'); CCC 2540 (Envy as sadness at another's good).
historicalContext: The prohibition against coveting (*chamad*) reaches into the interior will — prohibiting even the desire to take what belongs to another.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Lo tachmod beyth re'ekha lo tachmod esheth re'ekha ve-avdo va-amato ve-shoro va-chamoro ve-khol asher le-re'ekha*: *chamad* ('to covet/desire intensely/lust after' — an interior act of the will!).
crossReferences: Romans 7:7 ('I would not have known what it is to covet if the law had not said, *Lo tachmod*'); Romans 13:9; Luke 12:15; James 1:14-15.
historicalTrivia: St. Paul in Romans 7:7 explicitly cites *Lo tachmod* as the commandment that made him conscious of sin: 'I would not have known sin if it were not for the Law... the Law said *do not covet* and sin produced in me all kinds of covetous desire.' The 10th Commandment is the hinge between law and grace!

dominicalIntent: Now when all the people saw the thunder and the flashes of lightning and the sound of the trumpet and the mountain smoking, the people were afraid and trembled, and they stood far off (*...vayya'amdu me-rachok*). THE PEOPLE'S TERROR AT THE DIVINE VOICE! All the people witness the thunder, lightning, Shophar, and smoke and **TREMBLE IN MORTAL FEAR**, standing far off (*me-rachok*).
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (The people's fear at God's holy manifestation); Hebrews 12:18-21.
historicalContext: The terror of 2 million people witnessing the direct divine voice accompanied by cosmic pyrotechnics.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-khol-ha-am ro'im eth-ha-qoloth ve-eth-ha-lapidim ve-eth qol ha-shophar ve-eth ha-har ashen vayyar ha-am vayyanu'u vayyamdu me-rachok*: *vayyanu'u* ('they trembled/wavered'). *me-rachok* ('from far off').
crossReferences: Hebrews 12:18-21 ('the sound of a trumpet and a voice whose words made the hearers beg that no further messages be spoken to them'); Deuteronomy 5:25.
historicalTrivia: Deuteronomy 5:25 records Israel's honest confession: 'For who is there of all flesh, that has heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the midst of fire as we have, and has still lived?'

dominicalIntent: And they said to Moses: 'You speak to us, and we will listen; but do not let God speak to us, lest we die.' ISRAEL ASKS FOR A HUMAN MEDIATOR! In terror, Israel begs Moses: **'YOU speak to us — not God directly — lest we die!'** This request establishes the entire Prophetic office — and ultimately points to the need for the INCARNATION!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Moses as mediator prefiguring Christ the one Mediator, 1 Tim 2:5); CCC 702 (The prophets as God's voice to the people).
historicalContext: Israel's request for a human mediator establishes Moses as prophet par excellence (Deut 18:15-18).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mru el-Moshe dabber-attha immanu ve-nishmah ve-al-yedabber immanu Elohim pen-namuth*: *pen-namuth* ('lest we die').
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 18:15-18 (God promises a Prophet like Moses — fulfilled in Jesus!); 1 Timothy 2:5; Galatians 3:19; Hebrews 1:1-2.
historicalTrivia: Deuteronomy 18:15 quotes God: 'A PROPHET LIKE ME from among your brothers — Yahweh your God will raise up for you; to him you shall listen.' Peter in Acts 3:22 and Stephen in Acts 7:37 explicitly apply this to JESUS!

dominicalIntent: 'So I will stretch out my hand and strike Egypt with all the wonders that I will do in it; after that he will let you go' (*Ve-shalachti eth-yadi ve-hikkethi eth-Mitzrayim be-khol niphle'othai...*). STRIKING EGYPT WITH ALL DIVINE WONDERS! God promises: **'I will stretch out my hand and strike Egypt with all my wonders (*be-khol niphle'othai*)!'** The 10 Plagues announced.
cccReferences: CCC 2063 (The miraculous Plagues dismantling Egyptian idolatry); CCC 2575; Ps 105:27-36.
historicalContext: Prophetic announcement of the 10 Plagues (*niphla'oth*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-shalachti eth-yadi ve-hikkethi eth-Mitzrayim be-khol niphle'othai asher e'esseh be-qirbo ve-acharey-khen yeshallach ethkhem*: *niphle'othai* ('my wonders/miracles').
historicalTrivia: Acts 7:36 summarizes: 'He led them out, performing wonders and signs in Egypt and at the Red Sea'.

dominicalIntent: The people stood far off, while Moses drew near to the thick darkness (*ha-araphel*) where God was. MOSES ALONE ENTERS THE DIVINE DARKNESS! While all Israel trembles far off, **Moses alone enters the *ARAPHEL* — the thick, impenetrable darkness where God dwells!** TYPE OF CHRIST AS SOLE MEDIATOR ENTERING THE DIVINE MYSTERY!
cccReferences: CCC 2575 (Moses as unique mediator of the Sinai Covenant, type of Christ the one Mediator); CCC 159 (Divine mystery as incomprehensible light inaccessible to unaided human reason).
historicalContext: Moses entering the divine *araphel* (thick darkness) alone — paradoxically, God dwells in impenetrable darkness AND blinding light simultaneously.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'amod ha-am me-rachok u-Moshe nigash el-ha-araphel asher-sham ha-Elohim*: *ha-araphel* ('the thick darkness/dense cloud where God is' — from *araph* = drizzle).
crossReferences: 1 Kings 8:12 ('Yahweh has said that he would dwell in thick darkness'); Psalm 18:9-11; 2 Corinthians 12:1-4; Hebrews 12:22-24.
historicalTrivia: St. Gregory of Nyssa's *Life of Moses* interprets Moses entering the divine darkness as the ultimate mystical theology: the soul advances INTO the mystery of God, not away from it — the deeper one goes, the more unknown God becomes AND the more intimately known!

dominicalIntent: And the Lord said to Moses: 'Thus you shall say to the people of Israel: You have seen for yourselves that I have talked with you from heaven.' God confirms the heavenly origin of the Commandments.
cccReferences: CCC 2058 (The divine origin of the Decalogue confirmed); CCC 2060.
historicalContext: The Commandments are not human legislation but divine revelation from heaven (*min-ha-ssamayim*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Moshe koh thomar el-bney Yisra'el athem re'ithem ki min-ha-ssamayim dibbartti immakhem*: *min-ha-ssamayim* ('from the heavens').
historicalTrivia: Israel is the unique nation that heard God's own voice speaking directly from heaven (*min-ha-ssamayim*) — a claim made by no other people in human history!

dominicalIntent: 'You shall not make gods of silver to be with me, nor shall you make for yourselves gods of gold.' Reinforcement of the First and Second Commandments against metal idols.
cccReferences: CCC 2112-2114 (Idolatry: making gods of silver or gold); CCC 2129.
historicalContext: Silver and gold idol-making was standard Canaanite religious practice that Israel was to renounce entirely.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Lo tha'assun itti elohey kesef ve-elohey zahav lo tha'asssu lakhem*: *kesef* (silver). *zahav* (gold). The prohibition pointedly anticipates the golden calf disaster of Exodus 32!
historicalTrivia: This verse is placed immediately before the Altar Law — God wants ALTARS of simple earth and uncut stone, not shimmering golden idols!

dominicalIntent: 'An altar of earth (*mizbach adamah*) you shall make for me and sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and your peace offerings, your sheep and your oxen. In every place where I cause my name to be remembered I will come to you and bless you.' THE EARTHEN ALTAR AND GOD'S MULTIPLIED BLESSINGS! Simple earthen altars wherever God causes His name to be remembered; He will come and bless!
cccReferences: CCC 2099 (Sacrifice on the altar acceptable to God); CCC 2580 (Authentic worship in simplicity).
historicalContext: The simplest possible altars — earth or uncut field stones — emphasized that worship is about God's presence, not human artistry.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Mizbach adamah tha'asseh-li ve-zavachta alav eth-olatekha ve-eth-shlamekha eth-tzonkha ve-eth-bqarekha be-khol-ha-maqom asher azkir eth-shmi avo eleykha u-verakhtikha*: *mizbach adamah* ('altar of earth'). *azkir eth-shmi* ('where I cause my Name to be remembered').
crossReferences: Genesis 8:20; Genesis 12:8; Malachi 1:11 ('In every place incense is offered to my name'); John 4:21-24.
historicalTrivia: The earthen altar (*mizbach adamah*) prefigures the humble manger: God's presence does not require ornate human constructions — He comes to wherever He is genuinely invoked!

dominicalIntent: 'If you make me an altar of stone, you shall not build it of hewn stones (*azit*), for if you wield your tool (*cherev*) on it you profane it.' NO IRON TOOL ON THE ALTAR STONES! Iron is the metal of weapons (*cherev* = sword/chisel); using it on God's altar brings human violence into sacred space.
cccReferences: CCC 2099 (Sacred worship must not be profaned by the instruments of violence); CCC 2580.
historicalContext: Stone altars were built from uncut field stones, just as Solomon's Temple stones were hewn miles away so 'neither hammer nor axe nor any iron tool was heard in the temple' (1 Kings 6:7).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-im-mizbach avanim tha'asseh-li lo-thivneh ethen gazith ki charbkha henipta alav va-thchalleleha*: *azit/gazith* (dressed/hewn stone). *cherev* ('sword/cutting tool'). *va-thchalleleha* ('you profane it').
crossReferences: 1 Kings 6:7 ('When the house was built, it was with stone prepared at the quarry, so that neither hammer nor axe nor any iron tool was heard in the house while it was being built'); Deuteronomy 27:5-6.
historicalTrivia: 1 Kings 6:7 explicitly fulfills this law: Solomon's Temple was built in total silence — no iron tools on site — because the stones were fully prepared elsewhere!

dominicalIntent: 'And you shall not go up by steps to my altar, that your nakedness be not exposed on it.' Steps to the altar are prohibited to prevent indecent exposure of the priests — preserving the dignity of sacred worship. Altar ramps (*kevesh*) were used instead.
cccReferences: CCC 2099 (Dignity and reverence in sacred worship); CCC 2580.
historicalContext: Priests wore tunics and linen breeches (Exod 28:42-43) but steps with high winds could expose them; this law mandated a ramp approach.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-lo tha'aleh ve-ma'aloth al-mizbchi asher lo-tiggaleh ervatekha alav*: *ma'aloth* ('steps/stairs'). *ervatekha* ('your nakedness/shameful thing').
crossReferences: Exodus 28:42-43; Leviticus 21:23; Ezekiel 43:17 (Ezekiel's Temple ramp described).
historicalTrivia: The Mishnah records that the Temple altar in Jerusalem was indeed approached by a ramp (*kevesh*) 32 cubits long on the south side, exactly fulfilling this commandment!

dominicalIntent: 'Now these are the rules (*MISHPATIM*) that you shall set before them.' THE BOOK OF THE COVENANT BEGINS! *MISHPATIM* — THE CIVIL JUDGMENTS/ORDINANCES OF GOD! These are the practical outworkings of the 10 Commandments into everyday Israelite life.
cccReferences: CCC 2060 (The Decalogue applied through ordinances); CCC 1958 (Natural law expressed in positive law).
historicalContext: The Mishpatim (Exod 21-23) form the 'Book of the Covenant' (*Sepher ha-Brith*, Exod 24:7), the first written legal code given to Israel.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-elleh ha-mishpatim asher tassim liphneyhem*: *mishpatim* ('judgments/ordinances' — case law). *tassim liphneyhem* ('set before them' = present for instruction).
crossReferences: Exodus 24:7 (the 'Book of the Covenant'); Deuteronomy 4:8; Romans 2:13.
historicalTrivia: The Mishpatim represent the world's most ancient surviving comprehensive law code, predating even the fully developed Hammurabi Code!

dominicalIntent: 'When you buy a Hebrew slave, he shall serve six years, and in the seventh he shall go out free, for nothing (*CHOPHSHI*).' HEBREW SLAVE RELEASED FREE IN THE 7TH YEAR! The Sabbath principle extended to persons: 6 years of service, then release free (*chophshi*) in the 7th — the Sabbatical Year of Liberty!
cccReferences: CCC 2414 (The dignity of the human person prohibits treating persons as property); CCC 2172 (The Sabbath rest principle extended to servants).
historicalContext: The 7th-year release was revolutionary: no other ancient law code mandated the automatic liberation of slaves on a calendar cycle.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ki thikneh eved ivri shesh shanim ya'avod u-va-shvii yetze la-chophshi chinnam*: *eved ivri* ('Hebrew slave'). *chophshi* ('free/at liberty'). *chinnam* ('for nothing/without payment').
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 15:12-18; Leviticus 25:39-55; Jeremiah 34:8-22 (Israel violated this law!); Luke 4:18 (Jesus proclaims the ultimate Year of Jubilee).
historicalTrivia: Jeremiah 34:8-22 records God's furious judgment on Jerusalem for re-enslaving freed Hebrew slaves — directly breaking this 7th-year liberation commandment!

dominicalIntent: 'If he comes in single, he shall go out single; if he comes in married, then his wife shall go out with him.' The slave's existing family situation is preserved in his liberation.
historicalContext: Protection of the slave's family unit even within the constraints of ancient slavery.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Im be-gappo yavo be-gappo yetze im-ba'al ishah hu ve-yatze'ah ishto immo*: *be-gappo* ('in his body alone / single').
historicalTrivia: Ancient Near Eastern law codes like Hammurabi did NOT guarantee family unity for slaves — Israel's law was uniquely progressive.

dominicalIntent: 'If his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the wife and her children shall be her master's, and he shall go out alone.' Complex case: wife given by master remains with master — children belong to master. A tension that sets up the voluntary slavery of love in verse 5-6.
historicalContext: Children born of a master-provided wife were legally the master's property. This painful situation created the scenario of verses 5-6.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Im-adonav yitten-lo ishah ve-yaldah-lo vanim o vanoth ha-ishah ve-yaladeha thihyeh la-adoneiha ve-hu yetze be-gappo*: *adonav* ('his master/lord').
historicalTrivia: This legal tension between freedom and love forms the precise backdrop for the beautiful typological vow of voluntary slavery in verses 5-6.

dominicalIntent: 'But if the slave plainly says: I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free...' THE SLAVE WHO LOVES HIS MASTER AND CHOOSES PERPETUAL VOLUNTARY BONDAGE! **'I LOVE MY MASTER (*AHAVTHI ETH-ADONAI*)!'** — The slave refuses freedom out of LOVE!
cccReferences: CCC 2414 (Love transcending legal obligation); CCC 459 (Christ's voluntary self-emptying as the supreme act of love-slavery, Philippians 2:7).
historicalContext: The slave's voluntary renunciation of freedom out of love for his master and family.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-im-amor yomar ha-eved ahavthi eth-adonai eth-ishtti ve-eth-banai lo etze chophshi*: *ahavthi eth-adonai* ('I have loved my master!'). The root *ahav* is covenant love.
crossReferences: Philippians 2:7 ('Christ emptied himself, taking the form of a slave/servant'); Psalm 40:6-8 (LXX: 'Then I said: Behold I come... I delight to do your will, O God'); John 10:17-18.
historicalTrivia: Psalm 40:6-8 in the LXX (quoted in Hebrews 10:5-7) presents CHRIST's voice at the Incarnation as the supreme fulfillment: 'Sacrifice and offering you did not desire... Then I said: Behold I come to do your will, O God!' — Christ is the ultimate voluntary slave of love!

dominicalIntent: '...then his master shall bring him to God, and he shall bring him to the door or the doorpost. And his master shall bore his ear through with an awl (*MARTZEA*), and he shall be his slave forever.' THE AWL THROUGH THE EAR AT THE DOORPOST: VOLUNTARY PERPETUAL SLAVERY! The slave who loves his master has his ear bored (*ratza*) with an awl (*martzea*) through the DOORPOST (*mzuzah*) and becomes his master's slave FOREVER (*le-olam*)! **POWERFUL CHRISTOLOGICAL TYPE!**
cccReferences: CCC 459 (Christ's voluntary Incarnation as total self-gift, Phil 2:6-8); CCC 606 (Christ's voluntary acceptance of death as sacrifice of love).
historicalContext: The boring of the ear at the doorpost: a public, permanent mark of chosen slavery out of love.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-higgisho adonav el-ha-Elohim ve-higgisho el-ha-ddeleth o el-ha-mzuzah ve-ratzah adonav eth-ozno ba-martzea va-avado le-olam*: *ratzah* ('bored through'). *martzea* ('awl'). *mzuzah* ('doorpost'). *le-olam* ('forever').
crossReferences: Philippians 2:6-8 (Christ 'taking the form of a slave... becoming obedient to the point of death'); Psalm 40:6 ('You have given me an open ear'); Isaiah 50:5 ('The Lord God has opened my ear, and I was not rebellious').
historicalTrivia: Isaiah 50:5 (the 3rd Servant Song) presents the Suffering Servant's voice: 'The Lord GOD has opened my ear — and I was not rebellious; I did not turn backward.' The ear-boring of the voluntary slave at the doorpost is Christ accepting the Incarnation and Cross out of love for the Father!

dominicalIntent: 'When a man sells his daughter as a slave, she shall not go out as the male slaves do.' Female Hebrew slaves had different and MORE protective terms than male slaves — reflecting the betrothal context.
cccReferences: CCC 2414; CCC 2331 (Protection of women's dignity).
historicalContext: Daughters were often 'sold' as concubines or wives — which gave them marital protections rather than simple slave status.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-khi-yimkor ish eth-bitto le-amah lo thetze ke-tzetze ha-avadim*: *amah* ('female slave/maidservant' often in context of secondary wife/concubine).
historicalTrivia: The Mishpatim gave female slaves MORE legal protection than male slaves — a remarkable feature of Israel's legal code.

dominicalIntent: 'If she does not please her master, who has designated her for himself, then he shall let her be redeemed. He shall have no right to sell her to a foreign people, since he has broken faith with her.' Protection against abandonment: the female slave designated as wife cannot be sold to foreigners if she displeases her master.
historicalContext: Prohibition of selling a betrothed female slave to a foreign nation — protecting her from export into pagan servitude.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Im ra'ah be-eyney adoneiha asher-lo ye'adah ve-hephdhah le-am nokhri lo-yimshol le-mokhra bi-vegodo-vah*: *be-vegodo-vah* ('in his treachery/faithlessness toward her').
crossReferences: Malachi 2:14-16 (God as witness to marriage covenants).
historicalTrivia: The law uses *begad* (treachery/faithlessness) — a covenant term — showing that even this ancient form of betrothal was taken as a solemn covenant.

dominicalIntent: 'If he designates her for his son, he shall deal with her as with a daughter.' If the female slave is designated for the master's son, she receives full daughter status and rights.
cccReferences: CCC 2414; CCC 2204 (The dignity of the family).
historicalContext: Elevation of the female slave to daughter-status when designated for the son — full family membership.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-im le-vno yi'adennah ke-mishpat ha-banoth ya'asseh-lah*: *ke-mishpat ha-banoth* ('according to the law/right of daughters').
crossReferences: Galatians 4:5-7 ('God sent forth his Son... to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive adoption as sons').
historicalTrivia: This is a remarkable redemptive pattern: slave → designated bride of the son → elevated to daughter! Prefiguring Christian adoption!

dominicalIntent: 'If he takes another wife to himself, he shall not diminish her food, her clothing, or her marital rights (*ONAH*).' THREE LEGAL RIGHTS OF A WIFE: food (*she'er*), clothing (*kesuth*), and conjugal rights (*onah*) — even if a second wife is taken, these must not be diminished.
cccReferences: CCC 2380 (The rights and dignity of a spouse within marriage); CCC 2364 (Marriage as faithful, total, and exclusive gift of self).
historicalContext: The three minimum marital obligations under Mosaic law: sustenance, clothing, conjugal rights.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Im-achereth yiqach-lo she'erah kesutah ve-onatah lo yigra'*: *she'er* (food/sustenance). *kesuth* (clothing). *onah* (marital/conjugal rights — from *onah* = time/season).
crossReferences: 1 Corinthians 7:3-5 ('The husband should give to his wife her conjugal rights, and likewise the wife to her husband'); Ephesians 5:28-29.
historicalTrivia: The rabbinic Mishnah (Tractate Ketubot) extensively codifies these three rights (*she'er*, *kesuth*, *onah*) as the basis of the Jewish marriage contract (*ketubah*).

dominicalIntent: 'If he does not do these three things for her, she shall go out for nothing, without payment of money.' If any of the three marital obligations are violated, the wife is released free without any redemption payment.
historicalContext: Automatic liberation of the wronged wife — a revolutionary protection in the ancient world.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-im-shlosh-elleh lo ya'asseh-lah ve-yatze'ah chinnam eyn kesseph*: *chinnam* ('free/without payment'). *eyn kesseph* ('without money').
historicalTrivia: This law gave women an exit from abusive marriages — extraordinary in the ancient Near East where women had almost no legal personhood.

dominicalIntent: 'Whoever strikes a man so that he dies shall be put to death.' (*MAKKEH ISH VA-METH MOTH YUMATH*). THE DEATH PENALTY FOR MURDER! *MOTH YUMATH* — dying he shall die. Capital punishment for premeditated murder.
cccReferences: CCC 2266 (The traditional teaching that public authority has the right to inflict punishment proportionate to the gravity of the crime); CCC 2268.
historicalContext: The lex talionis principle applied to murder: life for life.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Makkeh ish va-meth moth yumath*: *Makkeh* ('one who strikes'). *moth yumath* (cognate absolute: 'dying he shall die' = certainly must be put to death).
crossReferences: Genesis 9:6 ('Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man shall his blood be shed'); Numbers 35:31; Romans 13:4.
historicalTrivia: Genesis 9:6 provides the theological foundation: human blood is sacred because man is made *be-tzelem Elohim* (in the image of God).

dominicalIntent: 'But if he did not lie in wait for him, but God let him fall into his hand, then I will appoint for you a place to which he may flee.' CITIES OF REFUGE FOR ACCIDENTAL HOMICIDE PREFIGURED! God Himself distinguishes murder from accidental manslaughter and provides sanctuaries.
cccReferences: CCC 2263 (Legitimate defense vs. murder); CCC 2264.
historicalContext: The Cities of Refuge (*Arey Miqlatot*) formally established in Numbers 35 and Deuteronomy 19 — here first prophetically promised.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Va'asher lo tzadah ve-ha-Elohim inah le-yado ve-ssamti lekha maqom asher yanuss ssammah*: *tzadah* ('lay in wait/premeditate'). *inah le-yado* ('God caused it to fall into his hand' = accident providentially permitted).
crossReferences: Numbers 35:6-34; Deuteronomy 19:1-13; Joshua 20 (6 Cities of Refuge established); Hebrews 6:18 (the hope set before us as a refuge *kataph*).
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 6:18 uses the City of Refuge as a type of Christ: 'We who have fled to take hold of the hope set before us'!

dominicalIntent: 'But if a man willfully attacks another to kill him by cunning, you shall take him from my altar, that he may die.' Even the altar provides no sanctuary for premeditated murderers — Adonijah and Joab later fled to the altar (1 Kings 1:50; 2:28) but were executed!
cccReferences: CCC 2268 (No sanctuary for premeditated murder).
historicalContext: The altar (*mizbeach*) was a traditional sanctuary in ancient Near Eastern culture; Israel's law denied it to murderers.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-ki-yazid ish al-re'ehu le-horgo ve-armah mi-im mizbchi thiqqachenu lamuth*: *yazid* ('act presumptuously/deliberately'). *armah* ('with cunning/craft').
crossReferences: 1 Kings 1:50-51 (Adonijah fled to the altar but Solomon pardoned him); 1 Kings 2:28-34 (Joab fled to the altar but was executed at Solomon's command!).
historicalTrivia: 1 Kings 2:29-34: Benaiah slew Joab at the altar at Solomon's command — directly fulfilling this law that the altar provides no immunity for murderers!

dominicalIntent: 'Whoever strikes his father or his mother shall be put to death.' (*MAKKEH AVIHU VE-IMMO MOTH YUMATH*). CAPITAL PUNISHMENT FOR STRIKING PARENTS! The 5th Commandment (Honor father and mother) carries the ultimate sanction.
cccReferences: CCC 2218 (The commandment to honor parents includes not striking or cursing them); CCC 2197.
historicalContext: Striking parents was a capital offense in Israel — reflecting the ultimate gravity of the 5th Commandment.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-makkeh avihu ve-immo moth yumath*: the same *moth yumath* formula as for murder in v.12.
crossReferences: Exodus 20:12; Deuteronomy 21:18-21 (stubborn and rebellious son condemned to death); Proverbs 30:17.
historicalTrivia: Ancient legal codes (Hammurabi §195) also prescribed harsh punishments for striking parents, but Israel's Mosaic law uniquely anchored this in the 5th Commandment of the Decalogue itself.

dominicalIntent: 'Whoever steals a man and sells him, and anyone found in possession of him, shall be put to death.' KIDNAPPING IS A CAPITAL CRIME! Theft of a human person — enslavement — is punished with death.
cccReferences: CCC 2414 (The grave sin of enslaving human beings as a violation of the 7th Commandment); CCC 2297.
historicalContext: Human trafficking (kidnapping to sell) was a capital crime in Israel — remarkable in a world where it was commonplace.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-gonev ish u-mkharou ve-nimtza ve-yado moth yumath*: *gonev ish* ('steals/kidnaps a man'). *u-mkharou* ('and sells him').
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 24:7; 1 Timothy 1:10 (Paul lists 'slave traders / *andrapodistais*' among those for whom the law was written).
historicalTrivia: 1 Timothy 1:10 places kidnappers/slave traders (*andrapodistai*) in the same category as murderers, adulterers, and the godless!

dominicalIntent: 'Whoever curses his father or his mother shall be put to death.' (*U-MEQALLEL AVIHU VE-IMMO MOTH YUMATH*). CURSING PARENTS IS A CAPITAL CRIME! **JESUS CITES THIS LAW DIRECTLY IN MARK 7:10 AND MATTHEW 15:4!**
cccReferences: CCC 2218 (The 5th Commandment prohibits dishonoring parents through word); CCC 2197.
historicalContext: Cursing parents (*meqallel* = to treat as trivial/worthless) is the opposite of honoring (*kavod* = treating as weighty/glorious).
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-meqallel avihu ve-immo moth yumath*: *meqallel* ('one who curses/treats lightly', root *qalal* = to be light/trivial — opposite of *kavad/kavod*).
crossReferences: Mark 7:10 ('Moses said: Honor your father and mother, and Whoever reviles father or mother must surely die'); Matthew 15:4; Leviticus 20:9.
historicalTrivia: Jesus in Mark 7:10 quotes BOTH Exodus 20:12 (Honor) AND Exodus 21:17 (Cursing = death) to rebuke the Pharisees for allowing *Corban* vows to override parental support!

dominicalIntent: 'When men quarrel and one strikes the other with a stone or with his fist and the man does not die but takes to his bed...' Injury law: non-fatal fight injury requires compensation.
cccReferences: CCC 2263 (Legitimate self-defense); CCC 1807 (Justice requires rendering what is owed).
historicalContext: Case law for non-fatal injury in a fight.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-khi-yrivun anashim ve-hikkah-ish eth-re'ehu be-even o ve-egroph ve-lo yamuth ve-naphal le-mishkav*: *be-even* ('with a stone'). *ve-egroph* ('or with a fist').
historicalTrivia: Ancient law codes (Hammurabi, Middle Assyrian Laws) had similar injury compensation laws, showing a common Near Eastern legal tradition.

dominicalIntent: '...if the man rises again and walks outdoors with his staff, he who struck him shall be clear; only he shall pay for the loss of his time, and shall have him thoroughly healed.' COMPENSATION FOR INJURY: LOST TIME AND MEDICAL CARE! The attacker pays for (1) lost wages (*shivto*) and (2) complete healing (*rapo yerappeh*).
cccReferences: CCC 2263; CCC 2411 (Justice requires making reparation for wrongs done).
historicalContext: Two compensation categories: lost productivity and medical expenses — remarkably modern!
translationNuances: Hebrew *Im-yaqum ve-hithhalekh ba-chutz al-mishanto ve-niqah ha-makkeh raq shivto yitten ve-rapo yerappeh*: *shivto* ('his cessation/loss of work'). *rapo yerappeh* (infinitive absolute: 'healing he shall heal' = fully pay for healing).
crossReferences: Luke 10:35 (the Good Samaritan: 'Take care of him, and whatever more you spend, I will repay you when I come back' — fulfilling this law!).
historicalTrivia: The Good Samaritan parable (Luke 10:33-35) perfectly enacts Exodus 21:19: he pays for healing (*rapo yerappeh*) and for ongoing care (*shivto*)!

dominicalIntent: 'When a man strikes his slave, male or female, with a rod and the slave dies under his hand, he shall be avenged.' A master who beats a slave to death must face legal consequences.
cccReferences: CCC 2414 (The dignity of the human person — even a slave — must be protected).
historicalContext: Revolutionary: no other ancient law code mandated punishment for killing one's own slave.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-khi-yakkeh ish eth-avdo o eth-amato ba-shevet va-meth thachath yado naqqom yinnaqem*: *naqqom yinnaqem* ('he shall certainly be avenged' = face the death penalty or comparable punishment).
crossReferences: Job 31:13-15 ('If I have rejected the cause of my manservant... what then shall I do when God rises up?').
historicalTrivia: Job 31:13-15 shows the theological basis: master and slave were both made by the same God — therefore the master cannot abuse the slave with impunity!

dominicalIntent: 'But if the slave survives a day or two, he is not to be avenged, for the slave is his money.' If the slave survives 1-2 days, no capital charge against the master — though the financial loss of his slave is his punishment.
historicalContext: Surviving slaves indicated the master's likely intention was discipline, not murder.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Akh im-yom o yomayim ya'amod lo yuqam ki khaspho hu*: *khaspho hu* ('he is his silver/money' = financial loss is sufficient punishment).
crossReferences: Leviticus 19:20-21; Philemon 16 (Paul: 'receive him back no longer as a slave, but better than a slave, as a dear brother').
historicalTrivia: Philemon (the runaway slave Onesimus) becomes a living fulfillment of the covenant law's trajectory: slave → brother in Christ!

dominicalIntent: 'When men strive together and hit a pregnant woman, so that her children come out, but there is no further harm, the one who hit her shall surely be fined, as the woman's husband shall impose on him...' INJURY TO A PREGNANT WOMAN AND HER UNBORN CHILD! The unborn child is legally protected under Mosaic law!
cccReferences: CCC 2270 (The inviolable right to life from the moment of conception); CCC 2271.
historicalContext: Prenatal injury law: the unborn child's harm is legally punishable — establishing the unborn's legal personhood.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-khi-yinnatzu anashim ve-nagphu ishah harah ve-yatze'u yaladeha ve-lo yihyeh assaon anosh ye'anesh*: *yaladeha* ('her children/offspring' — plural of *yeled*). *assaon* ('harm/injury').
crossReferences: Luke 1:41-44 (John the Baptist leapt in the womb — recognized as a person!); Psalm 139:13-16; Jeremiah 1:5.
historicalTrivia: The Hebrew text uses *yaladeha* (her children) for the unborn — confirming that Mosaic law regarded the unborn as legal persons deserving protection!

dominicalIntent: 'But if there is harm, then you shall pay life for life (*NEPHESH TACHAT NEPHESH*).' THE LEX TALIONIS PRINCIPLE: LIFE FOR LIFE! The *NEPHESH TACHAT NEPHESH* principle establishes absolute proportionality in punishment — the foundation of justice!
cccReferences: CCC 2262 (The principle of proportional justice — lex talionis — limiting disproportionate revenge); CCC 2302.
historicalContext: The Lex Talionis was actually a LIMITING principle: no MORE than life for life — preventing blood feuds and disproportionate revenge.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-im assaon yihyeh ve-nattatah nephesh tachat nephesh*: *nephesh tachat nephesh* ('life instead of life'). *assaon* ('harm/disaster').
historicalTrivia: The Lex Talionis was a REVOLUTIONARY LIMIT on revenge in the ancient world: tribal blood feuds could multiply casualties indefinitely; *nephesh tachat nephesh* limited punishment to EQUAL restitution, not escalation!

dominicalIntent: 'eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot...' (*AYIN TACHAT AYIN SHEN TACHAT SHEN...*). THE FULL LEX TALIONIS! **JESUS DIRECTLY QUOTES AND TRANSFORMS THIS IN MATTHEW 5:38-39!** The Lex Talionis principle: proportional, non-escalating justice.
cccReferences: CCC 2262 (The lex talionis as limit on disproportionate revenge); CCC 1789.
historicalContext: The full enumeration: eye, tooth, hand, foot, burn, wound, stripe — establishing total bodily proportionality.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ayin tachat ayin shen tachat shen yad tachat yad reghel tachat reghel*: *tachat* ('instead of/in place of').
crossReferences: Matthew 5:38-39 ('You have heard it said: An eye for an eye... But I say to you: Do not resist the one who is evil. But if anyone slaps you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also'); Romans 12:17.
historicalTrivia: Jesus in Matthew 5:38-39 does NOT abolish the Lex Talionis but TRANSCENDS it: from proportional justice (*ayin tachat ayin*) to supernatural mercy (turn the other cheek). This is the fulfillment (*plēroō*) of the Law's trajectory toward agape!

dominicalIntent: '...burn for burn, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.' Completion of the full bodily Lex Talionis.
historicalContext: Ancient judicial practice of physical punishment proportionate to the wound inflicted.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Keviyyah tachat keviyyah petza tachat patza chabbburah tachat chabburah*: *keviyyah* (burn). *petza* (wound). *chabbburah* (stripe/welt from beating).
crossReferences: Isaiah 53:5 ('By his stripes/chabburah we are healed') — JESUS BORE OUR STRIPES (*CHABBURAH*) ON THE CROSS! Leviticus 24:20; 1 Peter 2:24.
historicalTrivia: Isaiah 53:5 uses the EXACT WORD from Exodus 21:25: 'by his *chabburah* (stripes/welts) we are healed.' Jesus bore the full Lex Talionis punishment on our behalf!

dominicalIntent: 'When a man strikes the eye of his slave, male or female, and destroys it, he shall let the slave go free because of his eye.' A master who blinds a slave must RELEASE THE SLAVE AS FULL COMPENSATION! The slave's eye is worth the slave's freedom!
cccReferences: CCC 2414 (The slave's bodily dignity demands legal protection).
historicalContext: Slaves are legally protected from physical mutilation — revolutionary in the ancient world.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-khi-yakkeh ish eth-eyn avdo o eth-eyn amato ve-shichetah la-chophshi yeshallchenu tachat eyno*: *la-chophshi* ('to freedom'). *tachat eyno* ('in place of/as compensation for his eye').
crossReferences: Exodus 21:27; Galatians 3:28 ('There is neither slave nor free').
historicalTrivia: The slave's eye (*ayin*) is worth his freedom (*chophshi*) — the Lex Talionis principle applied to protect the weakest!

dominicalIntent: 'If he knocks out the tooth of his slave, male or female, he shall let the slave go free because of his tooth.' Same principle: a knocked-out tooth grants the slave full freedom as compensation.
historicalContext: Every bodily harm to a slave is met with automatic liberation — protecting the slave's dignity through the Lex Talionis.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-im-shen avdo o-shen amato yappil la-chophshi yeshallchenu tachat shinno*: *tachat shinno* ('in place of his tooth').
crossReferences: Exodus 21:26; Galatians 5:1 ('For freedom Christ has set us free'); Philemon 16.
historicalTrivia: This eye-and-tooth liberation law is the direct opposite of the Lex Talionis applied against masters: the slave's physical suffering automatically purchases his freedom!

dominicalIntent: 'When an ox gores a man or a woman to death, the ox shall be stoned, and its flesh shall not be eaten, but the owner of the ox shall not be liable.' Ox-goring law: the ox is executed (returning blood-guilt to the animal), but first-offense owners bear no personal liability.
cccReferences: CCC 2263; CCC 2415 (Animals under human stewardship must not become instruments of death through neglect).
historicalContext: The ox is stoned because it has shed human blood; its meat is unclean (the blood-guilt cannot be consumed).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-khi-yiggach shor eth-ish o eth-ishah va-meth saqol yissaqel ha-shor ve-lo ye'akhel eth-besaro u-va'al ha-shor naqi*: *saqol yissaqel* ('stoning he shall be stoned'). *naqi* ('innocent/guiltless').
crossReferences: Genesis 9:5 ('From the hand of every beast I will require a reckoning for the life of man'); Exodus 21:29.
historicalTrivia: The Talmud (Tractate Bava Qamma) extensively developed these ox-goring laws into a comprehensive theory of tort liability — foundational for Western legal concepts of negligence!

dominicalIntent: 'But if the ox has been accustomed to gore in the past, and its owner has been warned but has not kept it in, and it kills a man or a woman, the ox shall be stoned, and its owner also shall be put to death.' NEGLIGENT OWNER = CAPITAL LIABILITY! Prior warning + failure to restrain = owner's blood-guilt.
cccReferences: CCC 2268 (Negligent homicide as moral culpability); CCC 1735 (Culpability diminished by ignorance, but not when prior warning was given).
historicalContext: Known dangerous animal + owner's foreknowledge + failure to prevent = capital negligence.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-im shor naggach hu mi-tmol shilshom ve-hu'd ba-va'alav ve-lo yishmerenu ve-hemith ish o ishah ha-shor yissaqel ve-gham be'alo yumath*: *mi-tmol shilshom* ('from yesterday and the day before' = habitually). *hu'd* ('he was warned').
crossReferences: Numbers 35:16-21 (degrees of culpability in homicide law).
historicalTrivia: Prior knowledge (*hu'd*) transforms manslaughter into murder in Mosaic law — one of the earliest codifications of the legal concept of prior notice (scienter) in criminal liability!

dominicalIntent: 'If a ransom (*KOPHER*) is imposed on him, then he shall give for the redemption of his life whatever is imposed on him.' The negligent owner can sometimes redeem his life by paying a *KOPHER* (ransom/atonement payment)! THE KOPHER AS ATONEMENT TYPE!
cccReferences: CCC 613 (Christ's death as ransom/*lutron*/kopher for the many); CCC 601.
historicalContext: The *kopher* (ransom) is a substitutionary payment that redeems a life otherwise forfeit to death.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Im-kopher yussath alav ve-natan pidyon naphsho ke-kol asher-yussath alav*: *kopher* ('ransom/atonement price' from *kaphar* = to cover/atone). *pidyon naphsho* ('the ransom for his life').
crossReferences: Mark 10:45 ('The Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom/*lutron* for many'); Isaiah 53:10-12; Psalm 49:8.
historicalTrivia: *Kopher* (ransom) is the same root as *Kapporeth* (Mercy Seat) — the ox-owner's ransom prefigures the ultimate *Kopher* of Christ's blood as the Mercy Seat (Rom 3:25)!

dominicalIntent: 'If it gores a man's son or daughter, he shall be dealt with according to this same rule.' The ox-goring law applies equally to children as to adults — protecting the most vulnerable.
cccReferences: CCC 2270 (The equal dignity of every human person regardless of age).
historicalContext: Equal application of liability regardless of the victim's age or status.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Im-ben yiggach o-vat yiggach ka-mmishpat ha-zeh ye'asseh lo*: *ka-mmishpat ha-zeh* ('according to this same ordinance').
crossReferences: Matthew 18:1-6 (Jesus on the supreme dignity of children).
historicalTrivia: The equal application of ox-goring law to children was unusual in the ancient world, where children often had diminished legal standing.

dominicalIntent: 'If the ox gores a slave, male or female, the owner shall give to their master thirty shekels of silver (*SHELOSHIM SHEQEL KESEF*), and the ox shall be stoned.' THE PRICE OF A SLAVE: 30 SHEKELS OF SILVER — THE EXACT PRICE OF JUDAS' BETRAYAL OF JESUS! **ZECHARIAH 11:12-13 AND MATTHEW 26:15!**
cccReferences: CCC 601 (The price of Jesus' betrayal fulfilling Scripture); CCC 613.
historicalContext: 30 shekels of silver = standard slave price in the ancient Near East AND the price of Jesus' betrayal by Judas (Matt 26:15).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Im-eved yiggach ha-shor o amah kesef sheloshim sheqalim yitten la-adonav ve-ha-shor yissaqel*: *sheloshim sheqalim* ('thirty shekels').
crossReferences: Zechariah 11:12-13 ('They weighed out thirty pieces of silver as my wages... Throw it to the potter — the lordly price at which I was valued by them!'); Matthew 26:15; Matthew 27:3-10.
historicalTrivia: Matthew 27:9-10 fulfills Zechariah 11:12-13 AND Exodus 21:32: Jesus is valued at 30 shekels — THE PRICE OF A SLAVE GORED BY AN OX! Jesus takes the lowest legal monetary valuation of human life and transforms it into the price of infinite redemption!

dominicalIntent: 'When a man opens a pit, or when a man digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it...' PIT LIABILITY LAW! The negligent digger bears financial responsibility for animals that fall into an uncovered pit.
cccReferences: CCC 2411 (Responsibility for damage caused by negligence).
historicalContext: Pits for water or grain storage were common hazards in ancient Palestine.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-khi-yiphtach ish bor o khi-yikhreh ish bor ve-lo yekhassenhu ve-naphal ssammah shor o chamor*: *bor* ('pit/cistern'). *yekhassenhu* ('cover it').
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 22:8 (parapet around rooftops to prevent falls — same principle of duty of care); Luke 14:5.
historicalTrivia: Luke 14:5: Jesus himself uses a fallen-animal-in-pit scenario to teach about Sabbath healing — directly alluding to Exodus 21:33!

dominicalIntent: '...the owner of the pit shall make restoration. He shall give money to its owner, and the dead beast shall be his.' The pit-owner pays full market value for the dead animal and keeps the carcass.
cccReferences: CCC 2411 (Full restitution required for negligent damage).
historicalContext: Restitution principle: full market-value compensation for the dead animal.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ba'al ha-bor yeshalem kesef yashiv li-va'alav ve-ha-meth yihyeh-lo*: *yeshalem* ('shall make full payment' from *shalom/shlem* = completeness).
crossReferences: Leviticus 6:1-5; Numbers 5:5-8 (restitution with a fifth added).
historicalTrivia: The Hebrew word for full payment (*yeshalem*) is from the root *shalom* — suggesting that true peace (*shalom*) comes only through full restitution!

dominicalIntent: 'When one man's ox butts another's, so that it dies, then they shall sell the live ox and share its price, and the dead beast also they shall share.' Shared liability when one ox kills another — proportional justice between two innocent owners.
cccReferences: CCC 2411 (Equitable sharing of loss between equal parties).
historicalContext: Equal distribution of both loss (dead ox) and remaining value (live ox) between two parties of equal standing.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-khi-yiggoph shor-ish eth-shor re'ehu va-meth ve-makkhru eth-ha-shor ha-chai ve-chalqu eth-kaspo ve-gham eth-ha-meth yechellaqu*: *ve-chalqu* ('and they shall divide/share').
crossReferences: Exodus 21:36; Proverbs 18:18 ('The lot puts an end to quarrels and decides between powerful contenders').
historicalTrivia: This equal-sharing principle for mutual accident became a foundational precedent for the legal concept of shared contributory negligence in Western law!

dominicalIntent: 'Or if it is known that the ox has been accustomed to gore in the past, and its owner has not kept it in, he shall repay ox for ox, and the dead beast shall be his.' Known dangerous animal with negligent owner: full replacement ox owed.
historicalContext: Prior knowledge of the animal's dangerous nature removes the innocence of the owner.
translationNuances: Hebrew *O noda ki naggach ha-shor mi-tmol shilshom ve-lo yishmerenu ba'alav shalllem yeshallem shor tachat ha-shor ve-ha-meth yihyeh-lo*: *shalllem yeshallem* ('he shall certainly pay full restitution' — infinitive absolute emphatic).
crossReferences: Exodus 21:29 (same prior-knowledge principle for human death); Romans 13:7 ('Pay to all what is owed to them').
historicalTrivia: This verse introduces the *scienter* principle — prior knowledge of a dangerous propensity creates legal liability — foundational to modern tort law!

dominicalIntent: 'If a man steals an ox or a sheep, and kills it or sells it, he shall repay five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.' FIVEFOLD RESTITUTION FOR OX; FOURFOLD FOR SHEEP! The higher restitution for an ox reflects its greater economic value and the irreplaceable draft-labor lost.
cccReferences: CCC 2412 (Restitution for injustice — restoring what was taken).
historicalContext: Ox restitution is higher (5x) because the ox was an irreplaceable plow animal; the sheep (4x) was a food and wool producer.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ki yignov ish shor o-seh u-thvacaho o-mkharao chamishshah vaqqar yeshalem tachat ha-shor ve-arba tzon tachat ha-sseh*: *chamishshah vaqqar* ('five cattle'). *arba tzon* ('four sheep').
crossReferences: 2 Samuel 12:6 (Nathan's parable: the rich man who stole the poor man's lamb shall repay fourfold — a *rib* / legal dispute with David!); Luke 19:8 (Zacchaeus: 'I give half my goods to the poor, and if I have defrauded anyone of anything, I restore it fourfold').
historicalTrivia: Zacchaeus' voluntary fourfold restitution (Luke 19:8) shows his genuine repentance by exceeding the law's requirements — Jesus declares 'Salvation has come to this house today'!

dominicalIntent: 'If a thief is found breaking in and is struck so that he dies, there shall be no bloodguilt for him.' LAWFUL KILLING OF A BURGLAR IN DARKNESS: NO BLOOD GUILT! Self-defense against a nighttime intruder is legally justified.
cccReferences: CCC 2264 (Legitimate self-defense; defending oneself or others against an unjust aggressor is not murder).
historicalContext: Nighttime burglary (*machtereth* = breaking in) justified lethal self-defense — the homeowner cannot assess the danger in the dark.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Im ba-machttereth yimmatzeh ha-gganav ve-hukkah va-meth eyn lo damim*: *machttereth* ('breaking through' = burglary). *eyn lo damim* ('no blood [guilt] for him').
crossReferences: Luke 22:36 ('Let the one who has no sword sell his cloak and buy one'); John 15:13.
historicalTrivia: CCC 2264 quotes St. Thomas Aquinas on self-defense: 'It is natural to everything to want to keep itself in being, as far as possible.' Exodus 22:2 is the biblical foundation!

dominicalIntent: 'But if the sun has risen on him, there shall be bloodguilt for him. He shall surely pay. If he has nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.' DAYLIGHT KILLING OF A BURGLAR = MURDER! In daylight, the homeowner can assess the threat without lethal force; if the thief survives but has no money, he is sold into slavery for restitution.
cccReferences: CCC 2264 (Self-defense must be proportionate to the actual threat).
historicalContext: In daylight, the homeowner can identify the burglar and the actual threat level — lethal force becomes disproportionate.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Im-zarcha ha-sshemesh alav damim lo eyn kesseph ve-nimkar bi-gnivtho*: *damim* ('blood/bloodguilt'). *bi-gnivtho* ('for his theft').
crossReferences: Exodus 22:4; Luke 12:33 (lay up treasure in heaven where thieves cannot break in).
historicalTrivia: The distinction between nighttime and daytime burglary tracks exactly with the CCC's principle of proportionate self-defense (CCC 2264).

dominicalIntent: 'If the stolen beast is found alive in his possession, whether it is an ox or a donkey or a sheep, he shall pay double.' TWOFOLD RESTITUTION WHEN THE LIVE ANIMAL IS STILL IN THE THIEF'S POSSESSION! Lesser restitution (2x vs 4-5x) because the theft was caught early before the animal was consumed or sold.
cccReferences: CCC 2412 (Restitution proportionate to damage caused).
historicalContext: Finding the live animal in the thief's possession meant the economic harm was minimal — hence a lower twofold restitution.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Im-himmatze thimmatze ve-yado ha-ggenivah mi-shor ad-chamor ad-seh chayyim shnayim yeshalem*: *chayyim* ('living/alive'). *shnayim* ('double/two').
crossReferences: Exodus 22:7,9; Luke 19:8 (Zacchaeus's voluntary fourfold as exceeding the twofold law).
historicalTrivia: The graduated restitution system (2x, 4x, 5x) shows the Bible's sophisticated economic justice: the more serious the damage, the higher the restitution.

dominicalIntent: 'When a man causes a field or vineyard to be grazed over, or lets his beast loose and it feeds in another man's field, he shall make restitution from the best of his own field and of his own vineyard.' CROP DAMAGE RESTITUTION FROM THE BEST OF THE OFFENDER'S FIELD! The injured party receives PREMIUM restitution from the offender's BEST produce.
cccReferences: CCC 2411 (Justice requires restoring what is damaged); CCC 2412.
historicalContext: Free-ranging animals destroying crops was a major economic threat in agricultural communities.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ki yav'er-ish sadeh o-kerem ve-shillach eth-be'iro u-vi'er be-sedeh acherim meytav saddehu u-meytav karmo yeshalem*: *meytav* ('from the best of').
crossReferences: Romans 13:7 ('Pay to all what is owed'); Leviticus 6:2-5.
historicalTrivia: Restitution from the BEST (*meytav*) of the offender's field prevented the offender from using inferior produce as a cheap substitute — enforcing true justice.

dominicalIntent: 'When fire breaks out and catches in thorns so that the stacked grain or the standing grain or the field is consumed, he who started the fire shall make full restitution.' FIRE DAMAGE LIABILITY! The person who started the fire (even accidentally through brush burning) bears full restitution liability for all crop destruction.
cccReferences: CCC 2411 (Duty of care; negligent destruction demands restitution).
historicalContext: Brush fires spreading to neighboring fields were common hazards during dry Palestinian summers.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ki thetze esh u-matze'ah qotzim ve-ne'akhal gaddish o ha-qamah o ha-saddeh shalllem yeshallem ha-ma'ir eth-ha-bba'eirah*: *ha-ma'ir* ('the one who started/kindled the fire').
